athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bell returns as a senior wide receiver and special teams contributor after appearing in all 13 games in 2025 with one start, catching three passes for 54 yards and scoring his first career touchdown against Texas in the Citrus Bowl. The Kansas City, Missouri, native has played 25 career games with seven starts. He arrived from Park Hill as a three-star quarterback recruit and won the 2022 Simone Award.

athletes.name: Jyaire Hill
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $837,962; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Hill is Michigan's returning starting boundary cornerback and an honorable-mention All-Big Ten pick in 2025, when he posted 36 tackles, five pass breakups and an interception against Ohio State. He passed on the NFL Draft to return for his senior season.

athletes.name: Rod Moore
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $579,392; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Moore is a two-time All-Big Ten safety and two-time Michigan captain who was granted a sixth season by the NCAA after knee injuries limited him to three games over the past two years. He is expected to be full-go for preseason camp and start at free safety.

athletes.name: Shamari Earls
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A sophomore cornerback from Richmond, Virginia, Earls played six games as a freshman in 2025 to earn his first varsity letter, debuting in the secondary against Central Michigan and seeing action in the Citrus Bowl against Texas. He signed out of Thomas Dale as a four-star composite recruit rated the No. 86 player nationally and the No. 2 prospect in Virginia, and he won a Virginia 6A long jump state title.

athletes.name: Andrew Marsh
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $970,211; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Marsh led Michigan in receptions and receiving yards as a true freshman in 2025 with 651 receiving yards and enters 2026 as Bryce Underwood's top target. He also projects as the Wolverines' primary return specialist.

athletes.name: Smith Snowden
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $619,327; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Snowden is a Utah transfer defensive back who was an All-Big 12 selection and projects as Michigan's starting nickel corner. He followed head coach Kyle Whittingham from Salt Lake City to Ann Arbor.

athletes.name: Savion Hiter
athletes.source: Estimate (reported to be in line for roughly $1M in first-year NIL earnings; exact figure not disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Hiter is a five-star true freshman running back and the No. 1-ranked back in the 2026 class, who chose Michigan over Ohio State, Tennessee and Georgia. He rushed for 1,698 yards and 26 touchdowns as a high school junior and is expected to share carries with Jordan Marshall.

athletes.name: Jacob Oden
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Oden enters his junior season in Ann Arbor after playing 10 games in 2025, recording three tackles, two pass breakups and his first career interception against Washington. The Detroit native was an Academic All-Big Ten honoree in 2025 and is a two-time letter winner. He signed from Harper Woods, where he helped win a 2023 Division 4 state title, as a four-star recruit and Army All-American selection.

athletes.name: Jordan Young
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Young returns as a sophomore safety from Monroe, North Carolina, after a freshman season in which he played 10 games, made 15 tackles and broke up three passes, including a six-tackle performance against Texas in the Citrus Bowl. He shared defensive player of the week honors for his game at Northwestern. Young signed from Monroe High School as a four-star recruit ranked No. 150 nationally.

athletes.name: Dominic Nichols
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dominic Nichols, a junior edge rusher from Frederick, Maryland, appeared in 12 games for Michigan in 2025 and finished with 19 tackles and a sack, often deployed as a run-containing heavy edge. Entering 2026 he is competing for a larger share of snaps in the Wolverines' edge rotation alongside John Henry Daley and Cameron Brandt, and Michigan beat writers view him as a breakout candidate positioned to lead the room in future seasons.

athletes.name: Cameron Brandt
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $1,008,269; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Brandt is a returning starting edge rusher for Michigan who recorded 1.5 tackles for loss and a half-sack in 2025 after four tackles for loss and three sacks the year before. He withdrew from the transfer portal to stay in Ann Arbor.

athletes.name: Channing Goodwin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Goodwin is a junior wide receiver from Charlotte, North Carolina, who came to Michigan from Providence Day School. He has earned two varsity letters and appeared in all 13 games in 2025 with six starts, catching 12 passes for 148 yards. In high school he caught 65 passes for 1,094 yards and 14 touchdowns as a senior and helped Providence Day win three straight state titles.

athletes.name: Zeke Berry
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $829,344; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Berry is a returning starting cornerback who earned second-team All-Big Ten honors in 2025 with 33 tackles, a team-leading 10 passes defended and an interception. He withdrew from the transfer portal to return to Michigan for 2026.

athletes.name: Jaime Ffrench
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $904,326; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Ffrench is a former five-star wide receiver who transferred to Michigan from Texas after his freshman season and projects as a starting outside receiver. He is one of the fastest players on the Wolverines' roster.

athletes.name: Salesi Moa
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Salesi Moa arrives in Ann Arbor as one of the most decorated freshmen on Michigan's roster. A consensus top-50 national prospect in the 2026 class from Ogden, Utah, he originally committed to Tennessee, signed with Utah in December, then followed coach Kyle Whittingham to Michigan in January 2026. The 6-foot-2 playmaker caught 58 passes for 800 yards and 10 touchdowns as a high school senior and is expected to compete for immediate snaps at wide receiver.

athletes.name: Nathaniel Owusu-Boateng
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $519,296; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Owusu-Boateng is a sophomore linebacker and former top-ranked recruit who projects as a starter for Michigan in 2026. He is the younger brother of NFL linebacker Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah.

athletes.name: JJ Buchanan
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $962,500; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Buchanan is a Utah transfer pass catcher who followed Kyle Whittingham to Michigan and projects as a starting slot receiver. He was ranked No. 8 on Sports Illustrated's list of the Wolverines' most important players for 2026.

athletes.name: Aisea Moa
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moa is a graduate linebacker from North Ogden, Utah, who joined Michigan after three seasons at BYU and one at Michigan State. He has appeared in 27 career games with one start, totaling 29 tackles, 1.5 for loss, two pass breakups and a forced fumble. He played all 12 games for the Spartans in 2025 with 12 tackles. His brother Salesi is a Michigan receiver.

athletes.name: Tommy Carr
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Carr is a freshman quarterback from Saline, Michigan, who arrives after a prep career in which he threw for 5,247 yards and 64 touchdowns across two seasons as a starter and was named MLive Offensive Player of the Year in 2024. He was a three-star composite recruit. His father, Jason, played quarterback at Michigan, and his grandfather Lloyd Carr coached the program from 1995 to 2007.

athletes.name: Chase Herbstreit
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Herbstreit is a sophomore quarterback from Cincinnati who played at St. Xavier High School. He did not see game action as a freshman in 2025 but was named co-Scout Team Player of the Year on offense. A three-year starter for the Bombers, he threw for 3,983 yards and 32 touchdowns across 33 starts. He is the son of Kirk Herbstreit.

athletes.name: Aden Reeder
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reeder is a freshman linebacker from Monroe, Ohio, who arrived from St. Xavier High School in Cincinnati. He was named Greater Catholic League Linebacker of the Year as a senior in 2025 and earned first-team All-District honors twice. As a junior he recorded 74 tackles with 14.5 for loss and three sacks, and he also earned PrepStar All-Midwest Region recognition.

athletes.name: Jo'Ziah Edmond
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Edmond is a junior cornerback from Indianapolis and a two-time letter winner who has appeared in 10 career games, playing two in 2025 and eight as a freshman in 2024, when he recorded two tackles. He signed from NorthWood, which he transferred to after three years at Warren Central, as a four-star composite recruit ranked No. 263 nationally and No. 5 in Indiana.

athletes.name: Enow Etta
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $831,899; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Etta is a returning defensive tackle who played 295 snaps in a rotational role in 2025, posting 15 tackles and 2.5 tackles for loss. He withdrew from the transfer portal and is projected to start alongside Trey Pierce.

athletes.name: Brady Smigiel
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smigiel is a freshman quarterback from Thousand Oaks, California, who arrived from Newbury Park after starting four seasons and throwing for 12,846 yards with 162 touchdown passes. He led the Panthers to the 2024 CIF Division II state championship and was named Cal-Hi Sports Mr. Football that year. He signed as a four-star composite recruit ranked No. 343 nationally.

athletes.name: Troy Bowles
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $549,440; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Bowles is a Georgia transfer linebacker projected to start in the middle for Michigan in 2026 and is the most experienced player in the Wolverines' linebacker room. He is the son of NFL coach Todd Bowles.

athletes.name: Chris Bracy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chris Bracy, a junior safety from Mobile, Alabama, joined Michigan through the transfer portal in January 2026 after a productive season at Memphis, where he finished third on the team with 81 tackles and added 9.5 tackles for loss, nine pass breakups and an interception. He began his career at UAB before transferring to Memphis. Listed at 6-foot-1 and 195 pounds, he brings extensive starting experience and is projected to open the 2026 season in Michigan's starting secondary.

athletes.name: Jaylen Pile
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pile is a freshman wide receiver from Grapevine, Texas, who played at Parish Episcopal School. He caught 55 passes for 1,186 yards and 15 touchdowns as a senior captain in 2025 and added 63 catches for 1,367 yards and 19 scores as a junior. Parish Episcopal won the TAPPS 6A Division I state title in 2025, and he was a two-time first-team all-state selection.

athletes.name: Jordan Deck
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Deck is a freshman safety from Little Elm, Texas, and a graduate of Lone Star High School. He posted 106 tackles with 12 for loss as a senior in 2025, including a 96-yard interception return for a touchdown, and helped Lone Star finish 13-0 and reach the regional final. He was rated a four-star prospect by 247Sports and earned PrepStar All-Southwest Region honors.

athletes.name: Markel Dabney
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dabney is a freshman linebacker from Chesterfield, Virginia, who played at Huguenot High School. He finished his prep career with 151 tackles, including 25 for loss, and more than 2,300 all-purpose yards with 33 touchdowns as a two-way player. As a junior he added four sacks, four forced fumbles and two interceptions returned for scores, and he earned PrepStar All-Atlantic Region honors.

athletes.name: Jordan Marshall
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market roster valuation ~$900K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Marshall is Michigan's returning starting running back and ran for 932 yards and 10 touchdowns in 2025 after taking over as the lead back. He returned for 2026 rather than entering the NFL Draft.

athletes.name: Bryson Kuzdzal
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kuzdzal returns as a senior running back after the most productive season of his career in 2025, when he played nine games with two starts, rushed 76 times for 326 yards and four touchdowns, and ran for 100 yards and three scores at Maryland. The Grand Rapids, Michigan, native is a two-time letter winner who signed from Forest Hills Eastern as a two-star recruit and earned Detroit News All-State honors.

athletes.name: Jamarion Vincent
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Vincent is a freshman cornerback from Waco, Texas, who played at Waco Connally High School. He started at quarterback for two seasons before moving to receiver as a senior, rushing for 2,039 yards and 26 touchdowns and throwing for 1,709 yards over his career. As a senior he caught 54 passes for 839 yards and 12 scores and broke up 11 passes on defense.

athletes.name: Mason Curtis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mason Curtis, a 6-foot-5 junior safety from Nashville, was Michigan's first commitment in its 2024 recruiting class and a four-star prospect. He was named the team's defensive Rookie of the Year in 2024, then split starting duties at safety in 2025, recording 34 tackles, two tackles for loss and an interception. After early stints at linebacker and edge, he has settled at safety and is expected to hold a starting role in 2026.

athletes.name: Micah Ka'apana
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ka'apana is a junior running back from Waianae, Hawaii, who played at Bishop Gorman in Nevada. He is a two-time letter winner at Michigan and appeared in four games in 2025, rushing 10 times for 38 yards. Bishop Gorman won three consecutive Nevada Class 5A titles during his career, and he ran for 1,001 yards and 15 touchdowns in 2022.

athletes.name: Donovan Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a sophomore running back from Savannah, Georgia, who came to Michigan from IMG Academy in Florida. He did not see game action as a freshman in 2025. He transferred to IMG after his freshman season at Savannah Calvary Day, where he rushed for 1,336 yards and 10 touchdowns, and he was invited to the 2025 Navy All-American Bowl.

athletes.name: Taylor Tatum
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tatum, a junior from Longview, Texas, transferred to Michigan from Oklahoma and moved from running back to safety during spring practice, taking reps with the secondary in the spring game. He left the football program shortly before fall camp in 2026 to pursue baseball and is no longer listed on the Wolverines roster. He had been the top-rated running back in the 2024 recruiting class.

athletes.name: Ernest Nunley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nunley is a freshman safety from Carson, California, who finished high school at Western after three years at Narbonne. As a senior in 2025 he made 57 tackles with 20 pass breakups and five interceptions. He was named a Division 4 All-CIF honoree and Western's Lockdown Player of the Year that season.

athletes.name: I'Marion Stewart
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stewart is a junior cornerback from Chicago who spent his senior year at Kenwood Academy after three seasons at Bolingbrook. He has not seen game action in two seasons at Michigan but was twice named a scout team player of the week as a freshman. As a high school senior he caught 38 passes for 909 yards and nine touchdowns.

athletes.name: Kainoa Winston
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Winston is a sophomore safety from Montgomery Village, Maryland, who played at Gonzaga College High School. He made his debut in 2025, appearing in one game and recording two tackles to earn his first varsity letter. A four-star recruit, he also holds Gonzaga school records in the 55-meter and 200-meter dashes and qualified for New Balance Nationals in track.

athletes.name: Jonathan Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is a freshman running back from Westerville, Ohio, who played at St. Francis DeSales. He rushed for more than 2,000 career yards and ranks seventh in program history in rushing yards and eighth in touchdowns. As a junior in 2024 he carried 202 times for 1,295 yards and 16 touchdowns, and he earned PrepStar All-Midwest Region honors.

athletes.name: Chase Taylor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chase Taylor, a sophomore linebacker from Ellenwood, Georgia, played at Stockbridge High School and signed with Michigan as a three-star recruit in the 2025 class, choosing the Wolverines over offers from USC, Florida State and LSU among others. As a freshman in 2025 he appeared in 10 games, mostly on special teams, totaling 10 tackles and recovering an onside kick. With Michigan's linebacker rotation turning over in 2026, he is widely projected for a much larger defensive role.

athletes.name: Max Alford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alford is a graduate linebacker from Park City, Utah, who transferred to Michigan after three seasons at Utah State and one at BYU. He has played 28 career games with five starts, recording 62 tackles, 5.5 for loss and one sack, and posted 21 tackles for the Cougars in 2025. He is a two-time Academic All-Mountain West honoree and a nephew of Michigan running backs coach Tony Alford.

athletes.name: Nico Andrighetto
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Andrighetto is a graduate safety from Mountain View, California, and a four-time letter winner at Michigan. He was named co-Scout Team Player of the Year on defense in 2025 and is a three-time Academic All-Big Ten honoree. At Saint Francis he led his team with 61 tackles as a senior and was the West Catholic Athletic League defensive back of the year. His brother Lucas also played at Michigan.

athletes.name: Jeremiah Lowe
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lowe is a junior cornerback from Lexington, Kentucky, who played at Frederick Douglass High School. He made his collegiate debut in 2025, appearing in two games to earn a varsity letter, and was named Academic All-Big Ten. In high school he helped Douglass go 15-0 and win the 2022 KHSAA Class 5A state championship, and he recorded four interceptions as a sophomore.

athletes.name: Gary Stacy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stacy is a sophomore running back from Grosse Pointe Woods, Michigan, who joined the Wolverines as a walk-on in the spring of 2026. He played at University Liggett School under coach Andre Rison and rushed for 1,525 yards and 25 touchdowns as a junior, adding 798 yards and 10 scores as a senior. He was a three-time first-team All-Metro selection.

athletes.name: Kaden Catchings
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Catchings is a freshman linebacker from Jackson, Mississippi, who played at Hartfield Academy. A two-way player, he rushed for 1,065 yards and 16 touchdowns and made 47 tackles as a junior in 2024. Hartfield reached three straight state championship games from 2023 through 2025 and won back-to-back titles, and he earned PrepStar All-Southeast Region honors.

athletes.name: Stuart Blake
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Blake is a junior kicker from Jenkintown, Pennsylvania, who played at Jenkintown High School. He has not seen game action in his first two seasons on the Michigan roster, and the program lists no further biographical details for him.

athletes.name: Joshua Nichols
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nichols is a graduate cornerback from Detroit who played at Renaissance High School. He earned his first varsity letter in 2025 after appearing in one game in the secondary. As a high school senior he made 82 tackles with 11 forced fumbles and was a first-team Division 7 all-state selection. His brother Jeremy was also a Michigan linebacker.

athletes.name: Tomas O'Meara
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: O'Meara is a junior running back from Ann Arbor who played at Father Gabriel Richard High School. He earned his first varsity letter in 2025, appearing in two games and carrying 11 times for 83 yards, including eight rushes for 71 yards at Maryland. He was also recognized twice as a scout team offensive player of the week.

athletes.name: Julius Holly
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Holly is a sophomore edge rusher from Alpharetta, Georgia, who made his Michigan debut along the defensive line against Texas in the Citrus Bowl to earn his first varsity letter as a freshman in 2025. He signed from Alpharetta High School as a four-star composite recruit ranked No. 371 nationally, the No. 30 edge rusher and the No. 51 player in Georgia, after recording 57 tackles and eight sacks as a junior.

athletes.name: Sam Baron
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Baron is a senior defensive back from Cadillac, Michigan, who joined the football program as a walk-on in the spring of 2026 after running with the school's club track program. At Lake City Area he was a two-year captain in football and baseball and graduated as valedictorian. His father, Phil, played at Michigan State.

athletes.name: Bryce Wilcox
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilcox is a graduate wide receiver from Sharpsburg, Georgia, who played at Trinity Christian. He earned his first varsity letter in 2025 after appearing in one game, and was named the team's Scout Team Player of the Year on special teams as well as Academic All-Big Ten. In high school he totaled 1,319 receiving yards and 19 touchdowns and was a first-team all-state pick.

athletes.name: Max Reyes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reyes is a graduate safety from Southlake, Texas, who played at Southlake Carroll. He earned a varsity letter in 2024 after appearing in one game and assisting on a tackle against Northwestern. He received the Humphries-Miller Scholarship Award in 2025 and is a two-time Academic All-Big Ten honoree enrolled in the Ross School of Business.

athletes.name: Jeffrey Chukwu
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chukwu is a junior defensive back from Severna Park, Maryland, who joined the program in the fall of 2025 in his first year playing organized football. He was named a scout team special teams player of the week three times and earned Academic All-Big Ten honors. He previously excelled as a soccer forward at Severna Park High School.

athletes.name: Jalen Hoffman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hoffman is a senior tight end and fullback from Burke, Virginia, and a three-time letter winner. He appeared in all 13 games in 2025 in the H-back role and on special teams, making one tackle and recovering an onside kick at Michigan State. He was an Academic All-Big Ten honoree in 2024. At Lake Braddock he caught 33 passes for 563 yards and five touchdowns as a senior captain.

athletes.name: Zach Ludwig
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ludwig is a junior linebacker from South Park, Pennsylvania. He made his collegiate debut in 2025 against Central Michigan to earn his first varsity letter. He played quarterback and linebacker at South Park High School, recording 53 tackles as a senior, and was a PrepStar All-Eastern Region selection. His uncle, Ben Herbert, was a Michigan strength and conditioning coach.

athletes.name: Eli Owens
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Owens is a sophomore tight end from Alcoa, Tennessee, who played two games as a freshman in 2025, debuting at fullback and tight end against Central Michigan and contributing on special teams in the Citrus Bowl. He signed from Alcoa High School, a program that won 10 consecutive state titles, as a three-star composite recruit rated the No. 27 tight end nationally and the No. 20 player in Tennessee.

athletes.name: Nathaniel Staehling
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Staehling is a graduate linebacker from Baxter, Minnesota, who transferred to Michigan after four seasons at North Dakota State. He was a team captain in 2025 and posted 75 tackles, six for loss, 1.5 sacks and three interceptions across 13 games. He has 32 career appearances with 91 tackles. He played quarterback, running back, safety and specialist at Brainerd High School.

athletes.name: Gavin Magorien
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Magorien is a sophomore long snapper from Erie, Pennsylvania, who came to Michigan after appearing in all 12 games as Marshall's long snapper in 2025. He also caught a 12-yard pass against James Madison that season. At McDowell High School he was rated a five-star long snapper and the No. 11 snapper in the 2025 class by Rubio Long Snapping.

athletes.name: Crandall Quinn
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Quinn is a senior tight end from Grand Rapids, Michigan, who played at Forest Hills Central. He spent two seasons with the Michigan men's lacrosse program from 2024 to 2025 before joining football, and he earned his first varsity letter in 2025 after appearing in one game. He was also an Academic All-Big Ten honoree.

athletes.name: Adam Bazzi
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bazzi is a junior linebacker from Rochester Hills, Michigan, who joined the program in the fall of 2025 and was an Academic All-Big Ten honoree. At Stoney Creek High School he was a captain in football, wrestling and lacrosse, earned all-state honors twice on the mat and finished as state runner-up at 190 pounds as a senior.

athletes.name: Nico Crawford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Crawford is a graduate long snapper from Dublin, Ohio, who joins Michigan after a season at Illinois as a walk-on, a season at Charlotte and two at Pittsburgh. He has appeared in 37 career games as a long snapper, handling all 13 games in each of the last two seasons for the Panthers. He graduated from Pitt in 2025 with a degree in communication.

athletes.name: Luke Hamilton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hamilton is a junior offensive lineman from Avon, Ohio. He made his Michigan debut in 2025 against Central Michigan to earn his first varsity letter and was an Academic All-Big Ten honoree. A four-star recruit at Avon High School, he helped the Eagles win a school-record 14 games in 2023 and qualified for the state track meet in discus and shot put.

athletes.name: McHale Blade
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Blade is a freshman edge rusher from Country Club Hills, Illinois, who played his final two seasons at Simeon Career Academy after two years at Hillcrest. He was a team captain as a senior in 2025 and was rated a four-star prospect and a PrepStar Top 300 All-American, ranked among the top 10 players in Illinois.

athletes.name: Ace Hamilton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hamilton is a freshman offensive lineman from Clinton, Maryland, who played at St. John's College High School after beginning his career at Rock Creek. He was a three-time All-WCAC selection, earning first-team honors as a senior in 2025, and was named MVP and co-MVP at the 2025 Baltimore Under Armour Next camp.

athletes.name: Christian Pierce
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pierce is a sophomore linebacker from Chicago who played at Brother Rice High School. He was an All-Chicago Catholic League selection and his team's defensive MVP as a senior in 2024, and he twice made the Daily Southtown All-Area team. His brother, Trey Pierce, is a defensive lineman at Michigan.

athletes.name: Jake Guarnera
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $718,388; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Guarnera is Michigan's returning starting center after holding the job through the 2025 season. He withdrew from the transfer portal to return for 2026.

athletes.name: Deyvid Palepale
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Palepale is a junior defensive lineman listed from Anchorage, Alaska, who made his debut in 2025, playing two games along the defensive line to earn his first varsity letter. He was twice named scout team defensive player of the week that season. Born in Alaska, he moved to Pennsylvania at 14 and signed as a three-star composite recruit and a 2024 Polynesian Bowl selection.

athletes.name: Andrew Sprague
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $1,208,422; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Sprague is Michigan's returning starting right tackle and is viewed by the staff as an All-Big Ten-caliber lineman entering 2026. He is the highest-valued offensive lineman on the roster.

athletes.name: Nathan Efobi
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $788,229; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Efobi is a senior interior offensive lineman who projects as a starting guard for Michigan in 2026. He was ranked No. 20 on Sports Illustrated's list of the Wolverines' most important players.

athletes.name: Randy Keumogne
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Keumogne spent the 2025 season as a graduate edge rusher at Michigan, appearing in one game on special teams and along the edge to earn a varsity letter. The Oakdale, Minnesota, native is no longer listed on the Wolverines roster after he was not granted additional years of eligibility and turned to NFL tryouts. He was an All-State selection at Tartan High School.

athletes.name: Travis Moten
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moten is a sophomore defensive lineman from Louisville, Kentucky, who made his college debut along the defensive line against Central Michigan in 2025 to earn his first varsity letter. He signed from Fern Creek as a three-star composite recruit after a senior season with 95 tackles, 30 for loss and 19.5 sacks, and he was a two-time first-team all-district honoree.

athletes.name: Eli Musmand
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Musmand is listed as a sophomore edge rusher from Brooklyn, New York, with the Michigan Wolverines. He does not appear on the program's current official online roster, and no additional verified biographical details were available.

athletes.name: John Weidenbach
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Weidenbach is a senior linebacker from Naperville, Illinois, who played at Benet Academy. He earned his first varsity letter in 2025 after appearing in one game and is a two-time Academic All-Big Ten honoree. He recorded 114 tackles with 16 for loss as a high school senior. His grandfather, Jack Weidenbach, was Michigan's athletic director.

athletes.name: Brooks Bahr
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bahr is a senior offensive lineman from Lake Forest, Illinois, who played at Loyola Academy. He made his Michigan debut on the offensive line in 2025 to earn his first varsity letter and is a two-time Academic All-Big Ten honoree. He played defensive line in high school, making 49 tackles as a senior while helping Loyola win the Class 8A title.

athletes.name: James Kavouklis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kavouklis is a graduate offensive lineman from Tampa, Florida, who played at Berkeley Prep. He has earned two varsity letters, debuting at center as a freshman in 2022 and playing center again against Central Michigan in 2025. He is a three-time Academic All-Big Ten honoree and was a first-team Florida Class 3A all-state selection in high school.

athletes.name: Andrew Babalola
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Andrew Babalola, a sophomore offensive tackle from Overland Park, Kansas, was a five-star recruit in Michigan's 2025 class out of Blue Valley Northwest, notable for a player who only took up football as a high school junior. He missed the 2025 season with a knee injury but entered 2026 fall camp fully healthy and is competing with Blake Frazier for the starting left tackle job. Listed around 6-foot-6 and 315 pounds, he has drawn comparisons from coach Kyle Whittingham to first-round tackles he coached at Utah.

athletes.name: Dan Taraboi
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taraboi is a graduate offensive lineman from Cedarburg, Wisconsin. He is a three-time letter winner at Michigan, debuting along the offensive line against UConn in 2022 and playing again in 2025. He is a two-time Academic All-Big Ten honoree and was a first-team WFCA All-Region selection at Cedarburg High School.

athletes.name: Houston Ka'aha'aina-Torres
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ka'aha'aina-Torres is a sophomore offensive lineman from Waimanalo, Hawaii, who transferred to Michigan after one season at Nebraska, where he played two games in 2025 and earned a varsity letter. He signed out of St. Louis High School, a 2024 state champion, as a three-star composite recruit rated the No. 45 interior lineman nationally and the No. 4 player in Hawaii, and he played in the 2025 Polynesian Bowl.

athletes.name: Trent Middleton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Middleton is a senior long snapper from Fullerton, California, who came to Michigan from UCLA and did not see game action in 2025. He was a preferred walk-on with the Bruins out of Orange Lutheran, where Kohl's Kicking graded him a five-star snapper and the No. 7 long snapper nationally in the 2023 class.

athletes.name: Brady Norton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Norton is a senior offensive lineman from Mission Viejo, California, who transferred from Cal Poly and earned his first Michigan letter in 2025. He played seven games with three starts, opening at right guard against New Mexico and starting at right tackle against Texas in the Citrus Bowl. He started all 11 games at left tackle for Cal Poly in 2024 and was named an FCS Freshman All-American.

athletes.name: Evan Link
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Evan Link, a senior offensive lineman from Burke, Virginia, signed with Michigan as a four-star recruit and has become one of the line's most experienced players, appearing in all 13 games with 11 starts in 2024 and starting seven more in 2025 before a knee injury ended his season. Valued for his flexibility between tackle and guard, he started at left tackle in Michigan's spring game and is battling for a first-team job at multiple spots in 2026.

athletes.name: Peter Donini
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Donini is a sophomore offensive lineman from Summit, New Jersey, who joined the football program as a walk-on in the spring of 2026. He competed for Michigan's track and field team in the shot put as a freshman and won two national high school shot put titles in 2025, at the Nike indoor and New Balance outdoor meets, while at Delbarton.

athletes.name: Avery Gach
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gach is a sophomore offensive lineman from Franklin, Michigan, who played at Wylie E. Groves High School. He appeared in five games on special teams as a freshman in 2025 to earn his first varsity letter. A four-star recruit and four-year starter at tackle, he was the first two-year captain under Groves coach Brendan Flaherty.

athletes.name: Manuel Beigel
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Beigel is a junior lineman from Frankfurt, Germany, who moved to the United States to attend Choate Rosemary Hall in Connecticut. A two-time letter winner, he played in seven games in 2025, making a tackle and recovering a fumble. He played soccer before taking up football in 2020 and earned Academic All-Big Ten honors in 2025.

athletes.name: Blake Frazier
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $1,014,153; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Frazier is a returning Michigan offensive lineman who projects as the starting left tackle in 2026 after starting along the front in 2025. He is one of six linemen with starting experience back for the Wolverines.

athletes.name: Marky Walbridge
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Walbridge is a freshman offensive lineman from Hanover, Massachusetts, who arrives after four varsity seasons starting at left tackle for St. Sebastian's, where he was credited with allowing no sacks as a sophomore and junior. He was a four-star composite recruit ranked No. 228 nationally, the No. 24 offensive tackle and the No. 2 player in Massachusetts, and he won the ISL Lineman of the Year award in 2024.

athletes.name: Hogan Hansen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hansen is a junior tight end from Bellevue, Washington, who has 13 career receptions for 152 yards and a touchdown. He caught six passes for 74 yards across four games in 2025 and was named the team's offensive rookie of the year in 2024. He was an Academic All-Big Ten honoree in 2025 and signed as a four-star composite recruit ranked the No. 21 tight end nationally.

athletes.name: Jamar Browder
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Browder is a sophomore wide receiver from Jacksonville, Florida, who played at Santaluces Community High School. He appeared in seven games as a freshman in 2025 to earn his first varsity letter. In high school he caught 50 passes for 1,137 yards and 12 touchdowns as a senior after 39 receptions for 730 yards and 14 scores as a junior.

athletes.name: C.J. Charleston
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Charleston is listed as a graduate wide receiver from Cleveland, Ohio, with the Michigan Wolverines. He does not appear on the program's current official online roster, and no additional verified biographical details were available.

athletes.name: Zack Marshall
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zack Marshall, a senior tight end from Carlsbad, California, came to Michigan as a three-star recruit from Carlsbad High School. After two seasons spent mainly on special teams, he broke into the receiving rotation in 2025 with 16 catches for 199 yards and a touchdown. With Michigan shifting toward more one-tight-end sets under new head coach Kyle Whittingham and coordinator Jason Beck, Marshall's blocking ability and late-season growth as a pass catcher make him the projected lead tight end in 2026.

athletes.name: Jacob Washington
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Washington is a sophomore wide receiver from Harvey, Louisiana, who played at Archbishop Shaw after two years at New Orleans Jesuit. He appeared in two games as a freshman in 2025 to earn his first varsity letter. He helped Archbishop Shaw win consecutive district titles and was a 2024 first-team All-District selection on offense.

athletes.name: Logan Forbes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Forbes is a graduate wide receiver from Clarkston, Michigan, and a three-time letter winner. He played in all 13 games on special teams in 2025, making two tackles, and was twice named the team's Scout Team Player of the Year on offense. He is also a three-time Academic All-Big Ten honoree.

athletes.name: Travis Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a freshman wide receiver from Chesapeake, Virginia, who arrives from Oscar Smith after helping the Tigers win Class 6 state titles in 2024 and 2025. He caught 63 passes for 1,053 yards and 17 touchdowns as a junior and was a first-team all-state selection. He signed as a four-star composite recruit ranked No. 107 nationally, the No. 14 receiver and the No. 3 player in Virginia.

athletes.name: Lugard Edokpayi
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Edokpayi is a junior edge rusher from Bowie, Maryland, who earned his first varsity letter in 2025 after appearing in eight games off the edge and on special teams. He was an Academic All-Big Ten honoree that season. He signed from Bishop McNamara as a four-star composite recruit ranked No. 219 nationally, the No. 20 edge rusher and the No. 7 player in Maryland.

athletes.name: Deakon Tonielli
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tonielli is a senior tight end from Oswego, Illinois, who broke through in 2025, playing all 13 games with two starts and catching eight passes for 72 yards while adding two tackles on special teams. He was named the team's most improved player on special teams. He signed from Oswego High School as a four-star composite recruit ranked the No. 20 tight end nationally.

athletes.name: Kaleb Schlecht
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Schlecht is a senior wide receiver from Ann Arbor who played at Skyline High School. He made his collegiate debut against Central Michigan in 2025 to earn his first varsity letter and is a two-time Academic All-Big Ten honoree. He was also named a scout team offensive player of the week that season.

athletes.name: John Henry Daley
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $1,224,999; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Daley is a Utah transfer edge rusher who earned first-team Walter Camp All-America honors in 2025 with 48 tackles, 17.5 tackles for loss and 11.5 sacks in 11 games. He followed head coach Kyle Whittingham to Ann Arbor and projects as Michigan's top pass rusher.

athletes.name: Hudson Hollenbeck
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hudson Hollenbeck, a graduate punter from Collierville, Tennessee, returns as Michigan's incumbent starting punter, carrying a 43.2-yard average across 40 career punts with a long of 67 yards. Off the field he partners with the University of Michigan Health Rogel Cancer Center, donating to cancer research for every punt of 50 or more yards and every punt downed inside the 20, a cause he took up in honor of his late mother.

athletes.name: Jonah Lea'ea
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jonah Lea'ea, a senior defensive lineman from San Mateo, California, transferred to Michigan after starting all 13 games for Utah in 2025, when he recorded 38 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, a sack and a forced fumble. The 6-foot-5, 285-pound tackle followed head coach Kyle Whittingham and defensive line assistant Lewis Powell from Salt Lake City to Ann Arbor and is expected to be a core piece of Michigan's interior line rotation in 2026.

athletes.name: Ted Hammond
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hammond is a junior defensive lineman from Cincinnati who played at St. Xavier High School. He made his Michigan debut along the defensive line in 2025 to earn his first varsity letter and was an Academic All-Big Ten honoree. As a high school junior he recorded 46 tackles with 10.5 for loss and seven sacks.

athletes.name: Benny Patterson III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Patterson is a sophomore edge rusher from Newburgh, Indiana, who earned his first varsity letter in 2025 by playing five games, mostly on special teams, and appearing along the defensive line in the Citrus Bowl. He signed from Castle as a four-star composite recruit ranked No. 342 nationally after a senior year with 70 tackles, 14 for loss and seven sacks.

athletes.name: Hunter Robertson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Robertson is a senior punter from Huntington Woods, Michigan, who came to Michigan after two seasons at Clarion. He appeared in 22 games for the Golden Eagles, punting in 15 of them and handling kickoffs throughout. He made his Michigan debut holding on placekicks against Texas in the Cheez-It Citrus Bowl to earn his first varsity letter.

athletes.name: Nate Marshall
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Marshall is a sophomore edge rusher from Oak Park, Illinois, who played 11 games as a freshman in 2025, recording six tackles and recovering a kickoff while contributing on the edge and on special teams. He signed from Fenwick as a four-star composite recruit ranked No. 55 nationally and the No. 3 player in Illinois, and Rivals graded him a five-star prospect.

athletes.name: Trey Pierce
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market valuation $829,943; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Pierce is Michigan's returning starting defensive tackle who started all 13 games in 2025 and recorded 30 tackles. He withdrew from the transfer portal to return to the Wolverines for his senior season.

athletes.name: Chibi Anwunah
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anwunah is listed as a graduate defensive lineman from Canton, Michigan, with the Michigan Wolverines. He does not appear on the program's current official online roster, and no additional verified biographical details were available.

athletes.name: Trey Butkowski
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Trey Butkowski, a sophomore kicker from Orlando, transferred to Michigan in January 2026 after a record-setting debut season at Pittsburgh, where he made 20 of 23 field goals and 43 of 44 extra points, earned second-team All-ACC honors and was named to Pro Football Focus's All-Freshman team. A product of Orlando's Lake Nona High School, he was rated the nation's No. 9 kicking prospect by Kohl's Kicking and is the clear favorite to handle Michigan's placekicking in 2026.

athletes.name: Bobby Kanka
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kanka is a sophomore defensive lineman from Howell, Michigan, who made his college debut against Central Michigan in 2025 and recorded a tackle for loss from the interior to earn his first varsity letter. He signed from Howell High School as a three-star composite recruit ranked No. 491 nationally and was invited to the 2025 Army All-American Bowl. His father, Tom, played in the NFL.

athletes.name: Jayden Woods
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$843K for 2026; Rivals/On3 figures quoted at ~$780K-$1M; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Woods is Florida's starting JACK edge rusher and posted 28 tackles, 3.5 sacks and 5.0 tackles for loss as a true freshman in 2025 while logging 448 snaps, the most of any Gators defensive lineman. He was a third-team preseason All-SEC selection.

athletes.name: Vernell Brown III
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$566K for 2026; On3 lists a ~$1M NIL valuation; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Brown is Florida's leading returning receiver after catching 40 passes for 512 yards as a true freshman in 2025, the first true freshman in program history to lead the Gators in both categories. He was named second-team preseason All-SEC as a return specialist.

athletes.name: Bryce Thornton
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$603K for 2026; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Thornton is Florida's returning starting strong safety and led the Gators with six pass breakups in 2025. He re-signed with Florida Victorious for his senior season.

athletes.name: Lagonza Hayward
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hayward is a sophomore safety from Lyons, Ga., who arrived at Florida from Toombs County High School and is entering his second year in the program. He wears No. 2 and is listed at 207 pounds. Offseason roster reviews project him as a rotational backup in a safety group headlined by senior Bryce Thornton and Baylor transfer DJ Coleman, with special teams offering another route to snaps.

athletes.name: Onis Konanbanny
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Onis Konanbanny is a redshirt freshman cornerback listed at 6-0, 190 pounds who comes from London, England and played at Heathwood Hall Episcopal School in Columbia, South Carolina. He grew up playing soccer in Europe before taking up football, and he signed with Florida in the 2025 class after flipping his commitment from Tennessee.

athletes.name: Bailey Stockton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stockton is a redshirt junior wide receiver from Bogart, Ga., who transferred to Florida from Georgia Tech ahead of the 2026 season. He played at Prince Avenue Christian and posted his best college numbers in 2025, catching 21 passes for 233 yards across 11 appearances. Florida added him for slot quickness and depth behind Eric Singleton Jr., Vernell Brown III and Dallas Wilson.

athletes.name: TJ Abrams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Abrams is a wide receiver at Florida from Fort Myers, where he played at Dunbar High School. He appeared in 10 games in 2025 with one start, catching 13 passes for 201 yards. A four star signee in the 2024 class, he was ranked among the top wide receivers nationally by ESPN and has twice made the SEC Fall Academic Honor Roll. He wears No. 4 and is listed at 196 pounds.

athletes.name: Myles Graham
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$466K for 2026; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Graham led Florida with 76 tackles in 2025, becoming the first Gators linebacker to lead the team in tackles since 2021, and added two sacks and seven tackles for loss. He represented Florida at 2026 SEC Media Days.

athletes.name: Micah Mays Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mays is a redshirt junior wide receiver from West Palm Beach, Fla., who joined Florida through the transfer portal from Wake Forest. He played high school football at The Benjamin School and caught 18 passes for 302 yards and two touchdowns in 2025. He is one of three portal receivers Florida added for depth and rotation snaps this fall.

athletes.name: J'Vari Flowers
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Flowers is a sophomore cornerback from Miami, Fla., who signed with Florida out of Miami Northwestern. He saw considerable action as a freshman in 2025 and returns for a second season in a corner group that also includes Dijon Johnson and Cormani McClain. Listed at 189 pounds and wearing No. 6, he projects as a rotation piece with room to grow.

athletes.name: Dallas Wilson
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$508K for 2026; On3 does not publish a current figure; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Wilson is a former five-star recruit who caught 12 passes for 174 yards and three touchdowns in an injury-shortened 2025 redshirt season, including a program-record true-freshman debut of 111 yards and two scores against Texas. He re-signed with Florida Victorious for 2026.

athletes.name: Amir Jackson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson is a redshirt sophomore tight end from Statesboro, Ga., who came to Florida from Portal High School. He entered the transfer portal after the 2025 season before reversing course and returning to the Gators. Now in his third year in the program and listed at 232 pounds, he competes in a tight end room reshaped by portal additions Evan Chieca, Lacota Dippre and Luke Harpring.

athletes.name: Ty Jackson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson is a sophomore inside linebacker from Fort Lauderdale, Fla., who arrived at Florida out of Seminole Ridge High School. Entering his second year in the program at 228 pounds, he is projected as a rotational piece behind established starters Myles Graham and Jaden Robinson, with Aaron Chiles also ahead of him after an expanded role in 2025.

athletes.name: Aaron Chiles
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$400K for 2026; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Chiles is a projected starting linebacker for Florida entering his junior season and was a top-10 national linebacker recruit out of Our Lady of Good Counsel. He re-signed with Florida Victorious for 2026 and rotates between MIKE and WILL.

athletes.name: Tramell Jones Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is in a two-man competition with Aaron Philo for Florida's starting quarterback job after completing 21 of 35 passes for 191 yards and two touchdowns as a true freshman behind DJ Lagway in 2025. He re-signed with the Florida Victorious collective for 2026.

athletes.name: Drake Stubbs
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Drake Stubbs is a sophomore safety for the Florida Gators from Jacksonville, Florida, where he played at Mandarin High School. He wears No. 9 and is listed at 6-1, 203 pounds on the 2026 roster.

athletes.name: Cam Dooley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dooley is a junior safety from Valley, Ala., who transferred to Florida from Kentucky in the 2026 portal cycle. He played his high school football at Valley High School in his hometown and was regarded as one of the top 10 safeties available in the portal. Listed at 207 pounds and wearing No. 10, he joins DJ Coleman as an experienced addition to the Florida secondary.

athletes.name: Aaron Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Aaron Williams is a redshirt sophomore quarterback from Orlando, Florida who played at Winter Park High School. He is listed at 6-1, 206 pounds and wears No. 10 as a walk-on on the Gators' 2026 roster.

athletes.name: Will Griffin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Griffin is a freshman quarterback from Treasure Island, Fla., who signed with Florida out of Jesuit High School in Tampa. Listed at 219 pounds and wearing No. 11, he enters a quarterback room that also includes Georgia Tech transfer Aaron Philo, redshirt freshman Tramell Jones Jr. and redshirt junior Aidan Warner, making a developmental first season the likeliest outcome.

athletes.name: LJ McCray
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McCray is a former five-star recruit entering his redshirt sophomore season in Florida's edge rotation. He was widely cited as the Gators' top breakout candidate on defense after 2026 spring practice.

athletes.name: Ben Hanks III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hanks is a redshirt freshman cornerback from Overtown, Fla., who signed with Florida out of Booker T. Washington High School as a highly rated recruit. He is a Florida legacy whose father played for the Gators. Now in his second year in the program at 186 pounds, he is competing for rotation snaps behind Dijon Johnson and Cormani McClain.

athletes.name: Aaron Philo
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$1.51M for 2026, highest on Florida's roster; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Philo is competing for Florida's starting quarterback job after transferring from Georgia Tech alongside new offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner. He completed 57.8 percent of 102 career passes for 938 yards and two touchdowns over two seasons with the Yellow Jackets.

athletes.name: Jadan Baugh
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$1.3M for 2026; On3 NIL valuation quoted at ~$931K-$1M; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Baugh is Florida's featured running back and ran for 1,170 yards and eight touchdowns in 2025, becoming the program's first 1,000-yard rusher since 2015. He was a second-team preseason All-SEC pick and one of three Gators sent to 2026 SEC Media Days.

athletes.name: Jordy Lowery
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lowery is a redshirt senior cornerback from Bartow, Fla., who joined Florida through the transfer portal after stops at Western Carolina and East Carolina. He played at Bartow High School in his hometown. Listed at 183 pounds and wearing No. 13, he was added as a veteran capable of taking immediate snaps in a cornerback group working in several new faces.

athletes.name: KJ Ford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ford is a freshman edge rusher from Dallas, Texas, who signed with Florida out of Duncanville High School as one of the higher profile recruits in the Gators' class. Listed at 250 pounds and wearing No. 14, he plays the JACK position and joins a group that includes Jayden Woods, Kamran James and LJ McCray, so early snaps would likely come in rotation.

athletes.name: CJ Bronaugh
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: CJ Bronaugh is a freshman cornerback from Orlando who played at Windermere High School and signed with Florida in the 2026 class. He is also a state champion sprinter who won back to back Class 1A titles in the 100 meters, and as a senior he added two interceptions on defense along with two kickoff return touchdowns.

athletes.name: Luke Harpring
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Harpring is a redshirt sophomore tight end from Atlanta, Ga., who transferred to Florida from Georgia Tech ahead of 2026. He played at Marist School in Atlanta and is listed at 237 pounds. He is one of three portal tight ends the Gators added alongside Evan Chieca and Lacota Dippre, which sets up open competition for snaps behind the top of the depth chart.

athletes.name: TJ Bullard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bullard is a redshirt senior inside linebacker from Tampa, Fla., who transferred to Florida from UCF. He played at Berkeley Prep, where his brother Titus Bullard, now also on the Gators roster, went to school. Listed at 213 pounds and wearing No. 16, he profiles as a special teams contributor and depth linebacker behind Myles Graham and Jaden Robinson.

athletes.name: Aidan Warner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Warner is a redshirt junior quarterback from Winter Park, Fla., who came to Florida from Yale and attended Winter Park High School. He is entering his third year in the program at 202 pounds. He returns to a quarterback room reshaped by Georgia Tech transfer Aaron Philo, with Tramell Jones Jr. and freshman Will Griffin also in the mix for the job.

athletes.name: Titus Bullard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Titus Bullard is a redshirt sophomore edge rusher from Tampa, Florida who played at Berkeley Prep. Listed at 6-4, 239 pounds, he is a walk-on at the JACK position on Florida's 2026 roster.

athletes.name: Lacota Dippre
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dippre arrives at Florida as a redshirt junior tight end from Scranton, Pa., after stops at Charlotte and James Madison. He started 13 of 14 games for the Dukes in 2025, catching 17 passes for 192 yards and three touchdowns while also converting four fake punts on the ground, and he earned All-Sun Belt honorable mention. At Lakeland High School he was a two-time District 2 Player of the Year and finished with 113 career receptions for 1,494 yards. He is listed on Florida's 2026 roster in his first season with the Gators.

athletes.name: Davian Groce
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davian Groce is a freshman wide receiver from Frisco, Texas who played at Lone Star High School and was among the highest rated signees in Florida's 2026 class. He worked at both running back and receiver in high school, passing 2,000 career yards rushing and 2,000 receiving, and posted 15 catches for 310 yards and four touchdowns in a state semifinal win.

athletes.name: Jaylen Lloyd
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lloyd is a redshirt junior wide receiver from Omaha, Neb., who reached Florida through the transfer portal after previous stops at Nebraska and Oklahoma State. He played at Omaha Westside High School and is listed at 185 pounds wearing No. 19. He is one of three portal receivers the Gators added, joining Micah Mays Jr. and Bailey Stockton in a competitive rotation.

athletes.name: Duke Clark
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clark is a redshirt freshman running back from Tampa, Fla., who signed with Florida out of Plant High School. Listed at 208 pounds and wearing No. 20, he is entering his second year in the program. He returns to a deep backfield led by 1,000 yard rusher Jadan Baugh and reinforced by transfers Evan Pryor and London Montgomery, so carries will be contested.

athletes.name: Kanye Clark
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clark is a redshirt junior defensive back who transferred to Florida from UCLA and is listed at STAR, the Gators' nickel spot, in his first season in Gainesville. He appeared in nine games for the Bruins in 2025 with two starts at nickel, recording 22 tackles, one tackle for loss, two pass breakups and a forced fumble on special teams that UCLA returned for a touchdown. A Sacramento, Calif., native, he was a three-time first-team all-league pick at Capital Christian High School and also lettered in basketball and track.

athletes.name: CJ Hester
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: CJ Hester is a freshman defensive back from Titusville, Florida who played at Cocoa High School and is listed as a cornerback at Florida. As a junior he recorded 72 tackles, 10 pass breakups and three interceptions for a Cocoa team that finished 11-3 and won a Class 2A state championship.

athletes.name: Evan Pryor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pryor is a redshirt senior running back from Cornelius, N.C., who arrived at Florida through the portal after playing at Ohio State and Cincinnati. He attended Hough High School and was rated the No. 6 running back in the transfer portal. Listed at 189 pounds, he adds experienced depth behind Jadan Baugh alongside fellow addition London Montgomery.

athletes.name: Kofi Asare
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Asare is a redshirt senior edge rusher from Worcester, Mass., who came to Florida from UMass and played his high school football at Doherty Memorial. He is in his second year with the Gators, listed at 247 pounds and wearing No. 22. He plays the JACK spot in a group that includes Jayden Woods, Kamran James and Jacksonville State transfer Emmanuel Oyebadejo.

athletes.name: Kahleil Jackson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kahleil Jackson is a graduate student wide receiver from Hawthorne, Florida who played quarterback at Hawthorne High School and joined the Gators as a walk-on before earning a scholarship and moving to receiver. He comes from a Florida football family as the son of former Gators receiver Willie Jackson Jr. and grandson of Willie Jackson Sr.

athletes.name: Kamran James
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$941K for 2026; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: James is Florida's returning starting field-side edge rusher and recorded 44 tackles and 3.5 sacks in 2025 while playing through a torn labrum. He returned for his senior season and is a vocal leader of the defensive line.

athletes.name: London Montgomery
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Montgomery is a redshirt junior running back from Scranton, Pa., who joined Florida through the transfer portal after playing at Penn State and East Carolina. He attended Scranton Prep and rushed for roughly 700 yards in 2025. Listed at 192 pounds and wearing No. 24, he gives the Gators a proven complement behind Jadan Baugh alongside fellow transfer Evan Pryor.

athletes.name: Cormani McClain
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$650K for 2026; older On3 NIL valuation ~$300K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: McClain is Florida's projected starting boundary cornerback and a former No. 1-ranked cornerback recruit who transferred in from Colorado. He re-signed with Florida Victorious for his redshirt junior season.

athletes.name: Anthony Rubio
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Dijon Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$377K for 2026; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a returning starting cornerback for Florida who lost most of 2025 to a season-ending knee injury. He re-signed with the Gators for his redshirt junior season and is back to full health entering fall camp.

athletes.name: Byron Louis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He flipped his commitment from Florida State during the 2025 cycle, then made his college debut at Kentucky and took a redshirt season.

athletes.name: Elijah Owens
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He is listed on the Gators roster at the STAR position at 209 pounds wearing No. 28. As a junior college addition in his first year in Gainesville, he adds competition to a defensive backfield with several new pieces.

athletes.name: Jaden Robinson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Robinson is a senior inside linebacker from Lake City, Fla., who signed with Florida out of Columbia High School and is now in his fourth year in the program. Listed at 227 pounds and wearing No. 29, he is described in offseason roster reviews as one of the leaders of the linebacker group alongside junior Myles Graham.

athletes.name: Dylan Purter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Purter is a freshman defensive back from Tuskegee, Alabama, who signed with Florida out of Booker T. Washington High School and wears No. 30. A four-star safety rated the top player at his position in Alabama, he committed to LSU in March before flipping to the Gators during the early signing period. He recorded 148 tackles, three sacks and two interceptions across his sophomore and junior seasons.

athletes.name: Evan Jackson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Brian Case

athletes.name: DJ Coleman
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$622K for 2026; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Coleman is Florida's projected starting free safety after transferring from Baylor, where he started 12 of 13 games in 2025 with 46 tackles, 6.5 tackles for loss, six pass breakups and two interceptions. He was Jon Sumrall's first Florida transfer-portal commitment.

athletes.name: Kaiden Hall

He was named an Under Armour All-American and posted 129 tackles with four interceptions as a senior while also starting at quarterback, where he ran for 798 yards and 15 touchdowns.

athletes.name: Kelvin Jimenez
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kelvin Jimenez is a redshirt sophomore running back from Cape Coral, Florida who played at Mariner High School. He is a walk-on listed at 6-1, 216 pounds and wears No. 34 for the Gators.

athletes.name: Brayden Slade
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brayden Slade is a redshirt junior safety from Coconut Creek, Florida who played at Monarch High School. A walk-on listed at 6-1, 193 pounds, he wears No. 35 on Florida's 2026 roster.

athletes.name: Vincent Brown Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Vincent Brown Jr. is a redshirt junior cornerback from Gainesville who prepped at Wildwood High School and joined Florida as a preferred walk-on after two seasons at NAIA Southeastern University, where he earned second team All-Sun Conference honors in 2024 with 30 tackles and an interception. He is the son of former Gator Vincent Brown and grandson of Vernell Brown Sr.

athletes.name: Javion Toombs
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Javion Toombs is a redshirt senior cornerback from Fort Pierce, Florida who played at Centennial High School. He is a walk-on listed at 5-11, 188 pounds and wears No. 37 for the Gators.

athletes.name: Alec Clark
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clark, a redshirt junior punter from Perth, Australia, joins Florida for 2026 after punting at Marshall and Tulane. He averaged 46.5 yards on 48 punts for Tulane in 2025, the second-best single-season mark in program history, and earned first team All-American Athletic Conference honors along with CSC First Team Academic All-America recognition. He had previously served as Marshall's starting punter for all 13 games in 2024, averaging 42.4 yards and pinning 17 punts inside the 20-yard line.

athletes.name: Carter Milliron
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Milliron is a redshirt senior long snapper from Hoover, Ala., who spent four seasons at Louisiana before transferring to Florida for 2026. He snapped on punts in every game for the Ragin' Cajuns in 2022, 2023 and 2024, then handled the first four games of 2025 before redshirting. Out of Hoover High School he was rated the No. 18 long snapper in the country following the Kohl's National Scholarship Camp, where he averaged a 0.67-second snap time, and he chose Louisiana over offers from Troy and West Virginia.

athletes.name: Brandon Rabasco
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Liam Padron
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Padron is a redshirt sophomore kicker from St. Augustine, Fla., who joined Florida through the transfer portal from Texas A&M. He kicked at Bartram Trail High School and is listed at 191 pounds. He arrives alongside Tulane transfer Patrick Durkin, the American Conference Special Teams Player of the Year, which points toward a backup role in 2026.

athletes.name: Matthew Kade
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Matthew Kade is a redshirt sophomore linebacker from Gainesville who played at Buchholz High School, a few miles from campus. He is a walk-on listed at 6-0, 223 pounds and wears No. 42 for Florida.

athletes.name: Alfonzo Allen Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alfonzo Allen Jr. is a redshirt senior safety from Miami who won a Class 5A state title at Miami Central before signing with Baylor, where he appeared in all 13 games in 2022 and recorded a sack and 2.0 tackles for loss. He later transferred to Florida and picked up his first career interception in the Gasparilla Bowl.

athletes.name: Jaden Edgecombe
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jaden Edgecombe is a redshirt junior wide receiver from Cocoa, Florida who played at Cocoa High School. He is a walk-on listed at 5-8, 190 pounds and wears No. 43 for the Gators in 2026.

athletes.name: Myles Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Myles Johnson is a sophomore linebacker from Brewton, Alabama who played at T.R. Miller High School. He is listed at 6-1, 232 pounds and wears No. 44 in Florida's inside linebacker group.

athletes.name: Miller Fealy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fealy is a redshirt sophomore punter from Melbourne, Australia, who came to Florida from Southwestern Oklahoma after attending Marcellin College. Listed at 208 pounds and wearing No. 47, he was added as a veteran special teams option. He shares the punting job description with Tulane transfer Alec Clark, a first team All American Conference selection, so competition should be close.

athletes.name: Nicholas Inglis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Erich Seager
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Jalen Wiggins

athletes.name: Malik Morris
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Malik Morris is a freshman linebacker from Lakeland, Florida who signed with the Gators out of Lakeland High School as one of the higher rated defenders in the 2026 class. He put up 95 tackles, nine sacks and three forced fumbles as a junior and was named the Ledger All-County defensive player of the year.

athletes.name: Jason Zandamela
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zandamela is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Clearwater, Fla., who signed with Florida out of Clearwater Academy as one of the most highly rated interior line recruits in his class. He is listed at 286 pounds and wears No. 50. Now in his third year in the program, he is in the center competition with Georgia Tech transfer Harrison Moore.

athletes.name: Tyler Chukuyem
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tyler Chukuyem is a freshman offensive lineman from Douglasville, Georgia who played at South Paulding High School and committed to Florida after a single official visit. He signed in December 2025 as part of the Gators' 2026 class and climbed the recruiting rankings during his senior year, finishing as one of the group's highest rated linemen.

athletes.name: Dylan Leighton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dylan Leighton is a redshirt freshman linebacker from New Port Richey, Florida who played at J.W. Mitchell High School. He is a walk-on listed at 6-1, 229 pounds and wears No. 52 for Florida.

athletes.name: Harrison Moore
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moore is a junior offensive lineman from Southlake, Texas, in his first season at Florida after two years at Georgia Tech. He started eight of 11 games at center in 2025 and played 682 snaps for a Yellow Jackets line that allowed nine sacks, third fewest in the FBS, and was named one of 10 Joe Moore Award semifinalists. As a true freshman he logged 184 snaps at guard, center and tight end. Florida announced in August 2026 that he was placed on the Rimington Trophy preseason watch list. He was a three-star recruit at Southlake Carroll.

athletes.name: Bryce Lovett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lovett is a redshirt junior offensive lineman from Rockledge, Fla., who signed with Florida out of Rockledge High School and is in his fourth year in the program. Listed at 305 pounds and wearing No. 53, he has worked at right tackle, where Caden Jones started in his place during 2025. He returns to a tackle group also featuring Fletcher Westphal.

athletes.name: Javarii Luckas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Javarii Luckas is a freshman offensive lineman from Belle Glade, Florida who played at Glades Central and Rise Preparatory Academy. He committed to Florida in June 2025 over West Virginia and South Florida, and he has family ties to the program through his cousin Kelvin Taylor, a former Gators running back.

athletes.name: TJ Dice Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Jahari Medlock
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Hunter Solwold
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He redshirted at Washington in 2025 before transferring to Florida. His father, Mike Solwold, snapped in the NFL for five seasons.

athletes.name: Corey Brown
