athletes.name: G'Nivre Carr
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: G'Nivre Carr is a freshman offensive lineman from Ocala, Florida who played at IMG Academy in Bradenton. He drew scholarship offers from dozens of programs and committed to Florida in June 2025, choosing the Gators over Tennessee after repeated trips to Gainesville, and he signed with the 2026 class as an interior lineman.

athletes.name: Caden Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$800K for 2026; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a returning Florida offensive tackle projected to start at right tackle in 2026 after re-signing with the Gators for his redshirt junior season.

athletes.name: Eagan Boyer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Boyer is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Cornelius, N.C., who transferred to Florida from Penn State. He played at Hough High School, the same program as Gators running back Evan Pryor. Listed at 306 pounds and wearing No. 64, he was added as tackle depth in a line that also brought in TJ Shanahan Jr. and Harrison Moore.

athletes.name: Emeka Ugorji
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$800K for 2026; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Ugorji is Florida's projected starting left tackle after transferring from Stanford, where he made eight starts as a true freshman in 2025 between left guard and right tackle.

athletes.name: TJ Shanahan Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$645K for 2026; not exactly disclosed)

athletes.name: Fletcher Westphal
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fletcher Westphal is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Leesburg, Virginia who played at Tuscarora High School. He is listed at 6-8, 309 pounds, making him one of the tallest players on Florida's roster.

athletes.name: Roderick Kearney
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kearney is a redshirt junior offensive lineman from Jacksonville, Fla., who signed with Florida out of Orange Park High School and is entering his fourth year in the program. Listed at 303 pounds and wearing No. 71, he is valued for versatility, having taken snaps at guard and center, which keeps him in the interior rotation alongside veteran Knijeah Harris.

athletes.name: Daniel Pierre Louis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Daniel Pierre Louis is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Royal Palm Beach, Florida who played at Seminole Ridge High School. He is listed at 6-4, 327 pounds and wears No. 73 for Florida.

athletes.name: Mark Faircloth
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mark Faircloth is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Quincy, Florida who played at Florida State University School in Tallahassee. He is a walk-on listed at 6-5, 312 pounds and wears No. 76.

athletes.name: Knijeah Harris
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$543K for 2026; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Harris is Florida's returning starting left guard, having started all 12 games in 2025 and all 13 in 2024. He re-signed with the Gators for his senior season.

athletes.name: Desmond Green
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Desmond Green is a freshman offensive lineman from Alvin, South Carolina who played at Timberland High School and chose Florida over South Carolina and Georgia among roughly 20 scholarship offers. He was rated among the top 10 prospects in his state for the 2026 class and also competed in basketball and track and field.

athletes.name: Chancellor Campbell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chancellor Campbell is a freshman offensive tackle from St. Petersburg, Florida who played at Lakewood High School and is listed at 6-8, 318 pounds. He committed to Florida in June 2025 following an official visit, choosing the Gators over Georgia, Penn State and Ohio State, and signed with the 2026 class.

athletes.name: Ace Ciongoli
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ace Ciongoli is a redshirt freshman wide receiver from Needham, Massachusetts who played at St. Sebastian's School, where he earned Independent School League honorable mention recognition. He spent the 2025 season at Indiana as a walk-on without appearing in a game, then transferred to Florida with four years of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Justin Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Justin Williams is a freshman wide receiver from Gainesville who played at Buchholz High School near campus. He is listed at 5-11, 199 pounds and wears No. 83 on Florida's 2026 roster.

athletes.name: Micah Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Evan Chieca
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He caught 31 passes for 255 yards and four touchdowns in 2025 after 12 receptions the prior year, then transferred to Florida with two years of eligibility left.

athletes.name: Heze Kent
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Heze Kent is a freshman tight end from Brunswick, Georgia who signed with Florida in the 2026 class. He finished his high school career with 95 receptions for 2,051 yards and 21 touchdowns while adding 694 rushing yards and 19 scores, and he also played for the Brunswick varsity basketball team.

athletes.name: Marquez Daniel
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Marquez Daniel is a freshman wide receiver from Tuskegee, Alabama who played at Booker T. Washington High School. He scored 18 touchdowns over his final two prep seasons and averaged more than 19 yards per catch as a junior. He committed to Florida in June 2025, choosing the Gators over Auburn.

athletes.name: Tripp Brown Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tripp Brown Jr. is a freshman tight end from Tampa, Florida who played at Plant High School. He is a walk-on listed at 6-5, 240 pounds and wears No. 89 on Florida's 2026 roster.

athletes.name: Brendan Bett
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard open-market estimate ~$720K for 2026; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Bett is Florida's most experienced interior defensive lineman and posted 39 tackles with three sacks in 2025. He is projected to start at defensive tackle in 2026.

athletes.name: Patrick Durkin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Durkin is a redshirt sophomore kicker from Chicago, Ill., who transferred to Florida from Tulane. He made 25 of 28 field goals in 2025, an 89.3 percent rate that included two makes from 52 yards and a 4-for-6 mark from beyond 50, and he added 41 of 42 extra points with 69 touchbacks on 80 kickoffs. That season earned him American Athletic Conference Special Teams Player of the Year honors. Florida announced in August 2026 that he was named to the Lou Groza Award preseason watch list.

athletes.name: Jeramiah McCloud
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McCloud is a sophomore defensive lineman at Florida who wears No. 91 and is listed at 294 pounds. He debuted in the 2025 opener against LIU and appeared in 11 games as a freshman, finishing with 13 tackles, half a tackle for loss and two pass breakups, with a season high of four tackles against Tennessee. The Sylvester, Georgia native signed out of Lee County High School as a four-star recruit and made the SEC Fall Academic Honor Roll.

athletes.name: Sebastian Scott
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sebastian Scott is a redshirt junior defensive lineman from West Palm Beach, Florida who played at Cardinal Newman High School. He is a walk-on listed at 6-2, 360 pounds and wears No. 92.

athletes.name: DK Kalu
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kalu is a redshirt junior defensive lineman from Missouri City, Texas, who joined Florida through the transfer portal from Baylor. He played at Ridge Point High School and is listed at 309 pounds wearing No. 93. He arrived in the same portal cycle as Mason Clinton to add interior size behind returning linemen Jamari Lyons and Brendan Bett.

athletes.name: Kendall Guervil
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kendall Guervil is a freshman defensive lineman from Fort Myers, Florida who played at Fort Myers High School and is listed at 6-5, 309 pounds. He committed to Florida in July 2025 over Texas and Florida State, and he signed with the 2026 class as one of the higher rated defensive line prospects nationally.

athletes.name: Jamari Lyons
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lyons is a redshirt junior defensive lineman from Cocoa, Fla., who signed with Florida out of Viera High School and is now in his fifth year with the program. Listed at 312 pounds and wearing No. 95, he is projected as the starting nose tackle in 2026, anchoring an interior that added portal linemen DK Kalu and Mason Clinton.

athletes.name: JaReylan McCoy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: JaReylan McCoy is a freshman defensive lineman from Tupelo, Mississippi who played at Tupelo High School and helped the Golden Wave finish 14-0 with a Class 6A state championship in 2024, posting 30 tackles and 7.5 tackles for loss. He committed to LSU before reopening his recruitment and signing with Florida.

athletes.name: Joseph Mbatchou
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mbatchou is a sophomore defensive lineman from Loganville, Ga., entering his second season at Florida after playing in nine games as a freshman in 2025. He finished that year with 11 tackles, including one for loss, and posted a season high of six stops against Tennessee. A consensus four-star recruit out of Grayson High School, he was ranked the No. 12 defensive tackle nationally by Rivals and No. 225 overall by On3, and he chose the Gators over Alabama, Georgia and LSU among others. He made the SEC First-Year Academic Honor Roll.

athletes.name: Mason Clinton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clinton is a redshirt junior defensive lineman from Hattiesburg, Miss., who reached Florida through the transfer portal after stops at Louisiana, East Mississippi Community College and Southern Miss. He attended Petal High School and is listed at 293 pounds wearing No. 98. He joins DK Kalu as a first year addition to a defensive line rotation anchored by Jamari Lyons.

athletes.name: Emmanuel Oyebadejo
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Oyebadejo is a redshirt senior defensive lineman from Manchester, England, who came to Florida from Jacksonville State after beginning his career at the University of Exeter. He attended Loreto College in Manchester and is listed at 299 pounds wearing No. 99. Standing about 6 foot 7, he provides length and rotation depth on the edge of the Gators front.

athletes.name: Jordon Davison
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market estimate ~$559K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Davison is one of Oregon's projected starting running backs after contributing as a true freshman on the Ducks' 2025 College Football Playoff team. He signed with Oregon as a five-star recruit out of Mater Dei High School.

athletes.name: D'Antre Robinson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Robinson arrives in Eugene as a junior defensive lineman from Orlando, Florida, after stops at Florida and North Carolina. He played 11 games for the Tar Heels in 2025, recording 38 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, half a sack and a forced fumble, and posted 17 tackles with 1.5 sacks as a Florida freshman in 2024. A four-star Jones High School prospect, he played in the 2023 U.S. Army All-American Bowl and adds experienced rotation depth.

athletes.name: Bear Alexander
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market estimate ~$1.5M; On3 NIL valuation ~$1.2M; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Alexander is Oregon's returning starting nose tackle and set career highs with 50 tackles and 6.5 tackles for loss in 2025. The Georgia and USC transfer returned for a final college season instead of entering the NFL Draft.

athletes.name: Dakorien Moore
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market estimate ~$946K; On3 NIL valuation ~$712K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Moore is a projected starting wide receiver for Oregon and earned All-Big Ten honorable mention as a true freshman in 2025 with 34 catches for 497 yards and three touchdowns. He was the highest-rated recruit ever to sign with the Ducks.

athletes.name: Iverson Hooks
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market estimate ~$1.06M; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Hooks is Oregon's projected starting slot receiver after transferring from UAB, where he caught 72 passes for 927 yards and seven touchdowns in 2025. He was a second-team All-American Conference selection with 1,038 all-purpose yards.

athletes.name: Na'eem Offord
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Offord is a sophomore cornerback competing for a starting job in Oregon's secondary after playing as a true freshman in 2025. He was a five-star recruit who flipped from Ohio State to Oregon on signing day.

athletes.name: Jeremiah McClellan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McClellan is a projected starting wide receiver for Oregon after earning expanded playing time as a redshirt freshman in 2025. He flipped his commitment from Ohio State to Oregon in the 2024 class.

athletes.name: Koi Perich
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market estimate ~$1.1M; Minnesota coach P.J. Fleck publicly said Oregon's package was worth about $2M; On3 valuation ~$660K; terms not officially disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Perich is Oregon's projected starting strong safety after transferring from Minnesota, where he totaled 128 tackles, two forced fumbles and multiple all-conference honors in two seasons. He was rated the top safety available in the 2026 transfer portal.

athletes.name: Tradarian Ball
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard projected valuation ~$68K as a 2026 Oregon signee; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Ball is a freshman running back from Texarkana, Texas, and a consensus four-star signee whom 247Sports rated the nation's No. 4 running back. At Texas High School he rushed for 872 yards and nine touchdowns as a senior while adding 63 catches for 789 yards and nine scores, and he played in the 2025 Polynesian Bowl. His receiving ability gives him a path into Oregon's 2026 backfield rotation.

athletes.name: Brandon Finney Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market estimate ~$1.3M; On3 NIL valuation ~$654K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Finney is Oregon's returning starting cornerback and a Walter Camp preseason first-team All-American after starting all 15 games as a true freshman in 2025 with three interceptions, eight pass breakups and 42 tackles.

athletes.name: Davon Benjamin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL Valuation ~$191K, carried from his senior year at Oaks Christian; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Benjamin is a freshman safety from Westlake Village, California, and a consensus four-star recruit rated among the top 10 players in his state. He played both ways at Oaks Christian, recording 27 tackles, four interceptions and two pick sixes as a senior while catching 29 passes for 286 yards. He was invited to the 2026 Polynesian Bowl and joins a deep Oregon secondary competing for rotation snaps.

athletes.name: Dierre Hill Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hill is competing to be Oregon's lead running back in 2026 after a standout true freshman season in which he ran for 656 yards and five touchdowns on just 75 carries, averaging 8.7 yards per attempt. Pro Football Focus rated the Centralia, Ill. native as Oregon's best offensive player in 2025. The sophomore is battling classmate Jordon Davison for the No. 1 job while working to become an every-down back in pass protection.

athletes.name: Jerry Mixon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mixon returns as a starting linebacker for Oregon in 2026 after announcing he would come back for his senior season. The San Francisco native broke out in 2025 with 57 tackles, two interceptions and a fumble recovery, including a 26-yard interception return for a touchdown against Oklahoma State. With running mate Bryce Boettcher graduated, Mixon is expected to lead the middle of the Ducks' defense.

athletes.name: Ify Obidegwu
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Obidegwu is a projected starting cornerback for Oregon in 2026 after emerging in the rotation with 24 tackles in 2025. The redshirt sophomore from Baltimore redshirted in 2024 before winning an outside corner role opposite Brandon Finney Jr. At 6-foot-1 with notable length, he fits the outside corner mold in the Ducks' scheme and is viewed as one of the team's breakout candidates entering his third season in Eugene.

athletes.name: Evan Stewart
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market estimate ~$1.54M; On3 NIL valuation ~$1.5M; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Stewart is Oregon's veteran No. 1 wide receiver and returns healthy for 2026 after missing all of 2025 with a torn patellar tendon. The Texas A&M transfer caught 48 passes for 613 yards and five touchdowns in 2024.

athletes.name: Trey McNutt
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McNutt is a redshirt freshman safety from Cleveland, Ohio, and the highest rated safety ever to sign with Oregon according to 247Sports. Rivals ranked him the nation's No. 1 safety in the 2025 class, and he was a Navy All-American Bowl selection out of Shaker Heights High School. He did not play as a true freshman and took a redshirt, leaving him in the mix for secondary snaps in 2026. His father Richard lettered at Ohio State.

athletes.name: Devon Jackson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson enters his final season at Oregon in 2026 positioned for the biggest role of his career, with the coaching staff looking to make him an every-down linebacker after he spent previous seasons primarily as a passing-down contributor. A redshirt senior from Omaha, Neb., he is expected to help fill the vacancy beside returning starter Jerry Mixon created by Bryce Boettcher's graduation.

athletes.name: Jamari Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market estimate ~$800K; On3 NIL valuation ~$684K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is Oregon's returning starting tight end and a Walter Camp preseason second-team All-American after catching 32 passes for 510 yards and three touchdowns in 2025. He transferred to Oregon from Louisville.

athletes.name: Matayo Uiagalelei
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market estimate ~$2.0M; On3 NIL valuation ~$1.2M; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Uiagalelei is Oregon's returning starting edge rusher and recorded 34 tackles, 9.5 tackles for loss and six sacks across 15 games in 2025. He bypassed the 2026 NFL Draft to return for his senior season.

athletes.name: Akili Smith Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a redshirt freshman quarterback from San Diego, California, whose father, Akili Smith Sr., played quarterback at Oregon in 1997 and 1998 before going in the first round to Cincinnati. A consensus four-star out of Lincoln High School, he was an Elite 11 finalist and threw for more than 6,900 yards as a high school starter. He redshirted in 2025 and sits in the developmental group behind Oregon's veteran quarterbacks.

athletes.name: Dylan Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a redshirt sophomore inside linebacker from Carson, California, who played seven games in 2025 and totaled seven tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss and half a sack, with his first career pass breakup coming in the College Football Playoff. A consensus four-star from Long Beach Poly rated No. 58 nationally by Rivals, he was his league's defensive player of the year and projects as linebacker depth in 2026.

athletes.name: Brock Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a redshirt junior quarterback from Eugene, Oregon, and a Sheldon High School product whose father Aaron played for the Ducks from 1985 to 1989. He appeared in seven games in 2025, completing 12 of 16 passes for 130 yards and throwing his first career touchdown, a one-yard strike to offensive lineman Gernorris Wilson against Wisconsin. He enters 2026 as an experienced backup option.

athletes.name: Peyton Woodyard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Woodyard is a junior safety in Oregon's secondary rotation after transferring in from Alabama. He was a four-star St. John Bosco prospect who signed with the Crimson Tide in the 2024 class.

athletes.name: Gatlin Bair
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL Valuation ~$251K; On3's projected annual value index, not a disclosed deal)
athletes.blurb: Bair is a freshman wide receiver from Burley, Idaho, joining Oregon in the fall of 2026 after serving a mission. A consensus four-star in the 2024 class, he was rated the No. 36 overall recruit by 247Sports and caught 52 passes for 832 yards and 10 touchdowns as a senior. He was also Idaho's Gatorade boys track athlete of the year, setting state records of 10.15 in the 100 meters and 20.56 in the 200.

athletes.name: Gavin Nix
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nix is a redshirt freshman inside linebacker from Bradenton, Florida, who came to Oregon from IMG Academy. He appeared in seven games as a true freshman in 2025 while redshirting and made three tackles, two of them in the College Football Playoff first round against James Madison. He totaled 99 tackles and nine tackles for loss in three varsity seasons at IMG.

athletes.name: Ryder Hayes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hayes is a redshirt sophomore quarterback from Grandview, Texas, who has not yet appeared in a game for Oregon. At Grandview High School he threw for 2,700 yards and 40 touchdowns as a senior, earning first-team all-district honors and leading the Zebras to an 11-2 record and a district championship.

athletes.name: Aaron Scott Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Scott is a junior cornerback from Springfield, Ohio, who transferred to Oregon after two seasons at Ohio State. He appeared in 12 games for the Buckeyes in 2025 and finished with nine tackles including one for loss, after playing seven games as a freshman. On3 rated him the No. 1 recruit in Ohio and the nation's No. 2 cornerback out of Springfield High School. He adds experienced depth on the boundary.

athletes.name: Messiah Hampton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hampton is a freshman wide receiver from Rochester, New York, and the consensus top prospect in his state. He left James Monroe High School as its all-time receiving leader with 2,300 career yards and caught 62 passes for 1,224 yards and 13 touchdowns as a senior while helping the school to a 12-0 record and its first state title. He competes for rotation snaps in a crowded receiver room.

athletes.name: Carl Williams IV
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is expected to compete for a starting safety role at Oregon in 2026 after transferring from Baylor in January. The Baton Rouge, La. native was one of Baylor's top defensive backs in 2023 and 2024 before a medical redshirt cost him nearly all of the 2025 season. He committed to the Ducks less than a week after entering the portal and arrives with two seasons of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Azel Banag
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Banag is a freshman cornerback from Columbia, South Carolina, and a consensus three-star prospect out of A.C. Flora High School. As a senior he recorded 75 tackles, five interceptions, 12 passes defended and three fumble recoveries, and he helped A.C. Flora reach the third round of the South Carolina Class 4A playoffs.

athletes.name: Markus Dixon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dixon is a redshirt junior tight end from Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, who spent three seasons at Clemson before transferring. He played 29 offensive snaps across 10 games for the Tigers in 2024 and appeared in three games in 2025 following a move to defensive end. A first team All-Catholic League selection at Archbishop Wood, he was ranked the No. 12 player in Pennsylvania by 247Sports and adds depth in the tight end room.

athletes.name: Tre Watson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Watson is a junior cornerback from Sacramento, California, who joined Oregon from College of San Mateo. He was a unanimous first-team all-conference pick and his conference's Defensive Player of the Year in 2025, when San Mateo went 11-1 and won the California state championship. He posted 30 tackles and two interceptions that season.

athletes.name: Dorian Brew
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brew is a redshirt freshman cornerback from Conroe, Texas, and a consensus four-star recruit who earned an invitation to the Navy All-American Bowl. He played in two games as a true freshman, against Minnesota and in the College Football Playoff opening round against James Madison. He led Conroe to a 9-3 record as a senior.

athletes.name: Kendre Harrison
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Harrison is a true freshman tight end at Oregon and was rated the No. 1 tight end and a consensus five-star in the 2026 recruiting class out of Reidsville, N.C. He also plans to play basketball for the Ducks.

athletes.name: Braylon Hodge
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hodge is a freshman inside linebacker from Englewood, Colorado, and a consensus four-star recruit out of Cherry Creek High School. He made 111 tackles with nine tackles for loss as a senior while Cherry Creek finished 14-0 and won the Colorado 5A championship. He was invited to the 2026 Navy All-American Bowl.

athletes.name: Xavier Lherisse
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lherisse is a freshman defensive back from Melbourne, Florida, who played quarterback and safety at Eau Gallie High School. As a senior he rushed for 1,318 yards and 14 touchdowns, threw for 1,123 yards and 13 scores, and added 36 tackles with four interceptions while also handling the punting duties.

athletes.name: Aaron Flowers
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Flowers is projected to start at safety for Oregon in 2026 after playing more than half his snaps as a deep safety in 2025. A former four-star recruit from Forney, Texas, he signed with the Ducks in Dan Lanning's 2024 class and is expected to take on a leadership role in a secondary that lost a first-round NFL Draft pick, pairing with Minnesota transfer Koi Perich on the back end.

athletes.name: Da'Jaun Riggs
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Riggs is a redshirt sophomore running back from Washington, D.C., who has carried 28 times for 172 yards and a touchdown across his first two seasons. He appeared in five games in 2025, averaging 5.1 yards on 17 attempts, after scoring his first career touchdown against Washington in 2024. A consensus three-star from St. John's, he was the top rated running back prospect out of the District.

athletes.name: Devin Jackson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson is a freshman defensive back from Winter Garden, Florida, and a consensus four-star prospect who transferred to The First Academy after two seasons at West Orange High School. He recorded 80 tackles and four interceptions as a junior, then added three interceptions and two return touchdowns as a senior.

athletes.name: Simeon Price
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Price is a redshirt senior running back from Pensacola, Florida, who joins Oregon after stops at Mississippi State, Coastal Carolina and Colorado. He rushed 21 times for 143 yards and two touchdowns in four games for the Buffaloes in 2025, including a 38-yard scoring run against Houston. He carried 44 times at Coastal Carolina in 2024 and spent three seasons in Starkville, bringing veteran depth to Oregon's backfield.

athletes.name: Brayden Platt
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Platt is a redshirt sophomore inside linebacker from Yelm, Washington, who played Oregon's final seven games in 2025 and logged 30 defensive snaps with two tackles. A consensus four-star rated the No. 53 overall recruit by 247Sports, he was a finalist for the High School Butkus Award and a two-way standout who led Yelm to a Washington 3A state title. He also won the state 3A shot put championship.

athletes.name: Jett Washington
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Washington is a freshman safety from Las Vegas, Nevada, and one of the top rated defensive backs in Oregon's class, graded a five star by ESPN, Rivals and 247Sports, which listed him as the nation's No. 1 safety. He posted 48 tackles and four interceptions as a Bishop Gorman senior while helping the program to a fifth straight Nevada state title, and he was invited to the 2026 Polynesian Bowl.

athletes.name: Rocco Graziano
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Graziano is a redshirt freshman kicker from Eugene, Oregon, who did not appear in a game as a true freshman in 2025. At Sheldon High School he made seven of eight field goal attempts with a long of 46 yards and converted all 70 of his extra point tries as a senior.

athletes.name: Tristan Phillips
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Phillips is a freshman inside linebacker from Ventura, California, who was named the CIF Southern Section Division 6 Defensive MVP and a USA Today first-team All-West Region selection. He totaled 127 tackles, 17 tackles for loss and 11 sacks as a senior while leading Ventura to a section championship.

athletes.name: Brandon Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a freshman running back from Fresno, California, rated a four-star and the No. 17 running back in his class by 247Sports. He rushed for 2,189 yards and 32 touchdowns as a senior at Central East High School, added 88 tackles as a two-way player and was named the Fresno Bee player of the year while leading his school to a CIF state championship. His uncle Clifton Smith was an NFL Pro Bowl selection.

athletes.name: Bleu Dantzler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dantzler is a redshirt freshman outside linebacker from Chandler, Arizona, who transferred to Oregon after appearing in one game and making one tackle at Oregon State in 2025. A three-star recruit rated the No. 10 prospect in Arizona by 247Sports, he recorded 11 sacks, 37 tackles and 24 quarterback hurries as a senior at Basha High School and earned first team all region honors twice.

athletes.name: Anthony Jones Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a freshman edge rusher from Mobile, Alabama, rated a five-star and a top-35 edge by 247Sports and Rivals and the No. 30 overall prospect by ESPN. He recorded 100 tackles, 15 tackles for loss and 11 sacks as a senior at St. Paul's Episcopal, where he set the school career sack record, and he was selected for the Alabama-Mississippi All-Star Game. He should factor into the edge rotation.

athletes.name: Arlo Henderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Henderson is a junior defensive back from Yelm, Washington, who reached Oregon after stops at Southern Oregon and Mississippi Valley State. He made 18 tackles with an interception in eight games at Southern Oregon in 2024, then played 11 games at Mississippi Valley State in 2025. He was an all-region pick at Yelm High School.

athletes.name: Xavier Barksdale
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Barksdale is a redshirt junior defensive back from San Diego, California, who made three appearances in 2025, including the College Football Playoff quarterfinal against Texas Tech. He was an honorable mention all-conference pick at Steele Canyon High School. His grandfather, Don Barksdale, won Olympic gold in 1948 and is in the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame.

athletes.name: Aaron Bidwell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bidwell is a redshirt freshman wide receiver from Eugene, Oregon, who did not appear in a game as a true freshman. At Marist High School he caught 73 passes for 1,264 yards and 18 touchdowns while helping the team win a state championship. His parents, Josh and Bethany, were both Oregon student-athletes.

athletes.name: Nasir Wyatt
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wyatt is in line for a much bigger role on the Oregon edge in 2026 after a productive freshman season in which he recorded 11 tackles, four tackles for loss and three sacks in limited snaps. A five-star recruit out of Mater Dei High School in Santa Ana, Calif., he was ranked among the nation's top linebacker prospects in the 2025 class. The sophomore bulked up to around 238 pounds in the offseason and switched his jersey from No. 32 to No. 31.

athletes.name: Tony Cumberland
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cumberland is a freshman defensive lineman listed from Columbus, Ohio, who played at Willamette High School in Oregon. He was a consensus four-star recruit and the top-rated prospect in the state, recording 102 tackles, 26 tackles for loss and 14 sacks as a senior. USA Today named him its All-West Region Defensive Captain of the Year.

athletes.name: Zach Grisham
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Grisham is a redshirt senior defensive back from Portland, Oregon, and a Central Catholic High School product. He played in 12 of 15 games in 2025 and set a career high with nine total tackles, including three against Oklahoma State. Earlier in his career he recovered a fumble against Liberty in the Fiesta Bowl.

athletes.name: Cruz Rushing
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rushing is a redshirt senior linebacker from Tucson, Arizona, who began his college career as a preferred walk-on at Florida in 2022 and spent 2023 at Arizona before joining Oregon. He saw action in four games in 2025 and made his first collegiate tackle against Oklahoma State.

athletes.name: Keaton Emmett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Emmett is a junior kicker from Lake Oswego, Oregon, who arrived by way of Western Oregon and Nevada. He made 12 of 18 field goals and 28 of 29 extra points across 11 games for Western Oregon in 2024, including a career-long 48-yard make, then appeared in one game at Nevada in 2025.

athletes.name: Brody Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a redshirt freshman outside linebacker from Eugene, Oregon, who is listed with Idaho as his previous school. He played both ways at Sheldon High School, recording 43 tackles with 11.5 tackles for loss and five sacks as a senior while also catching 24 passes for 471 yards and eight touchdowns.

athletes.name: Will Straton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Straton is a redshirt junior inside linebacker from Honolulu who played in Oregon's final 14 games of 2025 and made 11 tackles, largely on special teams. He was a team captain and first-team all-state pick at Punahou School. His brother Robert played football at Dartmouth and earned All-Ivy League honors.

athletes.name: Bailey Ettridge
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ettridge is projected to take over punting duties for Oregon in 2026 after transferring from Nevada, where he averaged 44.7 yards on 47 punts as a freshman, put 18 punts inside the 20 and earned All-Mountain West honorable mention. A native of Lara, Australia, and a former welder who came to football late, the 28-year-old sophomore is the oldest player on the Ducks' roster and was Oregon's first transfer portal commitment of the cycle.

athletes.name: Cormac O'Flaherty
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cormac O'Flaherty is listed as a redshirt freshman safety from Sacramento, California, with the Oregon Ducks football program. He does not appear on the school's current official online roster, and no verified high school or college production details could be confirmed for him.

athletes.name: Zander Quinn
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Quinn is a redshirt junior running back from Hilo, Hawaii, who graduated from Oxford Area High School in Pennsylvania in 2022 and has not appeared in a game for Oregon. He earned one varsity football letter and four in track and field, winning league and district championships in the long jump.

athletes.name: Dutch Horisk
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Horisk is a freshman outside linebacker from Bellflower, California, who was named the 2025 Trinity League MVP at St. John Bosco. He recorded 59 tackles with 10 tackles for loss and 5.5 sacks as a senior, and he added 53 tackles with nine tackles for loss and four sacks as a junior.

athletes.name: Aydin Breland
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Breland is a redshirt sophomore defensive lineman from Santa Ana, California, who played in 12 of Oregon's 15 games in 2025 and logged 61 defensive snaps, with a season high of 12 at Penn State. Rated a five-star and the No. 16 overall recruit by 247Sports out of Mater Dei, he played in the Under Armour All-America Game and helped his high school win a CIF state open division championship.

athletes.name: Teitum Tuioti
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market estimate ~$1.5M; On3 NIL valuation ~$1.0M; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Tuioti is Oregon's returning starting Jack edge rusher and a Walter Camp preseason first-team All-American after leading the Ducks with 9.5 sacks and 16 tackles for loss in 2025. He also posted a career-high 68 total tackles.

athletes.name: Torrence Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Torrence Williams is listed as a redshirt sophomore tight end from Cape Girardeau, Missouri, with the Oregon Ducks football program. He does not appear on the school's current official online roster, and no verified high school or college production details could be confirmed for him.

athletes.name: Jay Harden
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jay Harden is listed as a redshirt freshman linebacker from Stevenson Ranch, California, with the Oregon Ducks football program. He does not appear on the school's current official online roster, and no verified high school or college production details could be confirmed for him.

athletes.name: Elijah Rushing
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL Valuation ~$215K; The Sideline 2026 range $260K-$540K; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Rushing is a redshirt sophomore edge rusher from Tucson, Arizona, who appeared in seven games in 2025 and made the first three tackles of his career. He was the consensus top recruit in Arizona and a five-star rated No. 14 overall by 247Sports after posting 55 tackles, 17.5 tackles for loss and 13.5 sacks as a Salpointe Catholic senior. His father George played tight end at Florida.

athletes.name: Demetri Manning
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Manning is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Bellevue, Washington, who made his lone 2025 appearance in Oregon's season opener against Montana State. Rated a four-star by 247Sports, he was listed as the No. 24 interior offensive lineman nationally and the No. 2 recruit in Washington, and he played left and right tackle at Bellevue High School while helping the program reach the 3A state title game.

athletes.name: Prince Tavizon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tavizon is a freshman outside linebacker from San Diego, California, and a consensus four-star recruit out of Lincoln High School. He posted 110 tackles with 15 tackles for loss, five sacks and eight passes defended as a senior, and he helped Lincoln win the 2024 CIF Division 1 state championship.

athletes.name: A'Mauri Washington
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market estimate ~$994K; On3 NIL valuation ~$881K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Washington is Oregon's returning starting defensive tackle and a Walter Camp preseason second-team All-American after posting 33 tackles, 4.5 tackles for loss and eight batted passes across 15 starts in 2025.

athletes.name: Devin Brooks
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brooks is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Clackamas, Oregon, who has appeared in two games and played eight offensive snaps through two seasons. The 247Sports Composite rated him a four-star and the No. 2 recruit in Oregon, and he was an Oregon 6A all-state first team pick as a junior and a three-time All-Mt. Hood Conference selection at Clackamas High School.

athletes.name: Matthew Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a redshirt freshman defensive end from Concord, California, who appeared in seven games in 2025, including all three College Football Playoff contests, and finished with four tackles on 56 defensive snaps. A four-star by 247Sports and the top rated defensive lineman in California, he posted 45 tackles, 11 tackles for loss and 8.5 sacks as a senior at De La Salle.

athletes.name: Douglas Utu
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Utu is competing for an open starting guard spot at Oregon in 2026 after redshirting as a freshman, when he played limited snaps exclusively at right guard. The Las Vegas native was one of the headline linemen in the Ducks' 2025 class, rated a five-star prospect by ESPN and Rivals and ranked the nation's top offensive guard by Rivals. He took reps at guard in the spring game and is pushing veterans for a place in the rotation.

athletes.name: Trent Ferguson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ferguson is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Salem, Oregon, who played in all 15 games in 2025 and logged 61 offensive snaps, including 36 at left tackle. He was part of an Oregon line named a finalist for the Joe Moore Award, and he was rated the top offensive tackle prospect in the state out of West Salem.

athletes.name: Zac Stascausky
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stascausky is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Portland, Oregon, who made his debut against Oklahoma State in 2025, playing four snaps at right tackle. A four-star recruit out of Central Catholic, he was the 2024 Mt. Hood Conference Offensive Player of the Year and a first-team all-state selection as a junior.

athletes.name: Ziyare Addison
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Addison is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Tampa, Florida, who played four snaps at left tackle in each of Oregon's first two games in 2025. A consensus four-star, he was rated the No. 57 overall recruit by Rivals and the No. 1 offensive tackle in Florida by 247Sports, and he chose Oregon over Clemson, Florida State, Georgia and Ohio State among others. He can line up at tackle or guard.

athletes.name: Fox Crader
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market estimate ~$900K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Crader is Oregon's projected starting left tackle after making his first career start as a redshirt freshman in 2025. He was a four-star signee out of Evergreen High School in Washington.

athletes.name: Thomas Donkerbrook
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Donkerbrook is a freshman long snapper from Phoenix, Arizona, who handled the snapping duties at Brophy College Prep. He was rated a five-star long snapper by Kohl's and competed at both the Kohl's Western Showcase and the Kohl's National Scholarship Camp before joining the Ducks.

athletes.name: Bryce Boulton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Boulton is a redshirt junior offensive lineman from Palm Desert, California, who has not yet appeared in a game for Oregon. He was a three-star recruit rated among the top 100 players in California and a PrepStar All-Western Region selection after helping Palm Desert to back-to-back CIF Southern Section Division 4 playoff appearances.

athletes.name: Beau CressAllen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: CressAllen is a redshirt junior offensive lineman from Portland, Oregon, who has not yet appeared in a game for the Ducks. He was a second-team all-state and first-team All-Mt. Hood Conference pick at Central Catholic, where he helped win the 2021 Oregon 6A title. He also lettered in swimming, volleyball, lacrosse and track.

athletes.name: Auston Mims
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mims is a redshirt junior offensive lineman listed from Akron, Ohio, who played at Chaminade College Prep in California. He did not begin playing football until his junior year and started as a senior on a team that reached the CIF Southern Section Division 2 semifinals. His Oregon bio lists NBA player LeBron James as his uncle.

athletes.name: Koloi Keli
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Keli is a freshman offensive lineman from Honolulu and a consensus three-star recruit out of Farrington High School. He was named offensive line most valuable player at the Under Armour Maui Camp and earned an invitation to the 2026 Polynesian Bowl. He helped Farrington earn a No. 8 state ranking as a senior.

athletes.name: RJ Todd
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Todd is projected to be Oregon's long snapper in 2026 after transferring from Western Michigan, where he started for three seasons and appeared in 39 games handling snaps on punts, field goals and extra points. The Rockford, Mich. native was one of the Ducks' first three portal additions of the cycle, all specialists, and steps in for graduated three-year starter Luke Basso with one season of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Iapani Laloulu
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market estimate ~$914K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Laloulu is Oregon's returning starting center and was a 2025 Rimington Trophy finalist and FWAA first-team All-American. He announced a return to Eugene for his senior season rather than entering the NFL Draft.

athletes.name: Kawika Rogers
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rogers is competing for a starting interior offensive line spot at Oregon in 2026 as one of the more experienced returners up front. A redshirt senior from Kapa'a, Hawaii, he signed with the Ducks in the 2022 class after ranking among the top players in the state, and he appeared in all 14 games with 198 snaps during Oregon's 2024 College Football Playoff season.

athletes.name: Dave Iuli
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Iuli returns as Oregon's starting right guard in 2026, one of only two offensive line starters back from a 2025 unit that was a Joe Moore Award finalist. The Puyallup, Wash. native started throughout the 2025 season and, alongside center Iapani Laloulu, gives the Ducks a veteran anchor as they rebuild the rest of the front. He enters his redshirt senior season as a leader of the position group.

athletes.name: Michael Bennett III
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 open-market estimate ~$1.2M; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Bennett is Oregon's projected starting right tackle after transferring from Yale, where he started all 12 games in 2025 and earned first-team All-Ivy League honors. He allowed just two sacks on 839 snaps last season.

athletes.name: Tommy Tofi
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tofi is a freshman offensive lineman from San Francisco who was the West Catholic Athletic League Offensive Lineman of the Year at Archbishop Riordan. He helped Riordan finish 12-1 and win its first CIF Central Section Open Division championship in 2025, and he was invited to the 2026 Polynesian Bowl.

athletes.name: Gernorris Wilson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilson is a redshirt junior offensive lineman from Lakeland, Florida, who played Oregon's first nine games in 2025 and made his first career start at right tackle in the road win at Iowa. He logged 171 offensive snaps and caught a one-yard touchdown pass against Minnesota, becoming the first Oregon offensive lineman with multiple career touchdown receptions. A consensus three-star recruit, he provides swing tackle depth.

athletes.name: Dillon Gresham
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gresham is a redshirt sophomore wide receiver from Hemet, California, and a consensus four-star recruit out of San Jacinto High School. He totaled 1,658 all-purpose yards as a senior in 2023, catching 49 passes for 819 yards and 12 touchdowns while adding 325 rushing yards and four scores.

athletes.name: Dayton Raiola
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Raiola is a freshman tight end from Buford, Georgia, who played quarterback at Buford High School. He completed 146 of 236 passes for 2,208 yards with 26 touchdowns and four interceptions as a senior, and he chose Oregon over Nebraska, Appalachian State and Charlotte.

athletes.name: Nathan McCoy II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McCoy is a redshirt freshman wide receiver from Dallas, Texas, who did not appear in a game as a true freshman. At Duncanville High School he helped the program win back-to-back state championships and earned second-team all-league and all-state honors as a junior, when he caught 14 passes for 131 yards.

athletes.name: Hudson Lewis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lewis is a freshman wide receiver from Boise, Idaho, and a consensus three-star recruit out of Timberline High School. He caught 62 passes for 1,026 yards and 14 touchdowns as a senior, finishing fifth in Idaho in receiving yards while helping Timberline reach the state championship game.

athletes.name: Jovon McRae II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McRae is a redshirt freshman wide receiver listed from Camden, New Jersey, who graduated from Mojave High School in Nevada in 2024. He earned three varsity letters in basketball and track and field, and he did not appear in a game as a true freshman for Oregon.

athletes.name: Andrew Olesh
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Olesh is a redshirt freshman tight end from Center Valley, Pennsylvania, who transferred to Oregon after redshirting at Penn State in 2025. A consensus four-star, he was rated the No. 43 overall prospect and the top recruit in Pennsylvania by On3 after catching 75 passes for 1,105 yards and 10 touchdowns as a senior at Southern Lehigh. He joins a crowded tight end room competing for snaps.

athletes.name: A.J. Pugliano
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pugliano is a redshirt sophomore tight end from Medford, Oregon, who has not yet appeared in a game. At North Medford he caught 37 passes for 452 yards and seven touchdowns in six games as a senior and was a finalist for The Oregonian's football player of the year. His brother Ty plays at Johns Hopkins.

athletes.name: Jack Ressler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ressler is a redshirt sophomore wide receiver from Irvine, California, who has yet to appear in a game after redshirting in 2024 and missing the 2025 season. Rated a four-star and a top-300 prospect by ESPN out of Mater Dei, he was selected for the Under Armour All-American Game and caught 42 passes for 534 yards and four touchdowns as a junior in 2022.

athletes.name: Brady Bidwell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bidwell is a redshirt sophomore wide receiver from Eugene, Oregon, who saw action in eight games in 2025 and played 16 offensive snaps. He was a first-team all-state receiver at Marist after catching 80 passes for 1,037 yards and 12 touchdowns as a senior. His brother Aaron is also an Oregon receiver.

athletes.name: Derrick Brown Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is a redshirt senior defensive lineman from Fort Washington, Maryland, who transferred to Oregon after four seasons at Howard. He played 12 games for the Bison in 2025 and recorded 23 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, two sacks and a blocked kick, following a 33-tackle season in 2024. A two-time MEAC champion and a MEAC All-Academic selection, he brings veteran interior depth.

athletes.name: Gage Hurych
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hurych is the frontrunner to take over Oregon's place-kicking job in 2026 after spending two seasons behind Atticus Sappington. The redshirt sophomore from West Linn, Ore. has handled kickoffs for the Ducks, and his 64.3 yards per kickoff was the highest mark among returning Big Ten kickers. A top-rated kicking prospect out of West Linn High School, he stayed home to sign with Oregon and announced his return to the program for 2026.

athletes.name: Jerome Simmons
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Simmons is a redshirt senior defensive lineman from Bamberg, South Carolina, whose path to Eugene ran through Highland Community College, South Carolina and Louisiana Monroe. He played eight games for the Warhawks in 2025 and finished with 10 tackles and a pass breakup, after recording 8.0 tackles for loss and 4.5 sacks in five junior college games in 2022. He was a first team all-state pick in high school.

athletes.name: AK Dear
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dear, a sophomore running back from Quitman, Mississippi, appeared in five games as a freshman in 2025 and gained 140 rushing yards with three touchdowns on 19 carries, adding three catches for 18 yards. He broke a 56-yard touchdown run against ULM. A consensus four-star recruit ranked No. 36 on the ESPN300, he ran for 2,016 yards as a high school junior and played in the Under Armour All-America Game. He projects as a rotational back in 2026.

athletes.name: Yhonzae Pierre
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Alabama roster valuation model ~$1.0M; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Pierre is Alabama's returning starting edge rusher at the Wolf position and led the team in 2025 with 14.5 tackles for loss, eight sacks and nine quarterback hurries. The Eufaula, Ala., native also forced three fumbles across 15 games.

athletes.name: Devan Thompkins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thompkins is Alabama's projected starting three-technique defensive lineman and transferred in from USC, where he started all 12 regular-season games in 2025 with 31 tackles, 6.5 tackles for loss and three sacks. He was rated the No. 3 defensive lineman in the 2026 transfer portal class.

athletes.name: Zabien Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Alabama roster valuation model ~$765K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Brown is Alabama's returning No. 1 cornerback and posted 39 tackles, six pass breakups and two pick-sixes in 2025. The Mater Dei (Calif.) product was named SEC Co-Defensive Player of the Week after a two-interception game against Tennessee.

athletes.name: Lotzeir Brooks
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Alabama roster valuation model ~$832K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Brooks is Alabama's projected starting slot receiver after catching 32 passes for 441 yards and two touchdowns as a true freshman in 2025. The Millville (N.J.) product set New Jersey state career records with 4,233 receiving yards and 63 touchdown catches.

athletes.name: Keon Sabb
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Alabama roster valuation model ~$843K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Sabb is a fifth-year starting safety and a Michigan transfer who won a national title with the Wolverines in 2023. He recorded 39 tackles, two interceptions and four pass breakups in seven starts before a season-ending injury in 2025.

athletes.name: Daniel Hill
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Alabama roster valuation model ~$507K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Hill is Alabama's projected starting running back after rushing 75 times for 284 yards and six touchdowns and adding 28 catches in 2025. The Meridian, Miss., product is the son of former Mississippi State defensive lineman Demetrius Hill.

athletes.name: Luke Metz
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Metz, a sophomore linebacker from Hoschton, Georgia, played in all 15 games in 2025, working mainly on special teams while taking defensive snaps. He finished with seven tackles, including four against Eastern Illinois, and was named a special teams player of the week by the Alabama staff for the LSU game. A four-star prospect out of Mill Creek High School, he was No. 82 on the Rivals100. He returns as a reserve inside linebacker.

athletes.name: Dijon Lee Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Alabama roster valuation model ~$683K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Lee is Alabama's projected starting cornerback opposite Zabien Brown and was a True Freshman All-American in 2025, playing every game with five starts. The 6-foot-4 Mission Viejo product was a five-star recruit and the No. 3 cornerback in the 2025 class.

athletes.name: Noah Rogers
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Alabama roster valuation model ~$756K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Rogers is a senior wide receiver who transferred in from NC State, where he caught 33 passes for 441 yards and two touchdowns in 2025. He was in line to start for Alabama before suffering an injury in the spring game that is expected to sideline him early in 2026.

athletes.name: Red Morgan
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Alabama roster valuation model ~$626K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Morgan is Alabama's projected full-time starter at the Husky nickel spot in Kane Wommack's defense after five starts in 2025. The Phenix City, Ala., native finished last season with 26 tackles, three tackles for loss and a forced fumble.

athletes.name: Kevin Riley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Riley, a junior running back from Northport, Alabama, took on an expanded role in 2025, playing 11 games with two starts before an injury sidelined him until the Rose Bowl. He rushed 59 times for 224 yards and two scores and caught 19 passes for 176 yards and a touchdown. A unanimous four-star at Tuscaloosa County High School, he ranked No. 69 on the ESPN300 and should stay in the backfield rotation.

athletes.name: Rico Scott
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Scott is a junior wide receiver from Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, who came to Alabama as a four-star prospect out of Bishop McDevitt High School in the 2024 recruiting class. He redshirted as a freshman after appearing in four games, then played in 15 games in 2025 and finished with 11 catches for 98 yards and two touchdowns. Scott briefly drew transfer portal interest in January 2026 before deciding to return to Tuscaloosa, and he enters the 2026 season competing for a larger share of snaps in the Crimson Tide receiver rotation.

athletes.name: Caleb Woodson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Woodson is Alabama's projected starting inside linebacker and a Virginia Tech transfer with 152 career tackles and 11.5 tackles for loss across 35 games. He finished second on the Hokies with 58 tackles in nine games in 2025 and has one season of eligibility left.

athletes.name: Justin Hill
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hill, a sophomore edge rusher from Cincinnati, played in all 15 games in 2025 and grew his role as the season progressed, finishing with 10 tackles, 2.5 for loss and one pass breakup. His best outing came against Georgia in Atlanta with four stops. A unanimous four-star ranked No. 60 on the ESPN300, he was the Ohio Division II District Defensive Player of the Year in 2023 at Winton Woods.

athletes.name: Cederian Morgan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Morgan is a true freshman wide receiver and was the No. 2 receiver in the 2026 recruiting class, choosing Alabama over Georgia, Florida and Colorado. The 6-foot-4 Alexander City, Ala., product caught 82 passes for 1,419 yards and 16 touchdowns as a high school senior.

athletes.name: Marshall Pritchett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pritchett, a sophomore tight end from Charleston, South Carolina, appeared in all 15 games in 2025, contributing on special teams and catching seven passes for 57 yards, including four receptions against Eastern Illinois. He came to Tuscaloosa from Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School, where he had 51 catches for 679 yards and 10 touchdowns as a senior. His father, Wes Pritchett, was an All-America linebacker at Notre Dame. He remains a rotational tight end.

athletes.name: Desmond Umeozulu
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Umeozulu, a senior edge rusher from Upper Marlboro, Maryland, joined Alabama after three seasons at South Carolina, where he played in all 36 games and recorded 30 tackles with 2.5 for loss and 1.5 sacks. He posted a career-best 19 stops in 2025. A unanimous four-star out of C.H. Flowers High School and No. 114 on the ESPN300, he adds experienced depth to the Crimson Tide pass rush in 2026.

athletes.name: Austin Mack
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Alabama roster valuation model ~$2.16M, highest on the roster; no contract figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Mack is Alabama's senior quarterback and is competing with Keelon Russell for the starting job in 2026. He followed Kalen DeBoer from Washington and completed 24 of 32 passes for 228 yards and two touchdowns as the backup in 2025.

athletes.name: Jireh Edwards
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Edwards, a freshman safety from Largo, Maryland, arrives as one of the most decorated defensive backs in Alabama's class. ESPN rated him a five-star, the nation's top safety and No. 9 on the ESPN300. At Saint Frances Academy he recorded 92 tackles, 17 for loss, six pass breakups and three forced fumbles as a junior and was a MaxPreps All-American. He chose Alabama over Georgia, Ohio State, Oregon and Texas A&M.

athletes.name: Xavier Griffin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Griffin, a freshman linebacker from Gainesville, Georgia, was rated a five-star and the No. 14 overall recruit by 247Sports, which also listed him as the top linebacker in the class. He made 78 tackles, including 12 for loss and four sacks, as a senior for Josh Niblett at Gainesville High School and earned a Navy All-American Bowl invitation. He picked Alabama over Auburn, Georgia and Ohio State among nearly 40 offers.

athletes.name: Tayden-Evan Kaawa
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kaawa is a freshman quarterback from Molokai, Hawai'i, who played his prep football at Orem High School in Utah after moving from Hawaii. Alabama's roster bio credits him with 163-of-268 passing for 2,503 yards and 34 touchdowns as a senior, following a junior season of 2,890 yards and 28 touchdowns. He signed with the Crimson Tide over BYU, Cal and Hawaii.

athletes.name: Zavier Mincey
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard lists ~$210K; The Sideline models a $150K-$435K range — no contract figure disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Mincey, a junior safety from Daytona Beach, Florida, played in all 15 games in 2025 and expanded his defensive role, finishing with 22 tackles, half a stop for loss, two quarterback hurries and a pass breakup. He added 16 tackles and two breakups in 13 games in 2024, including seven stops in his first career start against Michigan. A unanimous four-star from Mainland High School, he ranked No. 83 on the ESPN300.

athletes.name: John Gazzaniga
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gazzaniga is a sophomore quarterback from Rancho Santa Margarita, California. He joined the Crimson Tide during fall camp in 2025 and appeared in one game, earning his first collegiate action against Eastern Illinois with a one-yard rush. Alabama's coaching staff selected him as an offensive scout team player of the week ahead of the Georgia and Auburn matchups.

athletes.name: Ivan Taylor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taylor, a sophomore safety from Winter Garden, Florida, appeared in all 15 games in 2025, working mainly on coverage units while earning more defensive snaps late in the year. He totaled 14 tackles and a pass breakup, with four stops against Eastern Illinois. A consensus four-star ranked No. 50 on the ESPN300 out of West Orange High School, he is the son of former Pittsburgh Steelers defensive back Ike Taylor.

athletes.name: EJ Crowell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Crowell is a freshman running back from Jackson, Alabama, where he set the state single-season rushing record at Jackson High School in 2024 and then broke his own mark a year later. He rushed for 2,632 yards and 35 touchdowns as a junior, was named Alabama Mr. Football in 2025 and was invited to the Navy All-American Bowl.

athletes.name: Fatutoa Henry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Henry is a fifth-year defensive lineman from Lawndale, California, who reached Alabama through the junior college ranks. He originally signed with Oklahoma before transferring to Cerritos College, where he earned second team All-National Conference Central Division honors in 2023. He played five games for the Crimson Tide in 2025, recording three stops including a half tackle for loss.

athletes.name: Tyler Henderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Henderson, a junior wide receiver from Vicksburg, Mississippi, signed with Alabama out of Mississippi Gulf Coast Community College, where he played 21 games across two seasons. As a sophomore he led the Bulldogs with 1,202 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns on 67 catches after posting 33 receptions for 414 yards as a freshman. 247Sports rated him a top-60 junior college prospect and the No. 8 wideout in the class.

athletes.name: Duke Johnson II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a sophomore linebacker from Eastman, Georgia. He played nine games as a freshman in 2025, working mostly on special teams and totaling three tackles. A four-star recruit out of Dodge County High School, he played five different positions in high school before settling at linebacker and was selected to the Navy All-American Bowl.

athletes.name: Jett Thomalla
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomalla is a freshman quarterback from Omaha, Nebraska. At Millard South High School he threw for more than 130 touchdowns across four varsity seasons and set state Class A records for passing yards, touchdown passes and completions. He was named Nebraska's Gatorade Player of the Year in 2025 after completing 193 of 266 passes for 3,484 yards and 58 touchdowns.

athletes.name: Jorden Edmonds
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Edmonds, a freshman cornerback from Marietta, Georgia, was a five-star recruit by 247Sports, which ranked him the No. 1 corner in the class and the No. 20 prospect nationally. At Sprayberry High School he led the team in receiving while adding 39 tackles, four pass breakups and two interceptions as a senior. He was selected to the Navy All-American Bowl and chose Alabama over Auburn, Georgia and Ohio State.

athletes.name: Trae’shawn Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is a freshman running back from Huntsville, Texas. He rushed for 1,362 yards and 17 touchdowns as a senior at Huntsville High School, adding 13 receptions for 204 yards and topping 100 rushing yards in seven of his 11 games. He also ran track for the Hornets and chose Alabama over Arkansas State, Navy and North Texas.

athletes.name: Zyan Gibson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gibson is a freshman cornerback from Gadsden, Alabama, and a four-star signee out of Gadsden City High School. He was selected for the Alabama-Mississippi All-Star Game and also competed in basketball and track for the Titans, qualifying for the state meet three times in the 100-meter dash and taking bronze at the AHSAA 6A meet as a junior.

athletes.name: Bray Hubbard
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Alabama roster valuation model ~$912K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Hubbard is Alabama's returning starting safety and a 2025 first-team All-SEC and third-team All-American selection after leading the SEC with four interceptions. He enters 2026 as a Walter Camp preseason All-American.

athletes.name: Mack Sutter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sutter is a freshman tight end from Dunlap, Illinois, and a four-star signee who caught 35 passes for 505 yards and seven touchdowns as a junior at Dunlap High School. He also played basketball for the Eagles. His father, Ed Sutter, played linebacker in the NFL and led the Big Ten in tackles at Northwestern in 1990.

athletes.name: John Cooper
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cooper is a junior quarterback for Alabama from Mountain Brook, Alabama, where he played his high school football. He has been listed on the Crimson Tide roster since 2024 and has not yet appeared in a game.

athletes.name: Chuck McDonald III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McDonald, a sophomore defensive back from Santa Ana, California, saw action in six games as a freshman in 2025, working primarily on special teams and recording one tackle against Eastern Illinois. He debuted at Florida State and played late on defense in the Rose Bowl. A unanimous four-star from Mater Dei High School, he was No. 56 on the Rivals100 and played in the Navy All-American Bowl.

athletes.name: Jah-Marien Latham
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Latham is a sixth-year edge rusher from Reform, Alabama, who arrived at Alabama out of Pickens County High School and has since moved into the Wolf linebacker role, where his size helps set the edge against the run. His most productive season came in 2024, when he made 11 starts across 12 games and recorded 27 tackles, two tackles for loss, one sack, three quarterback hurries and a fumble recovery. He missed nearly all of the 2025 season with a neck injury and returned to the roster for 2026.

athletes.name: Khalifa Keith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Keith, a senior running back from Birmingham, joined Alabama as a late transfer addition after stops at Tennessee and Appalachian State. He played 16 games for the Volunteers from 2023 to 2024, gaining 124 yards and a touchdown on 32 carries, then appeared in six games for Appalachian State in 2025. At Parker High School he ran for 1,877 yards and 28 scores as a junior and earned all-state honors twice.

athletes.name: Dre Kirkpatrick Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kirkpatrick, a junior cornerback from Gadsden, Alabama, played in eight games in 2025 and posted nine tackles, one for loss, a forced fumble and a pass breakup, earning special teams player of the week honors for the Vanderbilt game. He appeared in all 13 games in 2024 with three stops. The son of former Alabama All-American Dre Kirkpatrick, he was a top-50 in-state recruit out of Gadsden City.

athletes.name: Maurice Mathis Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mathis is a freshman wide receiver from Warner Robins, Georgia. He caught 62 passes for 1,207 yards and 16 touchdowns as a senior at Houston County High School, helping the Bears to a 10-2 record, after a junior season of 64 receptions for 1,025 yards and 11 scores. He signed with Alabama in January after first committing to Samford.

athletes.name: Kedrick Bingley-Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bingley-Jones, a sixth-year defensive lineman from Concord, North Carolina, comes to Alabama with 40 games of Power Four experience. He spent 2020 through 2023 at North Carolina, appearing in 23 games, then transferred to Mississippi State, where he played all 13 games in 2025 and made 25 tackles. A four-star out of Providence Day School, he was a two-time first-team all-state pick and adds interior depth.

athletes.name: MJ Chirgwin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chirgwin is a fifth-year wide receiver from Huntington Beach, California, who joined the Crimson Tide as a walk-on in 2022. He played in two games in 2025 and caught two passes for 31 yards, including a 20-yard touchdown against ULM for his first career reception. He first saw the field in 2024 against Western Kentucky.

athletes.name: Cayden Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones, a junior linebacker from Asheville, North Carolina, served as an inside linebacker reserve and special teams contributor in 2025, playing 10 games despite a lower-leg injury and totaling eight tackles, a quarterback hurry and a fumble recovery. He added six stops and a pass breakup in 11 games in 2024. ESPN rated him a four-star, the top recruit in North Carolina and No. 62 on the ESPN300 out of Christ School.

athletes.name: Rihyael Kelley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kelley is a freshman safety from Cincinnati, Ohio, who played at Winton Woods High School. A consensus three-star recruit, he was rated among the nation's top 50 safeties by nearly every major outlet and ranked as one of Ohio's top 30 prospects in his class. He signed with Alabama over Cincinnati, Rutgers and Vanderbilt and can also contribute in the return game.

athletes.name: Amari Sabb
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sabb is a freshman wide receiver from Glassboro, New Jersey, and the younger brother of Alabama safety Keon Sabb. He played four varsity seasons at Glassboro High School and helped the Bulldogs to two state titles, finishing with 144 career receptions for 2,340 yards and 31 touchdowns along with 5,135 all-purpose yards.

athletes.name: Steve Bolo Mboumoua
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bolo Mboumoua, a junior defensive lineman from Saint Augustin de Desmaures, Quebec, worked in three games in his first season at Alabama in 2025 and recorded five tackles, including one for loss against ULM. He arrived from Southwest Mississippi Community College, where he made 46 tackles with seven for loss and 4.5 sacks in nine games. ESPN and 247Sports rated him the top recruit in Canada. He grew up in Cameroon.

athletes.name: Mhari Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a freshman defensive lineman from Muscle Shoals, Alabama. He helped Muscle Shoals High School to the state semifinals as a senior and earned Class 6A all-state honors from the Alabama Sportswriters Association in 2024.
