He was selected for the Alabama-Mississippi All-Star Game and chose the Crimson Tide over Auburn, Miami and Ole Miss.

athletes.name: Aubrey Walker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Walker, a freshman wide receiver from Birmingham, signed with Alabama out of Moody High School, where he caught 29 passes for 490 yards and seven touchdowns during the Blue Devils' Class 5A state championship season. Listed at 5-foot-10 and 170 pounds, he was rated a three-star prospect in the 2026 class by the 247Sports Composite. He joins a crowded receiver room and is expected to compete for reserve snaps.

athletes.name: Walter Sansing III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sansing is a senior safety from Homewood, Alabama, who has been with the Crimson Tide since 2023. He played in two games in 2025, seeing his first game action against ULM and appearing again versus Eastern Illinois. Alabama's staff named him a special teams scout team player of the week ahead of the Tennessee game in both 2024 and 2025.

athletes.name: Elijah Murray
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Murray is a senior wide receiver for Alabama from Buford, Georgia, where he attended Buford High School. He wears No. 27 on the Crimson Tide roster, which does not list prior college game experience for him.

athletes.name: Carmelo O'Neal
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: O'Neal, a junior cornerback from Atlanta, transferred to Alabama after two seasons at Mercer, where he played 23 games and recorded 54 tackles, 12 pass breakups, one sack and a forced fumble. He led the Bears with 10 breakups as a sophomore and started three games at corner as a true freshman. 247Sports ranked him a top-75 safety in its transfer portal rankings. He played at Westlake High School.

athletes.name: Fredrick Moore
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moore is a junior running back for Alabama from Cypress, Texas, where he played his high school football at Bridgeland. He has been on the Crimson Tide roster since 2024 and has not yet appeared in a game.

athletes.name: Nick Sherman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sherman is a junior cornerback who grew up in Tuscaloosa and played his prep ball at Northridge High School. He began his college career at Itawamba Community College in Mississippi, playing eight games and recording 24 tackles with one sack, two interceptions and six pass breakups before joining Alabama as a three-star junior college transfer.

athletes.name: Derek Meadows
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Meadows is a 6-foot-5 sophomore wide receiver projected as Alabama's third starter in 2026 after playing 12 games with one start as a freshman. The Bishop Gorman (Las Vegas) product won four straight Nevada state titles in high school.

athletes.name: Bubba Odom
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Odom is a senior linebacker from Parrish, Alabama, who played his high school football at Jasper. He joined the Crimson Tide in the summer of 2026 after stops at Northern Arizona and East Mississippi Community College. At East Mississippi in 2025 he recorded 16 tackles with 2.5 tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks.

athletes.name: Cooper Mollison
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mollison is a junior wide receiver from Vestavia Hills, Alabama, where he played his high school football. He appeared in one game as a freshman in 2024, seeing his first collegiate action late against Mercer. He did not play in 2025 but was named a special teams scout team player of the week ahead of the Oklahoma and Auburn games.

athletes.name: Conor Talty
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Talty, a senior kicker from Chicago, won the starting placekicking job in 2025 and appeared in all 15 games, scoring 96 points on 16 of 23 field goals and 48 of 48 extra points while handling kickoffs. He forced 42 touchbacks on 74 kickoffs. He handled kickoff duties in 2024 with 41 touchbacks. A Saint Rita product, he returns as Alabama's incumbent kicker in 2026.

athletes.name: George French II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: French is a freshman safety from Birmingham, Alabama, who played his high school football at Homewood. He wears No. 31 and joins the Crimson Tide secondary as a first-year player without prior college game experience.

athletes.name: Alex Asparuhov
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Asparuhov, a sophomore punter from Fresno, California, spent his first fall camp working back from injury and saw action in one game in 2025, debuting against ULM. He was regarded as one of the top punters in the 2025 signing class, rated the No. 2 punter nationally by 247Sports, and chose Alabama over Florida, Fresno State and Oklahoma. He played at San Joaquin Memorial High School.

athletes.name: Griffin Hanson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hanson is a junior cornerback from Florence, Alabama, who played at Mars Hill Bible School. He has been on the Alabama roster since 2024 without game action, and the staff named him a scout team player of the week before the Eastern Illinois contest.

athletes.name: Corey Howard Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Howard is a freshman defensive lineman from Valdosta, Georgia. He totaled 36 tackles, including 10 for loss and 4.5 sacks, as a junior at Valdosta High School and also played basketball for the Wildcats. A three-star edge prospect with long arms, he flipped his commitment from Georgia to sign with the Crimson Tide.

athletes.name: Adam Watford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Watford is a senior punter from Dothan, Alabama, who joined the Crimson Tide from North Alabama through the transfer portal in January 2026. He handled both punting and place kicking at Dothan High School before signing with the Lions. In 2025 he punted 66 times for 3,073 yards, an average of 46.6 yards that ranked among the national leaders, and he was named United Athletic Conference Co-Specialist of the Year, earned first-team all-conference honors and reached semifinalist status for the FCS punter of the year award.

athletes.name: London Hill
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hill is a junior cornerback from Mobile, Alabama, who played his high school football at McGill-Toolen. He did not see game action for the Crimson Tide in 2025.

athletes.name: Zay Hall
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hall is a freshman linebacker from Tuscaloosa who played at Hillcrest High School. A three-star recruit, he was rated the nation's 41st-best linebacker by ESPN.com and ranked among Alabama's top 50 prospects. He earned an invitation to the Alabama-Mississippi All-Star Game and stayed home with the Tide despite offers from Jacksonville State, Troy and Virginia Tech.

athletes.name: Abduall Sanders Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sanders is a sophomore linebacker from Santa Ana, California, who played at Mater Dei High School. He appeared in seven games as a freshman in 2025 and recorded one tackle on kickoff coverage against South Carolina. A four-star recruit ranked No. 172 on the ESPN300, he chose Alabama over Auburn and Tennessee.

athletes.name: QB Reese
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reese is a junior linebacker from Birmingham, Alabama, who signed with the Crimson Tide out of Ramsay High School as a three-star recruit ranked around the No. 72 linebacker nationally in the consensus rankings. Listed at roughly six feet and 224 pounds, he is undersized for the position but has drawn consistent praise through the offseason for his speed and physical play. Reese enters 2026 in line for a substantially larger defensive role after developing behind Alabama's veteran linebackers, and he has spoken about refining his plan for rushing the quarterback.

athletes.name: Brody McCutcheon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McCutcheon is a sophomore cornerback from Moody, Alabama, where he played his high school football. He appeared in two games in 2025, seeing time against ULM and entering on special teams versus Eastern Illinois. Alabama's coaches named him a special teams scout team player of the week before Georgia and a defensive scout honoree before LSU.

athletes.name: Jake Ivie
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ivie is a senior linebacker from Alabaster, Alabama, who played at Thompson High School. He has been with the Crimson Tide since 2023 and made his collegiate debut in 2025 against Eastern Illinois. The staff also named him a defensive scout team player of the week for his work leading up to that game.

athletes.name: Josh Ford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ford is a junior tight end from Stillwater, Oklahoma, who signed with Alabama out of the transfer portal in December 2025 as the Crimson Tide's first portal addition of the cycle. A three-star recruit in Oklahoma State's 2024 class, he stayed home to play for the Cowboys and appeared in 16 games over two seasons, recording 13 receptions for 137 yards and two touchdowns. Listed at 6-6 and 265 pounds, Ford chose Alabama over Auburn, Arkansas, Illinois and Oklahoma and worked into the tight end rotation during spring practice.

athletes.name: Jamarion Matthews
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Matthews is a freshman edge rusher from Huntsville, Alabama, who transferred to Gainesville High School in Georgia for his senior year. Across his sophomore and junior seasons at Sparkman High School he recorded 118 tackles, including 48 for loss and 30.5 sacks. A unanimous four-star recruit, he picked Alabama over Clemson, Florida and Ole Miss.

athletes.name: Ben Jackson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson is a sophomore wide receiver from Mobile, Alabama, who played his high school football at Murphy. He appeared in one game for the Crimson Tide in 2025, making his first collegiate appearance against Eastern Illinois.

athletes.name: Alex Rozier
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rozier, a fifth-year long snapper from Hattiesburg, Mississippi, handled snapping duties on Alabama's field goal and extra point units in 2025, appearing in 12 games and missing only the Missouri, South Carolina and LSU contests. He made his collegiate debut against Western Kentucky in 2024 and did not see action in 2022 or 2023. He came to Tuscaloosa from Oak Grove High School and remains a specialist contributor.

athletes.name: Nolan Wilson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilson is a freshman edge rusher from Picayune, Mississippi. As a senior at Picayune Memorial High School he recorded 81 tackles, including 19 for loss, with 11 sacks and 17 quarterback hurries. A four-star prospect, he was selected for the Under Armour All-American Game and the Alabama-Mississippi All-Star Game and chose Alabama over Auburn, Miami and Ole Miss.

athletes.name: Jay Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a junior long snapper from Ringgold, Georgia, who played at Heritage High School. He appeared in two games as a backup in 2024, entering late at snapper against Western Kentucky for his first collegiate action and also playing at Mercer, then handled snapping duties late in the 2025 Eastern Illinois game.

athletes.name: Peyton Fox
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fox is a fifth-year tight end from Pelham, Alabama, who played at Briarwood Christian. He has been with the Crimson Tide since 2022 and appeared in two games in each of the 2024 and 2025 seasons, debuting against Western Kentucky. He has been named both an offensive and a special teams scout team player of the week.

athletes.name: Eli Deutsch
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Deutsch is a freshman long snapper from Franklin, Wisconsin, where he played his high school football. He wears No. 47 and joins Alabama's specialist group as a first-year member of the roster.

athletes.name: Ethan Stangle
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stangle, a fifth-year long snapper from Bel Air, Maryland, transferred to Alabama after four seasons at Syracuse. He played in all 12 games for the Orange in 2025 and recorded one tackle, having earned his first action in the team's 2024 bowl game. Kohl's rated him a top-15 long snapper in the 2022 class out of John Carroll High School. He gives Alabama an experienced snapping option.

athletes.name: Casey Poe
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Poe, a junior offensive lineman from Lindale, Texas, has appeared in four games over two seasons, including two in 2025, and has twice been named an offensive scout player of the week by the Alabama staff. A unanimous four-star, he was rated the No. 1 interior offensive lineman in his class by On3 and the 247Composite and played in the Under Armour All-America Game. He won a Texas 4A shot put title.

athletes.name: Mal Waldrep Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Waldrep, a sophomore offensive lineman from Seale, Alabama, played in two games as a freshman in 2025, logging eight snaps and a knockdown block against Eastern Illinois. He was named an offensive scout player of the week for his preparation work ahead of the Tennessee game. A four-star by Rivals out of Central High School in Phenix City, he chose Alabama over Auburn, Clemson and Florida and offers interior depth.

athletes.name: Mac Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a senior offensive lineman from Birmingham, Alabama, who played at Mountain Brook High School. He has been on the Alabama roster since 2023 and played in one game as a reserve lineman in 2024, entering off the bench against Mercer.

athletes.name: Jayvin James
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: James is a senior offensive lineman from Deerfield Beach, Florida, who committed to Alabama in January 2026 with two years of eligibility remaining. He began his career at Akron, spent two seasons there and then moved to Mississippi State, where he started 12 games in 2025 including nine at left tackle. A three-star recruit out of Blanche Ely High School in the 2023 class, he is listed at 6-5 and 320 pounds and gives the Crimson Tide an experienced option on the edge of the offensive line.

athletes.name: Racin Delgatty
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Delgatty is a senior offensive lineman from La Canada Flintridge, California, who transferred to Alabama from Cal Poly and profiles as a center. He played high school football at St. Francis and logged 1,316 offensive snaps over three seasons with the Mustangs, with 1,302 of those coming at center, allowing just one sack across that stretch. Listed at 6-3 and 300 pounds, he was rated a three-star portal prospect and was the third offensive lineman Alabama added from the portal in the 2026 cycle.

athletes.name: Bear Fretwell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fretwell is a freshman offensive lineman from Brooklet, Georgia, who played at Southeast Bulloch High School. He was homeschooled before enrolling there and did not play varsity football until his sophomore year. A three-star tackle listed at 6-6 and 295 pounds, he committed to Georgia Tech before flipping to Alabama.

athletes.name: JD Martin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Martin is a junior offensive lineman from Pisgah, Alabama, where he played his high school football. He has been on the Crimson Tide roster since 2024 and has not yet appeared in a game.

athletes.name: Davis Peterson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Peterson is a senior offensive lineman from Birmingham, Alabama, who played at Mountain Brook High School. He has been with the Crimson Tide since 2023 and saw his first collegiate action against Mercer in 2024. In 2025 the coaching staff named him an offensive scout team player of the week ahead of Alabama's playoff game at Oklahoma.

athletes.name: Bryson Cooley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cooley is a freshman offensive lineman from Laurel, Mississippi, who played at West Jones High School. Rated a four-star tackle by nearly every major outlet, he was selected for the Alabama-Mississippi All-Star Game and also excelled in the shot put. He flipped his commitment from LSU to sign with the Crimson Tide.

athletes.name: Michael Carroll
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Alabama roster valuation model ~$1.2M; no contract figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Carroll is Alabama's only returning offensive line starter and was an FWAA Freshman All-American and Freshman All-SEC pick after six starts at right tackle in 2025. The former consensus five-star from IMG Academy re-signed with the Crimson Tide for 2026 and is projected to move inside to right guard.

athletes.name: Tyrell Miller
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Miller, a junior offensive lineman from Union City, California, joined Alabama from the junior college ranks after beginning his career at the College of San Mateo, where he played three games along the line in 2025. Rivals rated him the sixth-best junior college recruit, the No. 2 offensive tackle and the second-ranked player from California, while ESPN listed him a top-20 JUCO prospect. He played at James Logan High School.

athletes.name: Jared Graham
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Graham is a freshman offensive lineman from Atlanta, Georgia, who played his high school football at Banneker. He wears No. 66 and joins the Crimson Tide offensive line as a first-year player without prior college game experience.

athletes.name: Billy Roby
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Roby is a senior offensive lineman from Huntsville, Alabama, where he played his high school football. He has been on the roster since 2023 and played in one game as a reserve lineman in 2024, entering late against Mercer.

athletes.name: Baker Hickman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hickman is a senior offensive lineman from Tuscaloosa who played his prep football at Northridge High School. He has been with the Crimson Tide since 2023 and earned snaps in two games as a reserve in 2024, entering late against Western Kentucky for his first collegiate action and also playing on the offensive line against Mercer.

athletes.name: William Sanders
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sanders is a junior offensive lineman from Brookwood, Alabama, who signed with the Crimson Tide as a four-star prospect in the 2024 class, choosing the in-state program over LSU and Mississippi State after collecting more than 20 offers. He redshirted his first season, then played in all 15 games in 2025 and saw extended work at left guard against opponents including Georgia, Vanderbilt and LSU. Listed at 6-3 and 280 pounds, Sanders enters 2026 competing for the open left guard job and hosted a youth camp in Brookwood in June.

athletes.name: Nick Brooks
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brooks, a sophomore offensive lineman from Cedar Rapids, Iowa, transferred to Alabama from Texas, where he appeared in five games in 2025 and started three SEC contests against Oklahoma, Kentucky and Mississippi State. 247Sports rated him a top-135 portal player and the No. 7 interior lineman available. He was a four-star recruit who finished high school at Grayson in Georgia after earlier stops in Iowa and Alpharetta.

athletes.name: Ty Haywood
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Haywood is a sophomore offensive lineman from Denton, Texas, who played at Ryan High School. A five-star tackle by most outlets and a Navy All-American Bowl selection, he originally signed with Michigan and played in three games there as a freshman before transferring to Alabama. He also competed in the shot put and discus.

athletes.name: Chris Booker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Booker is a freshman offensive lineman from Atlanta, Georgia, who played at Hapeville Charter Career Academy. He spent time on both sides of the ball in high school before settling on the interior offensive line, where he earned four-star grades from nearly every major outlet. He signed with Alabama over Florida, Kentucky and USF.

athletes.name: Ethan Fields
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fields, a senior offensive lineman from Geismar, Louisiana, arrived from Ole Miss, where he played 19 games over three seasons. He appeared in all 15 contests as a reserve lineman and special teams contributor during the Rebels' College Football Playoff run in 2025. A unanimous three-star out of Dutchtown High School, he recorded more than 60 pancakes as a senior and earned District 5-5A first team recognition in 2022.

athletes.name: Jackson Lloyd
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Alabama roster valuation model ~$1.0M; no contract figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Lloyd is Alabama's projected starting left tackle in 2026 after backing up at the position as a freshman in 2025. He was a five-star grade on On3 and the No. 20 overall recruit nationally out of Carmel, Calif.

athletes.name: Kaden Strayhorn
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Strayhorn, a sophomore offensive lineman from Novi, Michigan, transferred to Alabama after beginning his career at Michigan, where he saw action in two games in 2025. He attended IMG Academy for three prep seasons and was rated a four-star by ESPN and Rivals. His father, Jason, was a team captain and first team All-Big Ten center at Michigan State. He competes for interior line depth in 2026.

athletes.name: Jaxon Shuttlesworth
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Shuttlesworth is a junior tight end from Chelsea, Alabama, who played his prep football at Chelsea High School and also competed in basketball for the Hornets. He spent his first two collegiate seasons at Jacksonville State without seeing game action before transferring to Alabama.

athletes.name: Kaleb Edwards
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Alabama roster valuation model ~$368K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Edwards is Alabama's projected starting tight end after appearing in all 15 games as a freshman in 2025 and finishing second among Tide tight ends with 11 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown. He was named to the Freshman All-SEC team by the league's coaches.

athletes.name: Lane Whisenhunt
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Whisenhunt is a senior linebacker from Vestavia Hills, Alabama, where he played his high school football. He moved from tight end to linebacker during fall camp in 2025 and played in two games, making his debut on special teams against ULM and recording two tackles versus Eastern Illinois. He has earned multiple scout team player of the week honors.

athletes.name: Warner Ross
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ross is a senior wide receiver from Dalton, Georgia, where he played his high school football. He wears No. 83 on Alabama's roster, which does not list prior college game action for him.

athletes.name: Jack Sammarco
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sammarco, a junior tight end from Cincinnati, joined Alabama after one season at West Virginia, where he played all 13 games and caught one pass as a freshman. He saw action in two games for the Crimson Tide in 2025, against ULM and Eastern Illinois. A three-star out of Anderson High School, he had 27 catches for 315 yards and five touchdowns and added eight sacks as a senior.

athletes.name: Jude Cascone
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cascone is a freshman tight end from Marietta, Georgia. He caught 16 passes for 238 yards and four touchdowns as a senior at Walton High School and also took snaps at linebacker for the Raiders. A three-star blocking tight end who also played baseball, he chose Alabama over in-state Georgia and Georgia Tech.

athletes.name: Danny Lewis Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lewis, a fifth-year tight end from New Iberia, Louisiana, has appeared in 38 games at Alabama since 2022. He played six contests in 2025 while dealing with injuries and caught two passes for 17 yards against Missouri. He appeared in all 13 games in 2024 and played 14 games with one start in 2023. A three-star from Westgate High School, he chose Alabama over Florida, LSU and Cincinnati.

athletes.name: Isaia Faga
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Faga, a junior defensive lineman from Phenix City, Alabama, provided depth along the front in all 15 games in 2025 and recorded nine tackles, half a stop for loss and a quarterback hurry. athletes.blurb: Jackson is a redshirt junior cornerback from Kissimmee, Fla. entering his second season at LSU after two years at Florida. A consensus four star recruit out of Osceola High School, he appeared in 11 games for the Tigers in 2025 and recorded six tackles across 84 defensive snaps. He posted seven tackles and three pass breakups as a Gators freshman in 2023 and projects as depth behind LSU's starting corners.

athletes.name: Dashawn Spears
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dashawn Spears is in line to start in LSU's secondary in 2026 after playing 26 games over his first two seasons. A junior from nearby Denham Springs, Louisiana, he has totaled 53 tackles, three tackles for loss, three pass breakups and two interceptions, highlighted by a two-interception game against Florida in 2025 that included a 58-yard return for a touchdown and earned him SEC Defensive Player of the Week honors. Head coach Lane Kiffin singled him out during spring practice as one of the roster's most improved players.

athletes.name: Landen Clark
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clark is a redshirt sophomore quarterback from Radford, Va. who transferred to LSU after two seasons at Elon. He started all 12 games in 2025, throwing for 2,321 yards and 18 touchdowns while rushing for 625 yards and 11 scores, and was named CAA Co-Offensive Rookie of the Year. He led Radford High School to a 15-0 state title season in 2023. He competes for backup snaps in a reshaped quarterback room.

athletes.name: PJ Woodland
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: PJ Woodland started all 13 games at cornerback for LSU in 2025 and ranked eighth in the SEC with 11 passes defended. A junior from Hattiesburg, Mississippi, he has appeared in 26 career games with 15 starts, recording 61 tackles, 12 pass breakups and two interceptions while allowing just one touchdown in coverage across his first two seasons. He pairs with DJ Pickett to give the Tigers one of the more experienced cornerback tandems in the conference heading into 2026, when he is again projected to start on the outside.

athletes.name: Malachi Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a junior tight end from Thomasville, Ga. who joined LSU after two seasons at Pittsburgh. He appeared in 26 games with one start for the Panthers, totaling 15 catches for 214 yards and three touchdowns, including 13 receptions for 192 yards and two scores in 2025. He helped Thomas County Central to an undefeated state championship and averaged 18.1 yards per catch as a senior. He adds depth to LSU's tight end rotation.

athletes.name: Dilin Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a redshirt sophomore running back from Laurel, Md. who transferred from Wisconsin. He opened 2025 as the Badgers' starter and ran for 300 yards and two touchdowns on 76 carries over seven starts before a season ending injury. A consensus four star recruit rated the nation's sixth best back by ESPN, he rushed for more than 2,100 yards at Our Lady of Good Counsel and twice won conference player of the year.

athletes.name: Faheem Delane
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Delane is a sophomore safety from Good Hope, Md. who transferred to LSU after one season at Ohio State, where he played 13 games as a true freshman and recorded 12 tackles. A four star prospect rated the No. 8 safety nationally and No. 3 player in Maryland, he was conference defensive player of the year at Our Lady of Good Counsel with 97 tackles and three interceptions. His brother Mansoor played cornerback for the Tigers in 2025.

athletes.name: Trey'Dez Green
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 LSU roster valuation ~$819K; not a disclosed contract figure)
athletes.blurb: Green is LSU's starting tight end and a second-team All-SEC selection in 2025, when he caught 33 passes for 433 yards and seven touchdowns. The 6-foot-7 junior also plays basketball at LSU.

athletes.name: Jaiden Braker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Braker is a redshirt freshman linebacker on the LSU roster, wearing No. 15. He comes from Snellville, Georgia, and played his high school football at South Gwinnett High School before joining the Tigers.

athletes.name: Phillip Wright III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wright is a redshirt freshman wide receiver for LSU who wears No. 15. He is from Shrewsbury, Louisiana, and played high school football at Destrehan High School, one of the state's steady pipelines to the Tigers.

athletes.name: John Hurley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hurley is a graduate defensive back from Vienna, Va. who joined LSU after four seasons at Virginia, where he was listed at safety before moving to cornerback. He was a first team all state defensive back and kick returner at James Madison High School and earned ACC academic honor roll recognition in 2022-23 and 2023-24. He arrives with limited game experience and projects as secondary and special teams depth.

athletes.name: Damien Shanklin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Shanklin is a redshirt freshman defensive end from Indianapolis who appeared in five games for LSU in 2025 and recorded two sacks in his debut against Southeastern Louisiana. A four star edge rusher rated the top overall prospect in Indiana, he posted 48 tackles with 16 for loss as a Warren Central senior. He made the 2025 SEC academic honor roll and competes for rotational pass rush snaps this fall.

athletes.name: Gabriel Reliford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gabriel Reliford signed with LSU in the 2024 class as one of the nation's highest-rated edge rushers, staying home after a standout high school career in Shreveport. The redshirt sophomore was expected to compete for a starting edge job in 2026 following the departures of Jack Pyburn and Patrick Payton, but his 2025 season ended after four games, and a knee injury suffered during spring practice in 2026 is widely reported to be likely to keep him out for the season.

athletes.name: Kaden Martin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Martin is a fifth-year quarterback from Atlanta who played his high school football at Buford High School in Georgia. He transferred to LSU from Middle Tennessee, where he spent an earlier part of his college career. The Tigers list him at 5-11 and 231 pounds, and he wears No. 19 in an experienced quarterback room.

athletes.name: Michael Turner Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Turner is a redshirt sophomore cornerback from Kenner, La. entering his third season at LSU. He has played 11 games over two years with three tackles and two pass breakups, appearing in seven games in 2025 mostly on kickoff coverage. A four star recruit at John Curtis, he played receiver and defensive back on a Division I select state championship team, catching 25 passes for 519 yards. He remains secondary and special teams depth.

athletes.name: Harlem Berry
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 LSU roster valuation ~$463K; Nike Blue Ribbon Elite NIL athlete)
athletes.blurb: Berry is LSU's projected starting running back as a sophomore after signing as the nation's top-rated running back recruit out of St. Martin's Episcopal in Metairie, La. He was the 2025 Louisiana high school player of the year coming out of prep.

athletes.name: Havon Finney Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Finney is a freshman cornerback from Carson, Calif. who reclassified in the spring to finish high school a year early and enroll at LSU. He was rated among the nation's top corners in his class, listed around No. 14 at the position by Rivals and as high as No. 9 by ESPN. At Sierra Canyon he recorded 37 tackles, four interceptions and two punt return touchdowns as a sophomore. He joins a crowded cornerback rotation.

athletes.name: Aidan Anding
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anding is a sophomore cornerback from Grambling, La. entering his second year at LSU after playing eight games as a true freshman in 2025, mostly on special teams, with two tackles. He was rated the No. 1 cornerback prospect in Louisiana for the 2025 class at Ruston High School, where he earned first team 5A all state honors in football and basketball and won a state title in 2023. He is expected to contribute in the secondary rotation.

athletes.name: Stacy Gage
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gage is a redshirt sophomore running back from Tampa, Fla. who transferred to LSU from UCF. He appeared in eight games in 2025, carrying 13 times for 63 yards with his first collegiate touchdown against North Carolina A&T. A four star recruit in the 2024 class, he rushed for 390 yards and six scores as a senior on a St. Thomas Aquinas team that went 14-1 and won a state title. He arrives with three years of eligibility.

athletes.name: Joseph Ebun
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ebun is a redshirt junior running back for LSU wearing No. 24. He is from John's Creek, Georgia, and played his high school football at Chattahoochee High School before arriving in Baton Rouge.

athletes.name: Tylen Singleton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Singleton is a redshirt sophomore linebacker from Many, La. who played all 13 games in 2025 and made his first career start in the Texas Bowl against Houston, posting a career best nine tackles with one for loss. He has 15 tackles across 17 career appearances and logged 147 defensive snaps last season. A consensus four star recruit, he was a four year starter at Many High School and won state titles in 2020 and 2022.

athletes.name: Aiden Hall
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hall is a freshman safety on the LSU roster, wearing No. 25. He is a New Orleans native who played his high school football at Edna Karr High School, a program that regularly sends players to major college teams.

athletes.name: Rod Gainey Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gainey is a redshirt sophomore running back from Tampa, Fla. who transferred to LSU after two seasons at Charlotte. He led the 49ers in rushing in 2025 with 260 yards and a touchdown on 74 carries, finishing there with 289 rushing yards and 17 receptions across 15 games and three starts. A three star recruit, he ran for 1,087 yards and 14 touchdowns as a Tampa Bay Tech senior. He competes for backfield rotation snaps.

athletes.name: Charles Ross II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ross is a sophomore linebacker from Houston who played 12 games as a true freshman in 2025, working mainly on special teams and recording one tackle. A consensus four star recruit ranked as high as No. 2 nationally at his position by 247Sports, he posted 71 tackles and six sacks as a North Shore junior and ran 10.36 in the 100 meters at the Texas state meet. He made the 2025 SEC academic honor roll.

athletes.name: Nolon Buckels
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Buckels is a freshman wide receiver for LSU who wears No. 26. He comes from Prosper, Texas, and played his high school football at Walnut Grove High School before joining the Tigers.

athletes.name: Dez Ellis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ellis is a freshman cornerback on the LSU roster, listed at No. 27. He is from Wisner, Louisiana, and played his high school football at Franklin Parish High School before signing with the Tigers.

athletes.name: Raycine Guillory Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Guillory is a redshirt freshman running back from Fort Worth, Texas, and an Aledo High School product. He came to LSU as a transfer from Utah. The Tigers list him at 5-10 and 179 pounds, making him one of the smaller backs in the room, and he wears No. 27.

athletes.name: Jhase Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a redshirt freshman safety from Destrehan, La. who appeared in five games in 2025, most notably blocking a Texas A&M punt that resulted in a safety. A consensus four star recruit ranked among the top safeties in Louisiana, he played both ways at Destrehan High School and ran 11.07 in the 100 meters. His father Fred Thomas spent 12 NFL seasons, eight with the New Orleans Saints. He projects as special teams and secondary depth.

athletes.name: Caden Durham
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation ~$99K; Nike Blue Ribbon Elite NIL athlete, terms undisclosed)
athletes.blurb: Durham is LSU's veteran running back and shares the backfield with Harlem Berry after leading the Tigers in rushing as a true freshman in 2024. He briefly entered the transfer portal after the 2025 season before returning to LSU.

athletes.name: Jordan Ross
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 LSU roster valuation ~$1.07M)
athletes.blurb: Ross is a starting edge rusher for LSU after transferring from Tennessee, where he recorded 26 tackles and 1.5 sacks across 22 games in two seasons. He was a five-star recruit in the 2024 class.

athletes.name: Treylan James
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: James is a redshirt junior cornerback and Baton Rouge native who joined LSU after playing at Southern in 2025 and Prairie View A&M before that. He appeared in 11 games for Southern and recorded 26 tackles, three tackles for loss and six pass breakups, with a nine tackle game against Mississippi Valley. The Madison Prep Academy product has 42 tackles and seven pass breakups over 21 career games and adds experienced depth at corner.

athletes.name: CJ Jimcoily
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jimcoily is a sophomore linebacker from Nashville who played all 13 games as a freshman in 2025, logging 187 special teams snaps and 32 defensive snaps with five tackles. He signed with LSU as a four star safety and moved to linebacker on arrival. At Lipscomb Academy he was ranked as high as No. 5 in Tennessee and No. 14 nationally at safety by Rivals. He is expected to remain a core special teams contributor.

athletes.name: Gavin Higgins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Higgins is a freshman kicker for LSU wearing No. 32. He grew up in Baton Rouge and played his high school football at Parkview Baptist School, staying in his hometown to continue his career with the Tigers.

athletes.name: Keylan Moses
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moses is a redshirt freshman linebacker on the LSU roster, wearing No. 32. He is a Baton Rouge native who played his high school football at University Lab High School, located on the LSU campus.

athletes.name: Isaiah Washington
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Washington is a freshman safety for LSU who wears No. 33. He comes from Haynesville, Louisiana, and played his high school football at Haynesville High School before signing with the Tigers.

athletes.name: Mason Dossett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dossett is a redshirt sophomore from Missouri City, Texas who transferred to LSU after two seasons at Baylor and is listed at wide receiver. He moved there from safety with the Bears and caught one pass for 11 yards in 2025. He also ran track, posting the sixth fastest 60 meter hurdles time in Baylor history at 7.82. A three star recruit at Ridge Point, he is the son of former Baylor receiver Martin Dossett.

athletes.name: Zach Weeks
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Weeks is a redshirt freshman linebacker on the LSU roster, wearing No. 35. He is from Oconee County, Georgia, and played his high school football at Oconee County High School before joining the Tigers.

athletes.name: Aidan Corbello
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Corbello is a redshirt junior kicker for LSU wearing No. 36. He is from New Orleans and played his high school football at Jesuit High School before continuing his career in Baton Rouge.

athletes.name: Emari Peterson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Peterson is a freshman cornerback on the LSU roster, listed at No. 36. He comes from Orlando, Florida, and played his high school football at Evans High School before signing with the Tigers.

athletes.name: Craig Walton Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Walton is a redshirt junior cornerback for LSU who wears No. 37. He is from Camden, New Jersey, and played his high school football at Camden High School before making his way to Baton Rouge.

athletes.name: Jackson Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a freshman safety on the LSU roster, wearing No. 38. He is a New Orleans native who played his high school football at Archbishop Shaw High School before joining the Tigers.

athletes.name: Lavonte Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a sophomore defensive back from Camden, South Carolina, where he played at Camden High School. He reached LSU by way of Georgia Military College, taking the junior college route into the Southeastern Conference. The Tigers list him at 6-3 and 180 pounds, a long frame for the secondary, and he wears No. 39.

athletes.name: Mack Mulhern
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mack Mulhern joined LSU through the transfer portal for 2026 after beginning his career at Florida, where the long snapper did not appear in a game as a freshman in 2025. A redshirt freshman from Scottsdale, Arizona, he was regarded as one of the top long snapping prospects in his class at Horizon High School. He followed special teams coordinator Joe Houston, who moved from Gainesville to Baton Rouge on Lane Kiffin's new staff, and is positioned to take over LSU's snapping duties.

athletes.name: Whit Weeks
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation ~$1.8M, No. 33 in the On3 NIL 100; The NIL Standard models his LSU roster share at ~$451K)
athletes.blurb: Weeks is LSU's returning starting middle linebacker and one of the SEC's most productive tacklers. He announced he would return to the Tigers for the 2026 season rather than enter the NFL Draft.

athletes.name: Davhon Keys
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Keys is a junior linebacker from Aledo, Texas entering his third season at LSU and one of the more experienced players in this group. He led the Tigers with 92 tackles in 2025, starting five of 13 games, and has 123 career tackles with five for loss over 25 appearances. He returned an interception 41 yards for a touchdown in the 2024 Texas Bowl and won three state titles at Aledo High School.

athletes.name: Silas Hall
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hall is a sophomore long snapper for LSU wearing No. 43. He grew up in Baton Rouge and played his high school football at Episcopal High School before joining the Tigers' specialist group.

athletes.name: Zach Grace
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Grace is a redshirt junior tight end from Kearney, Mo. who transferred to LSU after three seasons at Oregon, where he played 24 games and logged 101 offensive snaps split between tight end and fullback over his final two years. Valued as a short yardage blocker, he was a three star recruit and all state selection who scored 22 touchdowns as a Kearney High School senior. His brother Theo joined LSU as a linebacker.

athletes.name: Sean Perret
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Perret is a redshirt freshman kicker on the LSU roster, listed at No. 45. He is from Baton Rouge and played his high school football at Catholic High School, remaining in his hometown for college.

athletes.name: James Larson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Larson is a redshirt sophomore tight end from St. Charles, Illinois, where he played at St. Charles East High School. He transferred to LSU from SMU, moving from the Dallas program to Baton Rouge to continue his college career. He is listed at 6-4 on the Tigers roster and wears No. 46.

athletes.name: Seth Knothe
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Knothe is a fifth-year defensive back from Boise, Idaho, and a graduate of Bishop Kelly High School. He came to LSU from Boise State, the program in his hometown, bringing several years of college experience to the Tigers' secondary. He is listed at 6-1 and 214 pounds and wears No. 46.

athletes.name: JD LaFleur
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: LaFleur is a redshirt freshman tight end for LSU wearing No. 47. He is from Sulphur, Louisiana, and played his high school football at Sulphur High School before signing with the Tigers.

athletes.name: Malik Blocton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Malik Blocton committed to LSU on January 8, 2026, as a transfer from Auburn, choosing the Tigers over interest from Texas A&M, Clemson, Ole Miss and Alabama. A junior from Pike Road, Alabama, he played 24 games across two seasons for Auburn, totaling 34 tackles and 8.5 tackles for loss while lining up at defensive tackle and occasionally on the edge. On3's transfer portal industry rankings placed him among the top 15 defensive linemen in the cycle, and he is expected to hold down a starting spot on LSU's interior line.

athletes.name: Kolaj Cobbins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cobbins is a redshirt sophomore defensive end from St. Rose, La. entering his third season at LSU. He appeared in seven games in 2025 and posted a career high three tackles against Southeastern Louisiana, giving him nine career appearances. A four star prospect from Destrehan High School, he was a unanimous team captain, played in the 2024 All-American Bowl and made the SEC academic honor roll in 2024 and 2025.

athletes.name: Theo Grace
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Grace is a redshirt freshman linebacker from Kearney, Missouri, and a Kearney High School product. He began his college career at North Dakota before transferring to LSU, where he wears No. 49. The Tigers list him at 6-2 and 231 pounds.

athletes.name: William Satterwhite II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Satterwhite is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Barberton, Ohio, and a graduate of Archbishop Hoban High School. He transferred to LSU from Tennessee, a move that kept him inside the Southeastern Conference. The Tigers list him at 6-3 and 293 pounds, and he wears No. 50.

athletes.name: Ryan Miret
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Miret is a freshman offensive lineman on the LSU roster, wearing No. 51. He comes from Miami and played his high school football at Southridge Senior High School before signing with the Tigers.

athletes.name: Ja'Quan Sprinkle
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sprinkle is a redshirt junior offensive lineman from Orangeburg, South Carolina, where he played at Orangeburg-Wilkinson High School. He joined LSU after beginning his college career at North Carolina Central. The Tigers list him at 6-4 and 297 pounds, and he wears No. 52 on the offensive line.

athletes.name: Hayes Fuqua
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fuqua is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman for LSU wearing No. 53. He is from West Monroe, Louisiana, and played his high school football at West Monroe High School before joining the Tigers.

athletes.name: Ja'Mard Jones Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a sophomore offensive lineman from Metairie, Louisiana, who played his high school football at Archbishop Rummel. He came to LSU after a stop at Nicholls, keeping his entire college career inside his home state. The Tigers list him at 6-2 and 312 pounds, and he wears No. 54.

athletes.name: Aliou Bah
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 LSU roster valuation ~$692K)
athletes.blurb: Bah is a projected starting guard for LSU after transferring from Maryland for his fifth college season.

athletes.name: Lamar Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation ~$1M as the No. 1 overall prospect in the 2026 class; signing package not disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Brown is a true freshman defensive lineman who signed with LSU as the No. 1 overall prospect in the 2026 recruiting class out of University Lab in Baton Rouge. He chose the Tigers over Texas A&M, Texas and Miami.

athletes.name: Jake Ibieta
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ibieta is a redshirt junior linebacker on the LSU roster, wearing No. 56. He is from Metairie, Louisiana, and played his high school football at Country Day before continuing his career in Baton Rouge.

athletes.name: JaKolby Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a junior offensive lineman from Many, Louisiana, and a Many High School product. He took the junior college route to LSU, playing at Copiah-Lincoln Community College before signing with the Tigers. He is listed at 6-5 and 298 pounds and wears No. 57 on the offensive line.

athletes.name: Braelin Moore
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 LSU roster valuation ~$787K)
athletes.blurb: Moore is LSU's returning starting center in his fifth college season after beginning his career at Virginia Tech. He has appeared in 36 career games and allowed just four sacks.

athletes.name: Sean Thompkins Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thompkins is a redshirt junior offensive tackle from Covington, Ga. who joined LSU in January 2026 after three seasons at Baylor. He played 10 games in 2025 and started the final five at left tackle, taking 463 snaps while drawing only one penalty. A three star recruit from Newton High School, he was a first team all region pick as a senior. He arrives with 11 career games and five starts.

athletes.name: Solomon Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a redshirt freshman offensive tackle from Jacksonville, Fla. who redshirted in 2025 after an injury in fall camp cost him most of the season. He signed as a consensus five star recruit, rated the No. 2 interior offensive line prospect nationally and the top overall player in Florida in his class. At Raines High School he also won the Florida 2A discus state title in 2023. He made the 2025 SEC academic honor roll.

athletes.name: Bo Bordelon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bo Bordelon won LSU's starting left guard job during spring practice in 2026 after four seasons as one of the Tigers' most versatile reserves. The fifth-year lineman from Raceland, Louisiana, has appeared in 42 games at left guard, left tackle, right tackle, right guard and even tight end, with one prior start in 2024. Football runs in the family: his father, Ben Bordelon, was an LSU team captain in 1996 who went on to the San Diego Chargers, and his brother Brett is also an offensive lineman on the roster.

athletes.name: Brett Bordelon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bordelon is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Raceland, La. who redshirted in 2025 and provides interior depth. A consensus three star recruit from Isidore Newman, he earned first team 2A all state honors in 2022 and 2023 and became only the second player in school history to start all four seasons. His father Ben started three years on LSU's line and was all SEC in 1996, and his brother Bo is also on the roster.

athletes.name: Darrin Strey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Strey is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Paw Paw, Michigan, where he played at Paw Paw High School. He arrived at LSU as a transfer from Kentucky. Listed at 6-7 and 314 pounds, he is among the tallest linemen on the Tigers roster, and he wears No. 69.

athletes.name: Devin Harper
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Devin Harper returned home to Louisiana in January 2026, transferring to LSU after one season at Ole Miss. The sophomore from Shreveport starred at Calvary Baptist, where he was rated the No. 3 player in Louisiana and the No. 7 interior offensive lineman nationally in the 2025 class. He originally committed to LSU before flipping to Ole Miss late in 2024, then appeared in six games as a true freshman for the Rebels in 2025. His ability to play guard or tackle gives him a chance to compete for early snaps up front.

athletes.name: Brysten Martinez
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Martinez is a freshman offensive lineman for LSU who wears No. 71. He comes from Gonzales, Louisiana, and played his high school football at East Ascension High School before joining the Tigers.

athletes.name: Adrian Lamb
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lamb is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Beaufort, South Carolina, where he played at Beaufort High School. He reached Baton Rouge by way of the junior college route, spending time at Georgia Military College before joining the Tigers. LSU lists him at 6-5 and 290 pounds, and he wears No. 73.

athletes.name: Braden Augustus
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Augustus is a redshirt junior offensive lineman on the LSU roster, wearing No. 74. He grew up in Baton Rouge and played his high school football at The Dunham School before continuing his career at home.

athletes.name: Weston Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 LSU roster valuation ~$902K)
athletes.blurb: Davis is LSU's returning starting right tackle and a former five-star recruit in the 2024 class. He withdrew from the transfer portal after the 2025 season to stay in Baton Rouge.
