athletes.name: Tyree Adams
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas A&M roster valuation $1.20M; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Adams is Texas A&M's projected starting left tackle after transferring from LSU, where he started nine games at the position in 2025 and allowed one sack. The 6-foot-7 former four-star recruit has two years of eligibility left.

athletes.name: Robert Bourdon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bourdon is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Collierville, Tennessee who is in the mix at tackle for Texas A&M in 2026, with post-spring projections pairing him alongside LSU transfer Tyree Adams. Listed at 6-6 and 312 pounds, he is viewed as versatile enough to play either tackle spot as the Aggies replace four starters.

athletes.name: Sam Roseborough
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sam Roseborough is a freshman offensive lineman from Clearwater, Florida, listed by Texas A&M at 6-3 and 303 pounds. He wears No. 64 and came to the Aggies directly out of high school.

athletes.name: Tyler White
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: White is a redshirt junior punter from Southlake, Texas who returns as the Aggies' starter after starting all 13 games in 2025. He averaged 44.26 yards on 50 punts that season, dropped 19 inside the 20 and had 16 punts of 50 or more yards, including a season long of 63 against Auburn. He was a Ray Guy Award semifinalist and an SEC All-Freshman selection in 2024. A consensus three-star recruit out of Southlake Carroll, he has a twin brother, Jared, on the roster.

athletes.name: Wilkin Formby
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas A&M roster valuation $1.44M, second-highest on the roster; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Formby is Texas A&M's projected starting right tackle after transferring from Alabama, where he started 14 games in 2025. The 6-foot-7, 324-pound lineman arrived in January 2026 with two seasons of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Hunter McKinney
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hunter McKinney is a freshman offensive lineman from Montgomery, Texas, listed at 6-3 and 319 pounds on the Texas A&M roster. He wears No. 55 and joined the Aggies as a high school signee.

athletes.name: Ashton Funk
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Funk is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Katy, Texas listed at 6-6 and 319 pounds. He is part of a returning group described as the depth behind a Texas A&M line that replaced four starters with proven SEC transfers, and he enters 2026 competing for interior and swing tackle rotation snaps.

athletes.name: Joshua Moses
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Joshua Moses is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Houston who wears No. 72 for Texas A&M. The Aggies list him at 6-2 and 334 pounds, a compact and heavy interior build.

athletes.name: Tyler Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Dickinson, Texas and, at 6-4 and 350 pounds, the heaviest player listed on the Texas A&M roster. He preserved eligibility during the 2025 season and is among the returning linemen projected as depth behind the transfer starters the Aggies brought in for 2026.

athletes.name: Zaden Krempin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zaden Krempin is a freshman offensive lineman from Prosper, Texas, north of Dallas. Texas A&M lists him at 6-4 and 298 pounds, and he wears No. 74 in his first season with the Aggies.

athletes.name: Nelson McGuire
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nelson McGuire is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Dallas, listed at 6-4 and 332 pounds on the Texas A&M roster. He wears No. 56 and has been with the Aggies since arriving from high school.

athletes.name: Jayden Warren
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jayden Warren is a freshman wide receiver from Rosharon, Texas, southwest of Houston. Texas A&M lists him at 6-1 and 214 pounds, heavier than most of the Aggie receivers, and he wears No. 81.

athletes.name: Chace Sims
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chace Sims is a redshirt freshman defensive tackle from Richmond, Texas, who wears No. 59 for the Aggies. Texas A&M lists him at 6-3 and 293 pounds. He joined the program out of high school.

athletes.name: Mark Nabou Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nabou is a graduate offensive lineman from Lynnwood, Washington who returns as Texas A&M's starting center in 2026. He has played 28 career games with 26 starts and 1,618 snaps at center and guard, including 12 starts and 797 snaps in 2025 for a line that ranked third nationally in tackles for loss allowed. He started 12 games at left guard in 2023. Nabou was a three-star prospect at O'Dea High School and a 2022 Polynesian Bowl selection, and he graduated from Texas A&M in May 2026.

athletes.name: Marcus Garcia
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Marcus Garcia is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Denton, Texas, listed by Texas A&M at 6-3 and 307 pounds. He wears No. 62 and came to the Aggies as a high school signee.

athletes.name: Trovon Baugh
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Baugh is a graduate offensive lineman from Atlanta who transferred to Texas A&M in January 2026 and projects into the interior line rotation. He played three seasons at South Carolina from 2023 through 2025, appearing in 35 games with 19 starts and 1,460 snaps, mostly at guard. Pro Football Focus named him a Freshman All-American in 2023 and he made the Freshman All-SEC team that year. A four-star recruit out of Pace Academy, he was a two-time SEC Academic Honor Roll pick and graduated in May 2026.

athletes.name: Isendre "Papa" Ahfua
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ahfua is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Seattle who came to Texas A&M from O'Dea High School and wears No. 50. A four-star interior lineman, he was rated the top prospect in the state of Washington and played in both the All-American Bowl and the Polynesian Bowl. He made his college debut in 2024 against New Mexico State and is competing for guard snaps at 6-3 and 342 pounds.

athletes.name: Richie Anderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anderson, listed by Texas A&M as Richie Anderson III, is a redshirt junior tight end from Tualatin, Oregon who transferred in from Fresno State. He was the second tight end the Aggies added from the portal in this cycle, joining UTSA transfer Houston Thomas, and at 6-4 and 265 pounds he competes for snaps in a reshaped position group.

athletes.name: Colton Chmelar
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Colton Chmelar is a redshirt freshman kicker from College Station, Texas, meaning he plays for the Aggies in his own hometown. Texas A&M lists him at 6-0 and 190 pounds, and he wears No. 83.

athletes.name: Blake Ivy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ivy is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from League City, Texas listed at 6-3 and 324 pounds. He is grouped with Tyler Thomas and Ashton Funk as returning interior linemen providing depth on a Texas A&M front rebuilt around four transfer starters heading into the 2026 season.

athletes.name: Luke Braden
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Luke Braden is a redshirt sophomore tight end from Stratford, Texas, a small Panhandle town. The Texas A&M roster lists him at 6-4 and 238 pounds, and he wears No. 81 for the Aggies.

athletes.name: Will Hargett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Will Hargett is a redshirt freshman wide receiver from College Station, Texas, playing in his hometown. The Aggies list him at 5-9 and 167 pounds, the lightest listed receiver on the roster, wearing No. 83.

athletes.name: Houston Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a graduate tight end from College Station who transferred to Texas A&M in January 2026 after four seasons at UTSA. He played 42 games with 15 starts for the Roadrunners, catching 78 passes for 918 yards and five touchdowns, and earned third-team all-conference honors in 2025. His best game came against Tulsa in 2024, when he gained 132 receiving yards. A three-star prospect at College Station High School, he finished his prep career with 106 receptions for 1,540 yards and 13 touchdowns.

athletes.name: Ryan Burtin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ryan Burtin is a redshirt junior cornerback from Bryan, Texas, just up the road from campus. Texas A&M lists him at 5-7 and 170 pounds, the shortest listed player on the roster, and he wears No. 86.

athletes.name: Micah Riley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Riley is a redshirt senior tight end from Omaha, Nebraska and a team captain for Texas A&M in 2026, where he projects mainly as a blocking tight end. He has appeared in 42 career games with one start, catching three passes for 43 yards and two touchdowns, including a 32-yard score against Samford in 2023 and a three-yard touchdown against New Mexico in 2024. Riley spent three seasons at Auburn from 2022 through 2024 and was an all-state pick at Bellevue West High School.

athletes.name: Coen Echols
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas A&M roster valuation $817.3K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Echols is Texas A&M's projected starting left guard for 2026. The Katy, Texas, native came to College Station from LSU and is a redshirt sophomore with multiple seasons of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Kade Stewart
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kade Stewart is a redshirt freshman wide receiver from Temple, Texas, who wears No. 89 for the Aggies. Texas A&M lists him at 6-2 and 202 pounds. He joined the program out of high school.

athletes.name: Lamont Rogers
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rogers is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Mesquite, Texas who has been floated as a candidate to contend for the starting left tackle job at Texas A&M in 2026. Listed at 6-6 and 340 pounds, he was among the higher rated signees in his recruiting class and preserved eligibility during the 2025 season.

athletes.name: Asher Murray
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Asher Murray is a freshman kicker from Shreveport, Louisiana, one of the few Louisiana natives on the Aggie roster. Texas A&M lists him at 5-10 and 175 pounds, and he wears No. 90.

athletes.name: Jerome Myles
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Myles is a redshirt freshman wide receiver from Draper, Utah who signed with Texas A&M ranked among the top 200 prospects nationally in his class. Listed at 6-2 and 230 pounds, he is unusually large for the position and returns in 2026 after a season-ending knee injury, competing for snaps in a deep Aggie receiver room.

athletes.name: CJ Mims
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas A&M roster valuation $1.08M; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Mims is Texas A&M's projected starting nose tackle after transferring from North Carolina, where he made 42 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss and two sacks over 12 games in 2025. He was a nine-game starter for the Tar Heels.

athletes.name: DJ Sanders
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sanders is a redshirt freshman defensive tackle from Bellville, Texas who saw limited action as a true freshman in 2025. Listed at 6-3 and 316 pounds, he is expected to factor into the Texas A&M interior rotation in 2026 alongside the veteran linemen the Aggies added through the transfer portal.

athletes.name: Nathan Mabon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nathan Mabon is a redshirt freshman defensive tackle from Arlington, Texas, listed at 6-0 and 298 pounds on the Texas A&M roster. He wears No. 93 and is a compact interior presence for the Aggies.

athletes.name: Jonah Wilson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jonah Wilson is a redshirt junior wide receiver from Houston listed with the Texas A&M program at No. 82. Details beyond his position, class and hometown are not confirmed on the current official Aggie roster page.

athletes.name: Chase Burton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chase Burton is a redshirt junior wide receiver from Dallas who wears No. 85 for Texas A&M. The official roster lists him at 5-10 and 187 pounds, and he has been with the Aggies since high school.

athletes.name: Angelo McCullom
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McCullom is a junior defensive tackle from Pickerington, Ohio who transferred to Texas A&M from Illinois. He has logged close to 300 career defensive snaps with 21 tackles and two sacks, and at 6-2 and 317 pounds he adds interior size to an Aggie line replacing NFL draft picks Tyler Onyedim and Albert Regis in 2026.

athletes.name: Waylon Peters
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Waylon Peters is a freshman punter from Montgomery, Texas, listed by Texas A&M at 6-4 and 214 pounds. He wears No. 96 and is one of three punters carried on the Aggie roster.

athletes.name: Jermaine Kinsler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jermaine Kinsler is a freshman defensive tackle from Ocala, Florida, and at 6-5 and 311 pounds he is among the largest first-year players on the Texas A&M roster. He wears No. 98 for the Aggies.

athletes.name: Alex Abbott
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alex Abbott is a redshirt sophomore punter from Montgomery, Texas, who came to Texas A&M from Houston, staying in state for his transfer. The Aggies list him at 6-0 and 185 pounds wearing No. 95. He is one of two Montgomery natives punting for Texas A&M, alongside freshman Waylon Peters, and the lightest listed specialist in that group.

athletes.name: Jesse Chukwu
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jesse Chukwu is a redshirt senior defensive end from Cypress, Texas, who wears No. 98 for the Aggies. Texas A&M lists him at 6-0 and 225 pounds, the lightest listed edge player on the roster.

athletes.name: Landon Rink
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rink is a sophomore defensive tackle from Cypress, Texas who appeared in 10 games as a true freshman in 2025 and blocked a kick against Samford. Listed at 6-2 and 295 pounds, he has been discussed as a candidate to win a starting job in 2026, though Texas A&M also added several interior linemen from the transfer portal.

athletes.name: DeDe Murray
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: DeDe Murray is a redshirt freshman running back from Bellville, Texas, who came to Texas A&M from Arkansas State, returning to his home state after starting his college career in the Sun Belt. The Aggies list him at 5-10 and 219 pounds wearing No. 23, a compact build shared with fellow Aggie back Tiger Riden Jr.

athletes.name: Evan Jacobson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Evan Jacobson is a freshman tight end from Waukee, Iowa, and the only Iowa native listed on the Texas A&M roster. The Aggies list him at 6-5 and 241 pounds, and he wears No. 86.

athletes.name: Sylvester Smith-Reed
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith-Reed is a senior safety from Munford, Alabama who returns to Auburn's secondary after starting six games in 2025. He played all 12 games that year and recorded 28 tackles, 2.0 tackles for loss, three pass breakups and a fumble recovery, with a career-high six stops against Ball State. He also made six starts in 2024, when he returned an interception 33 yards against Arkansas. A four-star recruit out of Munford High School, he was a two-time ASWA first-team all-state selection.

athletes.name: Jonathan Echols
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Echols is a sophomore tight end from Franklin, Georgia who transferred to Auburn after two seasons at South Florida and projects into the tight end rotation in 2026. He played 12 games with seven starts for the Bulls, totaling 10 receptions for 168 yards and four touchdowns, with nine catches, 109 yards and three scores coming in 2025 after he redshirted in 2024. A four-star recruit, Echols attended IMG Academy and earlier played quarterback, receiver and defensive end at Heard County High School.

athletes.name: Champ Anthony
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A senior safety from Fort Worth, Texas, Anthony came to Auburn from Tyler Junior College in Texas after posting 14 tackles and an interception in six games there. He played high school ball at Trinity Leadership and has been on the Auburn roster since 2023, appearing in every game as a junior college newcomer that first fall. Teammates voted him a captain in the offseason, and he offers the staff snaps at safety, cornerback and nickel in 2026.

athletes.name: AnQuon Fegans
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation ~$500K)
athletes.blurb: Fegans is a projected starting safety for Auburn entering his sophomore season after signing as a four-star recruit from Thompson High School. He recorded six tackles in the 2026 A-Day spring game.

athletes.name: Locklan Hewlett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hewlett is a sophomore quarterback from St. Augustine, Fla., who prepped at St. Augustine High School and signed with South Florida in 2025. He played in two games as a true freshman for the Bulls, completing seven of 12 passes and throwing his first career touchdown in the season opener against Boise State. He followed head coach Alex Golesh to Auburn as the staff's first transfer addition.

athletes.name: Saint Farrior
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Farrior is a junior defensive lineman from Durham, North Carolina, and a Hillside High School product. He spent two seasons at Hampton before transferring to Appalachian State, where he recorded 15 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss and half a sack in 2025. Auburn signed him out of the portal as one of several interior additions, and at 6-3 and 340 pounds he projects as a run-stopping presence in the defensive tackle rotation.

athletes.name: Jeremiah Koger
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation ~$731K)
athletes.blurb: Koger is a projected starting wide receiver for Auburn after a breakout freshman season at USF, where he caught 38 passes for 597 yards and eight touchdowns in 2025. He followed head coach Alex Golesh to the Plains.

athletes.name: Malik Autry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Autry is a sophomore defensive lineman from Opelika, Alabama, the town next door to campus. A four-star prospect and the first commitment of Auburn's 2025 class, he was rated among the top prospects in the state after finishing his Opelika High career with 152 tackles, 26 tackles for loss and 19 sacks. He played nine games as a true freshman and finished with eight tackles, with a three-tackle outing against Mercer.

athletes.name: Rayshawn Pleasant
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation ~$605K)
athletes.blurb: Pleasant is a projected starting cornerback and Auburn's primary kick returner, ranking second in the SEC with 412 kick return yards in 2025. He transferred to Auburn from Tulane and was named to Thorpe and Walter Camp watch lists.

athletes.name: Jourdin Crawford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Crawford is a sophomore defensive lineman from Birmingham, Alabama, who arrived as a four-star signee in the 2025 class after ranking among the top defensive line prospects nationally. At Parker High School he was a two-year all-state pick with 155 career tackles and 38 sacks, won a Class 6A state title and was named Class 6A lineman of the year. He appeared in nine games as a freshman and recorded two tackles.

athletes.name: Chas Nimrod
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation ~$880K)
athletes.blurb: Nimrod is a projected starting wide receiver for Auburn after catching 23 passes for 466 yards and three touchdowns in seven injury-shortened games at USF in 2025. He spent his first three college seasons at Tennessee.

athletes.name: Cody Sigler
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation ~$650K)
athletes.blurb: Sigler is Auburn's projected starting defensive tackle after transferring from Arkansas State, where he started 11 games in 2025 and recorded 35 tackles, 7.0 tackles for loss and 5.0 sacks.

athletes.name: Eric Winters
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation ~$540K)
athletes.blurb: Winters is a projected starting safety for Auburn after a productive true freshman season in 2025 in which he made 24 solo tackles. He signed with the Tigers as a four-star recruit out of Enterprise, Alabama.

athletes.name: Charley Schwinger
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Schwinger is a junior kicker for Auburn out of Houston, Texas. He came to the Tigers from Second Baptist School and is listed at 6-foot-2 on the official roster, where he wears No. 93.

athletes.name: Bryce Cain
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cain is a redshirt sophomore receiver at Auburn who wears No. 6 and is listed at 5-10 and 165 pounds. He played all 12 games in 2025, catching a career high three passes for 28 yards against Alabama and returning a kickoff 31 yards, and he made the SEC Academic Honor Roll. A four-star signee from Baker High in Mobile, he caught 43 passes for 948 yards and 16 touchdowns as a senior.

athletes.name: De'marcus Riddick
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Riddick is a junior linebacker from Clanton, Alabama, and a Chilton County High School product who arrived as a five-star recruit after flipping his commitment from Georgia. He earned SEC all-freshman honors in 2024 with 27 tackles, 5.0 tackles for loss and 3.0 sacks. In 2025 he played 10 games with four starts, adding 13 tackles, a sack and two pass breakups. He returns as an experienced piece of the linebacker rotation.

athletes.name: Nate Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a senior edge rusher from Gaffney, South Carolina, who signed with Auburn out of the transfer portal with one year of eligibility left. A three-star recruit in the 2023 class out of Gaffney High School, he began at Appalachian State and put up 77 tackles, 12 tackles for loss and 10 sacks over two seasons there. He then spent 2025 at Missouri, playing nine games and recording six tackles.

athletes.name: Kaleb Harris
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation ~$594K)
athletes.blurb: Harris is Auburn's returning starting safety after playing all 12 games with 10 starts in 2025, when he ranked third on the team with 50 tackles and added 2.0 tackles for loss, a sack and an interception.

athletes.name: Jake White
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: White is a sophomore wide receiver for Auburn and a hometown product, listed from Auburn, Ala. He played his high school football at Lee-Scott Academy and wears No. 89 for the Tigers.

athletes.name: Christian Neptune
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Neptune is a sophomore wide receiver from Cantonment, Florida, and a Tate Senior High School product. He spent his freshman season at South Florida under Alex Golesh, catching 38 passes for 335 yards and a touchdown, then followed Golesh to Auburn as one of more than a dozen former Bulls to make the move. He enters 2026 with experience in the same offensive system and competes for rotational receiver snaps.

athletes.name: DJ Broughton Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Broughton is a freshman tight end from Mobile, Ala., who played at Mary G. Montgomery. He caught 32 passes for 497 yards and seven touchdowns as a senior and finished his prep career with 46 receptions for 751 yards and 11 scores. He was selected for the Alabama-Mississippi All-Star Classic and was the first commitment of the Alex Golesh era at Auburn.

athletes.name: Elijah Melendez
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Melendez is a sophomore linebacker from Kissimmee, Florida who is positioned for a larger role in 2026 after a productive true freshman season. He appeared in all 12 games with one start in 2025 and recorded 29 tackles, 3.0 tackles for loss and a sack, and he tied for the team lead with two interceptions, one of which he returned 41 yards for a touchdown against Mercer. He earned SEC All-Freshman honors and On3 Midseason True Freshman All-America recognition after prepping at Osceola High School.

athletes.name: Antonio Melendez
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Melendez is a junior linebacker from Kissimmee, Fla., who came to Auburn from Osceola High School, where he also played baseball. He is the older brother of Auburn linebacker Elijah Melendez, a four-star signee out of the same program, and the two now share the Tigers' linebacker room. He wears No. 45.

athletes.name: Hunter Herring
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Herring is a senior tight end from West Monroe, La., who prepped at Ouachita Christian. He spent the previous three seasons at Louisiana-Monroe, working as a backup quarterback and special teams contributor while completing 22 of 42 passes for 251 yards and two touchdowns and adding 241 rushing yards. Auburn signed him out of the portal to play tight end.

athletes.name: Ryan Ghea
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ghea is a sophomore tight end from Milton, Ga., who was a team captain and first-team all-region selection for Milton High School's Class 7A state champions, finishing with 53 catches for 651 yards and four touchdowns. He played in five games for Auburn in 2025 and recorded receptions against Ball State and Georgia.

athletes.name: DeShawn Spencer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Spencer is a freshman wide receiver from Mobile, Alabama, who signed with Auburn in the 2026 class as a three-star recruit out of Saraland High School. As a senior he broke the Saraland single-season receiving record previously held by Ryan Williams, finishing with 1,709 yards. Listed at 5-11 and 175 pounds, he arrives as a true freshman working for playing time behind a receiver group stocked with transfers.

athletes.name: Xavier Newsom
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Newsom is a sophomore tight end from Detroit, Michigan, who played high school football at Martin Luther King Jr. He spent his freshman season at Howard, appearing in seven games and catching one pass for a nine-yard touchdown, then transferred to Auburn with three years of eligibility. At Auburn he reunites with former Howard head coach Larry Scott, now the Tigers' tight ends coach, in a room that added several veteran transfers.

athletes.name: Walter Mathis Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mathis is a sophomore defensive lineman from Savannah, Georgia, and a Calvary Day School product who was an Auburn target in the 2025 recruiting cycle before signing with LSU. He appeared in 12 games as a true freshman for the Tigers of Baton Rouge and finished with nine tackles, then entered the portal and signed with Auburn with three years of eligibility remaining. He joins a defensive line rebuilt largely through transfers.

athletes.name: Arlis Boardingham
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Boardingham is a senior tight end from Van Nuys, California, who played at Birmingham High School and signed with Florida in the 2022 class. He caught 26 passes for 289 yards and four touchdowns for the Gators in 2023 and added 18 catches for 128 yards and two scores in 2024, then spent 2025 at Bowling Green. He joins an Auburn tight end room that also added transfers from North Carolina, Howard and South Florida.

athletes.name: Tristan Ti'a
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ti'a is a sophomore quarterback from Livermore, California, and an Amador Valley High School product who was rated the No. 21 quarterback in the 2025 class by 247Sports. He signed with Oregon State, redshirted and appeared in three games late in the season, completing 37 of 53 passes for 385 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions. He transferred to Auburn with four years of eligibility and joins a quarterback room fronted by Byrum Brown.

athletes.name: Erick Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a sophomore wide receiver for Auburn out of Selma, Ala. He came to the Tigers from Southside High School and is listed at 6-foot-4 on the official roster, wearing No. 81.

athletes.name: Keshaun Singleton
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation ~$974K)
athletes.blurb: Singleton is a projected starting wide receiver for Auburn after transferring from USF, where he led the Bulls with 50 catches for 877 yards and eight touchdowns in 2025. He has 76 career receptions for 1,285 yards and 11 scores.

athletes.name: Will Upton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Upton is a junior wide receiver for Auburn out of Jackson, Miss. He played his high school football at Jackson Preparatory School and wears No. 80 for the Tigers.

athletes.name: Darrion Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a sophomore defensive lineman from Annapolis, Maryland, who played at St. Frances Academy in Baltimore. A three-star recruit listed at 6-2 and 263 pounds, he had been committed to Tennessee since the summer before flipping to Auburn on signing day in the 2025 class. He is one of three St. Frances defenders Auburn signed that cycle, joining linebacker Bryce Deas and cornerback Blake Woodby in the defensive rotation.

athletes.name: Jo Simmons
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation ~$1.01M)
athletes.blurb: Simmons is Auburn's projected starting right tackle after transferring from James Madison, where he started every game at left tackle for a College Football Playoff team in 2025 and earned honorable mention All-Sun Belt honors.

athletes.name: Brady Marchese
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Marchese is a freshman wide receiver from Acworth, Ga., who starred at Cartersville High School. He caught 41 passes for 981 yards and 15 touchdowns as a senior after posting 44 receptions for 1,051 yards and 11 scores as a junior. He signed with Michigan in December, was granted a release from his letter of intent, and then committed to Auburn.

athletes.name: Mason Mathis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mathis is a freshman offensive lineman from Pace, Fla., who played at Pace High School and has experience at several spots along the line. He originally committed to South Florida and flipped to Auburn during the signing period to follow head coach Alex Golesh. He also placed among the top 10 in Florida in powerlifting as an 11th grader.

athletes.name: Blake Woodby
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Woodby is a sophomore cornerback from Upper Marlboro, Maryland, and a St. Frances Academy product in Baltimore. He signed with Auburn in the 2025 class as a four-star prospect after drawing offers from Oregon, Maryland, Penn State, Notre Dame, LSU, Alabama and Georgia. He is part of a St. Frances pipeline that also brought linebacker Bryce Deas and defensive lineman Darrion Smith to Auburn, and he competes for rotation snaps at corner in 2026.

athletes.name: Wilson Zierer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zierer is a freshman offensive lineman from Munich, Germany, who played at Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School in Georgia. He signed with Auburn in the 2026 class as a four-star offensive tackle ranked inside the top 350 nationally. His older brother, Kilian Zierer, previously played offensive tackle at Auburn. Listed at 6-6 and 315 pounds, he arrives as a developmental tackle behind an offensive line reshaped by transfer additions.

athletes.name: Jack Leyrer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Leyrer is a senior offensive lineman from Dallas, Texas, and a Highland Park High School product who was a three-star recruit. He spent his career at Stanford, redshirting in 2021, starting three games in each of the next two seasons and then appearing in all 12 games with 10 starts in 2024. He has taken snaps at both left tackle and left guard, and he signed with Auburn with one year of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Kory Pettigrew
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pettigrew is a sophomore wide receiver from Kathleen, Ga., who helped Perry High School win a Georgia Class 4A state title in 2023 and caught 73 passes for 787 yards and five touchdowns as a senior. He played four games at South Florida in 2025 and redshirted, finishing with three receptions, then followed head coach Alex Golesh to Auburn.

athletes.name: Bear McWhorter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McWhorter is a freshman offensive lineman from Kingston, Ga., who played at Cass High School, earning all-region honors as a senior and a spot in the Under Armour All-America Game. He signed with Michigan during the early period, was granted a release, and then committed to Auburn, where he joins former Cass teammate Kail Ellis.

athletes.name: Shamar Arnoux
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Arnoux is a sophomore cornerback from Ft. Lauderdale, Florida, who starred at Carrollton High School in Georgia. A three-star recruit whose long recruitment included a commitment to Auburn before he signed with Florida State, he played 11 games with four starts as a true freshman for the Seminoles and recorded 27 tackles and a pass deflection. He entered the portal and signed with Auburn with three years of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Hudson Kaak
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kaak is a senior punter from Seymour, Australia who returns as Auburn's starter in 2026. He handled all 12 games in 2025, averaging 42.0 yards on 49 punts for 2,060 yards, a mark that ranked eighth in the SEC. He forced 27 fair catches, dropped 11 punts inside the 20 and allowed just one touchback, with a long of 55 against Kentucky. Kaak transferred from Oklahoma State, where he averaged 43.13 yards on 30 punts in 2024, and he trained at ProKick Australia.

athletes.name: Tavian Branch
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Branch is a freshman defensive lineman from Taylor, Pa., who was a four-year starter and team captain at Riverside High School. He earned all-state recognition twice and recorded 61 tackles, 27 tackles for loss and 11.5 sacks as a senior while also blocking three field goals. He chose Auburn over Penn State, Ole Miss and Virginia Tech.

athletes.name: Brian Williams Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a freshman wide receiver from Orlando, Florida, who played at The First Academy. He signed with Auburn in the 2026 class as a three-star recruit after flipping his commitment from Alabama in early December. Listed at 6-4 and 210 pounds, he brings unusual size to the position and arrives as a true freshman working behind a receiver group heavily reinforced through the transfer portal.

athletes.name: Jacobe' Ward
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ward is a sophomore offensive lineman from Savannah, Georgia, who signed with Auburn out of Benedictine Military School. A three-time all-state selection who helped the Cadets win Class 4A state titles as a freshman and sophomore, he was picked for the U.S. Army Bowl and also lettered in wrestling and track and field. Ward saw limited action as a freshman in 2025, appearing against Ball State and Mercer.

athletes.name: Da'Shawn Womack
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation ~$1.08M)
athletes.blurb: Womack is Auburn's projected starting Buck edge rusher after transferring from Ole Miss, where he logged 27 tackles, 4.5 tackles for loss and 2.0 sacks across 15 games in 2025. A former five-star recruit, he began his career at LSU.

athletes.name: John Colvin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Colvin is a junior quarterback for Auburn out of Birmingham, Ala. He played his high school football at Mountain Brook and wears No. 16 for the Tigers on the official roster.

athletes.name: Cole Best
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Best is a senior offensive lineman from Winter Park, Florida who transferred to Auburn from South Florida and projects to compete at center in 2026. He appeared in 39 games with 23 starts for the Bulls at center and left guard, and he started all 13 games in 2025 for an offense that ranked third nationally in total yards per game. That season he earned third-team all-conference honors. Best attended Trinity Prep, where he played both sides of the line as a senior.

athletes.name: Bryce Deas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Deas is a sophomore linebacker from Prince George's County, Maryland, who played at St. Frances Academy in Baltimore. He signed with Auburn in the 2025 class as a three-star prospect rated the No. 27 linebacker nationally and the No. 12 recruit in Maryland, having been recruited as a safety before adding weight. He is one of three St. Frances defenders in that class and is listed at 6-1 and 225 pounds.

athletes.name: Tai Buster
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Buster is a sophomore offensive lineman at Auburn, listed at 6-3 and 319 pounds in No. 71. He played in two games as a freshman in 2025, seeing his first college action against Ball State and later appearing against Mercer. A four-year starting tackle at A.L. Brown High School in Kannapolis, North Carolina, he was a two-time all-state pick, a Shrine Bowl of the Carolinas selection and rated the No. 11 prospect in the state by ESPN and Rivals.

athletes.name: Xavier Atkins
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation ~$1.0M)
athletes.blurb: Atkins is Auburn's returning starting inside linebacker and a 2025 All-American who led the SEC with 17 tackles for loss and paced the Tigers with 9.0 sacks. He announced his return for 2026 rather than leave via the portal or draft.

athletes.name: Parker Pritchett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pritchett is a freshman offensive lineman listed from Fort Mitchell, Ala., who played at Carver High School in Columbus, Ga. He committed to Auburn at the program's Big Cat Weekend in April 2025 and held that pledge through signing day, choosing the Tigers over Georgia, Florida and Mississippi State. He is listed at 6-foot-5 and 315 pounds.

athletes.name: Byrum Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation $3.0M; separate reporting cited an On3 NIL valuation near $1.6M)
athletes.blurb: Brown is Auburn's projected starting quarterback after following head coach Alex Golesh from USF, where he passed for 3,158 yards and 28 touchdowns and rushed for 1,008 yards and 14 scores in 2025. He led all FBS quarterbacks with 42 total touchdowns last season.

athletes.name: Jacob Strand
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He spent his career at Oregon State and appeared in six games in 2025, starting all of them at left tackle. He signed with Auburn in January as a redshirt senior with one year of eligibility left and was one of five transfer additions to the Tigers' offensive line, joining linemen from South Florida, James Madison and Michigan State.

athletes.name: J.J. Faulk
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Faulk is a sophomore edge rusher from Highland Home, Alabama, who signed with Auburn in the 2025 class as a four-star prospect ranked among the top 125 players nationally, choosing the Tigers over Alabama, Clemson, Florida and Georgia. He was a team captain and Class 2A state lineman of the year at Highland Home, where his older brother Keldric also played. He appeared in three games as a freshman and recorded four tackles.

athletes.name: Stanton Ramil
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

A four-star recruit, Ramil prepped at Thompson High School in Alabaster, Alabama, where ESPN rated him the state's top offensive tackle and he was a two-time first-team all-state selection.

athletes.name: Sam Turner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He caught 61 passes for 1,100 yards and 17 touchdowns as a senior after a junior season of 56 receptions for 903 yards and six scores. He was committed to Georgia Tech before flipping to Auburn in October 2024.

athletes.name: Rhys Brush
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He was committed to South Florida before flipping to Auburn in December to follow head coach Alex Golesh. He is also regarded as a baseball pitching prospect.

athletes.name: Benton Cantey

athletes.name: Jacoby Mathews
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation ~$152K)
athletes.blurb: Mathews is a veteran safety in Auburn's secondary rotation who transferred in from Texas A&M as a former five-star recruit. He intercepted a pass in the 2026 A-Day spring game.

athletes.name: John Henry Flatt
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He is listed at 6-foot-4 and 315 pounds.

athletes.name: Gavin Jenkins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He began his career at South Florida under Alex Golesh and signed with Auburn out of the transfer portal alongside former Bulls teammates Jonathan Echols and Nykahi Davenport. Listed at 6-2 and 190 pounds, he is one of several defensive backs Auburn added for 2026 and brings familiarity with the staff to the cornerback rotation.

athletes.name: Cole Skinner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He appeared in 28 games with eight starts for the Bulls, including 12 games and four starts at right guard in 2025, and he also scored two rushing touchdowns as a short-yardage fullback. A three-star recruit, Skinner earned First Team All-Shore honors at Point Pleasant Boro, which won a sectional title in 2021.

athletes.name: Tae Meadows
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Meadows is a senior running back from Roanoke, Ala., who signed out of Handley High School as a three-star recruit and rushed for 264 yards while earning MVP honors in the 2020 AHSAA Class 4A state championship game. He led Troy in rushing with 695 yards and six touchdowns in 2025 before transferring to Auburn.

athletes.name: Alvin Henderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Henderson is an Auburn running back and former top-rated national recruit from Elba, Alabama, who rushed for a state-record 3,620 yards as a high school senior. He appeared in just one game as a true freshman in 2025 and announced his return for 2026.

athletes.name: Andre Jordan Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation ~$633K)
athletes.blurb: Jordan is a projected starting cornerback for Auburn after transferring from UCLA, where he played in 2025 following an earlier stint at Oregon State. Beat writers credited his spring for easing Auburn's biggest secondary concern.

athletes.name: Jeremiah Cobb
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Auburn roster valuation ~$650K)
athletes.blurb: Cobb is Auburn's returning starting running back and a 2025 third-team All-SEC selection who ran for 969 yards on 175 carries, sixth-most in the SEC. He is the only 2025 Auburn offensive starter projected to hold his job in 2026.

athletes.name: Fred Gaskin III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gaskin is a junior safety from Ocala, Florida, who played at Vanguard High School. He had a breakout 2025 season at South Florida with 53 tackles, including 28 solo stops, two interceptions, two pass breakups, a sack and a forced fumble. He then followed head coach Alex Golesh to Auburn out of the transfer portal. At 5-10 and 202 pounds he arrives as one of the more productive defensive backs in Auburn's portal class.

athletes.name: Nykahi Davenport
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davenport is a sophomore running back from Roswell, Ga., who set Roswell High School single-season records with 1,904 rushing yards and 23 rushing touchdowns. He redshirted at South Florida in 2024, then ran for 612 yards and seven touchdowns in 2025 before following head coach Alex Golesh to Auburn.

athletes.name: Kenneth McManus IV
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He appeared in 12 games for Akron as a true freshman in 2025 and started six of them at left guard, then transferred to Auburn in January with three years of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Shadarius Toodle
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Toodle is a freshman linebacker from Mobile, Ala., who signed with Auburn as a four-star prospect out of Cottage Hill Christian Academy. He was named Alabama's Class 3A Lineman of the Year in 2025 and earned ASWA first-team all-state honors, finishing his prep career with 492 tackles, 12 sacks and eight interceptions. His older brother Shadrick also plays for the Tigers.

athletes.name: Cole Gamble
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Christian Burnette
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Burnette is a junior running back for Auburn out of Mobile, Ala. He came to the Tigers from Faith Academy and wears No. 26 on the official roster.

athletes.name: Deryc Plazz
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Plazz is a sophomore offensive lineman from Jacksonville, Florida who transferred to Auburn after two seasons at Miami. He saw action in five games across those years, including four in 2025 as the Hurricanes reached the national championship game, and he played left tackle and special teams as a redshirt freshman in 2024. A consensus three-star recruit out of Mandarin High School, he was ranked No. 709 overall in the 247Sports Composite and the No. 101 player in Florida.

athletes.name: Wayne Henry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Henry is a freshman safety from Baltimore who played at St. Frances Academy. He committed to Auburn in August 2024 and held that pledge through signing day, joining a group of St. Frances products already on the roster that includes Bryce Deas and Blake Woodby. Auburn recruited him to play both safety and nickel back.

athletes.name: William Grier McDuffie
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McDuffie is a sophomore linebacker for Auburn out of Birmingham, Ala. He played his high school football at Mountain Brook and wears No. 52 for the Tigers on the official roster.

athletes.name: Devin Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a sophomore cornerback for Auburn out of Dacula, Ga. He came to the Tigers from Buford High School, is listed at 5-foot-9 and wears No. 27 on the official roster.

athletes.name: Shadrick Toodle Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Toodle is a junior safety from Mobile, Ala., who prepped at Cottage Hill Christian Academy and then played at Mississippi Gulf Coast Community College, where he recorded 26 tackles, an interception and five pass breakups and earned first-team All-MACCC South recognition. He signed with Auburn alongside his younger brother Shadarius, a linebacker in the same signing class.

athletes.name: Omar Mabson II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mabson is a sophomore running back from Auburn, Alabama, who stayed home after starring at Auburn High School. As a freshman in 2025 he appeared in 10 games, carrying 16 times for 71 yards with a touchdown against Missouri, and he added two catches for 25 yards. He was a first team Class 7A all-state pick and set a school record with 29 rushing touchdowns as a junior.

athletes.name: Jaquez Wilkes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilkes is a freshman edge rusher from Wadley, Alabama, who played at Wadley High School. He signed with Auburn in the 2026 class as a four-star recruit ranked around No. 115 nationally, among the top linebacker prospects in his cycle and one of the highest rated players in the state. Some programs recruited him as an edge rusher while Auburn evaluated him as a linebacker, and at 6-4 and 245 pounds he arrives with room to grow.

athletes.name: Michael Matthews-Canty
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He signed with Auburn as its first portal linebacker addition of the cycle with two years remaining.

athletes.name: Bryson Washington
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

Over 26 games with 23 starts he totaled 1,861 rushing yards, 18 touchdowns and nine 100-yard games while averaging 5.49 yards per carry. He arrives at Auburn with two years of eligibility.

athletes.name: Kail Ellis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He played eight games as a freshman in 2025 and started at center against Arkansas and Kentucky, helping Auburn to 230 rushing yards against the Razorbacks. He was named to the SEC All-Freshman Team.

athletes.name: Joe Phillips
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

Washington High School and posted 130 tackles, 28 tackles for loss, seven sacks and five forced fumbles as a senior. He enrolled at Auburn early and made his debut as a true freshman in 2024 against Alabama A&M.

athletes.name: Cade Carlson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Kamari Todd
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

Auburn signed him in January as the seventh defensive back and fifth cornerback of its portal class, and he is the only one of that group making the jump from the FCS level.

athletes.name: Dallas Walker IV
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Travis Wakefield

athletes.name: Will Myers

athletes.name: Hunter Ousley

athletes.name: Connor Gibbs

athletes.name: Coleman Granberry

He chose Auburn over Missouri and Kentucky.

athletes.name: Chris Murray
