athletes.name: Jordan Ochoa
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jordan Ochoa is a sophomore defensive lineman from Castle Rock, Colorado, who played at Castle View High School. Nebraska lists him at 6-foot-4 and 255 pounds on its roster, and he wears jersey No. 94.

athletes.name: Gabe Moore
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gabe Moore is a junior defensive lineman who transferred to Nebraska after beginning his college career at Mississippi State. He stayed close to home for high school, playing at Louisville High School in his hometown of Louisville, Mississippi. The Huskers roster lists him at 6-foot-5 and 300 pounds, and he wears jersey No. 95.

athletes.name: Williams Nwaneri
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL Valuation reported in the ~$489K-$1M range for the former consensus five-star; no deal terms publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Nwaneri is Nebraska's projected starting edge rusher and a former consensus five-star recruit who transferred in from Missouri. He posted 3.0 sacks and 28 pressures across 13 games in his first extended action in 2025.

athletes.name: Mac Markway
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mac Markway is a junior defensive lineman who came to Nebraska after starting his college career at LSU. A St. Louis, Missouri, native, he played his high school football at De Smet Jesuit. The Nebraska roster lists him at 6-foot-4 and 265 pounds and assigns him jersey No. 97.

athletes.name: Conor Connealy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Conor Connealy is a junior defensive lineman from Elkhorn, Nebraska, who played at Mount Michael Benedictine. The Nebraska roster lists him at 6-foot-4 and 265 pounds, and he wears jersey No. 98.

athletes.name: Dylan Parrott
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dylan Parrott is a senior defensive lineman from Eldridge, Iowa, who played his high school football at North Scott. The Nebraska roster lists him at 6-foot-5 and 320 pounds, and he wears jersey No. 99.

athletes.name: Hayden Ainsworth
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hayden Ainsworth is a freshman offensive lineman from Biloxi, Mississippi, who played at Biloxi High School. Nebraska lists him at 6-foot-5 and 310 pounds on its roster, and he wears jersey No. 50.

athletes.name: Jase Reynolds
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jase Reynolds is a freshman linebacker from Elkhorn, Nebraska, who played his high school football at Elkhorn North. The Nebraska roster lists him at 6-foot-2 and 220 pounds, and he wears jersey No. 52.

athletes.name: Dylan Berymon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Berymon is a freshman defensive lineman from Monroe, Louisiana, who signed with Nebraska in February 2026 out of Ouachita Parish, choosing the Huskers over Kentucky after decommitting from Texas. Ranked No. 217 in the ESPN 300, he was among the last uncommitted prospects in his class. He recorded 49 tackles and four sacks as a senior and adds size to the interior defensive line.

athletes.name: Maurice Purify II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Maurice Purify II is a freshman wide receiver from Omaha, Nebraska, who played at Omaha Westside. The Nebraska roster lists him at 6-foot-4 and 190 pounds, and he wears jersey No. 89.

athletes.name: Kyson Gana
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kyson Gana is a freshman long snapper from Hickman, Nebraska, who played his high school football at Norris. The Nebraska roster lists him at 6-foot-1 and 180 pounds, and he wears jersey No. 50.

athletes.name: Jamari Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jamari Brown is a freshman wide receiver from Chicago, Illinois, who played at Mount Carmel High School. The Nebraska roster lists him at 5-foot-11 and 180 pounds, and he wears jersey No. 85.

athletes.name: Anthony Jones Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A senior edge rusher out of Las Vegas, Nev., Jones is competing for a spot in the Cornhuskers' two-deep this fall after stops at Liberty and Michigan State.

athletes.name: Donovan Starr
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Starr is a sophomore cornerback from Bloomington, Ill., who arrived at Clemson from Auburn after signing out of Ravenwood High School as a four-star prospect in the 2025 class. He appeared in nine games as a true freshman for Auburn, working on special teams and as a defensive reserve without recording statistics. He joined the Tigers with three years of eligibility remaining and is one of several portal defensive backs competing for rotation snaps in 2026.

athletes.name: Naeem Burroughs
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Naeem Burroughs is a true freshman wide receiver who enrolled at Clemson in January 2026 after a decorated career at Jacksonville's Bolles School. A consensus four-star recruit, he was rated the No. 9 wide receiver nationally in the 247Sports Composite and chose the Tigers over Alabama and Ohio State. He took first-team snaps during spring practice and is pushing veteran Tyler Brown for the slot receiver job, giving him a path to an immediate role in Clemson's 2026 receiving rotation.

athletes.name: Branden Strozier
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Strozier is a senior cornerback from Lovejoy, Ga., who signed with Clemson out of Saint Francis High School as a four-star prospect in the 2023 class. He took on his largest role in 2025, appearing in 12 games with one start and finishing with 21 tackles, one for loss, and five pass breakups across roughly 340 defensive snaps. He enters 2026 positioned as a primary backup at cornerback.

athletes.name: T.J. Moore
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$907K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Moore is Clemson's leading returning receiver, starting all 13 games in 2025 and catching 52 passes for 837 yards and four touchdowns.

athletes.name: Ashton Hampton
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$764K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Hampton is Clemson's returning starting cornerback and started all 13 games in 2025, recording 47 tackles, an interception and 11 pass breakups.

athletes.name: Tait Reynolds
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reynolds is a freshman quarterback on Clemson's roster. He comes from Queen Creek, Arizona, and played his high school football at Queen Creek High School. The Tigers list him at 6-2 and 215 pounds.

athletes.name: Elliot Washington II
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$690K; portal package not disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Washington is Clemson's projected starting boundary cornerback in 2026 after transferring in from Penn State.

athletes.name: Tristan Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Tristan Smith is a fifth-year wide receiver from LaGrange, Georgia, who joined Clemson from Southeast Missouri State ahead of the 2025 season. At SEMO in 2024 he caught 76 passes for 934 yards and six touchdowns, ranking among the FCS leaders in receptions. In his first Clemson season, the 6-foot-5 target added 24 catches for 239 yards and a touchdown over 13 games with four starts, and he returns in 2026 as one of the veterans in the Tigers' receiver room.

athletes.name: Brock Bradley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bradley is a freshman quarterback from Birmingham, Alabama, who played at Spain Park High School before joining Clemson. He is listed at 6-0 and 190 pounds on the Tigers' roster and wears No. 5.

athletes.name: Ronan Hanafin
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Ronan Hanafin, a senior from Burlington, Massachusetts, was Clemson's first signee from that state since Christian Wilkins and has converted from wide receiver to safety. The move paid off in 2025, when he was credited with 72 tackles, third most on the team, plus four pass breakups, two forced fumbles and an interception across 13 games with five starts. He enters 2026 with 38 career games played and is expected to anchor a rebuilt Clemson secondary.

athletes.name: Jerome Carter III
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$686K; portal package not disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Carter is Clemson's projected starting strong safety after transferring from Old Dominion, where he posted 76 tackles and six interceptions in 2025 and earned second-team All-Sun Belt honors.

athletes.name: Tyler Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Brown is a senior wide receiver from Greenville, S.C., who stayed home after playing at Greenville Senior High School. He was named a Freshman All-American by ESPN in 2023, when he led Clemson in both receptions and receiving yards. Through the 2025 season he had 79 career catches for 752 yards and four touchdowns, including 22 receptions for 191 yards in 2025, a year in which his snap counts declined over the final month.

athletes.name: Jeremiah Alexander
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$522K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Alexander is a projected starting linebacker for Clemson and a graduate transfer from Alabama who made 33 tackles in 13 games with three starts in 2025.

athletes.name: Logan Brooking
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Brooking is a sophomore tight end from Bluffton, S.C., who signed with Clemson as a four-star prospect in the 2025 class out of Savannah Christian Prep. He is the son of former NFL linebacker Keith Brooking, who coached him in high school. Brooking finished his prep career with 84 receptions for 1,206 yards and six touchdowns across 47 games. He enrolled in January 2025 and appeared in five games as a freshman while redshirting.

athletes.name: Corian Gipson
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$573K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Gipson is Clemson's projected starting nickelback after taking over the Tigers' nickel role late in 2025, when he made 14 tackles and three pass breakups in 12 games with three starts.

athletes.name: Gideon Davidson
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$466K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Davidson is Clemson's projected starting running back after rushing for 260 yards on 60 carries and adding 11 catches as a true freshman in 2025.

athletes.name: Colson Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is a senior quarterback from North Augusta, South Carolina, who took an unusual route to Clemson. He played at North Augusta High School, then spent time at Georgia Tech before moving on to Anderson University, a Division II program in his home state. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-3 and 205 pounds.

athletes.name: Drew Woodaz
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Woodaz is a junior linebacker from Tampa, Fla., who came to Clemson from Jesuit High School, where he recorded 216 tackles, 14 pass breakups and four interceptions over 46 games. He is the younger brother of Wade Woodaz, a Clemson linebacker from 2022 through 2025. Woodaz enters 2026 with 13 career appearances, most of them on special teams, having played 15 defensive snaps with one tackle.

athletes.name: Juju Preston
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Preston is a sophomore wide receiver from Alexandria, Va., who finished his prep career at Hayfield Secondary as the all-time receiving touchdown leader in Virginia high school history with 67 scores on 185 catches for 3,700 yards. He redshirted in 2025, playing seven offensive snaps across two appearances and debuting against Furman with a four-yard reception and a 10-yard punt return. Clemson coaches noted steady improvement from him late in the season.

athletes.name: Misun Kelley
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Kelley is a senior from Central, S.C., who came to Clemson from nearby D.W. Daniel High School as a multi-sport athlete. He contributed at wide receiver in 2023 and 2024 before moving to defensive back full time in 2025, when he was credited with 17 tackles and a pass breakup across 266 defensive snaps in 12 games with five starts. He worked at the Tiger position in Tom Allen's defense and is listed at both defensive back and receiver.

athletes.name: Olsen Patt-Henry
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Olsen Patt-Henry is Clemson's returning starter at tight end, a senior from Naples, Florida, who started 10 of the 11 games he played in 2025 and caught 16 passes for 126 yards. He enters 2026 with 28 career receptions for 289 yards and three touchdowns over 31 games, and he figures to see an expanded role as new offensive coordinator Chad Morris leans more heavily on the tight end position.

athletes.name: Polo Anderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anderson is a freshman safety from Spartanburg, South Carolina, who played at Dorman High School. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-2 and 190 pounds, and he wears No. 11.

athletes.name: Bryant Wesco Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$766K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Wesco is a starting outside receiver for Clemson who posted 31 catches for 537 yards and six touchdowns in an injury-shortened seven-game 2025 season.

athletes.name: Shavar Young Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Young is a freshman cornerback from Knoxville, Tennessee. He played his high school football at the Webb School of Knoxville and is listed at 5-11 and 190 pounds on Clemson's roster.

athletes.name: Connor Salmin
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Salmin is a freshman wide receiver from Round Hill, Va., who spent three seasons at Woodgrove before finishing at the Bullis School in Maryland. As a senior he caught 57 passes for 1,013 yards and 14 touchdowns, earning IAC Offensive Player of the Year honors. He is also a decorated sprinter with four state track titles and three All-America selections. Salmin signed in December 2025 and enrolled at Clemson in January 2026.

athletes.name: Will Heldt
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation $1.30M, second on the roster; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Heldt is Clemson's returning starting defensive end and led the Tigers with 15.5 tackles for loss and 7.5 sacks in 2025, his first season after transferring from Purdue.

athletes.name: London Merritt
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Merritt is a sophomore edge rusher from Atlanta, Ga., who transferred to Clemson from Colorado in January 2026 after signing out of IMG Academy as a four-star prospect. As a freshman in 2025 he played all 12 games with one start and posted 23 tackles, eight tackles for loss and a sack, earning freshman all-America recognition from Pro Football Focus. He was among Clemson's first portal additions in a defense-focused offseason.

athletes.name: Trent Pearman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pearman is a fifth-year graduate quarterback and walk-on from Clemson, South Carolina. At D.W. Daniel High School he passed for 3,769 yards and 45 touchdowns as a senior, added 306 rushing yards and eight scores, and led the Lions to a 14-0 season and a state championship. He is a two-time South Carolina Gatorade Player of the Year and the son of longtime Clemson staffer Danny Pearman.

athletes.name: Chris Denson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Denson is a sophomore quarterback from Plant City, Fla., who signed with Clemson in December 2024 out of Plant City High School. He redshirted in 2025, playing 11 offensive snaps across two games while completing all four of his passes for 22 yards and a touchdown and rushing seven times for 108 yards and a score. Clemson plans to expand his role in 2026 by giving him snaps at running back and wide receiver in addition to quarterback.

athletes.name: Jahiem Lawson
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation $1.17M, third on the roster; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Lawson is projected to start at defensive end for Clemson after recording 24 tackles, 6.5 tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks as a reserve in 2025. He is the younger brother of former Clemson All-American Shaq Lawson.

athletes.name: Chris Johnson Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Chris Johnson Jr. is a senior running back who transferred to Clemson from SMU, where he ran for 479 yards and four touchdowns in 2025 and scored against the Tigers in SMU's win that season. A Fort Lauderdale native who signed with Miami as a three-star recruit in 2023, he brings verified sprinter speed, having won Florida 3A state titles in the 100 and 200 meters in high school. He was the first offensive player added in Clemson's 2026 portal class and should figure prominently in the backfield rotation.

athletes.name: Myles Oliver
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Oliver is a fifth-year graduate cornerback from Villa Rica, Georgia, who played at Douglas County High School. Clemson's roster lists him at 5-11 and 185 pounds, and he wears No. 16.

athletes.name: Ari Watford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Watford is a sophomore edge rusher from Norfolk, Va., and was the highest-ranked signee in Clemson's 2025 class, listed No. 31 in the ESPN 300 out of Maury High School. As a senior he recorded 52 tackles, 22 for loss and eight sacks while helping Maury to a 15-0 record and a state title. He enrolled in January 2025 and redshirted, recording one tackle in seven defensive snaps in his lone appearance.

athletes.name: Christopher Vizzina
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation $1.75M, highest on the roster; On3 player NIL pages not publicly accessible; no deal figure disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Vizzina is Clemson's starting quarterback in 2026 after backing up NFL-bound Cade Klubnik, completing 45 of 71 passes for 406 yards with four touchdowns and one interception across five appearances in 2025. He carries the highest NIL valuation on the Tigers' roster.

athletes.name: Kylon Griffin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Griffin is a fifth-year graduate safety from Montgomery, Ala., who signed with Clemson in the 2022 class out of Montgomery Catholic Preparatory. He enters 2026 credited with 46 tackles, three interceptions, three pass breakups, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery across roughly 599 snaps in 34 career games with four starts. In high school he was a three-time all-conference defensive back and an all-state selection as a senior.

athletes.name: Tayveon Wilson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilson is a freshman tight end from Huntington, West Virginia, and a product of Huntington High School. He is listed at 6-1 and 210 pounds on Clemson's roster and wears No. 18.

athletes.name: Brayden Reilly
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reilly is a freshman linebacker from Cincinnati, Ohio, who played at St. Xavier High School. Clemson lists him at 6-3 and 220 pounds on its roster, where he wears No. 19.

athletes.name: Gordon Sellars III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sellars is a freshman wide receiver from Charlotte, N.C., who committed to Clemson in April 2025 out of Providence Day School, choosing the Tigers over South Carolina, Georgia and Michigan. As a senior he caught 59 passes for 917 yards and 15 touchdowns on a 13-0 state championship team, finishing his prep career with 133 receptions for 2,419 yards and 29 scores. ESPN ranked him among the top 25 receivers nationally in his class.

athletes.name: Clark Sanderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sanderson is a junior wide receiver from Birmingham, Ala., who joined Clemson as a preferred walk-on out of Mountain Brook High School, choosing that path over a scholarship offer from Samford. As a senior he caught 44 passes for 936 yards and six touchdowns and earned all-South Metro honors, after posting 53 receptions for 955 yards and nine scores as a junior, when he was an all-state selection by the Alabama Sports Writers Association.

athletes.name: Jakarrion Kenan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kenan is a sophomore safety from Bennettsville, South Carolina, and a Marlboro County High School product. He is listed at 6-1 and 190 pounds on Clemson's roster and wears No. 20.

athletes.name: Jarvis Green
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Green is a senior running back from Irmo, South Carolina, who played at Dutch Fork High School. Clemson's roster lists him at 5-9 and 205 pounds, and he wears No. 21.

athletes.name: Kobe McCloud
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Kobe McCloud is a graduate linebacker from Tampa who signed with Clemson in the 2022 class and enters 2026 projected to start alongside Sammy Brown. He has been credited with 45 career tackles, including 6.0 for loss, with a sack, a forced fumble and five pass breakups over 28 games, and he posted Clemson's highest Pro Football Focus grade among linebackers in 2025. McCloud completed a communication degree in December 2025 and is the veteran presence in a thinned linebacker room.

athletes.name: Cole Turner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Turner is a fifth-year graduate wide receiver from Vestavia Hills, Ala., who signed with Clemson in the 2022 class. His brother Nolan was an All-America safety for the Tigers in 2020 and played 65 career games at Clemson, and his late father, Kevin, was a teammate of Dabo Swinney at Alabama before eight NFL seasons. In high school Turner caught 42 passes for 581 yards and seven touchdowns and totaled 1,160 all-purpose yards as a senior.

athletes.name: Corey Myrick
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$684K; portal package not disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Myrick is a projected starting safety for Clemson who committed in January 2026 out of Southern Miss, where he recorded 91 tackles and two interceptions in 2025.

athletes.name: C.J. Wesley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wesley is a fifth-year edge rusher from West Orange, N.J., who transferred to Clemson from Howard in January 2026 after signing out of Saint Peter's Prep. He recorded 33 tackles, 5.5 tackles for loss, five sacks and two forced fumbles in 2025, finishing his Howard career with 47 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss and seven sacks over 26 games. He was the second portal defensive end Clemson added, joining London Merritt.

athletes.name: Peyton Streko
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Streko is a senior running back from Cumming, Georgia, and a West Forsyth High School product. He is listed at 5-10 and 195 pounds on the Clemson roster, where he wears No. 23.

athletes.name: David Eziomume
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Eziomume is a junior running back from Acworth, Ga., who signed with Clemson out of North Cobb High School, committing on his 17th birthday in March 2023. He enters 2026 having carried 26 times for 133 yards across 14 career games. In 2025 he appeared in nine games, rushing 16 times for 71 yards and catching three passes for 10 yards in 64 offensive snaps, and remains in a crowded backfield rotation.

athletes.name: Logan Anderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anderson is a sophomore linebacker from Fyffe, Alabama. He starred as a running back at Fyffe High School, finishing with 631 career carries for 7,021 yards and 110 touchdowns, and Rivals ranked him among the top 100 prospects nationally. He committed to Clemson in July 2024 over offers from Georgia, Arkansas, Georgia Tech, Washington and Ole Miss, then enrolled in January 2025.

athletes.name: Keil McGriff
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McGriff is a freshman wide receiver from Gainesville, Florida, who played at Buchholz High School. Clemson's roster lists him at 5-10 and 165 pounds, and he wears No. 25.

athletes.name: Marcell Gipson Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gipson is a freshman cornerback from Dallas who played at South Oak Cliff High School. He was a three-time first-team all-district pick and earned first-team all-state honors as both a defensive back and a kick returner in 2024, a season in which he posted 56 tackles, four pass breakups and three interceptions. His father played cornerback at Wyoming.

athletes.name: C.J. Kubah-Taylor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kubah-Taylor is a junior linebacker from Frederick, Md., who signed with Clemson in December 2023 out of Our Lady of Good Counsel. As a senior he was a first-team All-WCAC selection with 87 tackles, eight for loss, six sacks, three interceptions and eight pass breakups on a team that won the conference title. He played in seven games on special teams in 2025 and has seen limited defensive snaps across his first two seasons.

athletes.name: Jay Haynes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Haynes is a senior running back from Roanoke, Alabama, who arrived at Clemson with little recruiting attention. At Handley High School he ran for 2,669 yards and 37 touchdowns over his final two seasons, averaging better than 10 yards a carry. He once rushed for 476 yards in a single game, one of the largest single-game totals in Alabama high school history.

athletes.name: Jack Purkerson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Purkerson is a fifth-year wide receiver and walk-on from Clemson, South Carolina, who lettered at D.W. Daniel High School. He first worked for the program as a student coaching assistant, then walked on through tryouts in the springs of 2024 and 2025 before making his game debut in November 2025. He is listed at 5-7 and 160 pounds.

athletes.name: Noah Dixon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dixon is a junior safety from LaGrange, Ga., who signed with Clemson in the 2024 class out of Troup County High School, where he was Region 4A Athlete of the Year as a senior. He redshirted in 2024 and appeared in five games in 2025, recording two tackles in 17 defensive snaps plus a special teams tackle against Furman. He remains a depth option in a safety group that returns experience.

athletes.name: Champ Thompson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thompson is a junior defensive tackle from Gainesville, Ga., who signed with Clemson in the 2024 class after posting 36 tackles, 7.5 sacks and four pass breakups as a high school senior. He appeared in eight games in 2025 with one start, recording four tackles, one for loss, and his first career sack at Boston College. He worked with the first-team defensive line alongside Markus Strong during spring practice in 2026.

athletes.name: Chase Byrd
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Byrd is a junior wide receiver from Greenville, South Carolina, and a Greer High School product. Clemson's roster lists him at 5-10 and 185 pounds, and he wears No. 29.

athletes.name: Kylen Webb
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Webb is a senior graduate safety from Tampa, Florida, who played at Sumner High School. He is listed at 6-0 and 205 pounds on Clemson's roster, where he wears No. 30.

athletes.name: Joe Wilkinson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilkinson is a junior safety from Rome, Georgia, and a Rome High School product. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-1 and 200 pounds, and he wears No. 31 for the Tigers.

athletes.name: Michael Foster
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Foster is a freshman edge rusher from Charlotte who played two seasons at Indian Land High School in South Carolina. As a senior in 2025 he recorded 140 tackles, 12 sacks, two forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries and four pass breakups, and he was named Region 3-AAAAA Defensive Player of the Year. He committed to Clemson in December 2025.

athletes.name: Caden Story
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Story is a fifth-year graduate defensive lineman from Lanett, Ala., who played for his father, Clifford Story, at Lanett High School before signing with Clemson as a four-star prospect in 2022. He appeared in five games in 2025, recording five tackles and a half sack in 71 defensive snaps, including four tackles against Penn State. He briefly entered the transfer portal in January 2026 before withdrawing and returning to Clemson.

athletes.name: Armon Mason
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mason is a sixth-year graduate edge rusher from Richmond Hill, Georgia, where he played at Richmond Hill High School. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-3 and 240 pounds, and he wears No. 34.

athletes.name: Max Wilson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilson is a junior running back from Bogart, Georgia, and a North Oconee High School product. He is listed at 5-10 and 200 pounds on Clemson's roster, where he wears No. 34.

athletes.name: Tyler Conner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Conner is a senior defensive back from Suwanee, Georgia, who played at Peachtree Ridge High School. Clemson's roster lists him at 5-11 and 185 pounds, and he wears No. 35.

athletes.name: Davion Joyner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Joyner is a fifth-year cornerback from North Charleston, South Carolina. He played at Fort Dorchester High School and spent time at Limestone before joining Clemson, where he is listed at 6-1 and 180 pounds.

athletes.name: Dominic Staten
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Staten is a sophomore linebacker from Florence, South Carolina, and a Wilson High School product. Clemson's roster lists him at 5-9 and 215 pounds, and he wears No. 38 for the Tigers.

athletes.name: Robert Gunn III
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Robert Gunn III is a graduate kicker from Seminole, Florida, who has spent four seasons as one of the nation's most reliable kickoff specialists, recording touchbacks on 193 of 236 career kickoffs. He earned Freshman All-America honors in that role in 2023 and handled kickoffs in all 13 games in 2025, averaging 64.1 yards with 57 touchbacks on 71 kicks. In 2026 he is competing with Jonathan Weitz for Clemson's placekicking job while continuing his kickoff duties.

athletes.name: J.D. Bonamy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bonamy is a freshman linebacker from Birmingham, Alabama, who played at Spain Park High School, the same program that produced Clemson quarterback Brock Bradley. He is listed at 5-9 and 200 pounds on the roster.

athletes.name: Brodey Conn
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Conn is a fifth-year graduate long snapper from Clemson, South Carolina, who played at nearby D.W. Daniel High School. He is listed at 6-1 and 210 pounds on the Tigers' roster and wears No. 40.

athletes.name: Connor McFadden
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McFadden is a freshman edge rusher from Fort Mill, South Carolina, and a Catawba Ridge High School product. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-3 and 240 pounds, and he wears No. 41.

athletes.name: Hevin Brown-Shuler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown-Shuler is a junior defensive lineman from Atlanta who played at Pace Academy. He is listed at 6-3 and 305 pounds on Clemson's roster, one of the heavier interior linemen on the team, and wears No. 42.

athletes.name: Billy Wilkes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilkes is a junior linebacker from Charlotte, North Carolina, who played at Providence High School. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-1 and 215 pounds, and he wears No. 43 for the Tigers.

athletes.name: J.R. Buckner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Buckner is a junior long snapper from Auburn, Alabama. He played at Auburn High School and spent time at Auburn University before transferring to Clemson, where he is listed at 5-11 and 260 pounds.

athletes.name: Jack Wolf
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wolf is a sophomore tight end from Gurnee, Illinois, and a Warren Township High School product. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-4 and 210 pounds, and he wears No. 44.

athletes.name: Kourtney Kelly
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kelly is a junior defensive lineman from Columbus, Georgia. He played at G.W. Carver High School and spent time at West Georgia before joining Clemson, which lists him at 6-3 and 290 pounds.

athletes.name: Vic Burley
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$807K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Burley is a projected starting defensive tackle for Clemson who appeared in all 13 games with one start in 2025, finishing with 15 tackles. He was the highest-rated recruit in Clemson's 2023 signing class.

athletes.name: Jackson Reach
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Jackson Reach is a freshman long snapper from Hermosa Beach, California, believed to be the first player Clemson has ever signed out of high school specifically at that position. Ranked the nation's No. 2 long snapper by Rubio Long Snapping, he starred at Mira Costa High School, where he was also a productive linebacker with 301 career tackles and 18 sacks. He enrolled in January 2026 as a pre-business major and is in line to take over Clemson's snapping duties.

athletes.name: Sammy Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation $1.0M; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Brown is Clemson's starting middle linebacker and led the team with 107 tackles, 13.5 tackles for loss and 5.0 sacks in 2025. A former consensus five-star recruit, he was a Freshman All-American in 2024.

athletes.name: Charlie Reed
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reed is a junior placekicker and punter from Austin, Texas, who handled field goals, punts and kickoffs at Vandegrift High School and served as a team captain there. He came to the football program after time as a goalkeeper with Clemson soccer, and his older brother, Ian Reed, is an offensive lineman on the same Tigers roster.

athletes.name: Darien Mayo
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mayo is a junior edge rusher from York, Pa., who signed with Clemson out of Our Lady of Good Counsel as a four-star prospect ranked among the top 150 players nationally and, by Rivals, the tenth-best defensive end in his class. He enrolled early for the summer semester and appeared in seven games in 2025, recording two tackles in 62 defensive snaps with appearances against Troy, Furman and Penn State.

athletes.name: Collin Sadler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sadler is a fifth-year graduate offensive lineman from Inman, S.C., who came to Clemson from Greenville Senior High School. He was a regular starter in 2025, appearing in 10 games and starting nine of them for roughly 608 offensive snaps, with seven starts at left guard and two at left tackle. His experience at both spots makes him one of the more versatile veterans in the Tigers' 2026 offensive line room.

athletes.name: Fletcher Cothran
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cothran is a fifth-year graduate linebacker from Anderson, S.C., who joined Clemson as a walk-on in the summer of 2022 after playing at nearby T.L. Hanna High School, where he was also a baseball player. He enters 2026 credited with 12 tackles, a forced fumble and a half sack across 36 defensive snaps in 30 career games, with most of his contributions coming on special teams.

athletes.name: Gavin Blanchard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Blanchard is a sophomore offensive lineman from Tampa, Fla., who flipped his commitment from UCF to Clemson and signed in December 2024 out of Wiregrass Ranch High School. He was rated among the top interior linemen in the 2025 class and, as a senior, graded out at 88 percent with 30 pancake blocks while helping his team to an 11-2 record. He enrolled early in January 2025 and is developing in the interior line rotation.

athletes.name: Elyjah Thurmon
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Elyjah Thurmon is a third-year offensive lineman from Rienzi, Mississippi, who signed with Clemson in 2024 as a consensus four-star recruit rated among the nation's top interior line prospects. The 6-foot-4, 325-pound guard missed most of the 2025 season after a widely reported season-ending shoulder injury but returned healthy for 2026 and, despite his youth, is one of the most tenured members of a rebuilt line, taking on a leadership role in a young position group.

athletes.name: Joseph Roberto II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Roberto is a junior linebacker from Helena, Alabama, who played at Helena High School. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-2 and 225 pounds, and he wears No. 53 for the Tigers.

athletes.name: Ian Reed
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reed is a senior offensive lineman from Austin, Texas, who signed with Clemson as a four-star prospect out of Vandegrift High School, where he earned second-team MaxPreps All-America honors on a team that reached the Texas 6A title game. He appeared in three games in 2025, playing 26 offensive snaps with debuts at North Carolina and Boston College and additional work against Furman. He is competing for a larger rotation role in 2026.

athletes.name: Kam Cody
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cody is a freshman defensive lineman from Savannah, Georgia, who played at Benedictine Military School. He finished his prep career with 248 tackles, 37 tackles for loss and 22.5 sacks, and as a senior he was named Region 1-4A Defensive Player of the Year after posting 82 tackles, 13 for loss and 5.5 sacks. He committed to Clemson in March 2026.

athletes.name: Harris Sewell
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$637K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Sewell is Clemson's projected starting center in 2026 after starting nine games along the interior offensive line in 2025.

athletes.name: Makhi Williams Lee
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams Lee is a sophomore defensive lineman from Atlanta who played at Lakeside High School. He is listed at 6-2 and 300 pounds on Clemson's roster, where he wears No. 55.

athletes.name: Andy Burburija
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Burburija is a junior defensive tackle from Crystal Lake, Ill., who arrived at Clemson in January 2026 from Iowa Western Community College. He was a first-team junior college All-American after recording 18.5 tackles for loss and 11 sacks. He originally signed with Kansas State and was briefly committed to Nebraska before flipping to Clemson, becoming the Tigers' third portal defensive tackle addition alongside Markus Strong and Kourtney Kelly.

athletes.name: Dietrick Pennington
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pennington is a sixth-year graduate offensive lineman from Memphis, Tenn., who signed with Clemson in the 2021 class out of Evangelical Christian School. He announced in December 2025 that he would return for a sixth season. He appeared in all 12 games in 2025 and has been used regularly in short-yardage packages, though he has yet to make a career start. At 6-5 and 355 pounds he is the heaviest lineman on the roster.

athletes.name: Danny Stein
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stein is a sophomore offensive lineman from Bellaire, Texas, who joined Clemson in 2026 after a season at Furman. He played guard and center at Lamar High School in Houston, where he was part of three district championship teams, including a junior-year squad that went 12-1 and reached the third round of the state playoffs, and he served as a senior captain.

athletes.name: Bryce Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a senior offensive lineman from Six Mile, South Carolina, who played at D.W. Daniel High School near campus. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-3 and 280 pounds, and he wears No. 62.

athletes.name: Easton Ware
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$829K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Ware is a Clemson offensive tackle projected to start at right tackle in 2026 after developing behind the Tigers' veteran line as a freshman.

athletes.name: Grant Wise
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wise is a freshman offensive lineman from Pace, Florida, and a Pace High School product. He is listed at 6-4 and 300 pounds on Clemson's roster, where he wears No. 64.

athletes.name: Chapman Pendergrass
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pendergrass is a fifth-year graduate offensive lineman from Anderson, S.C., who joined Clemson as a walk-on in the summer of 2022 after lettering at T.L. Hanna High School. He enters 2026 with 36 career appearances and 73 offensive snaps. In 2025 he played 22 offensive snaps and started on Clemson's punt shield in all 13 games, making special teams his most consistent contribution.

athletes.name: Carlito Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a senior offensive lineman from Anderson, South Carolina, who played at Pendleton High School. At 6-8 and 275 pounds he is among the tallest linemen listed on Clemson's roster, and he wears No. 67.

athletes.name: Chance Barclay
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Barclay is a freshman offensive lineman from Minneola, Florida, who played at The First Academy. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-4 and 295 pounds, and he wears No. 70 for the Tigers.

athletes.name: Leo Delaney
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Delaney is a freshman offensive lineman from Charlotte, North Carolina, and a Providence Day School product. He is listed at 6-5 and 300 pounds on Clemson's roster, where he wears No. 71.

athletes.name: Adam Guthrie
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Guthrie is a freshman offensive lineman from Washington Court House, Ohio, who played at Miami Trace High School. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-6 and 285 pounds, and he wears No. 72.

athletes.name: Hayes Galloway
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Galloway is a senior offensive lineman from Concord, North Carolina. He played at Cannon School and spent time at North Carolina before transferring to Clemson, where he is listed at 6-4 and 310 pounds.

athletes.name: Brayden Jacobs
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$835K, highest among Clemson offensive linemen; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Jacobs is Clemson's projected starting left tackle after playing 10 games with four starts along the offensive line as a freshman in 2025.

athletes.name: Tucker Kattus
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kattus is a sophomore offensive lineman from Cincinnati, Ohio, who was a three-year starter at left tackle for St. Xavier High School. He was named his conference's offensive lineman of the year as both a junior and a senior and earned first-team all-state honors in 2024 while captaining a team that reached the state quarterfinals. He had been committed to Kentucky before flipping to Clemson in December 2024 and enrolled the following summer.

athletes.name: Mason Wade
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wade is a junior offensive lineman from Hamilton, Va., who flipped his commitment from Duke to Clemson and signed out of Loudoun Valley High School, where he was a four-year starter at left tackle, a two-time captain and a first-team 4A all-state selection. He redshirted in 2024 and was an ACC Honor Roll selection. In 2025 he appeared in three games for 22 offensive snaps, including 19 against Furman.

athletes.name: Ronan O'Connell
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Ronan O'Connell is a third-year offensive lineman from Franklin, Tennessee, who enrolled at Clemson in January 2024 after leading Page High School to three straight state championship game appearances. The 6-foot-5, 320-pound blocker made his first career start against Penn State in 2025, playing 66 snaps, and enters 2026 with 130 career offensive snaps over 15 games. He is competing for the starting right guard job and offers versatility at guard or tackle.

athletes.name: Carter Scruggs
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Scruggs is a freshman offensive lineman from Leesburg, Virginia, who played at Loudoun County High School. He is listed at 6-5 and 300 pounds on Clemson's roster, where he wears No. 78.

athletes.name: Braden Wilmes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilmes is a freshman offensive lineman from Lawrence, Kansas, who played at Lawrence Free State High School. At 6-8 and 300 pounds he is one of the tallest players listed on Clemson's roster.

athletes.name: Luke Stubbs
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stubbs is a fifth-year graduate wide receiver from Charlotte, North Carolina, who played at SouthLake Christian Academy. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-2 and 200 pounds, and he wears No. 80.

athletes.name: Nolan Hauser
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$123K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Hauser is Clemson's starting placekicker and made 17 of 21 field goals with a long of 50 yards in 2025, leading the team with 89 points.

athletes.name: Sam Earle
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Earle is a junior wide receiver from Clemson, South Carolina, who played at D.W. Daniel High School just down the road from campus. He is listed at 5-10 and 175 pounds on the Tigers' roster.

athletes.name: Cam Blivens
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Blivens is a freshman wide receiver from Nashville, Tennessee, and a Lipscomb Academy product. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-1 and 190 pounds, and he wears No. 83 for the Tigers.

athletes.name: Avery Wieting
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wieting is a junior wide receiver from Lincoln, Nebraska, who played at Wahoo High School. He is listed at 5-9 and 180 pounds on Clemson's roster, where he wears No. 84.

athletes.name: Charlie Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a senior graduate tight end from Columbia, South Carolina, who played at Ben Lippen School. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-4 and 245 pounds, and he wears No. 85.

athletes.name: Jaylen Brown-Wallace
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown-Wallace is a senior wide receiver from Central, South Carolina. He played at nearby D.W. Daniel High School and spent time at Wingate before joining Clemson, which lists him at 6-2 and 175 pounds.

athletes.name: Christian Bentancur
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$407K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Bentancur is Clemson's projected starting tight end after catching 20 passes for 215 yards and three touchdowns in 2025.

athletes.name: Clay Swinney
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Swinney is a fifth-year graduate wide receiver and walk-on from Clemson, South Carolina, who played at D.W. Daniel High School. He has appeared in 41 career games, largely on special teams as the holder on placekicks, a role his older brothers Will and Drew also filled. He is the son of Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney and a four-time ACC Honor Roll selection.

athletes.name: Grady Sherrill
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sherrill is a fifth-year graduate wide receiver from Greensboro, North Carolina, whose college path has run through three programs. He played at Page High School, then spent time at North Carolina and later South Dakota before joining Clemson. The Tigers list him at 5-10 and 185 pounds, and he wears No. 89.

athletes.name: Jack Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Jack Smith is Clemson's returning starting punter, a graduate from Saraland, Alabama, who enrolled in January 2022. He held the job for all 13 games in 2025, averaging 41.4 yards on 50 punts with 22 downed inside the 20-yard line against just two touchbacks. He enters 2026 with a 40.9-yard career average across 17 games and gives the Tigers an experienced, proven option at the position in his final season.

athletes.name: J.R. Hardrick
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hardrick is a freshman edge rusher from South Pittsburg, Tennessee, who played at South Pittsburg High School. Clemson's roster lists him at 6-5 and 240 pounds, and he wears No. 90.

athletes.name: Devarrick Woods
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Woods is a fifth-year graduate defensive tackle from Bossier City, La., who came to Clemson in May 2026 after playing at Hinds Community College and then Texas State. In his lone FBS season he recorded 16 tackles and a sack in nine games for the Bobcats. He chose Clemson over interest from Florida State, Florida, NC State and Colorado, and adds needed depth to a defensive tackle room rebuilt largely through the portal.

athletes.name: Amare Adams
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Clemson roster valuation ~$405K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Adams is a projected starting defensive tackle for Clemson who played 10 games with 10 tackles as a true freshman in 2025. He signed as a consensus top-100 national recruit out of South Florence High School.

athletes.name: Patrick Swygert
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Swygert is a senior graduate defensive lineman from Batesburg-Leesville, South Carolina, who played at Batesburg-Leesville High School. He is listed at 6-5 and 285 pounds on Clemson's roster, where he wears No. 97.

athletes.name: Markus Strong
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Strong is a senior defensive tackle from Raiford, Fla., who transferred to Clemson from Oklahoma in January 2026 after playing his high school football at Union County. He appeared in 10 games for the Sooners in 2025, recording eight tackles and a sack, and finished his Oklahoma career with 11 tackles and three sacks over three seasons. He worked with the first-team defensive line during Clemson's spring practices in 2026.

athletes.name: Quindarrius Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Quindarrius Jones is a senior defensive back from Meridian, Mississippi, who signed with Florida State out of Meridian High School as a three-star prospect in the 2023 class. Recruited as a safety, he now works at cornerback and was awarded the No. 0 jersey for 2026, a number previously worn by Earl Little Jr. Coaches have pointed to his skill set and 6-foot-2 length as reasons he could claim a starting role in a retooled Seminole secondary.

athletes.name: Duce Robinson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation reported ~$1.1M; The NIL Standard 2026 model ~$1.5M; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Robinson is Florida State's No. 1 outside receiver and became the Seminoles' first 1,000-yard receiver since 2019 with 56 catches for 1,081 yards and six touchdowns in 2025, his first season after transferring from USC. The 6-foot-6 senior returns as Florida State's highest-profile NIL asset in 2026.

athletes.name: Darryll Desir
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Darryll Desir is a sophomore defensive end from Miami who arrived at Florida State as a four-star edge rusher out of Norland High School. As a true freshman in 2025 he played 12 games with two starts, totaling 23 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss and a sack, including a career-high seven tackles against NC State. He and his twin brother Mandrell briefly entered the transfer portal before withdrawing, and both return as key pieces of the Seminoles' 2026 pass rush plans.

athletes.name: Malachi Marshall
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Marshall reached Florida State in the 2026 signing class after stops at Stony Brook and Iowa Western Community College. 247Sports ranked the South Pointe High School product the No. 47 junior college prospect nationally and the No. 2 junior college quarterback in the cycle. Listed at 6-2 and 168 pounds, the junior from Charlotte, North Carolina, wears No. 1 and enters fall camp behind veteran additions Ashton Daniels and Dean DeNobile.

athletes.name: Mandrell Desir
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 FSU roster model ~$908,143; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Desir is Florida State's projected starting defensive tackle as a sophomore after drawing national attention as a true freshman in 2025. He and twin brother Darryll came to FSU together from Miami Norland and both re-signed with the Seminoles in January 2026.

athletes.name: Samuel Singleton Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Samuel Singleton Jr. is a redshirt junior running back from Charleston, South Carolina, entering his fourth season at Florida State. He earned the team's Most Improved honor on offense for 2025, a year that included a 91-yard rushing game with a touchdown against Wake Forest and an 82-yard, one-score outing on just four carries against East Texas A&M. Having improved his production each season, he is positioned to be one of the top two backs in the Seminoles' 2026 rotation.

athletes.name: Dean DeNobile
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dean DeNobile is a fifth-year quarterback from Upper Saddle River, New Jersey, who transferred to Florida State from Lafayette. He started 35 straight games for the Leopards, passing for 6,956 yards and 53 touchdowns while adding 10 rushing scores. He was named Patriot League Player of the Week four times and served as a team captain twice. He attended Morris Catholic.

athletes.name: Charles Lester III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lester is a junior defensive back from Sarasota, Florida, who played at Riverview High School. He appeared in 10 games for Florida State in 2025 and finished with four tackles, three of them solo. Listed at 6-1 and 195 pounds and wearing No. 4, he returns as a rotational cornerback in a secondary that added transfers Karson Hobbs from Notre Dame and CJ Richard Jr. from Illinois State.

athletes.name: Daniel Lyons
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 FSU roster model ~$799,820; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Lyons is Florida State's projected starting nose tackle, a redshirt senior from Homestead who anchors the interior of Tony White's three-man front.

athletes.name: Quintrevion Wisner
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 FSU roster model ~$564,283; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Wisner is Florida State's projected starting running back after transferring from Texas, where he rushed for 1,064 yards in 2024. He goes by Tre and arrived in the 2026 portal cycle with two years of eligibility.

athletes.name: Ja’Bril Rawls
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 FSU roster model ~$601,822; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Rawls is a projected starting cornerback for Florida State in 2026, a Pensacola Catholic product who developed inside the program rather than arriving through the portal.

athletes.name: Desirrio Riles
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 FSU roster model ~$545,151; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Riles is Florida State's projected starting tight end, a senior who transferred from East Carolina. He tops a tight end room that also includes Landen Thomas and Chase Loftin.

athletes.name: Ashlynd Barker
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 FSU roster model ~$833,119; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Barker is Florida State's projected starting rover safety, a redshirt senior who reached Tallahassee by way of Iowa Western Community College. He is one of the more experienced pieces in Tony White's secondary.

athletes.name: Jasen Lopez
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jasen Lopez is a true freshman wide receiver from Hollywood, Florida, who signed with Florida State out of Chaminade-Madonna Prep as a four-star recruit, choosing the Seminoles over Miami, Florida and Georgia. A two-sport athlete also recruited for basketball, he caught 313 career high school passes for 5,211 yards and 59 touchdowns with four straight 1,000-yard seasons. Head coach Mike Norvell repeatedly singled him out during spring practice, and CBS Sports named him among the ACC's top true freshmen to watch in 2026.
