athletes.name: Kasen Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a first-year walk-on linebacker from Sioux City, Iowa, who played at Bishop Heelan Catholic. He is listed at 6-foot-2 and 230 pounds and wears No. 9 on the Iowa roster.

athletes.name: Luke Brewer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brewer is a first-year walk-on tight end from Norwalk, Iowa, who played at Norwalk High School. He is listed at 6-foot-4 and 239 pounds and wears No. 18 for the Iowa Hawkeyes.

athletes.name: Matty McLaughlin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McLaughlin is a first-year walk-on long snapper from St. Louis who played at De Smet Jesuit High School. He is listed at 6-foot-1 and 195 pounds and wears No. 54 on the Hawkeye roster.

athletes.name: Noah Daniel
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Daniel is a first-year walk-on defensive back from Fort Dodge, Iowa, who played at Fort Dodge Senior High. He is listed at 6-foot and 197 pounds and wears No. 29 for the Iowa Hawkeyes.

athletes.name: Tradon Bessinger
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bessinger is a first-year quarterback from Kaysville, Utah, who signed with Iowa in December 2025 after decommitting from Boise State. He was a three-year starter at Davis High School and was named Utah player of the year in 2025. He arrived in Iowa City as one of the highest rated quarterback prospects in the Hawkeye class.

athletes.name: Tyler Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is Iowa's projected starting free safety after transferring from James Madison, where he started all 14 games in 2025.

athletes.name: Trent Wilson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilson is a projected starting offensive lineman for the Iowa Hawkeyes out of Southlake, Texas, after transferring from James Madison.

athletes.name: Taariq Al-Uqdah
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Al-Uqdah arrived from Washington State in January 2025 and started the season opener against Colorado State with six tackles. He added a team high five tackles against UC Davis before his season ended after the win at Washington State. In 2024 he started all 12 regular season games for the Cougars with 76 tackles, three interceptions and five fumble recoveries. The fifth year linebacker from South Central Los Angeles played prep football at Inglewood.

athletes.name: Demond Williams Jr.
athletes.source: Reported ~$4M contract to return to Washington for 2026 (Forbes/Mercury News put the full rev-share + NIL package near $5M); The NIL Standard model $4.5M
athletes.blurb: Williams is Washington's returning starting quarterback and threw for more than 3,000 yards in 2025 while earning honorable mention All-Big Ten. He briefly entered the transfer portal in December 2025 before agreeing to return to the Huskies for 2026.

athletes.name: Rahshawn Clark
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clark is a Seattle native who redshirted in 2024 and then played all 12 games in 2025, starting five at nickel back for Washington. He recorded a 14 yard sack against Colorado State, forced a fumble at UCLA and picked off his first career pass in the win over Illinois, adding another interception in the Huskies' LA Bowl victory over Boise State. He was a first team All-Metro League pick at Garfield High and enters 2026 as an experienced piece in the secondary.

athletes.name: Dezmen Roebuck
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$624K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Roebuck is Washington's returning slot receiver and was the team's second-leading receiver as a freshman in 2025. He is a projected starter in the 2026 offense.

athletes.name: Emmanuel Karnley
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$604K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Karnley is a projected starting cornerback for Washington in 2026 after transferring from Virginia, where he played following two seasons at Arizona. He steps into a secondary that lost NFL Draft picks Ephesians Prysock and Tacario Davis.

athletes.name: Rashid Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$392K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a projected starting wide receiver for Washington in 2026 and caught a 43-yard touchdown from Demond Williams Jr. in the Huskies' spring game. The junior emerged alongside Dezmen Roebuck as a top target during spring practice.

athletes.name: Rylon Dillard-Allen
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$476K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Dillard-Allen is a returning starting safety for Washington and recorded 40 tackles in 2025. The sophomore is one of the young cornerstones of the Huskies' rebuilt secondary.

athletes.name: Jordan Washington
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Washington is a third-year running back from Long Beach, Calif., who played in 10 games in 2025 and rushed for 108 yards on five carries against Purdue, including a 68-yard touchdown run. At Long Beach Jordan High he ran for 3,024 yards on 291 carries and earned first-team All-CIF Southern Section honors in each of his three varsity seasons.

athletes.name: Derek Colman-Brusa
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Colman-Brusa is a first-year defensive lineman from Seattle who joined Washington out of Kennedy Catholic High School. He was named North Puget Sound League 4A Player of the Year as a senior in 2025 after posting 50 tackles, 19 for loss and eight sacks, and 247Sports rated him the No. 1 prospect in Washington and the No. 17 edge nationally. His older brother Lowen is also an offensive lineman at Washington.

athletes.name: Christian Moss
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$835K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Moss is a senior wide receiver who joined Washington from Kennesaw State after an earlier stop at Virginia Tech. He is a projected contributor in a Huskies receiving corps replacing Denzel Boston.

athletes.name: Mason James
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: James is a first-year wide receiver from Norman, Okla., who caught 64 passes for 930 yards and 12 touchdowns as a senior at Norman North and was named second-team all-state by The Oklahoman. As a junior he had 56 receptions for 1,233 yards and 17 scores and was his conference's wide receiver of the year.

athletes.name: Dylan Robinson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Robinson enters his second season at Washington as a projected starting cornerback after an unusually productive first year. He enrolled in June 2025 and played in 12 games with five starts as a true freshman, drawing assignments against top receivers despite arriving from Bonita High School in La Verne, California, where he was used mostly as a wide receiver. Listed at 6-3 and around 210 pounds, he has been singled out by Washington coaches as one of the program's highest-upside young defensive backs.

athletes.name: Alex McLaughlin
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$624K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: McLaughlin is Washington's returning starting safety and led the Huskies with 94 total tackles in 2025. He transferred to Washington from Northern Arizona.

athletes.name: Ramonz Adams Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Adams enrolled at Washington in January 2025 and debuted against UC Davis, also appearing against Purdue, at UCLA and in the L.A. Bowl win over Boise State. He spent his senior year at Bastrop after transferring from Smithville, catching 43 passes for 775 yards and 13 touchdowns while adding three interceptions. 247Sports ranked the second year cornerback from Smithville, Texas the No. 79 corner in his class.

athletes.name: Chris Lawson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lawson played eight games as a freshman in 2025, catching passes against UC Davis, Rutgers, Illinois, Wisconsin, UCLA, Oregon and in the L.A. Bowl win over Boise State. At Archbishop Riordan he was West Catholic Athletic League Utility Player of the Year as a senior and league Wide Receiver of the Year as a junior. 247Sports rated the second year receiver from San Francisco the No. 26 wideout nationally.

athletes.name: Dash Beierly
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Beierly is a second-year quarterback from Temecula, Calif., who enrolled at Washington in January 2025 and redshirted. He transferred to Mater Dei for his senior year after three seasons at Chaparral, then completed 159 of 252 passes for 2,175 yards and 26 touchdowns while leading the Monarchs to a 13-0 record and the California Open Division title.

athletes.name: Jacob Manu
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$392K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Manu is a projected starting linebacker for Washington in 2026 and a former Arizona standout who followed head coach Jedd Fisch to Seattle. He is the veteran anchor of the Huskies' linebacker room.

athletes.name: Xe'ree Alexander
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$528K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Alexander is a projected starting linebacker for Washington in 2026 after a breakout 2025 season. He reached the Huskies by way of Idaho and UCF.

athletes.name: Treston "Kini" McMillan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McMillan is a second-year quarterback from Mililani, Hawai'i, who enrolled at Washington in January 2025 and redshirted before playing in the L.A. Bowl. He was Hawai'i's Gatorade Player of the Year as a junior at Mililani High, passing for 3,521 yards and 42 touchdowns and rushing for 575 yards and 11 more scores.

athletes.name: Jordan Clay
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clay is a first-year wide receiver from San Antonio, Texas. At Madison High he caught 41 passes for 900 yards as a junior and 42 for 819 yards and 11 touchdowns as a sophomore, and he was Texas District 28-6A Offensive Newcomer of the Year as a freshman. He played in the 2025 Navy All-American Game.

athletes.name: Ramzak Fruean
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fruean is a first year edge rusher who signed with Washington after reopening his recruitment late in the 2026 cycle. As a Bethel High School senior he recorded 62 tackles, nine for loss, six sacks and three interceptions while also catching 24 passes for 625 yards and seven touchdowns, earning 4A first team all state honors and league co-player of the year. He moved from Nanakuli, Hawaii to Washington before his junior year.

athletes.name: Trez Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davis is a first-year wide receiver from West Monroe, La., who caught 53 passes for 998 yards and eight touchdowns as a junior at West Monroe High. He won a 5A regional triple jump title in track, and his father, Tramissian Davis, played at Louisiana Tech and signed with the New Orleans Saints.

athletes.name: Logan George
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: George joins Washington as a fourth year edge rusher after stops at Idaho State and Ohio State, adding experience to the 2026 pass rush rotation. Listed at 6 foot 4 and 260 pounds, he is a Pocatello, Idaho native who played his high school football at Highland High School in his hometown.

athletes.name: Rahsjon Duncan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Duncan is a first-year cornerback from Oakland, Calif. As a senior at McClymonds he recorded 57 tackles, three interceptions, 16 pass breakups and four forced fumbles while also catching 37 passes for 976 yards and nine touchdowns, helping the Warriors to an 11-2 record and a CIF Oakland Section championship.

athletes.name: Rahim Wright II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wright missed the 2025 season and earned a spot on the Big Ten All Academic team. He appeared in one game in 2024, the opener against Weber State, then redshirted. At Rancho Cucamonga High he recorded 114 tackles as a senior and earned first team All CIF Southern Section Division II, and he won a CIF Southern Section Division 1 long jump title. The third year safety is from Fontana, California.

athletes.name: Derek Zammit
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zammit is a first-year quarterback from Lincoln Park, N.J., who started four seasons at DePaul Catholic and helped the Spartans to three New Jersey Non-Public B state championships. As a junior he completed 150 of 221 passes for 2,582 yards and 35 touchdowns, and he played in the Under Armour All-America Game.

athletes.name: Justice Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams played the first four games of 2025, mostly on special teams, and caught two passes for 28 yards against UC Davis. He redshirted in 2024 and made the Big Ten All Academic team. At Oaks Christian in Westlake Village he had 54 catches for 910 yards and 10 touchdowns as a junior, and On3 ranked the third year receiver the No. 22 wideout in his class.

athletes.name: Elijah Durr
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Durr is a first-year cornerback listed from Los Angeles, Calif., who played at Mt. Tahoma High in Tacoma. He was Washington's Gatorade State Player of the Year in 2025 and the state coaches' 3A co-defensive player of the year, adding 427 receiving yards, eight touchdowns, three punt return scores and five blocked punts as a senior.

athletes.name: Jayden Limar
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$493K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Limar is Washington's projected starting running back for 2026 after transferring in from Oregon. The Lake Stevens, Washington native takes over a backfield that lost Jonah Coleman to the NFL Draft and Adam Mohammed to Cal.

athletes.name: Kai McClendon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McClendon transferred to Washington from Mississippi State in January 2026 with three seasons of eligibility remaining. A three star recruit in the 2024 class, the Gulfport, Mississippi native started five of 12 games as a true freshman for the Bulldogs and finished with 30 tackles and two tackles for loss. A knee injury cost him the 2025 season, and he returned to full work during his first spring in Seattle. Coach Jedd Fisch has said the sophomore was brought in to be a large part of the defensive line rotation.

athletes.name: Bodpegn Miller
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Miller comes to Washington from Ohio State and is listed as a second year wide receiver on the 2026 roster. He stands 6 foot 3 and 200 pounds. A native of Mansfield, Ohio, he played his high school football at Ontario High School before beginning his college career in the Big Ten.

athletes.name: D’Aryhian Clemons
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clemons is a second-year running back from Spanaway, Wash., who redshirted in 2025 and made one tackle in the win over UC Davis. At Spanaway Lake he played four varsity seasons at cornerback and running back, rushing for 1,037 yards on 152 carries as a sophomore while also returning kicks and punts.

athletes.name: Quaid Carr
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Carr is a second-year running back from Riverside, Calif., who saw his first Washington action against Purdue. At Servite he rushed for 1,102 yards and 12 touchdowns as a senior and 1,201 yards and 17 scores as a junior, earning first-team All-CIF Southern Section honors in both seasons.

athletes.name: Gavin Day
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Day is a first-year safety from Las Vegas who signed with Washington out of Faith Lutheran, where he started three seasons on varsity. As a senior in 2025 he made 101 tackles with 12 for loss, two interceptions, eight pass breakups and three forced fumbles, was team defensive MVP and first-team all-league, and helped the Crusaders reach the Nevada 5A final. He was rated the No. 2 recruit in Nevada by 247Sports.

athletes.name: Trey Cooley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cooley arrives as a sixth year running back with stops at Louisville, Georgia Tech and Troy behind him, adding veteran depth to the Washington backfield in 2026. Listed at 5 foot 11 and 215 pounds, he is from Raleigh, North Carolina and played his high school football at Knightsdale.

athletes.name: Zaydrius Rainey-Sale
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rainey-Sale was rated the No. 1 recruit in Washington and the No. 10 linebacker nationally by 247Sports out of Bethel High in Tacoma, where he was named the state's defensive MVP. He enrolled early at Washington and played eight games as a freshman in 2025, starting the season finale against Oregon with four tackles and a sack. He intercepted his first career pass against Purdue and won the Huskies' Newcomer of the Year award. He is a sophomore in 2026.

athletes.name: Jeron Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a first-year cornerback from Mission Viejo, Calif., who played four varsity seasons for the Diablos. As a senior he had 49 tackles, 10 pass breakups and four interceptions and was named first-team All-CIF Southern Section Division 1. He also won a league title in the 200 meters as a freshman.

athletes.name: Donovan Robinson Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Robinson redshirted as a freshman in 2025 without seeing game action. He played defensive back and returned kicks at Loyola Academy, recording 36 tackles and an interception as a senior and earning first team All Chicago Catholic League while the Ramblers won a third straight Illinois Class 8A title. 247Sports ranked the second year linebacker from Chicago the No. 10 prospect in Illinois.

athletes.name: Elias Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson appeared in three games in 2025, playing against Colorado State and at UCLA and making a tackle in the L.A. Bowl win over Boise State. He also earned Big Ten All Academic honors after redshirting in 2024. At Jesuit High he had five receiving touchdowns and 47 tackles as a senior, and recruiting services rated the third year cornerback from Tualatin the No. 8 prospect in Oregon.

athletes.name: Beck Walker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Walker is a fourth-year linebacker from Sammamish, Wash., who enrolled at Washington through the transfer portal in January 2025 and redshirted. He spent two seasons at Golden West Junior College, rushing for 248 yards and three touchdowns in 2024 and scoring in the Southern California Bowl. He earned first-team all-league honors at Skyline High.

athletes.name: Ksani Jiles
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jiles is a first-year cornerback from Inglewood, Calif., who played all four high school seasons at IMG Academy in Bradenton, Fla. As a senior he was credited with 26 tackles and two interceptions as IMG finished 9-0 and ranked fourth nationally in the USA Today poll. His earlier teams went 10-0 and 8-1.

athletes.name: Julian McMahan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McMahan is a second-year running back from San Ramon, Calif., who enrolled at Washington in January 2025 and redshirted. At Monte Vista he rushed for 1,436 yards and 20 touchdowns on 245 carries as a senior and set a school record with 307 rushing yards in a playoff game against Bishop O'Dowd.

athletes.name: Kayden Greene
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Greene is a third-year cornerback from Renton, Wash., who earned Big Ten All-Academic honors and saw his first Washington action in the L.A. Bowl win over Boise State. At Eastside Catholic he was first-team All-Metro League Mountain Division at safety as a senior and second team as a junior.

athletes.name: Ansu Sanoe
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sanoe is a first-year running back from Gresham, Ore., who caught 88 passes for 770 yards and 10 touchdowns and rushed for 837 yards and 11 scores as a senior at Lakeridge. He was a unanimous first-team All-Three Rivers League selection and was second-team 6A all-state as a junior.

athletes.name: Paul Mencke Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mencke played seven games in 2025, debuting against Ohio State and recording a tackle against Purdue, and he was voted the Huskies Mark Drennan Defensive Scout Squad MVP at the postseason banquet. He redshirted in 2024. On3 ranked the third year safety the No. 15 safety nationally out of Samuel Clemens High. His father, Paul Sr., played at Washington State. He is from Cibolo, Texas.

athletes.name: Ryken Moon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moon is a second-year running back from Bellevue, Wash., who played in three games in 2025 and rushed for 22 yards against Purdue. He was SBLive's Class 3A state player of the year as a senior at Bellevue High after running for 1,297 yards and 13 touchdowns. His father, Warren Moon, played quarterback at Washington.

athletes.name: Darin Conley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Conley joined Washington from Ball State in the 2026 transfer portal cycle after the Huskies made him a priority target to shore up their defensive line. The Kansas City, Missouri native redshirted as a true freshman and then played 24 games over three seasons for the Cardinals, recording 16 tackles with three for loss and two sacks in 2024 before posting 28 tackles, 4.5 tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks and a pass breakup in 2025. He is listed at 6-3 and 284 pounds with two years of eligibility left.

athletes.name: Ryan Kean
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kean joined Washington through the transfer portal after three seasons at Utah Tech, where he earned all conference honors in 2023 as a redshirt freshman. In his first year with the Huskies he handled all but one of the team's 105 field goal, extra point and punt snaps, and he has now snapped in 36 college games. The Corona, California native played both wide receiver and long snapper at Centennial High School and returns as Washington's clear starting specialist in 2026.

athletes.name: Brian Bonner Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bonner is a first year Washington running back from Santa Clarita, California, who signed in the 2026 class out of Valencia High School as a four star prospect rated among the top running backs nationally. He rushed for 1,051 yards and 13 touchdowns on 113 carries as a senior and shared Foothill League Most Valuable Player honors, after running for 1,493 yards and 25 touchdowns as a junior. He chose the Huskies over UCLA.

athletes.name: Jace Burton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Burton is a third-year wide receiver from Portland, Ore., who earned Big Ten All-Academic honors and debuted in the L.A. Bowl win over Boise State. He played cornerback, safety and receiver at Jesuit High. His father, Nigel Burton, lettered three years as a Washington defensive back and captained the 1998 team.

athletes.name: C.J. Wallace
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wallace is a first-year placekicker at Washington from Manhattan Beach, California, who played at St. John Bosco. He handled both kicking and punting across three varsity seasons and made 54 extra points and three field goals in 2025 as Bosco went 9-2 and reached the CIF Southern Section Division 1 quarterfinals. Ranked among the top kicking prospects in the 2026 class by 247Sports and On3, he was one of Washington's earliest commitments in that class.

athletes.name: Hunter McKee
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McKee is a second-year kicker from Spokane, Wash., who spent 2025 at Eastern Washington as the Eagles' kickoff specialist, kicking off 51 times with 37 touchbacks and attempting one 51-yard field goal. At Mt. Spokane he was first-team All-Greater Spokane League as a senior and was invited to the Chris Sailer Kicking Camp Top 12.

athletes.name: Ezaya Tokio
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tokio is a first-year linebacker from Oceanside, Calif., who recorded 76 tackles, 11 tackles for loss, eight sacks and an interception as a senior at Oceanside High. He added 28 tackles and 7.5 sacks in four games the previous year and spent his first two high school seasons at St. Augustine in San Diego.

athletes.name: Ben Ferber
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ferber is a first-year long snapper from Delray Beach, Fla., who spent the 2025-26 school year at IMG Academy after three years at North Broward Prep in Coconut Creek. IMG finished 9-0 and ranked fifth nationally in the final USA Today poll during his senior season. He played long snapper and linebacker at North Broward.

athletes.name: Kade Eldridge
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Eldridge transferred in from USC in January 2025 and started the 2025 opener against Colorado State as a second tight end, scoring on a one yard run. He played the first seven games before his season ended at Michigan. He appeared in 12 games at USC in 2024 with three receptions. The fourth year tight end from Lynden was a 1A Northwest Conference Defensive MVP at Lynden Christian.

athletes.name: Hayden Moore
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moore is a fourth-year edge rusher from Parker, Colo., who played in all 13 games in 2025 and made two tackles against UC Davis. He spent 2023 at Michigan before transferring to Washington in the summer of 2024. At Regis Jesuit he recorded 197 tackles as a senior and was named all-state by CHSAA.

athletes.name: Luke Dunne
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dunne handled every Washington punt in 2025 after transferring from Oregon, including six against Oregon and a 47 yarder in the win over Illinois. He spent two seasons with the Ducks and averaged 42.7 yards on nine punts in 2024. The fourth year punter grew up in Benalla, Australia playing Australian rules football and trained at ProKick Australia before coming to the United States.

athletes.name: Jacob Lane
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$1.13M, second on the roster; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Lane is a projected starting edge rusher for Washington in 2026 and the Huskies' most durable returning option on the edge. He is a Puyallup, Washington native who signed out of Emerald Ridge High School.

athletes.name: David Schwerzel
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Schwerzel is a first-year defensive lineman from Seattle who was first-team All-Metro League at both defensive tackle and tight end in 2025 and a state coaches' 3A first-team all-state tight end. He helped O'Dea to 14-1 and 13-0 records and consecutive 3A state championships in his junior and senior seasons.

athletes.name: Devin Hyde
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hyde played all 13 games as a freshman in 2025, opening with a seven yard sack against Colorado State and adding three tackles and a quarterback hurry at UCLA before winning the team Iron Dawg Award. At Menlo-Atherton he was Peninsula Athletic League Bay Defensive Player of the Year with 55 tackles as a senior. 247Sports rated the second year edge rusher from Menlo Park the No. 68 edge in his class.

athletes.name: Parker Cross
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cross is a fourth-year offensive lineman from Seattle who made his Washington debut in the L.A. Bowl win over Boise State and earned Big Ten All-Academic honors. At Seattle Prep he played three varsity seasons and was first-team All-Metro Mountain Division 3A at center as a senior. He also threw the shot put and discus.

athletes.name: JD Hill
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hill is a first-year defensive lineman from Mission Viejo, California, who signed with Washington out of Mission Viejo High School and wears No. 54. Listed at 6-2 and 275 pounds, he committed to the Huskies in November 2025 and chose them over West Virginia. As a senior he posted 108 tackles with 25.5 tackles for loss, 13 sacks and 18 quarterback hurries for a 9-2 team.

athletes.name: Kolt Dieterich
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dieterich joins the Huskies as a fourth year offensive lineman after time at Sam Houston State, giving Washington another experienced body in the 2026 line rotation. He is listed at 6 foot 6 and 300 pounds. A native of Riesel, Texas, he played his high school football at Riesel High School.

athletes.name: Victor Sanchez Hernandez
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sanchez Hernandez is a second-year edge rusher from Mukilteo, Wash., who redshirted in 2025. He was first-team 4A All-Wesco on the defensive line as both a junior and senior at Kamiak High after previously attending Lynnwood. Before taking up football he competed in taekwondo, winning three national titles and two Pan-American championships.

athletes.name: Geirean Hatchett
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$574K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Hatchett is Washington's returning starting right guard and an Oklahoma transfer entering his final season. He is the older brother of Huskies center Landen Hatchett and also came out of Ferndale High School.

athletes.name: Ta'a Malu

He recorded 36 tackles, 11 for loss and two forced fumbles as a senior at Annie Wright Schools, where he began playing football as a junior.

athletes.name: Jesse Ewell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ewell is a first-year linebacker who grew up in Washington state and attended San Clemente High in California, where he spent three seasons on the varsity. He served as a captain as a senior on a team that went 9-5 and advanced to the CIF Southern Section Division 2 championship game.

athletes.name: DeSean Watts

Listed at 6 foot and 315 pounds, he is a Fresno, California native who played his high school football at Clovis West and now competes for interior snaps in the Huskies 2026 defensive line rotation.

athletes.name: Tufanua Ionatana Umu-Cais
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Umu-Cais is a first-year defensive lineman from Englewood, Colo., who made 92 tackles and 15 tackles for loss as a senior at Cherry Creek, helping the Bruins finish 14-0 and win the Colorado 5A championship. He had 75 tackles as a junior on another title team and was selected for the 2026 Polynesian Bowl.

athletes.name: Jack Shaffer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Shaffer is a second-year offensive lineman from Bismarck, N.D., who enrolled in January 2025 and made his Washington debut at UCLA before winning the team's Husky Fever 12th Man Award. He was first-team AAA all-state at Bismarck High as both a junior and senior and placed second in the state shot put and discus.

athletes.name: Landen Hatchett
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$501K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Hatchett is Washington's returning starting center and a multi-year starter on the Huskies' offensive line. He missed the end of the 2025 season and spring 2026 practice while recovering from wrist surgery.

athletes.name: Aidan Anderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anderson is a fourth-year offensive lineman from Olympia, Wash., who has been named to Big Ten academic teams in each of the past two seasons. He played both lines at North Thurston High and earned first-team all-league honors as a senior. He also won the Washington 3A 285-pound state wrestling championship in 2023.

athletes.name: Soane Faasolo
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Faasolo played in all 13 games in 2025 and earned Big Ten All Academic honors. In 2024 he appeared in all 13 games with four starts, including the first three at left tackle and another at Indiana. He redshirted in 2023. At Menlo-Atherton the fourth year lineman from East Palo Alto was Peninsula Athletic League Bay Division Offensive Lineman of the Year.

athletes.name: Justin Hylkema
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hylkema made his college debut in the L.A. Bowl win over Boise State in 2025 and earned a spot on the Big Ten All Academic team after redshirting in 2024. At Wilcox High he was named Peninsula Athletic League Bay Division Offensive Lineman of the Year in 2023 and earned San Francisco Chronicle All Metro first team honors. The third year lineman is from Santa Clara, California.

athletes.name: Ah Deong Yang
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Yang is a first-year offensive lineman from Puyallup, Wash., who played his senior season at Puyallup High after a junior year at Roosevelt in Seattle. He was second-team All-North Puget Sound League 4A North as a senior and, at Roosevelt, was Metro League co-Offensive Lineman of the Year and 3A first-team all-state.

athletes.name: John Mills
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$451K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Mills is Washington's returning starting left guard after breaking into the lineup as a true freshman in 2025. He is one of four returning starters on the Huskies' offensive line.

athletes.name: Champ Taulealea
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taulealea enrolled in January 2025 and played five games as a freshman, preserving a year of eligibility with appearances against UC Davis, Purdue, UCLA, Oregon and Boise State in the L.A. Bowl. At Valley Christian he was a CalHiSports first team all state pick and West Catholic Athletic League Co Offensive Lineman of the Year. 247Sports rated the second year lineman from Milpitas the No. 19 interior lineman nationally.

athletes.name: Drew Azzopardi
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$1.11M; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Azzopardi is Washington's returning starting right tackle and one of four returning starters on the Huskies' 2026 offensive line. He came to Washington as a transfer from San Diego State.

athletes.name: Lowen Colman-Brusa
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Colman-Brusa did not see game action as a freshman in 2025. At Kennedy Catholic he was named the state 4A defensive player of the year by the Washington State Football Coaches Association and made the All North Puget Sound League first team on both sides of the ball as a senior while the Lancers went 11-1. The second year lineman from Seattle is listed at 6 foot 6 and 330 pounds.

athletes.name: Kodi Greene
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$725K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Greene is a five-star true freshman offensive tackle from Mater Dei High School and the highest-rated signee in Washington's 2026 class. He is the projected starter at left tackle.

athletes.name: Elishah Jackett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackett has not seen game action in three seasons at Washington and redshirted in 2023. He arrived as a highly rated tackle out of El Modena High, where he helped the team to an 11-1 record as a senior and earned CalHiSports second team all state honors. 247Sports rated him the nation's No. 35 offensive tackle. The fourth year lineman is from Orange, California.

athletes.name: Jake Flores
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Flores enrolled in January 2025, redshirted the season and made his first appearance in the L.A. Bowl win over Boise State. At JSerra Catholic he was a CalHiSports first team all state selection and a two time first team All CIF Southern Section Division 1 pick. 247Sports rated the second year lineman from Mission Viejo the No. 68 interior offensive lineman in his class.

athletes.name: Dominic Harris
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Harris is a first-year offensive lineman from Las Vegas who helped Clark High to a 7-5 record and the 4A Southern semifinals as a senior, part of playoff appearances in each of his four seasons. Recruiting services listed him among the top offensive tackle prospects nationally. He also threw the shot put and discus and played basketball.

athletes.name: Blaise LaVista
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
