As a junior he caught 60 passes for 1,447 yards and 24 touchdowns and earned first-team all-state honors, following 47 catches for 1,091 yards and 15 scores as a sophomore.

athletes.name: Asa Thompson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thompson is a first-year wide receiver from Sammamish, Wash., who played four varsity seasons at Eastside Catholic. He was first-team All-Metro League at wide receiver in each of his final three years and added first-team honors at defensive back as a senior, when the Crusaders went 10-2 and reached the 3A state semifinals.

athletes.name: Deji Ajose
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ajose is a second-year wide receiver from Hercules, Calif., who redshirted in 2025 and played in the L.A. Bowl win over Boise State. At Bishop O'Dowd he caught 47 passes for 813 yards and 12 touchdowns as a senior and added 47 tackles and two interceptions on defense, earning all-area honors.

athletes.name: Kekua Aumua
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Aumua is a first-year tight end from Hau'ula, Hawai'i, who helped Kahuku to an 8-4 record, a 6-0 league mark and the Division I Open state semifinals as a senior. He spent his junior year at IMG Academy in Florida and was selected to play in the 2026 Polynesian Bowl.

athletes.name: Baron Naone
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Naone debuted against UC Davis in 2025 and went on to play against Michigan, Illinois, Purdue, UCLA, Oregon and Boise State, earning the Huskies Bob Jarvis Offensive Scout Squad MVP award. He helped West Linn to an Oregon 6A state title as a senior and was a unanimous first team all league tight end. 247Sports ranked the second year tight end from West Linn the No. 2 prospect in Oregon.

athletes.name: Decker DeGraaf
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$413K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: DeGraaf is Washington's returning starting tight end with 47 catches for 593 yards and five touchdowns across his first two seasons. He has opened 16 games in two years and is expected to take on a larger role in 2026.

athletes.name: Sam Vyhlidal
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Vyhlidal is a first-year tight end from Lake Oswego, Ore., who transferred to Lake Oswego High before his senior season after attending Mountainside in Beaverton. He was a unanimous first-team All-Three Rivers League selection at both tight end and outside linebacker as the Lakers went 12-1 and won the Oregon 6A Open championship.

athletes.name: Charlie Crowell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Crowell is a third-year tight end from Bend, Ore., who has earned Big Ten All-Academic honors. At Summit High he caught 32 passes for 507 yards and six touchdowns as a senior and was first-team All-Intermountain League and honorable mention all-state. As a junior he helped Summit win the Oregon 5A state title.

athletes.name: Elinneus Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$631K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Davis is Washington's returning starting defensive tackle and started 13 games with 29 tackles in 2025. The junior anchors an interior line rebuilt through the transfer portal.

athletes.name: Isaiah Ward
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$1.06M; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Ward is a senior edge rusher projected to start for Washington in 2026 after transferring in from Arizona. Health has been the main question surrounding his final college season.

athletes.name: Hunter Green
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Green returns to his hometown area as a senior punter after three seasons at Northern Colorado and one at San Diego State. He averaged 47.0 yards on 63 punts for the Aztecs in 2025, ranked sixth nationally, dropped 26 inside the 20 and earned second team All-Mountain West honors. He was a first team All-Big Sky pick in 2023 and 2024 at Northern Colorado. A Redmond native from Lake Washington High, he is the son of former Husky kicker Phil Green.

athletes.name: Joseph Peko
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Peko is a first-year defensive lineman from Calabasas, Calif., who earned first-team All-Marmonte League honors on the defensive line in each of his last three seasons at Oaks Christian and was selected for the 2026 Polynesian Bowl. His father, Domata Peko, played 14 NFL seasons and now coaches the Pittsburgh Steelers defensive line.

athletes.name: Tyler Robles
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Robles takes over Washington's placekicking job in 2026 after transferring from Texas State, where he was a second-team All-Sun Belt selection. The Encinitas, California native made 19 of 21 field goals and 53 of 54 extra points for the Bobcats, including multiple conversions from beyond 50 yards. He began his college career at USC, spending the 2023 and 2024 seasons there before moving to Texas State. He entered the portal in January and committed to the Huskies, who expect him to handle field goals and extra points.

athletes.name: Omar Khan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Khan saw his only 2025 action in the win over UC Davis and earned Big Ten All Academic honors after redshirting in 2024. At Bridgeland High he had 29 tackles, 8.5 for loss and five sacks as a senior and was a unanimous first team All District 16-6A pick. He also won a Texas district wrestling title at 285 pounds. The third year lineman is from Cypress, Texas.

athletes.name: Russell Davis II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davis missed the 2025 season and returns for a fifth year in the Washington edge rotation. In 2024 he played three games and earned Big Ten Defensive Player of the Week against UCLA with three sacks, a forced fumble and a recovery. He spent 2022 and 2023 at Arizona, posting 5.5 tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks in 2023. The Chandler, Arizona native prepped at Hamilton High.

athletes.name: CJ Christian
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: CJ Christian is listed as a senior safety from Normal, Ill., with the Washington football program. He does not appear on the school's published 2026 football roster, so no further verified biographical details are available at this time.

athletes.name: Elijah Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Washington roster valuation ~$426K; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Brown is Washington's backup quarterback after transferring in from Stanford. He was a highly recruited passer at Mater Dei High School in Santa Ana, California.

athletes.name: Austin Simmons
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A redshirt freshman tight end out of Albany, Ore., Simmons is competing for a spot in the Huskies' two-deep this fall.

athletes.name: Demon June
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: June is North Carolina's returning lead running back, rushing for 464 yards and two touchdowns on 84 carries as a true freshman in 2025 while adding 17 receptions for 159 yards and a score.

athletes.name: Isaiah Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a redshirt senior defensive lineman from Camden, New Jersey, listed at 6-foot-2 and 320 pounds on the 2026 North Carolina roster. He finished high school at Chandler in Arizona and spent three seasons at Arizona before transferring to Chapel Hill, where he posted 41 tackles and two sacks in his first year with the Tar Heels, third-most stops among Carolina defensive linemen. He re-signed with the program rather than entering the portal and projects as a starting interior lineman in 2026.

athletes.name: Greg Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is North Carolina's projected starting strong safety, a 6-foot-3 defensive back who transferred to Chapel Hill from Florida ahead of the 2025 season.

athletes.name: Jordan Shipp
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Shipp is North Carolina's leading returning receiver and a 2025 All-ACC honorable mention after catching 60 passes for 671 yards and six touchdowns. The Charlotte native re-signed with the Tar Heels despite outside NIL interest.

athletes.name: Kaleb Cost
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cost is a senior defensive back from Atlanta who came to North Carolina out of Sandy Creek High School and is listed at 5-foot-11 and 195 pounds. He recorded 45 tackles in 2025, fifth on the Tar Heel defense and second among defensive backs, adding two tackles for loss and an interception in the season opener against TCU. Cost has 114 career tackles and three interceptions, including a pick-six against Pittsburgh in 2024, and re-signed to return as a starting corner.

athletes.name: Trech Kekahuna
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kekahuna is North Carolina's projected starting slot receiver after transferring from Wisconsin, where he started all 12 games in 2025 with career highs of 26 receptions for 211 yards plus 129 rushing yards and a 61-yard touchdown run.

athletes.name: Ade Willie
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Willie is North Carolina's projected starting cornerback opposite Jaiden Patterson, recording 16 tackles and two tackles for loss in 2025 after transferring from Michigan State.

athletes.name: Travis Burgess
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Burgess is a freshman quarterback from Grayson, Georgia, who played at Grayson High School. He was selected to the Elite 11 Finals for the nation's top high school quarterbacks and helped Grayson to a Georgia 6A state championship as a junior, finishing 14-1. That season he threw for 2,225 yards and 23 touchdowns on 154 of 256 passing and added 596 rushing yards.

athletes.name: Jalon Thompson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thompson arrived at North Carolina from Orlando's Olympia High as a three-star prospect who posted 97 tackles, 12 interceptions and 31 pass breakups across three prep seasons and helped Olympia to a district title. Now a junior listed at 5-11 and 185 pounds, the Florida native is in the defensive back rotation and competing for secondary snaps in 2026.

athletes.name: Mason Humphrey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Humphrey is a senior wide receiver from Loganville, Georgia, who arrived at North Carolina in January 2026 as a transfer from Lehigh. The 6-foot-4, 215-pound target played high school football at Grayson and caught 35 passes for 650 yards and four touchdowns in 2025 after 45 receptions for 587 yards and five scores the previous season. He was the 11th addition to the Tar Heels' portal class and has one year of eligibility, projecting into the receiver rotation.

athletes.name: Donovan Hoilette Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hoilette is a graduate defensive lineman from West Palm Beach, Florida, who joined North Carolina in January 2026 after five seasons at Richmond. Listed at 6-foot-4 and 245 pounds out of Palm Beach Central High School, he moved from linebacker to the defensive line before the 2024 season and then started all 12 games in 2025, earning first-team All-Patriot League honors with 48 tackles, 13 tackles for loss and 9.5 sacks. He has one year of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Kaleb Jackson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson is a 234-pound running back who transferred to North Carolina from LSU, where he scored four touchdowns as a freshman and averaged over five yards per carry before a reduced role in 2025.

athletes.name: Dayton Sneed
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sneed transferred to North Carolina from Tennessee in 2025 after joining the Volunteers as a preferred walk-on out of Donelson Christian Academy, where he set school single-season records with 1,214 receiving yards and 17 touchdowns and was named 2021 TSSAA Division II-A Offensive Player of the Year. The redshirt junior from Hermitage, Tennessee, caught two passes in seven games with the Vols and works in the Tar Heels receiver rotation.

athletes.name: Tre Miller
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Miller signed with North Carolina in the 2023 class as a three-star cornerback rated among the top recruits in Oklahoma after a senior season at Edmond's Deer Creek High, which went 10-2. He had previously played at Hoover in Alabama. Now a redshirt junior listed at 5-10 and 180 pounds, the Birmingham native is a depth piece in the Tar Heels secondary.

athletes.name: Benjamin Hall
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hall is a 235-pound backup running back and kick returner for North Carolina who transferred from Michigan, where he served as a short-yardage back across the 2023 and 2024 seasons.

athletes.name: Peyton Waters
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Waters is a safety in North Carolina's secondary rotation who transferred from Washington, where he played all 13 games as a true freshman. He followed Steve Belichick to Chapel Hill.

athletes.name: Jonathan Agumadu
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Agumadu came to Chapel Hill from Oklahoma State in May 2025 after redshirting with the Cowboys, where he appeared in four games as a freshman. A three-star recruit out of McKinney High in Texas, he recorded 37 tackles and six sacks as a high school senior. The redshirt sophomore from Dallas is listed at 6-2 and 220 pounds and is competing for rotational linebacker snaps.

athletes.name: Miles O'Neill
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: O'Neill transferred to North Carolina from Texas A&M in January 2026, reuniting with Bobby Petrino, who helped recruit him to College Station. The Marblehead, Massachusetts, native was New Jersey Gatorade Player of the Year at the Hun School after throwing for 2,151 yards, and he completed seven of 14 passes for 120 yards and a touchdown as an Aggie backup. The redshirt sophomore stands 6-5, 220.

athletes.name: Billy Edwards Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Edwards is North Carolina's projected starting quarterback for 2026, a graduate transfer from Wisconsin who threw for 2,881 yards and 15 touchdowns as Maryland's full-season starter in 2024. He is the headline addition of Bill Belichick's second portal cycle.

athletes.name: Melkart Abou Jaoude
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Abou Jaoude is North Carolina's returning starting edge rusher and a 2025 second-team All-ACC selection, finishing eighth nationally with 10.5 sacks in his first season after transferring from Delaware. He turned down larger offers elsewhere to re-sign with the Tar Heels for 2026.

athletes.name: Au'Tori Newkirk
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Newkirk joined North Carolina's 2025 class from Maury High in Norfolk, where the left-handed passer threw for 8,838 career yards and 114 touchdowns, won two Class 5 state championships and earned VHSL Player of the Year honors. He rose to four-star status after committing. Listed at 6-3 and 200 pounds, the redshirt freshman is a developmental option behind the Tar Heels' veteran quarterbacks in 2026.

athletes.name: Peyton Seelmann
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Seelmann is North Carolina's projected starting weakside linebacker, a Richmond transfer who ranked seventh nationally in FCS with 120 tackles in 2025 while adding two interceptions and a forced fumble.

athletes.name: Jaylen Harvey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Harvey transferred from Penn State to North Carolina in January 2026 with three years of eligibility remaining. He recorded nine tackles, 1.5 for loss and a sack in nine games for the Nittany Lions as a redshirt freshman. A team captain at Gaithersburg's Quince Orchard, which won 39 straight games during his career, the redshirt sophomore is listed at 6-2 and 246 pounds.

athletes.name: Nathan Leacock
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Leacock returned to his home state in May 2025, committing to North Carolina after signing with Tennessee out of Raleigh's Millbrook High in the 2023 class. He redshirted as a freshman and caught one pass for 13 yards across five games with the Volunteers in 2024. The redshirt junior from Rolesville, listed at 6-3 and 217 pounds, gives the Tar Heels size on the perimeter.

athletes.name: Calvin Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a freshman linebacker from Houston, Texas, who played at Cypress Ranch High School. He earned first team All-District honors and recorded 47 tackles, 13.5 tackles for loss and eight sacks in 13 games as a senior after posting 69 tackles, 8.5 tackles for loss and seven sacks as a junior. He also won district titles in the 300-meter hurdles and 4x400 relay.

athletes.name: C.J. Sadler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sadler is a freshman wide receiver from Detroit who played at Cass Technical High School. He was a four-time first team All-State, All-Region and All-City honoree and helped Cass Tech win a football state championship during his junior season. A two-sport athlete, he also contributed to a state title in basketball as a freshman.

athletes.name: Tarvorise Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown joined North Carolina in January 2026 as a transfer from Florida, where he played in three games and made four tackles as a walk-on. Out of Heritage High in Miami he first signed with Hutchinson Community College in the 2023 class. Listed at 6-7 and 296 pounds, the redshirt junior gives the Tar Heels length in the interior defensive line rotation.

athletes.name: Derek McDonald
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McDonald is North Carolina's projected starting middle linebacker, a graduate transfer from Syracuse who compiled 155 tackles and 3.5 sacks before a season-ending hip injury limited him to three games in 2025.

athletes.name: DJ Mazzone
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mazzone is a redshirt sophomore walk-on quarterback from Atlanta who prepped at IMG Academy. He quarterbacked the undefeated IMG National team that won the 2023 national championship, was a four-year varsity player and a team captain in both football and golf, and earned IMG's top academic award as a National Honor Society member. He won a Georgia Class AAAA state title as a freshman.

athletes.name: Coleman Bryson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bryson is North Carolina's projected starting free safety, a Waynesville, N.C. native who transferred home from Minnesota after totaling 54 tackles over three seasons with the Golden Gophers.

athletes.name: Zamaurious Robertson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Robertson is a freshman wide receiver from Dillon, South Carolina, who played at Dillon High School. He caught 58 passes for 1,206 yards and 13 touchdowns as a senior and was named one of five finalists for South Carolina Mr. Football. He served as a captain his final two seasons and finished his prep career with 141 receptions for 2,505 yards and 26 touchdowns.

athletes.name: Jakob Weatherspoon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Weatherspoon is a freshman defensive back from Avon, Ohio, who played at Avon High School. He earned first team All-Conference and All-Ohio honors and helped Avon reach the state championship game in consecutive years, posting 73 tackles and two interceptions as a junior on a 16-0 state title team. He was also a state champion in the 400-meter dash.

athletes.name: Nyqir Helton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Helton is a freshman wide receiver from Sicklerville, New Jersey, who played at Winslow Township for coach Bill Belton. A captain as a junior and senior, he set his school's single-season record with 17 receiving touchdowns as a senior while catching 57 passes for 1,174 yards. He won a state championship as a junior, when he had 47 catches for 852 yards.

athletes.name: Andres Miyares Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Miyares is a redshirt sophomore walk-on quarterback from Miami who started four years at Belen Jesuit. He left with school career records of 3,912 passing yards and 31 touchdowns and a single-season record of 1,562 yards as a senior. He was a Miami-Dade all-county selection, a two-time captain and team MVP, and he redshirted his first season at Carolina.

athletes.name: Jaiden Patterson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Patterson is North Carolina's top returning cornerback, posting 55 tackles, an interception and five pass deflections as a sophomore in 2025 before re-signing for 2026.

athletes.name: Jaxxon Warren
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Warren is a redshirt sophomore tight end from Flower Mound, Texas, and one of the tallest players on the North Carolina roster at 6-foot-8, 245 pounds. A Marcus High School product, he began his career as a quarterback at North Texas, played a season at Navarro College, then spent two years at Colorado State. He opened the 2025 season with six catches for 79 yards and a touchdown against Washington before signing with the Tar Heels in January 2026.

athletes.name: Reggie Love II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Love is a redshirt junior defensive back at North Carolina, listed at 5-8 and 175 pounds in No. 19. He provided depth in the secondary as a true freshman in 2023 and did not appear in a game in 2024. At Rolesville High School he was a two-time all-conference and academic all-conference pick who had 39 tackles, an interception and 12 pass breakups as a senior. His father played football at North Carolina.

athletes.name: Crew Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davis is a freshman running back from Fairfield, Connecticut, who played at Iona Preparatory. He was named MaxPreps New York State Player of the Year as a junior, when he totaled 2,078 yards and 23 touchdowns for a state championship team, then ran for 1,257 yards and 15 touchdowns as a senior. His father, Joshua, played college football at Army.

athletes.name: Xavier Jackson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson is a freshman defensive back from Willingboro, New Jersey, who spent his final two prep seasons at Bergen Catholic after two years at Burlington Township. He won a state championship in his first year at Bergen Catholic in 2024 and was an all-conference selection. As a senior he recorded 42 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, four pass breakups and an interception.

athletes.name: Kenton Dopson III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dopson is a freshman defensive back from Miami who played at Miami Norland High School. He earned MaxPreps All-America honors and posted 59 tackles, six interceptions and 28 pass breakups in 10 games as a senior. He helped Norland win a state championship during his freshman season and also competed in track.

athletes.name: Charleston French
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: French is a redshirt junior running back from Amory, Mississippi, who transferred from Itawamba Community College. He earned NJCAA All-Region 23 honors after rushing for 924 yards and eight touchdowns in 2023, and he finished as Amory High School's all-time leading rusher with 5,610 yards and 70 touchdowns. His father, Rufus, was an All-American tight end at Ole Miss.

athletes.name: Khristian Dunbar-Hawkins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dunbar-Hawkins is a redshirt sophomore defensive back listed from the Inland Empire in California. He began his career at UCLA, redshirting in 2024, and appeared in three games for Carolina in 2025. He was an Under Armour All-American at Tustin High School, the first in more than 20 years there, and was ranked the No. 31 cornerback nationally by ESPN and Rivals.

athletes.name: Jaden Jefferson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jefferson is a freshman wide receiver from Oakland, California, who played running back and defensive back at De La Salle High School. He won a CIF state championship in the 100-meter dash and was an All-State honoree as a junior. He rushed for 1,048 yards and 12 touchdowns while adding 19 tackles and an interception in his final prep season.

athletes.name: Javion Butts
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Butts is a redshirt freshman defensive back from Gray, Georgia, who signed with North Carolina out of Jones County High School as a three-star recruit and one of the highest rated players in the Tar Heels class. He enrolled early and played four games in 2025 while preserving a redshirt, finishing with seven tackles, five of them solo. He is listed at 6-1 and 175 pounds in No. 24.

athletes.name: Joseph Mupoyi
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mupoyi left Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of the Congo to play basketball in the United States before taking up football, and he signed with Penn State in 2023 as a four-star prospect. He redshirted, then appeared in two games and recorded a tackle before transferring to North Carolina in April 2025. The redshirt junior is listed at 6-5 and 261 pounds along the defensive line.

athletes.name: DQ Forkpa
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Forkpa is a freshman linebacker from Plymouth, Minnesota, who played at St. Frances Academy. He earned Under Armour All-America honors during his prep career. As a junior he recorded 67 tackles, seven forced fumbles and five interceptions, and he had totaled 73 tackles across his first two high school seasons.

athletes.name: JoJo Troupe
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Troupe is a redshirt freshman running back from Tampa who played at Berkeley Prep. He ran for 3,444 yards and 42 touchdowns over four seasons with 17 games of 100 yards or more, peaking as a junior in 2023 with 1,510 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns. He also played linebacker as an underclassman and played baseball at Berkeley Prep.

athletes.name: Graham Reintjes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reintjes is a redshirt freshman walk-on defensive back from Austin, Texas, who played at the Regents School of Austin. He redshirted as a freshman at Carolina in 2025. As a senior he captained a 10-2 team and started all 12 games, seven at star and five at safety, finishing with 93 tackles, seven tackles for loss, five sacks and five pass breakups.

athletes.name: Jaylen McGill
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McGill reclassified from the 2026 class to enroll at North Carolina a year early after rushing for 1,658 yards and 24 touchdowns as a junior at Mountain View Prep in Spartanburg. He was rated among the top recruits in South Carolina and had been committed to Rutgers before choosing the Tar Heels. The sophomore is listed at 5-10 and 200 pounds in a crowded backfield.

athletes.name: Jamarrion Gordon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gordon is a freshman defensive back listed from Jackson, Alabama, who played at Jackson High School. He was selected to the Alabama-Mississippi All-Star Game and recorded 41 tackles, six tackles for loss and five interceptions as a senior after helping Jackson win a 4A state championship. His brother Jamaal Pritchett played at South Alabama and his cousin Nehemiah Pritchett played at Auburn.

athletes.name: Zavion Griffin-Haynes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Griffin-Haynes is a freshman defensive lineman from Rolesville, North Carolina, who played at Rolesville High School. His brother Jayden, a linebacker, signed with Carolina in the same class and is also on the Tar Heels roster.

athletes.name: Jaziel Hart
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hart is a freshman defensive back listed from Roanoke, Virginia, who played at North Cross School. He was a four-time first team All-State selection on defense and a three-time first team pick on offense, won three VISAA state championships and was named VISAA player of the year twice. As a junior he had 50 tackles, four interceptions and 19 offensive touchdowns.

athletes.name: Julian Peterson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Peterson is a freshman defensive back from Sicklerville, New Jersey, who played at Winslow Township High School. He recorded 30 tackles and an interception through 11 games as a senior. According to Carolina's roster bio, he becomes the seventh member of his family to play college football.

athletes.name: Jermaine Anderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anderson is a redshirt freshman defensive back from Fredricksburg, Virginia, who played strong safety at Calvert Hall and helped the Cardinals reach the playoff semifinals. He appeared in two games as a freshman at Carolina in 2025, against Wake Forest and NC State, while redshirting the season. He is also a member of the North Carolina men's lacrosse team.

athletes.name: Tyler Houser
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Houser is a redshirt freshman linebacker from Sparta, New Jersey, who played at Pope John XXIII. He finished his prep career with 341 tackles, including 225 solo stops, and 13.5 sacks, with 7.0 of those sacks coming in 10 games as a senior. He added an interception and a fumble recovery in each of his final two seasons and redshirted at Carolina in 2025.

athletes.name: David Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davis is a freshman defensive back from Pittsburgh who played at Imani Christian Academy. He was a first team All-Conference pick at defensive back, running back and kick returner, and he was voted a team captain. As a senior he recorded 30 tackles, four interceptions and six pass breakups in 10 games.

athletes.name: Ashton Blatt
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Blatt is a freshman linebacker from Pittsburgh who played at Pittsburgh Central Catholic. A two-time All-Conference honoree, he recorded 50 tackles, 19.5 tackles for loss and 13.5 sacks in 13 games as a senior after posting 32 tackles, 13 tackles for loss and seven sacks on a WPIAL championship team as a junior. His father, Andy, played at Westminster College.

athletes.name: Jayden Griffin-Haynes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Griffin-Haynes is a freshman linebacker from Rolesville, North Carolina, who played at Rolesville High School. He was an NAC-6 All-Conference honoree with 72 tackles and 14 tackles for loss during the 2025 regular season, following a junior year of 107 tackles, six sacks and two forced fumbles. His brother Zavion signed with Carolina in the same class.

athletes.name: Julian Burns
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Burns is a freshman defensive back from Monroe, Louisiana, who played at Neville High School. He earned All-State recognition and recorded 102 tackles, 29.5 tackles for loss, 11.5 sacks and two interceptions through 12 games as a senior, after 86 tackles and two interceptions as a junior. His father, Jeremiah, played college football at Louisiana-Monroe.

athletes.name: Roman Wazni
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wazni is a freshman walk-on long snapper from Tampa, Florida, who prepped at Berkeley Prep. Carolina's official roster lists him at 6-0 and 205 pounds wearing No. 40, and it carries no further biographical details.

athletes.name: Jordan Avinger
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Avinger is a freshman linebacker from Orangeburg, South Carolina, who played at Orangeburg Wilkinson High School. He earned All-Region honors and posted 38 tackles and an interception through seven games as a senior after recording 50 tackles, six tackles for loss and a forced fumble as a junior. He also played basketball and baseball in high school.

athletes.name: Lantz Pascal
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pascal is a redshirt freshman linebacker from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, who played middle linebacker for two seasons at St. Thomas Aquinas. He finished with 144 career tackles and 14.0 tackles for loss, with his best year as a junior when he had 109 total hits, 11.0 tackles for loss, four sacks and four fumble recoveries. He redshirted at Carolina in 2025.

athletes.name: Jake Bauer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bauer flipped his commitment from Navy to North Carolina in January 2025 after a Malvern Prep career that included 90 tackles, seven stops for loss and three interceptions as a junior. He was rated among the top prospects in Pennsylvania. The redshirt freshman from West Chester is listed at 6-1 and 225 pounds and is pushing for linebacker snaps in 2026.

athletes.name: Jelani Thurman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thurman is a tight end who transferred to North Carolina from Ohio State, where he totaled 13 catches for 144 yards and two touchdowns over three seasons. The former four-star recruit arrives with two years of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Henry Martello
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Martello is a redshirt freshman walk-on fullback from Culver, Indiana, who attended Culver Academy and played on both the offensive and defensive lines. He was a Class 4A Indiana All-State selection as a senior and a team captain as both a junior and senior. He was also a 2023 IHSAA sectional champion in the shot put and discus and wrestled at the state qualifying level.

athletes.name: Gannon Burt
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Burt is a redshirt junior long snapper from Fort Mill, South Carolina, who transferred to North Carolina from Florida. He was rated the nation's top long snapping prospect by Rubio Long Snapping coming out of Fort Mill High School and joined the Gators as a walk-on in 2023. Burt earned Freshman All-SEC recognition in Gainesville after stepping in during games against Tennessee and Kentucky, and he projects as Carolina's primary snapper on placements and punts in 2026.

athletes.name: Peter Pesansky
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pesansky is a redshirt sophomore walk-on offensive lineman from Tampa who played defensive line at Jesuit High School. Rivals ranked him the nation's 24th-best defensive lineman, and he was a four-time all-state pick and two-year captain who totaled 392 tackles, 43 sacks and 59 tackles for loss in four prep seasons. He helped Jesuit win a 6A state championship as a sophomore.

athletes.name: Rowan Byrne
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Byrne signed with North Carolina in January 2026 after one season at Clemson, where he played two snaps in a single game as a true freshman. A multiple-time all-state selection at Iona Prep and ranked among the top offensive line prospects in the 2025 class, the redshirt freshman from Bronxville, New York, is listed at 6-5 and 296 pounds with four years of eligibility.

athletes.name: Jonah Rodriguez
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rodriguez took a winding route to Chapel Hill, signing with San Diego State out of Madison High in his native San Diego, then moving on to Arizona before playing offensive tackle at Southwestern College in Chula Vista. He committed to North Carolina in November 2025 over Colorado and California. The redshirt junior is listed at 6-4 and 294 pounds and adds experience to the line.

athletes.name: Timir Hickman-Collins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hickman-Collins committed to North Carolina in May 2025 after redshirting at Florida State without seeing game action. A three-star prospect ranked among the top recruits in South Carolina, he chose the Seminoles over Georgia Tech coming out of Indian Land High. The redshirt sophomore from Fort Mill is listed at 6-2 and 215 pounds and is competing for rotational linebacker work.

athletes.name: Brandon Homady
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Homady signed with North Carolina in January 2026 after one season at West Virginia, where he appeared in 11 games and played mostly on special teams. He earned all-conference and all-district honors at Padua Franciscan in Cleveland before joining the Mountaineers in the 2025 class. The redshirt freshman is listed at 6-3 and 298 pounds and figures into the interior line depth.

athletes.name: Christo Kelly
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kelly is North Carolina's returning starting center and a team captain who represented the Tar Heels at 2026 ACC Kickoff. He was an All-Patriot League first-team pick at Holy Cross and Bill Belichick's first transfer portal signing at UNC.

athletes.name: Viliami Moala
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moala is a freshman defensive lineman whose hometown Carolina lists as West Valley City, Utah, and who played at Thompson High School in Alabama. He was named a 2024 Under Armour All-American and earned a Polynesian Bowl invitation. He recorded 70 tackles and 15 tackles for loss as a senior on a state finalist team after posting 99 tackles and 12.5 sacks as a junior.

athletes.name: Will Conroy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Conroy is a freshman offensive lineman from Valley View, Ohio, who played his senior season at IMG Academy after starting his career at St. Ignatius. He was a 2025 Under Armour All-American and helped IMG to an undefeated season and the Sunshine State Independent Association championship. He was a captain and an All-Ohio selection at St. Ignatius in 2023 and 2024.

athletes.name: Cristian Alvarez
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alvarez is a freshman offensive lineman from Woodcliff Lake, New Jersey, who prepped at St. Joseph Regional. Carolina's official roster lists him at 6-4 and 285 pounds wearing No. 60 and carries no further biographical details for him.

athletes.name: Zion Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a freshman offensive lineman from Townsend, Delaware, who was a four-year starter at left tackle for DeMatha Catholic. He was a first team All-WCAC selection in 2024 and 2025 and captained a senior team that went 11-0 and won the WCAC championship, part of a 21-game winning streak. His cousin Earl Winfield played football at Carolina from 1982 to 1985.

athletes.name: Dujuan Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davis is a freshman offensive lineman from Clearwater, Florida, who prepped at Clearwater Central Catholic. Carolina's official roster lists him at 6-9 and 380 pounds wearing No. 67 and carries no further biographical details for him.

athletes.name: Aidan Banfield
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Banfield is a junior offensive lineman from Buford, Georgia, listed at 6-foot-3 and 300 pounds. He came to North Carolina from Mill Creek High School, where he was a two-time all-state selection, and started 11 games as a true freshman in 2024 on a line that blocked for All-American running back Omarion Hampton. Banfield earned FWAA Freshman All-America honors that season, the first Carolina offensive lineman to be recognized by the organization, and returns as a starter.

athletes.name: Byron Nelson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nelson is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Katy, Texas, who enrolled early after a four-year lettering career at Katy High School. A three-star prospect, he started 20 varsity games and allowed only one sack, earning first-team all-district honors and a captaincy. He helped Katy reach the state championship game at 11-2 as a senior behind a rushing offense averaging 229.1 yards.

athletes.name: Jacqawn McRoy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McRoy is North Carolina's projected starting right tackle, a 6-foot-8, 335-pound transfer from Arkansas who began his career at Oregon as a four-star recruit out of Clay-Chalkville (Ala.).

athletes.name: Eidan Buchanan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Buchanan is a sophomore offensive lineman at North Carolina and one of the largest players on the roster at 6-9 and 330 pounds in No. 72. The Montgomery Village, Maryland native appeared in 10 games as a freshman in 2025, starting the season opener against TCU and also playing special teams. North Carolina lists him out of Watkins Mill, and he played offensive tackle at Our Lady of Good Counsel, earning 2024 All-WCAC first team honors.

athletes.name: J.B. Shabazz
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Shabazz is a freshman offensive lineman from Winston-Salem, North Carolina, who played at Oak Grove High School. He was a two-time All-Conference lineman across stops at Oak Grove and East Forsyth, and he helped Oak Grove reach the third round of the NCHSAA 5A playoffs as a senior. He also earned All-Conference honors in basketball.

athletes.name: Nick Fiumara
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fiumara is a freshman offensive lineman from Foxboro, Massachusetts, who started four years at Belmont Hill. He was named to the Massachusetts High School Football Coaches Association Super 26 team and the Boston Herald All-Scholastic team, captained as a senior, and did not allow a sack as a junior on a NEPSAC championship team. He also earned All-New England honors in the discus.

athletes.name: Andrew Threatt
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Threatt is North Carolina's projected starting right guard, a senior transfer from Charleston Southern who started at both right tackle and left guard across three seasons there.

athletes.name: Trey Blue
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Blue committed to North Carolina in September 2023, more than a year before signing, and stayed home after a three-year starting career at Cary High that included a Shrine Bowl selection. The three-star tackle also held offers from Maryland and Charlotte. Now a redshirt freshman listed at 6-6 and 330 pounds, he is working into the offensive line rotation.

athletes.name: Anthony Hall
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hall is a freshman offensive lineman from Brookline, Massachusetts, who played at Dexter Southfield. He earned All-NEPSAC honors during his high school career and was also a member of his school's track program before arriving in Chapel Hill. His brother, Leroy Brown, played college football at UMass Dartmouth.

athletes.name: Kymistrii Young
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Young is a freshman wide receiver from Parrish, Florida, who played at Cardinal Mooney Catholic. He caught 43 passes for 947 yards and eight touchdowns in 13 games as a senior. As a junior he had 25 receptions for 626 yards and 10 touchdowns, and as a sophomore he added 22 catches for 433 yards and 10 scores.

athletes.name: Keeyun Chapman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chapman is a freshman wide receiver from Jackson, Alabama, who played at Jackson High School. He posted his biggest prep season as a junior with 51 catches for 1,322 yards and 19 touchdowns, then had 15 receptions for 278 yards and two touchdowns in six games as a senior. He also competed in basketball and track in high school.

athletes.name: Carnell Warren
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Warren is a freshman wide receiver from Bluffton, South Carolina, who played at Bluffton High School. He earned Under Armour All-America honors and was a three-time All-Region selection, catching 62 passes for 977 yards and 11 touchdowns in 11 games as a senior after 56 receptions for 856 yards and 14 scores as a junior. He was also an All-State basketball player.

athletes.name: Shamar Easter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Easter is a tight end in North Carolina's rotation who transferred from Arkansas, where he was the No. 10 tight end nationally in the 2023 recruiting class and the top prospect in his state.

athletes.name: Dream Rashad
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rashad is a freshman tight end from Buford, Georgia, who played quarterback at Buford High School. He helped Buford win the 6A All-Region championship and was a second team All-Region selection as a junior, when he also earned Gwinnett Daily Post Player of the Week honors. He took the team academic award in 2024 with a grade point average above 4.0.

athletes.name: Madrid Tucker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tucker signed with North Carolina in 2025 after a Fort Myers High career that produced 95 receptions for 1,828 yards and 24 touchdowns, plus 753 rushing yards. A three-sport athlete, he chose the Tar Heels over West Virginia. The redshirt freshman from Lehigh Acres, Florida, is listed at 5-10 and 170 pounds and is competing for reps in a deep receiver group.

athletes.name: Carson Sneed
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sneed is a freshman tight end from Nashville, Tennessee, who played at Donelson Christian Academy. He earned All-State honors as both a sophomore and a junior, catching 38 passes for 540 yards and six touchdowns in his junior season. He also played basketball and ran track, and his brother Dayton is a member of the Carolina football program.

athletes.name: Deems May
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: May is a redshirt senior walk-on tight end from Charlotte who played at Myers Park. He appeared in every game in 2024 as a special teams contributor and made his first career start in the Duke's Mayo Bowl in 2023. His father, Deems, played at Carolina from 1987 to 1991 and in the NFL with the Chargers and Seahawks, and his mother, Susan, was a Carolina gymnast.

athletes.name: Vodney Cleveland
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cleveland is a freshman defensive lineman from Montgomery, Alabama, who played at Parker High School. He was selected for the 2025 Mississippi-Alabama All-Star Game and named an Army Bowl All-Star. He recorded 37 tackles as a senior and helped Parker win a state championship as a junior, when he posted 50 tackles, 10 tackles for loss and seven sacks.

athletes.name: Emmanuel Nwaiwu
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nwaiwu is a redshirt freshman defensive lineman from Chateauguay, Quebec, who came to Carolina after playing on the defensive line for Vanier College in Montreal. He was rated a three-star prospect by 247Sports, which ranked him the No. 152 edge rusher in his class.

athletes.name: Xavier Lewis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lewis reached North Carolina by an unusual path, having been recruited by Austin Peay before his Rolesville High coach recommended him to the Tar Heels staff. The Raleigh native is now a sophomore defensive lineman listed at 6-0 and 250 pounds, wearing No. 90 and working for interior snaps in the 2026 rotation.

athletes.name: Adam McCann-Gibbs
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McCann-Gibbs flipped from a Penn State pledge to North Carolina in November 2025 and enrolled in January. A native of Northern Ireland with a background in soccer and Gaelic football, he took up the sport only in 2025 and developed through the Leader Kicking programme. The freshman is listed at 6-0 and 208 pounds and is in the mix for punting duties.

athletes.name: Leroy Jackson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson is North Carolina's returning starting defensive tackle, recording 37 tackles in 2025 as the interior anchor next to edge rusher Melkart Abou Jaoude.

athletes.name: Aeron Burrell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Burrell is a junior kicker from Bossier City, Louisiana, who transferred to North Carolina from LSU in January 2026. A Parkway High School product rated among the top kicking prospects in the 2024 recruiting class, he spent two seasons in Baton Rouge as the Tigers' kickoff specialist. In 2024 he handled 74 kickoffs with a touchback rate near 89 percent, which led the SEC and ranked third nationally. He has two seasons of eligibility with the Tar Heels.

athletes.name: Jimmy-Phrisco Alo-Suliafu
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alo-Suliafu is a freshman defensive lineman whose hometown Carolina lists as Hau'ula, Hawaii, and who attended Jordan High School in Fulshear, Texas. He was named a MaxPreps All-American, a Polynesian Bowl All-American and a member of the All-Greater Houston Touchdown Club. As a senior he had 37 tackles, 13 tackles for loss, four sacks and two forced fumbles.

athletes.name: Jacob Horvath
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Horvath is a redshirt junior punter from Melbourne, Australia, who signed with North Carolina in April 2025 after two seasons at Eastern Illinois. Listed at 6-foot-1 and 190 pounds, he attended McKinnon Secondary College in Victoria and came to American football through the Pro Kick Australia program. Horvath averaged 44.3 yards on 54 punts for the Panthers and earned second-team All-Big South/OVC recognition, and he is in line to handle punting duties for the Tar Heels.

athletes.name: Trashawn Ruffin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ruffin is a freshman defensive lineman from Calypso, North Carolina, who played at North Duplin High School. He was a four-time all-conference selection and a senior captain who recorded 47 tackles, 12 tackles for loss and three sacks in 11 games while leading North Duplin to a 10-2 record. He had 52 tackles and four sacks as a sophomore.

athletes.name: David Jackson III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson is a freshman defensive lineman from Washington, D.C., who played at Our Lady of Good Counsel. He was a two-time first team All-WCAC selection as a junior and senior after second team honors as a sophomore, and he posted 115 tackles and 36 tackles for loss as a junior. His father, David, has played professional basketball overseas for 18 seasons.

athletes.name: Daniel Anderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anderson is a redshirt sophomore linebacker from Memphis who came to North Carolina out of Germantown High School. He redshirted in 2024, then appeared in 11 games in 2025 as a primary special teams contributor, recording three tackles including two against Richmond. A three-star early enrollee, he was a two-time team captain in high school and posted 103 tackles and 18 sacks over three varsity seasons.

athletes.name: Nicco Maggio
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Maggio flipped his commitment from Wake Forest to North Carolina in January 2025 after a Buford High career that produced 58 tackles, 12 stops for loss and 5.5 sacks, including 40 tackles and 10 tackles for loss as a senior. The redshirt freshman from Buford, Georgia, is listed at 6-1 and 290 pounds and provides interior defensive line depth.

UNLV carries him at 6-5 and 350 pounds, the heaviest listing among the team's freshman linemen.

athletes.name: Poe Purcell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He was a unanimous three-star recruit rated the No. 9 prospect in Nevada by Rivals and chose UNLV over Cal and Kansas State. After two seasons at Eldorado High, he transferred to Bishop Gorman and recorded 65 tackles with 28 tackles for loss as a senior on an 11-1 state championship team.

athletes.name: Griffin Scroggs
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He began his career at Georgia, redshirting on the Bulldogs' 2022 national championship team, then played 36 games with nine starts over three seasons at Appalachian State, including five starts at left guard in 2024. A redshirt senior from Grayson, Georgia, the 6-foot-3, 330-pound lineman is expected to compete for a starting spot on the Rebels' interior line.

athletes.name: Andrew O'Reilly
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Josh Haney

athletes.blurb: Josh Haney is a freshman offensive lineman who wears No. 60 for UNLV. The Rebels list his hometown as Mission Viejo, California, and his high school as JSerra Catholic. UNLV carries him at 6-4 and 280 pounds.

athletes.name: Fuad Maali
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
