athletes.name: Eli Sanchez
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sanchez is a true freshman interior offensive lineman from Sandusky, Ohio, joining the Rebels line room in 2026. A unanimous three-star recruit ranked the No. 81 interior lineman nationally by ESPN, he chose UNLV over Virginia Tech among several FBS offers. He lettered four seasons at Perkins High, earned first team Northwest District lineman honors and helped the Pirates go 14-2 and win a regional championship in 2024.

athletes.name: Joe Metzger
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Joe Metzger transferred to UNLV from Holy Cross, where he started all 12 games he played in 2025, splitting time between right tackle and left guard, after starting eight games the previous season on a line that led the Patriot League in fewest sacks allowed. A 6-foot-5, 310-pound senior from Franklinville, New Jersey, he also competed for Holy Cross's track and field team and owns the school's outdoor shot put record.

athletes.name: Ace Robinson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ace Robinson is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman wearing No. 65 for UNLV. He is from Oakland, California, and played at De La Salle High School. The Rebels roster lists him at 6-4 and 285 pounds.

athletes.name: BJ Tolo
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: BJ Tolo transferred to UNLV from New Mexico State, where he was a two-year starter who played right guard, left guard and center and started all 12 games on the Aggies' offensive line in 2025. A redshirt junior from Santa Ana, California, the 6-foot-1, 320-pound interior lineman played in Las Cruces under former UNLV head coach Tony Sanchez and adds versatile, experienced depth to the Rebels' front for 2026.

athletes.name: Malik White
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Malik White is a freshman offensive lineman who wears No. 67 for UNLV. He comes from Rancho Cucamonga, California, and played at Rancho Cucamonga High School. The Rebels roster lists him at 6-5 and 305 pounds.

athletes.name: Ivan Peña
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ivan Pena is a freshman offensive lineman for UNLV who wears No. 68. He is from Las Vegas, and the Rebels list two high schools for him, Sierra Canyon High School in California and Bishop Gorman High School at home in Las Vegas. UNLV carries him at 6-6 and 345 pounds, making him one of the largest linemen on the roster.

athletes.name: Alekai Afoa
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alekai Afoa is a junior offensive lineman for UNLV who wears No. 70. He comes from San Ramon, California, where he played at California High School, and reached the Rebels through Diablo Valley College. UNLV lists him at 6-4 and 295 pounds and carries him as a squad member rather than a scholarship signee.

athletes.name: Ed Haynes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ed Haynes is a sophomore offensive lineman wearing No. 71 for UNLV. He is from Henderson, Nevada, and played at Liberty High School. The Rebels roster lists him at 6-4 and 310 pounds.

athletes.name: Will Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is UNLV's projected starting left tackle, a 6-foot-7 senior who transferred in from New Mexico State.

athletes.name: Jesus Garcia II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jesus Garcia II is a freshman offensive lineman who wears No. 73 for UNLV. He comes from southeast San Diego, California, and played at Lincoln High School. The Rebels roster lists him at 6-5 and 290 pounds.

athletes.name: Amare Taase
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taase is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Scottsdale, Arizona, competing for a spot in the Rebels line rotation in 2026. He appeared in four games in 2025 after not playing in 2024. A three-star recruit rated by ESPN as the No. 112 offensive guard nationally and the No. 39 prospect in Arizona, he was an all-conference senior blocker at Saguaro High and chose UNLV over Hawai'i and New Mexico State.

athletes.name: Mateo Bilaver
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bilaver is a true freshman offensive tackle from North Hollywood, California, adding to the Rebels line depth in 2026. He was a unanimous three-star recruit listed as the No. 92 player in California by Rivals and was named the 2025 Mission League most valuable lineman after his senior season. He blocked for a Chaminade College Prep team that twice reached the CIF Southern Section semifinals.

athletes.name: Chrysanthos Fetokakis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fetokakis is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Houston who was a member of the UNLV squad in 2025 but did not appear in a game. He is competing for line depth in 2026. He spent four seasons at Strake Jesuit College Prep, where he played guard and center and helped the Crusaders reach the third round of the Texas playoffs as a senior.

athletes.name: Colton Thomasson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomasson is a 6-foot-8 redshirt junior offensive lineman who transferred to UNLV from Baylor after beginning his career at Texas A&M and is the Rebels' top backup at both left tackle and left guard.

athletes.name: Jackson Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is UNLV's projected starting right tackle after transferring from Pittsburgh, where he landed following the start of his career at California.

athletes.name: Austin Boyd
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Boyd is UNLV's returning starting center and a 2026 preseason All-Mountain West selection who has started all 14 games in each of his three seasons with the Rebels.

athletes.name: Jesse Harden
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jesse Harden is a freshman wide receiver wearing No. 80 for UNLV. He is from Tampa, Florida, and played at Spoto High School. The Rebels roster lists him at 6-3 and 185 pounds.

athletes.name: Vincent Carner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Vincent Carner is a freshman wide receiver who wears No. 81 for UNLV. He comes from Newbury Park, California, and played at Newbury Park High School. The Rebels roster lists him at 6-4 and 205 pounds.

athletes.name: Peyton Zachary
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Peyton Zachary is a freshman wide receiver wearing No. 82 for UNLV. He is from Atlanta, Georgia, and played at Carrollton High School. The Rebels roster lists him at 5-8 and 170 pounds.

athletes.name: Cassidee Miles
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Miles is a redshirt freshman receiver listed from Fort Worth, Texas, who appeared in one game against Hawai'i in 2025 and is competing for rotation snaps in 2026. He was a unanimous three-star recruit rated the No. 4 wide receiver in Arizona by ESPN while at Central High in Phoenix, and he chose UNLV over Arizona, Iowa State, Kansas State, Oregon and Bowling Green.

athletes.name: Keyan Burnett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Burnett is a senior tight end who transferred to UNLV from Arizona and projects as a co-starter at the position in Dan Mullen's 2026 offense.

athletes.name: Matt Byrnes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Matt Byrnes returns to UNLV's tight end room in 2026 after appearing in all 14 games in 2025, when he caught two passes for 24 yards. The 6-foot-6 senior from Chicago began his career at Iowa Western Community College and then played 25 games with four starts at Houston, catching 10 passes for 94 yards and a touchdown while earning academic all-conference honors in both the AAC and the Big 12. He is also a repeat Academic All-Mountain West honoree with the Rebels.

athletes.name: David Titone-Perez
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: David Titone-Perez is a sophomore wide receiver who wears No. 86 for UNLV. He comes from Hacienda Heights, California, and played at Los Altos High School. The Rebels roster lists him at 6-0 and 170 pounds.

athletes.name: Demari Nunley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Demari Nunley is a freshman wide receiver wearing No. 87 for UNLV. He is from Los Angeles, California, and played at St. Pius X-St. Matthias Academy. The Rebels roster lists him at 6-3 and 195 pounds.

athletes.name: Mo Abbasher
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Abbasher is a junior defensive lineman from Coppell, Texas, who came to UNLV by way of Navarro College. He was a member of the squad in 2025 but did not appear in a game, and he is working for a spot in the Rebels defensive line rotation in 2026. He is listed on the official roster at 6-3 and 305 pounds.

athletes.name: Velltray Jefferson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jefferson is a senior tight end from Fresno, California, who appeared in all 14 games in 2025 and earned Academic All Mountain West recognition. He reached UNLV after a season at Fresno State and two years at Fresno City College. A three-star recruit out of Edison High, he originally signed with Utah as a linebacker. He returns as a rotational tight end for the Rebels in 2026.

athletes.name: Andreas Diaz-Nicolaidis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Andreas Diaz-Nicolaidis is a freshman tight end who wears No. 89 for UNLV. The Rebels list his hometown as Portland, Oregon, and his high school as Bishop Gorman in Las Vegas. UNLV carries him at 6-3 and 250 pounds.

athletes.name: Eliah Logo
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Logo appeared in five games as a freshman in 2025 and recorded four tackles, positioning him for more defensive line snaps in 2026. The Henderson, Nevada native is the son of UNLV defensive line coach Ricky Logo. He was a three-star recruit ranked the No. 2 defensive lineman in Nevada by 247Sports and posted 48 tackles with nine sacks at Liberty High.

athletes.name: Elias Rudolph
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Elias Rudolph was a consensus four-star recruit and ESPN300 member in the 2024 class who chose Miami over offers from Florida State, Georgia, Michigan and Ohio State. After redshirting with the Hurricanes, he transferred to UNLV and played all 14 games in 2025, recording 10 tackles and 1.5 sacks, including a sack in a win at Colorado State. A redshirt sophomore from Deerfield Beach, Florida, the 6-foot-5 edge rusher is positioned for an expanded pass-rush role in 2026.

athletes.name: Herb Gray
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Herb Gray adds size to UNLV's defensive line as a 6-foot-3, 275-pound transfer from Tennessee, where he redshirted in 2024 and made his college debut in 2025 against East Tennessee State, recording one tackle and half a tackle for loss. A redshirt sophomore from Upper Marlboro, Maryland, he was a three-star recruit at Charles Herbert Flowers High School according to both On3 and 247Sports.

athletes.name: Lucas Conti
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Conti is UNLV's returning starting defensive tackle and a 2026 preseason All-Mountain West selection after recording 22 tackles, four tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks in 12 games in 2025.

athletes.name: Bryce Waters
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bryce Waters is a freshman defensive lineman wearing No. 95 for UNLV. He is from Tampa, Florida, and played at Carrollwood Day High School. The Rebels roster lists him at 6-4 and 320 pounds.

athletes.name: Prin Fox
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fox is a true freshman defensive lineman from Cashmere, Washington, joining the Rebels front in 2026. A unanimous three-star recruit ranked among the top 15 prospects in Washington, he chose UNLV over Arizona, Wake Forest and Boston College. He was a two-time all-conference selection and the 2025 SCAC lineman of the year at Cashmere High, helping the Bulldogs to an 11-2 record and a Class 1A state championship appearance.

athletes.name: Bryce Robinson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bryce Robinson is a freshman defensive lineman who wears No. 97 for UNLV. He comes from Marietta, Georgia, and played at Locust Grove High School. The Rebels roster lists him at 6-3 and 280 pounds.

athletes.name: Jordan Covington
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Covington is a redshirt freshman defensive lineman from McKinney, Texas, who was on the roster in 2025 without appearing in a game and is competing for rotation snaps in 2026. A unanimous three-star recruit listed as the No. 14 defensive lineman in Texas by 247Sports, he was previously committed to Oklahoma State. He recorded 71 tackles, 15 tackles for loss and nine sacks at McKinney High.

athletes.name: Landen Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a projected starting defensive lineman for the UNLV Rebels out of Zachary, La., after transferring from Arizona State.

athletes.name: Carson Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams arrives in Bloomington after two seasons at Montana State, where the Houston, Texas, native appeared in 20 games with seven starts and forced three career turnovers. The redshirt sophomore cornerback made his first collegiate start against Idaho State in 2025 and recorded at least one tackle in all 16 games that fall. He earned first team All-District 14-6A honors at Westfield High School with three interceptions and 21 pass breakups as a senior. He projects as secondary depth in 2026.

athletes.name: Amare Ferrell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ferrell is Indiana's returning starting free safety, recording 48 tackles, seven passes defended and four sacks across all 16 games of the 2025 national title season.

athletes.name: Turbo Richard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Richard is a projected co-starter at running back and Indiana's top kickoff return option after transferring from Boston College, where he led the Eagles with 749 rushing yards and nine touchdowns while adding 30 catches.

athletes.name: Byron Baldwin Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Baldwin is a sophomore safety from Baltimore and was Indiana's highest-rated signee in the 2025 recruiting class. A four-star Top247 prospect out of St. Frances Academy, he was ranked the nation's No. 21 safety and the No. 11 recruit in Maryland, and he was selected as an Under Armour All-American. Baldwin enrolled early in January 2025 and worked with the first-team defense for stretches of his first training camp. He is positioned to compete for a starting safety job in 2026.

athletes.name: Grant Wilson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilson is a graduate quarterback from Arlington, Virginia, who has appeared in 25 career games with 14 starts across stops at Fordham and Old Dominion. He accounted for 21 total touchdowns while starting 11 games for Old Dominion in 2023, then played three games for Indiana in 2025. He holds a finance degree and is pursuing an MBA at the Kelley School of Business. He figures as an experienced backup behind Josh Hoover.

athletes.name: Jaylen Bell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bell played in 14 games as a true freshman in 2025, one of 12 Hoosiers to debut that season, and made his first collegiate tackle against Indiana State before posting three stops at Maryland. The sophomore cornerback, listed from Union, New Jersey, attended Grayson High School in Georgia and was a consensus three star prospect ranked among the top 60 defensive backs nationally. He is competing for rotation and special teams snaps.

athletes.name: Kortez Rupert
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kortez Rupert is a freshman wide receiver from East Saint Louis, Illinois, who played for East Saint Louis High School. He was a consensus three-star recruit and earned Illinois High School Football Coaches Association first-team Class 6A all-state honors as a senior, when he caught 30 passes for 679 yards and 10 touchdowns. He helped the Flyers win a Class 6A state title as a freshman and finish state runner-up as a senior.

athletes.name: Davion Chandler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chandler saw action in seven games as a true freshman in 2025 and turned his first collegiate catch into a 65 yard touchdown at Purdue. The Indianapolis native starred at Lawrence North, where he was a four star recruit per On3, the No. 37 receiver nationally, and a two time Marion County Offensive Player of the Year with 2,039 career receiving yards. The sophomore is competing for rotation snaps at receiver.

athletes.name: A.J. Harris
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Harris is a projected starting cornerback for Indiana after transferring from Penn State, where he made 26 starts in 27 games and recorded 81 tackles and six pass breakups. He began his career at Georgia.

athletes.name: Rolijah Hardy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hardy is Indiana's returning starting linebacker and the Big Ten's preseason Defensive Player of the Year, leading the Hoosiers with 102 tackles, 15 tackles for loss and eight sacks in 2025.

athletes.name: Lebron Bond
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bond appeared in 13 games as a true freshman in 2025, debuting against Old Dominion and catching his first collegiate pass in that opener. The sophomore receiver from Norfolk, Virginia, helped Maury High School win the 2023 Virginia Class 5 state title and was rated the No. 51 receiver nationally by ESPN. Listed at 5-9, he profiles as a slot and special teams contributor this fall.

athletes.name: Preston Zachman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zachman is a redshirt senior safety from Elysburg, Pennsylvania, who joined Indiana from Wisconsin in January 2026 as the Hoosiers' first transfer portal commitment of the cycle. A three-star recruit from Southern Columbia Area, where he played on three Pennsylvania state title teams, he appeared in 35 games with 20 starts for the Badgers and recorded 130 tackles and seven interceptions. He started all 12 games in 2024 and brings experience and versatility to an Indiana secondary in need of a veteran.

athletes.name: Chiddi Obiazor
athletes.source: Estimate (reported at ~$1.5M in published 2026 Indiana defensive-line NIL spending breakdowns; not a disclosed contract figure)
athletes.blurb: Obiazor is a projected starting defensive end for Indiana after transferring from Kansas State, where he earned honorable mention All-Big 12 honors. He is part of a rebuilt edge group replacing Mikail Kamara.

athletes.name: Shazz Preston
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Preston joins Indiana as a redshirt senior after 31 career games between Alabama and Tulane. He started 13 of 14 games for Tulane in 2025, caught a pass in every game, and posted 125 yards on five receptions against Ole Miss in the College Football Playoff. The Saint James, Louisiana, native was a consensus four star recruit and a top 90 national prospect. He adds veteran depth to the receiver rotation.

athletes.name: Josh Burnham
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Burnham is a projected starting defensive end for Indiana after transferring from Notre Dame, where he appeared in 40 career games. He has one season of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Tyler Morris
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Morris is Indiana's projected starting slot receiver and top punt-return option after transferring from Michigan and missing the 2025 national championship season with a knee injury. He spent three seasons at Michigan, including its 2023 national title team.

athletes.name: Seaonta Stewart Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stewart redshirted in 2025 without game action and enters 2026 as a redshirt freshman safety looking for rotation and special teams snaps. The Cincinnati native was a consensus three star prospect out of Winton Woods, rated the No. 19 defensive back nationally by Rivals and a top 65 recruit in Ohio. He recorded 12 tackles and eight pass breakups as a senior and won an Ohio Division I title as a freshman.

athletes.name: Ryland Gandy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gandy is a redshirt senior cornerback from Buford, Georgia, who transferred to Indiana from Pittsburgh in January 2025. A three-star recruit in the 2022 class, he chose the Panthers over offers that included Notre Dame, Penn State, Michigan State and North Carolina, then reached starter status in 2024 with 40 tackles and a tackle for loss. He enters the 2026 season as one of the leading candidates for the Hoosiers' second starting cornerback job.

athletes.name: Josh Hoover
athletes.source: Reported ~$2.5M NIL valuation/package on transferring from TCU to Indiana (On3 profile valuation cited as high as ~$4M; exact deal terms not disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Hoover is Indiana's starting quarterback in 2026 after transferring from TCU, where he threw for 3,472 yards with 29 touchdowns and 13 interceptions in 2025. He entered the season as the active FBS leader in career passing yards and passing touchdowns.

athletes.name: Nick Marsh
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation ~$725K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Marsh is Indiana's projected No. 1 outside receiver after transferring from Michigan State, where he caught 59 passes for 662 yards and six touchdowns in 2025. He was Indiana's top-rated portal addition and is a projected 2027 first-round pick.

athletes.name: Jacob Bell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jacob Bell is a redshirt freshman quarterback from Naperville, Illinois. At Naperville North he set school single-season records with 3,082 passing yards and 38 touchdown passes as a senior, earning all-state recognition from the Illinois High School Football Coaches Association and Player of the Year honors from the Naperville Sun and Daily Herald. He redshirted his first college season in 2025 without appearing in a game.

athletes.name: Tobi Osunsanmi
athletes.source: Estimate (reported at ~$1.5M in published 2026 Indiana defensive-line NIL spending breakdowns; not a disclosed contract figure)
athletes.blurb: Osunsanmi is Indiana's highest-rated defensive transfer addition for 2026, arriving from Kansas State to compete for the starting 'Stud' edge role. He is one of four candidates for two starting spots on a fully rebuilt edge group.

athletes.name: Quan Sanks
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sanks transfers in from Cincinnati, where the junior safety appeared in 24 games with 12 starts over two seasons and created four turnovers. He became the first true freshman to start a Bearcats season opener since 2015 and started seven games in 2025. The Columbus, Georgia, native was a consensus three star recruit at Central in Alabama and earned second team all state honors. He should push for immediate rotation work.

athletes.name: Maverick Geske
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Maverick Geske is a redshirt freshman quarterback from Indianapolis who joined Indiana as a walk-on. At Brebeuf Jesuit he was a finalist for Indiana Mr. Football and a two-time Indiana Football Coaches Association all-state pick, finishing with school records of 8,904 career passing yards and 104 touchdown passes. He led the state with 4,039 passing yards as a senior and redshirted in 2025.

athletes.name: Kaiden Turner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Turner is a redshirt senior linebacker from Fayetteville, Arkansas, who played 13 games with one start in 2025 and intercepted his first career pass at Maryland. He also fielded a blocked punt against Oregon. An Academic All-Big Ten honoree who has earned his degree in sport marketing and management, he was ranked the No. 31 linebacker nationally by ESPN out of Fayetteville High School. He returns as veteran depth and a special teams regular.

athletes.name: Tyler Cherry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cherry is a redshirt freshman quarterback from Greenwood, Indiana, who debuted against Western Illinois in 2024 but did not play in 2025 and served as a student assistant coach. He was a four star recruit and the No. 105 overall prospect per On3 after going 23-4 as the starter at Center Grove, where he set school records with 5,461 passing yards and 56 touchdown passes. He sits behind Josh Hoover in 2026.

athletes.name: Nico Radicic
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Radicic is a redshirt junior kicker from Coppell, Texas, and one of the more decorated specialists in the Big Ten. Rated the No. 3 kicker in the 2023 class, he made 10 of 11 field goals and all 69 extra point attempts in 2024 before earning Big Ten Kicker of the Year honors and first-team All-Big Ten recognition in 2025. Born in California and raised partly in Croatia, he took up place-kicking in eighth grade and returns as Indiana's starter.

athletes.name: Jamar Owens
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jamar Owens is a freshman safety from Jonesboro, Georgia, who finished his prep career at Douglas County High School after three seasons at Jonesboro. A consensus three-star recruit, he recorded 70 tackles, three interceptions and two forced fumbles as a junior and earned All-Region 3-6A honors as a sophomore. He helped Jonesboro reach the Georgia Class 6A state semifinals.

athletes.name: Daniel Ndukwe
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ndukwe is a junior edge rusher from Lithonia, Georgia, who emerged during Indiana's 2025 postseason run. He played all 12 games as a true freshman in 2024, mostly on special teams, recording one tackle and two blocked kicks. He made his first career start in the Peach Bowl against Oregon and posted three tackles, two sacks, a forced fumble and a blocked punt, finishing the postseason with seven tackles and two sacks. The Arabia Mountain High School product has secured a spot in the Hoosiers defensive end rotation.

athletes.name: Jackson Wasserstrom
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson Wasserstrom is a redshirt senior wide receiver from Westfield, Indiana, who joined Indiana as a walk-on in 2022. He caught 29 passes for 529 yards and four touchdowns as a senior at Westfield High School. He appeared in seven games in 2025 and caught his first collegiate pass against Kennesaw State. He has repeatedly earned Academic All-Big Ten honors.

athletes.name: Parker Elmore
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Parker Elmore is a freshman tight end from Columbus, Indiana, who played at Columbus North High School. A consensus three-star recruit and consensus top-five prospect in Indiana, he was rated the No. 16 tight end nationally by ESPN. As a senior he led Columbus North with 58 receptions, 927 receiving yards and 13 touchdown catches, and earned all-conference honors.

athletes.name: Billy Gowers
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gowers is a sophomore punter from Melbourne, Australia, who transferred to Indiana from Hawaii in January 2026. He played five seasons of professional Australian rules football in the AFL before training with Prokick Australia and converting to American football. In his first college season in 2025 he averaged 46.2 yards on 49 punts, ranking 10th nationally, with 18 kicks traveling more than 50 yards and a long of 67. He arrives to replace departing Hoosiers punter Mitch McCarthy.

athletes.name: Zacharey Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zacharey Smith is a redshirt freshman cornerback from Union City, Georgia, who played at Hapeville Charter Academy. A consensus three-star recruit, he led Georgia with eight interceptions as a junior and was a first-team All-Region 6-4A selection that season. As a senior he added 20 tackles, seven interceptions and 10 pass breakups. He redshirted in 2025.

athletes.name: Sean Cuono
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sean Cuono is a redshirt freshman running back from Clearwater, Florida, who finished high school at Clearwater Central Catholic after two seasons at Calvary Christian. A consensus three-star recruit, he rushed for 3,328 career yards and 34 touchdowns, including 1,786 yards as a sophomore. He made his college debut against Indiana State and gained 17 yards on two carries.

athletes.name: Jacob Savage
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jacob Savage is a freshman linebacker from Union, Kentucky, who played at Ryle High School. He won the Paul Hornung Award as Kentucky's top high school football player as a senior and finished his career with a program-record 511 tackles and 39 tackles for loss. He led the state with 163 tackles as a sophomore and helped Ryle to a Class 6A runner-up finish.

athletes.name: Jayreon Campbell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jayreon Campbell is a freshman running back from Powder Springs, Georgia, who played at McEachern High School. A consensus three-star recruit rated among the top 70 running backs nationally, he rushed for 930 yards and 18 touchdowns on 168 carries as a junior. He earned Class 6A honorable mention all-state that season and first-team all-region as a sophomore.

athletes.name: Jamari Sharpe
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sharpe is Indiana's returning starting cornerback and the surest lock in the secondary, posting 50 tackles, six tackles for loss and six pass breakups in 16 games in 2025.

athletes.name: Henry Ohlinger
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Henry Ohlinger is a freshman linebacker from Columbus, Ohio, who played linebacker and running back at Grandview Heights High School. Rated a four-star prospect by ESPN and Rivals/On3, he was a two-time Ohio Division VI All-Ohio selection. He rushed for 1,582 yards and 27 touchdowns as a junior and added 1,322 yards and 16 scores as a sophomore.

athletes.name: Ja'Dyn Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ja'Dyn Williams is a freshman linebacker from Massillon, Ohio, who played at Washington High School. Rated a four-star prospect by 247Sports and the No. 11 recruit in Ohio, he posted 115 tackles, 12.5 tackles for loss and seven sacks as a senior and earned first-team All-Northeast Inland District. He helped the Tigers win an Ohio Division I state title as a sophomore.

athletes.name: D'Montae Tims
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: D'Montae Tims is a freshman safety from Tampa, Florida, who played at Armwood High School. A consensus three-star recruit rated among the top 50 safeties nationally, he recorded 50 tackles, 12 tackles for loss and two sacks as a senior, adding three forced fumbles and two interceptions. He was a second-team All-Western Conference pick as a junior.

athletes.name: Cade Kaiser
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cade Kaiser is a redshirt freshman wide receiver from Batesville, Indiana, who joined Indiana as a walk-on. At Batesville High School he caught 91 passes for 1,354 yards and 23 touchdowns, setting a program record with 17 receiving touchdowns as a junior. He also lettered in basketball, earning Indiana Basketball Coaches Association all-state honors as a junior and senior.

athletes.name: Kasmir Hicks
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kasmir Hicks is a freshman cornerback from Indianapolis who played at Decatur Central High School. Rated a four-star prospect by Rivals/On3 and a consensus top-10 recruit in Indiana, he was a two-time Mid-State Conference Defensive Player of the Year. He totaled 103 tackles, seven interceptions and 30 pass breakups, and helped Decatur Central win a Class 5A state title as a junior.

athletes.name: Khobie Martin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Martin is Indiana's leading returning running back, rushing for 505 yards and six touchdowns on 70 carries across 14 games in 2025. Pro Football Focus rated him the No. 3 returning Big Ten running back entering 2026.

athletes.name: Lee Beebe Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Beebe is a redshirt senior running back from Montgomery, Alabama, who transferred in from UAB, where he earned third team All-American Athletic Conference honors in 2024 while starting 10 games. He owns 1,485 career rushing yards and 13 total touchdowns. He played three games for Indiana in 2025, running for 90 yards and a touchdown against Kennesaw State before a season ending injury. He returns as backfield depth.

athletes.name: PJ Nelson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nelson played two games as a true freshman in 2025 and made his first collegiate tackle on kickoff coverage. The redshirt freshman linebacker from Cincinnati was a consensus three star recruit out of Princeton High School and was named Ohio Prep Sports Writers Association Defensive Player of the Year as a junior. He totaled 137 tackles with 24 tackles for loss and eight sacks as a senior. He is competing for rotation and special teams snaps.

athletes.name: Anthony Chung
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anthony Chung is a redshirt junior safety from Mequon, Wisconsin, who joined Indiana as a walk-on in 2023. At Homestead High School he was a first-team all-state pick by the Associated Press and the Wisconsin Football Coaches Association and the North Shore Conference Defensive Back of the Year as a senior. He appeared in all 16 games in 2025, mostly on special teams.

athletes.name: Garrett Reese
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reese appeared in 10 games as a true freshman in 2025, debuting in the opener against Old Dominion and recovering a fourth quarter fumble for his first career takeaway. The sophomore safety from Chicago won three Illinois Class 3A state titles at Nazareth Academy and was rated the No. 84 defensive back nationally by ESPN. He also qualified for the state track meet in the triple jump as a junior.

athletes.name: Jeff Utzinger
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Utzinger joined the program as a walk-on in 2022 and was added to scholarship before the 2025 season, in which the Carmel, Indiana, native played all 16 games, mostly on special teams. The redshirt senior linebacker has appeared in 29 career games. He won a Class 5A state title at Cathedral and was a two time Indiana Football Coaches Association all state pick. He remains a special teams regular.

athletes.name: Paddy McAteer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McAteer arrives from Troy, where the redshirt senior kicker appeared in 26 games and set the program record with a 53 yard field goal at Texas State in 2025, earning Sun Belt Special Teams Player of the Week. A native of Mullaghbawn, Ireland, he played Gaelic football before first kicking an American football in April 2024 at age 20. He competes for kicking duties this fall.

athletes.name: Clay Conner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clay Conner is a redshirt junior safety on the Indiana Hoosiers roster. He is from Boonville, Indiana, and played at Boonville High School. He is listed at 6-4 and 206 pounds and wears No. 36.

athletes.name: Heath Kizer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Heath Kizer is a redshirt sophomore safety from Indianapolis who joined Indiana as a walk-on. He played quarterback at North Central High School and was an All-Metropolitan Interscholastic Conference selection as a senior. His father, Bob Kizer, was an Indiana football letterwinner in 1993 and 1994. Kizer earned Academic All-Big Ten in 2025.

athletes.name: Kaden McConnell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kaden McConnell is a redshirt sophomore linebacker from Greenwood, Indiana, who joined Indiana as a walk-on. At Center Grove he made 81 tackles as a senior and was part of a state title team as a junior. He also wrestled, finishing state runner-up at 195 pounds as a junior. He appeared in three games in 2025.

athletes.name: Trevor Gibbs
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Trevor Gibbs is a freshman tight end from Crown Point, Indiana, who played tight end and linebacker at Crown Point High School. A consensus three-star recruit and consensus top-15 prospect in Indiana, he was a two-time Duneland Athletic Conference Defensive MVP. He caught 35 passes for 600 yards as a junior and added 60 tackles on defense.

athletes.name: Quentin Clark
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clark played 14 games in 2025, mostly on special teams, after debuting at Michigan State as a true freshman in 2024. The redshirt sophomore from Dexter, Georgia, was a consensus three star recruit and the No. 26 linebacker nationally per ESPN out of West Laurens, where he posted 105 tackles, six sacks and five forced fumbles as a junior. He is listed on the defensive front for 2026.

athletes.name: Keishaun Calhoun
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Calhoun redshirted in 2025 without game action and enters 2026 as a redshirt freshman defensive lineman seeking rotation snaps. The Groveport, Ohio, native was a consensus three star prospect at Groveport-Madison, ranked among the top 100 defensive linemen nationally by ESPN and On3 and a top 45 recruit in Ohio. He was a first team all conference and second team all district selection as a junior.

athletes.name: Kevontay Hugan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kevontay Hugan is a freshman edge rusher from Sarasota, Florida, who played at Booker High School. A four-star prospect per ESPN and 247Sports, he recorded 118 tackles, 36 tackles for loss and 18 sacks as a junior. He helped Booker reach back to back Florida Class 3A state semifinals and also lettered in track and field as a shot put state qualifier.

athletes.name: Bryce Taylor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bryce Taylor is a redshirt freshman kicker from Bloomington, Indiana, who joined Indiana as a walk-on. At Bloomington South he made 20 of 22 field goals and 149 of 158 extra points, scoring 209 points, and set a school record with a 53-yard field goal in 2024. He was a first-team all-conference pick as a junior and senior.

athletes.name: Amari Kamara
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Amari Kamara is a redshirt freshman linebacker from Ashburn, Virginia, who played at Stone Bridge High School. He recorded 104 tackles and two sacks as a senior and helped Stone Bridge reach the Virginia Class 5A state championship game in 2023. His brother Mikail was a defensive lineman at Indiana and a second-team All-American in 2024.

athletes.name: Sam Lindsey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lindsey is a redshirt junior long snapper from Lilburn, Georgia, who joined Indiana as a walk-on and did not see game action in 2025. He appeared in 11 games at Georgia State in 2024 and owns three career tackles. Rated a five star snapper by Rubio Long Snapping, he was named Gwinnett County Specialist of the Year as a junior and senior at Parkview High School.

athletes.name: Lincoln Murff
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lincoln Murff is a redshirt junior cornerback from Indianapolis who joined Indiana as a walk-on in 2023. He played receiver at Ben Davis High School, catching 65 passes for 667 yards and seven touchdowns as a senior and earning all-conference and Indiana Football Coaches Association Academic All-State honors. He has been named Academic All-Big Ten in each college season.

athletes.name: Isaiah Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is Indiana's projected starting middle linebacker replacing Aiden Fisher, after totaling 78 tackles, 15.5 tackles for loss, seven sacks and an interception in 2025.

athletes.name: Jackson Tolle
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson Tolle is a freshman long snapper from Fishers, Indiana, who played at Hamilton Southeastern High School. He was rated the No. 1 long snapper in the nation by Kohl's Kicking, which also graded him a five-star snapper and named him third-team All-America. He earned Academic All-State honors from the Indiana Football Coaches Association.

athletes.name: Drew Clausen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clausen is a graduate long snapper from Grimes, Iowa, who committed to Indiana out of the transfer portal in January 2026. He began at Northern Iowa, where he redshirted and later appeared in all 11 games in 2023, then moved to Iowa State and played in all 14 games in 2024 before starting all 12 games as the Cyclones' long and short snapper in 2025. With one year of eligibility left, he is expected to take over Indiana's snapping duties.

athletes.name: Jhrevious Hall
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hall is a third-year Indiana defensive lineman from Columbia, Tennessee, who came to Bloomington from Columbia Central High School and wears No. 50 at 6-2 and 305 pounds. He started all 16 games in 2025 and earned second-team All-Big Ten honors from both the media and coaches panels, posting a career-high 13 tackles at Oregon. Hall has played all 29 games of his career with 20 starts and returned an interception for a touchdown as a true freshman.

athletes.name: Clayton Allen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clayton Allen is a redshirt junior linebacker from Fishers, Indiana, who joined Indiana as a walk-on in 2023. At Hamilton Southeastern he totaled 103 career tackles, including 76 stops with 4.5 tackles for loss as a senior, and helped the school win its first regional title since 2005. He has earned Academic All-Big Ten honors.

athletes.name: Rodney White
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rodney White is a freshman defensive lineman from Baltimore who played at Concordia Preparatory School. A consensus three-star recruit, he was a first-team All-MIAA selection as a junior and senior and made the Baltimore Touchdown Club's Super 22 as a junior. He finished with 70 career tackles, 15.5 tackles for loss and nine sacks.

athletes.name: Joe Brunner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brunner is a projected starting guard for Indiana after transferring from Wisconsin, where he played 39 games with 24 starts, including 24 straight starts across 2024 and 2025. He reunites with offensive line coach Bob Bostad.

athletes.name: CJ Scifres
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: CJ Scifres is a freshman offensive lineman from Bargersville, Indiana, who played at Center Grove High School. A consensus three-star recruit rated the No. 18 prospect in Indiana by ESPN, he was a 2024 Indiana Football Coaches Association all-state pick as a junior and an Indianapolis Star Central Indiana Super Team selection as a senior.

athletes.name: Baylor Wilkin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilkin appeared in four games as a true freshman in 2025, debuting against Kennesaw State and taking fourth quarter snaps. The redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Van Buren, Ohio, was a consensus three star recruit out of Findlay, ranked among the top 90 offensive line prospects nationally and a consensus top 10 player in Ohio. He is developing behind an experienced line.

athletes.name: Drew Evans
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Evans is a returning starting interior offensive lineman for Indiana and is regarded as one of the best guards in college football. He started on the Hoosiers' 2025 national championship line.

athletes.name: Chance Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chance Johnson is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Jeffersonville, Indiana, who joined Indiana as a walk-on. He played at Jeffersonville High School, where he was a first-team All-Hoosier Hills Conference selection as a senior. He did not appear in a game in 2025 and redshirted his first college season.

athletes.name: Evan Parker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Parker is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Carmel, Indiana, who committed to Indiana in the 2025 class as a three star interior prospect and the second offensive lineman to pledge to Curt Cignetti and line coach Bob Bostad. He was named to the Indiana Junior All State team after the 2023 season at Carmel High School and has not yet appeared in game action for the Hoosiers.

athletes.name: Austin Leibfried
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Leibfried has appeared in 13 career games, including nine in 2025, after debuting in the 2024 season opener against FIU. The redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Mount Horeb, Wisconsin, was a consensus three star recruit, a top 120 offensive line prospect nationally and the Badger Conference Offensive Lineman of the Year as a senior. He provides interior depth in 2026.

athletes.name: Ben Novak
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ben Novak is a freshman offensive lineman from Crown Point, Indiana, who played at Andrean High School. A consensus three-star recruit and consensus top-15 prospect in Indiana, he helped Andrean win an Indiana Class 2A state title as a senior. He was a first-team All-Northwest Crossroads Conference pick as a junior and senior.

athletes.name: Adedamola Ajani
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ajani is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Indianapolis who has already worked his way into Indiana's rotation. A three-star recruit out of Speedway High School, he was named to the Indianapolis Star Central Indiana Super Team and earned first-team All-Marion County honors as a senior. He redshirted in 2024 and then appeared in 12 games as a redshirt freshman in 2025, making four starts, three at left guard and one at right tackle. He projects as a starting interior lineman in 2026.

athletes.name: Bray Lynch
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lynch is a two-year starting guard for Indiana and the leading candidate to move to center in 2026, replacing NFL departee Pat Coogan.

athletes.name: Sam Simpson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sam Simpson is a freshman offensive lineman from River Falls, Wisconsin, who played at River Falls High School. A consensus three-star recruit rated the No. 4 prospect in Wisconsin by 247Sports and Rivals/On3, he was a Wisconsin Football Coaches Association first-team all-state selection as a junior and senior and a three-time first-team Big Rivers Conference pick.

athletes.name: Matt Marek
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Marek played three games as a true freshman in 2025, debuting against UCLA and taking fourth quarter snaps. The redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Orland Park, Illinois, was a consensus three star recruit out of Sandburg, ranked among the top 100 offensive linemen nationally by ESPN and On3 and a top 30 prospect in Illinois. He is developing as line depth.

athletes.name: Charlie Becker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation ~$893K; On3 whisper valuation ~$650K; no deal figure disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Becker is Indiana's returning big-play receiver, catching 34 passes for 679 yards and four touchdowns across all 16 games of the Hoosiers' 2025 national championship season. He is widely projected as a 2027 first-round NFL Draft pick.

athletes.name: Myles Kendrick
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Myles Kendrick is a redshirt freshman wide receiver from Jacksonville, Florida, who played at Riverside High School. A consensus three-star recruit rated the No. 111 receiver nationally by ESPN, he finished with 96 career receptions for 1,344 yards and 13 touchdowns, including 710 yards as a junior. He redshirted his first college season in 2025.

athletes.name: Hunter Stroud
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hunter Stroud is a redshirt freshman wide receiver from Martinsville, Indiana, who joined Indiana as a walk-on. He holds Martinsville High School records with 198 career receptions, 2,672 receiving yards and 28 touchdown catches, and led the state with 106 catches as a senior. He was a two-time Indiana Football Coaches Association all-state selection.

athletes.name: Blake Thiry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thiry redshirted in 2025 without game action and enters 2026 as a redshirt freshman tight end competing for rotation snaps. The Prairie du Chien, Wisconsin, native was a consensus three star recruit and a consensus top 10 player in his state, named Wisconsin Football Coaches Association Small School Offensive Player of the Year as a senior after catching 40 passes with 14 touchdowns.

athletes.name: Andrew Barker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Barker is a redshirt freshman tight end from Kokomo, Indiana, who stayed in state to play for the Hoosiers. A consensus three-star recruit, he was the 14th commitment in Indiana's 2025 class and chose the Hoosiers over offers from Army, Ball State, Dartmouth and Gardner-Webb. He caught 23 passes for 324 yards and four touchdowns as a junior at Kokomo High School and was a two-time team captain. Barker enrolled early in spring 2025 and made one appearance as a freshman, against Kennesaw State.

athletes.name: Bruno Massel IV
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bruno Massel IV is a redshirt freshman wide receiver from Elmhurst, Illinois, who joined Indiana as a walk-on after playing quarterback at York High School. He passed for 1,685 yards and 11 touchdowns and rushed for 1,248 yards and 18 touchdowns as a senior, helping York to a Class 8A state runner-up finish. He also lettered in track and field.

athletes.name: Brock Schott
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Schott is a redshirt freshman tight end from Fort Wayne, Indiana, who transferred to Indiana from Miami ahead of the 2026 season. A consensus four-star recruit in the 2025 class, he was a two-way standout at Leo High School, where he totaled 101 catches for 1,717 yards and 19 touchdowns while also recording 41 sacks on defense. He appeared in two games for the Hurricanes in 2025 and caught two passes for 24 yards. He is a leading candidate to start at tight end.

athletes.name: Joe Hjelle
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hjelle transfers in from Tulsa, where the redshirt senior defensive lineman appeared in 24 games over two seasons and recorded his first solo sack in the 2025 finale against UAB. Before that he won back to back NJCAA national titles at Iowa Western Community College, posting 11 tackles for loss and 6.5 sacks in 2023. The Decorah, Iowa, native adds size at 318 pounds.

athletes.name: Josh Placzek
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Josh Placzek is a redshirt sophomore kicker from Carmel, Indiana, who joined Indiana as a walk-on. At Carmel High School he converted all six field goal attempts and all 17 extra points as a senior, with three makes of 40 or more yards. He made his college debut against Indiana State in 2025, handling five kickoffs.

athletes.name: Blake Smythe
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Blake Smythe is a freshman defensive lineman from Trafalgar, Indiana, who played at Franklin Community High School. A consensus three-star recruit, he totaled 261 career tackles, 52 tackles for loss and 20 sacks and was a two-time Indiana Football Coaches Association Class 5A all-state pick. His grandfather Mark Smythe lettered for Indiana from 1979 to 1983.

athletes.name: Gabe Hill
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gabe Hill is a freshman defensive lineman from Naperville, Illinois, who played at Naperville North High School. A four-star recruit per ESPN and Rivals/On3, he was named Naperville Sun Player of the Year and Southwest Valley Conference Defensive Player of the Year as a senior. He made 141 career tackles with 52 tackles for loss and 17 sacks.

athletes.name: Ronelle Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ronelle Johnson is a freshman edge rusher from Kansas City, Missouri, who played at Blue Springs High School. Rated a four-star recruit by Rivals/On3 and a consensus top-10 prospect in Missouri, he was a Missouri Football Coaches Association first-team all-state pick as a junior after recording 60 tackles, 14 tackles for loss and 4.5 sacks.

athletes.name: Quinn Warren
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Warren has appeared in 20 career games as a kickoff specialist and punter, playing 13 in 2025 when 33 of his 56 kickoffs went for touchbacks and three of five punts landed inside the 10 yard line. The junior from Indianapolis was an Indianapolis Star Mr. Football positional winner at punter at Brebeuf Jesuit and has earned Academic All-Big Ten honors.

athletes.name: Kyler Garcia
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Garcia appeared in one game as a true freshman in 2025, debuting against Indiana State. The redshirt freshman defensive lineman from Nashville was a consensus three star recruit out of Pearl-Cohn, ranked among the top 100 defensive linemen nationally by ESPN and On3, and he helped his high school win a Tennessee Class 4A state title as a junior. He is competing for interior depth snaps.

athletes.name: Tyrique Tucker
athletes.source: Estimate (reported at $1,155,422 in published 2026 Indiana roster NIL valuation breakdowns; not a disclosed contract figure)
athletes.blurb: Tucker is Indiana's returning starting defensive tackle and a 2025 All-American and first-team All-Big Ten selection, posting 40 tackles, 12 tackles for loss and six sacks in 16 starts. He passed on the NFL Draft to return for 2026.

athletes.name: Mario Landino
athletes.source: Estimate (reported at ~$1.5M in published 2026 Indiana defensive-line NIL spending breakdowns; not a disclosed contract figure)
athletes.blurb: Landino is Indiana's returning starting defensive tackle alongside Tyrique Tucker, appearing in all 16 games with 11 starts in 2025 and recording 32 tackles, six tackles for loss and five sacks.

athletes.name: Cam McHaney
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cam McHaney is a freshman defensive lineman from Indianapolis who finished high school at IMG Academy after two seasons at Indianapolis Lutheran. A four-star recruit per ESPN and Rivals/On3, he helped IMG win back to back state titles and Indianapolis Lutheran win two Indiana Class A titles. He earned Indiana Football Coaches Association all-state honors as a sophomore.

athletes.name: Tyrone Burrus Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Burrus played two games as a true freshman in 2025, debuting in the regular season finale at Purdue. The redshirt freshman edge rusher from Indianapolis was a consensus three star prospect and a consensus top 100 defensive lineman out of Warren Central, rated a top 10 recruit in Indiana. He posted 36 tackles with 15 tackles for loss and six sacks as a senior. He is pushing for rotation snaps.

athletes.name: Carter Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (reported at $1,545,325 in published 2026 Indiana roster NIL valuation breakdowns; not a disclosed contract figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is Indiana's returning starting left tackle and an All-America-caliber blindside protector who bypassed the NFL Draft to return for 2026. He started on the Hoosiers' undefeated national championship line in 2025.

athletes.name: Girard Pringle Jr.
