athletes.blurb: Woodrow is a freshman offensive lineman from Orlando who committed to Miami in May 2025 and signed in the 2026 class as a three-star interior prospect. He started at Boone High School from his freshman year onward and can play both guard and center. He chose the Hurricanes from a list of 17 scholarship offers that included Florida, Florida State, Penn State and Stanford, and he begins his career as a developmental interior lineman.

athletes.name: Ben Congdon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Congdon is a freshman offensive lineman from Zoarville, Ohio, who committed to Miami in March 2025 after visiting on the first day of spring practice, choosing the Hurricanes over Penn State, Wisconsin and Minnesota. He played left tackle at Tuscarawas Valley and earned honorable mention All-Ohio honors as a junior. He also wrestled heavyweight, winning a conference title and placing sixth at the state meet, and drew notice in his first Miami spring.

athletes.name: Samson Okunlola
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Okunlola is Miami's projected starting left guard on a line replacing four starters. He arrived from Thayer Academy in Massachusetts as a five-star tackle prospect.

athletes.name: Ralph Scroggins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Scroggins is a sophomore offensive lineman listed at No. 64 on Miami's 2026 football roster. Other listings place his hometown in Savannah, Ga. The official roster does not list a high school for him.

athletes.name: Seuseu "SJ" Alofaituli
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alofaituli is a sophomore offensive lineman from Las Vegas who was the highest-rated member of Miami's 2025 signing class, ranked No. 10 in the ESPN 300. Born in Ewa Beach, Hawaii, he was a four-year starter at national power Bishop Gorman and is regarded as one of the most technically sound interior linemen of his class. He chose the Hurricanes over Michigan and Nebraska and can play guard or center.

athletes.name: Max Buchanan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Buchanan is a sophomore offensive lineman from Sanford, Florida who wears No. 66 for Miami. He came out of Seminole High School as a four star prospect by Rivals, which ranked him the No. 134 player nationally and the No. 4 guard in his class, and appeared at No. 345 in On3's industry rankings. He picked the Hurricanes over Auburn, Clemson, Colorado, Ole Miss and Penn State. As a true freshman in 2025 he played in five games as a reserve, seeing his heaviest work in the opener against Bethune-Cookman, and is pushing for interior snaps.

athletes.name: Joel Ervin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ervin is a freshman offensive lineman from Fort Myers, Fla., who played at Fort Myers High School. He wears No. 70 on Miami's 2026 football roster for the Hurricanes.

athletes.name: Jamal Meriweather
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Meriweather is a redshirt junior offensive lineman from Brunswick, Ga., who transferred to Miami from Georgia. He signed with the Bulldogs as a three-star prospect in the 2023 class out of Brunswick High and appeared in 15 games over two seasons in Athens, including 12 as a reserve lineman in his final year there, with time at guard. Listed at 6-7, he arrives with two years of eligibility and adds interior depth.

athletes.name: Demetrius Campbell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Campbell is a freshman offensive lineman who played at Orlando Christian Prep. Miami's official roster lists his hometown as Winter Park, Fla., and gives him No. 72 on the 2026 Hurricanes roster.

athletes.name: Jaden Wilkerson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilkerson is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Orlando who signed with Miami in the 2025 class as a three-star tackle ranked among the top 100 at his position by both 247Sports and On3. He transferred into Edgewater for his senior season after earning all-metro honors at left tackle for Lake Nona, and he chose the Hurricanes over Rutgers, Syracuse and UCF, citing line coach Alex Mirabal and Mario Cristobal's development track record.

athletes.name: Yerovi Valdes Alfonso
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Valdes Alfonso is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman listed at No. 74 on Miami's 2026 football roster. Other listings place his hometown in Cape Coral, Fla. The official roster does not list a high school.

athletes.name: Ryan Rodriguez
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rodriguez is a sixth year offensive lineman from Miami who wears No. 76 at 6-2 and 300 pounds. A four star prospect by ESPN and a U.S. Army All-American at Christopher Columbus, he helped his high school win a Florida Class 8A state championship as a junior. He opened the 2024 season starting at left guard against Florida but a season ending injury in that game cost him the rest of the year. He returned in 2025 to appear in all 16 games as a reserve, including all four College Football Playoff contests, and adds veteran depth up front.

athletes.name: Juan Minaya
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Minaya is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Paramus, N.J., who signed with Miami in the 2024 class as a consensus three-star prospect, choosing the Hurricanes over Florida, Penn State and Michigan State. He earned All-Bergen County honors after both his junior and senior seasons at Paramus Catholic and also threw shot put. He redshirted in 2024, then appeared in three games in 2025, debuting against Bethune-Cookman and playing in the Fiesta Bowl.

athletes.name: Matthew McCoy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McCoy is Miami's projected starting right tackle and one of the few returning contributors on an offensive line that lost four starters. He is a redshirt senior from St. Johns, Florida.

athletes.name: Jackson Cantwell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation $1.9M; reported $1.5M-$2M first-year Miami package, not officially disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Cantwell is Miami's projected starting left tackle and was the No. 1 offensive lineman in the 2026 recruiting class out of Nixa, Missouri. He is also a national-class shot putter and the son of two Olympic throwers.

athletes.name: Hunter Carver
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Carver is a redshirt sophomore tight end wearing No. 80 on Miami's 2026 football roster. Other listings give his hometown as Woodbury, Minn. The official roster does not list a high school for him.

athletes.name: Riply Luna
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Luna is a redshirt sophomore wide receiver from Kellogg, Idaho, who played at Kellogg High School. He wears No. 81 on Miami's roster, which also lists receiver Kolby Luna out of the same school.

athletes.name: Jack Olsen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Olsen is a sixth year kicker from Wheaton, Illinois who wears No. 82 after transferring to Miami from Northwestern, where he spent 2021 through 2025 following one season at Michigan State in 2020. He finished his Northwestern career 40 for 51 on field goals, capped by a 19 for 21 season in 2025 that included a perfect 14 for 14 from beyond 30 yards. He earned All-Big Ten honorable mention in both 2023 and 2025 and was a five star kicking recruit at Wheaton-Warrenville South, where he set an IHSA record with eight field goals in a game.

athletes.name: Dylan Reiman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reiman is a redshirt sophomore tight end wearing No. 82 on Miami's 2026 football roster. Other listings give his hometown as Jupiter, Fla. The official roster does not list a high school for him.

athletes.name: Tyran Evans
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Evans is a freshman wide receiver from the Charlotte, N.C., area who played at Hough High School. He wears No. 83 on Miami's 2026 football roster for the Hurricanes.

athletes.name: Jack Nickel
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nickel is a redshirt senior tight end from Milton, Ga., who is at his third school after signing with Michigan State in the 2022 class and spending 2024 at UAB. He redshirted as a freshman with the Spartans and played ten games in 2023, then appeared in 12 games for the Blazers largely as a blocker, catching one pass. He joined Miami alongside his younger brother, quarterback Luke Nickel.

athletes.name: Jackson Carver
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Carver is a redshirt sophomore tight end who played at Culver Academy in Indiana. He wears No. 85 on Miami's 2026 football roster, which also lists tight end Hunter Carver in the same class.

athletes.name: Kolby Luna
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Luna is a redshirt junior wide receiver from Kellogg, Idaho, who played at Kellogg High School. Miami's official roster lists him at 6-2 and 215 pounds and also includes receiver Riply Luna from Kellogg.

athletes.name: Gavin Mueller
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mueller is a freshman tight end from Wayne, Ill., who flipped his commitment from Colorado to Miami in October and signed in the 2026 class as a four-star prospect rated the No. 7 tight end nationally by the 247Sports Composite. A former basketball standout who took up football as a junior, he played tight end, quarterback, running back and defensive end at South Elgin, totaling 1,325 yards and 30 touchdowns.

athletes.name: Luka Gilbert
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gilbert is a sophomore tight end from West Chester, Ohio, who committed to Miami in April 2024 and signed as a four-star prospect rated the No. 18 tight end nationally by 247Sports, choosing the Hurricanes over Ohio State, Michigan and Texas A&M. He caught 16 passes for 243 yards and three touchdowns in eight games as a Lakota West senior. A former basketball player, he is valued as a blocker and contested-catch target.

athletes.name: DeAnthony Lafayette
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lafayette is a freshman from Orlando, Fla., who played at Lake Nona High School. Miami's official roster lists him as a defensive lineman wearing No. 88 on the 2026 Hurricanes roster.

athletes.name: Cole McConathy II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McConathy is a redshirt sophomore tight end who played at Spanish Fort High School. Miami's official roster lists his hometown as Daphne, Ala., and gives him No. 86 on the 2026 roster.

athletes.name: Jarquez Carter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Carter is a sophomore defensive lineman from Newberry, Fla., who transferred to Miami from Ohio State, where he played seven games and recorded two tackles. A four-star recruit rated the No. 18 defensive lineman in his class by the 247Sports Composite, he was named the Gainesville Sun's Big School Defensive Player of the Year as a senior after leading Newberry to a district title. He rejoins high school teammate Mykah Newton with the Hurricanes.

athletes.name: Samuel Coufal
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Coufal is a redshirt sophomore defensive lineman from Wisconsin who played at Kettle Moraine High School, located in Wales. He wears No. 92 on Miami's 2026 football roster for the Hurricanes.

athletes.name: Fred Sainteus
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sainteus is a freshman defensive lineman who played at St. John Neumann. He wears No. 93 on Miami's 2026 football roster. The official roster does not give a specific hometown listing for him.

athletes.name: Dylan Joyce
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Joyce is a senior punter from Kyabram, Australia who wears No. 94 and came to Miami through Prokick Australia after playing Australian rules football. He has been the Hurricanes' starting punter for three straight seasons and averaged 44.4 yards on 54 punts in 2025 with a long of 73 yards. As a freshman in 2023 he earned All-ACC honorable mention and a spot on the 247Sports True Freshman All-America team, and he was named to the Ray Guy Award watch list in 2024. He returns as the established starter for 2026.

athletes.name: Tucker Tevepaugh
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tevepaugh is a redshirt sophomore punter from Bluffton, S.C., who joined Miami in the 2024 signing class. He transferred into Hilton Head Christian Academy for his final two high school seasons and became a key contributor there before graduating in 2024. He has yet to take over the Hurricanes' primary punting duties and enters 2026 competing for the job on a roster that carries multiple specialists.

athletes.name: Keona Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davis is a projected starting defensive tackle for Miami after transferring from Nebraska in the 2026 portal cycle. He was one of the headline additions to a top-five Hurricanes transfer class.

athletes.name: Will Rocha
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rocha is a redshirt sophomore kicker wearing No. 97 on Miami's 2026 football roster. Other listings give his hometown as Mandeville, La. The official roster does not list a high school for him.

athletes.name: Ahmad Moten Sr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moten is Miami's starting defensive tackle and had 4.5 sacks in a breakout 2025 season. ESPN's survey of personnel staffers ranked him fifth among returning defensive players nationally entering 2026.

athletes.name: Mikal Harrison-Pilot
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Harrison-Pilot, a junior from Temple, Texas, arrived at Texas Tech from Houston, where he signed as a four-star recruit in the 2023 class out of Temple High School. He played four games as a freshman while preserving his redshirt and has since moved from wide receiver to safety. Listed at 6-0 and 205 pounds, he wears No. 0 and is competing for secondary rotation snaps in 2026.

athletes.name: Quinten Joyner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Joyner is a junior running back from Austin, Texas who came to Texas Tech from USC, where he ran for 478 yards on 63 carries at 7.6 yards per attempt in 2024 and added 12 catches for 89 yards across 12 games. He tore an ACL in preseason camp and missed the 2025 season after arriving as a projected featured back. He returns to the 2026 Red Raiders backfield alongside J'Koby Williams and is expected to compete for significant carries.

athletes.name: Micah Hudson
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$745K; On3 NIL valuation previously reported ~$406K)
athletes.blurb: Hudson is Texas Tech's projected starting X receiver and the highest-rated signee in program history, a former five-star who returned to Lubbock in 2025 after a brief transfer to Texas A&M.

athletes.name: Julien Laventure
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Laventure is a senior defensive lineman from Upper Darby, Pa., who joined Texas Tech from Akron in January 2026 after earning second team All-MAC honors in 2025 with 45 tackles, 10.5 tackles for loss, four sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. He spent three prior seasons at Division II PennWest California, where he was All-PSAC West first team in 2024. He is listed at 6-0 and 290 pounds.

athletes.name: Trey White
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$1.47M; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: White is a San Diego State transfer edge rusher and two-time first-team All-Mountain West pick with 19.5 career sacks. He steps in for NFL-bound pass rushers David Bailey and Romello Height.

athletes.name: Coy Eakin
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$949K; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Eakin is Texas Tech's returning slot receiver and a team captain who caught 48 passes for 637 yards and six touchdowns in 2025. He was named offensive player of the game in the Big 12 title win over BYU.

athletes.name: Peyton Morgan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Morgan is a sophomore safety from Round Rock, Texas, who signed with Texas Tech in the 2024 class out of Pflugerville Weiss, choosing the Red Raiders over Nebraska and Arizona. He was a consensus three-star or better prospect and closed his senior season with 88 tackles, five tackles for loss and nine interceptions. Listed at 6-0 and 185 pounds, he also competed in hurdles and jumps in track.

athletes.name: Kenny Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$988K; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a Pittsburgh transfer receiver projected to start at Z for Texas Tech after catching 48 passes for 695 yards and five touchdowns for the Panthers in 2025.

athletes.name: Davin Martin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Martin is a junior cornerback from Houston who signed with Texas Tech out of the transfer portal in January 2026 following three seasons at UTSA. He started eight games for the Roadrunners in 2025 and finished with 26 tackles, a tackle for loss, two pass breakups and an interception. A three-star signee out of Klein Cain in 2023, he is listed at 6-2 and 185 pounds.

athletes.name: Matt Ludwig
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ludwig is a freshman tight end from Billings, Montana, who played at Billings West High School. He caught 50 passes for 736 yards and 10 touchdowns as a senior and was named Montana High School Player of the Year by MaxPreps. He earned all-state honors three times and was invited to the 2026 Navy All-American Bowl, the only Montana player selected.

athletes.name: Oliver Miles III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Miles is a sophomore safety from El Campo, Texas, and a consensus three-star member of Texas Tech's 2024 signing class. He chose the Red Raiders over reported offers from Notre Dame, Baylor, Nebraska, Utah and Vanderbilt. A four-sport athlete at El Campo, he won the Class 4A state title in the triple jump as a junior with a mark of 50 feet, 10 inches. He is listed at 6-2 and 190 pounds.

athletes.name: John Curry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Curry is a junior linebacker who grew up in Lubbock and played at Coronado High School before signing with the hometown Red Raiders. He redshirted in 2023, recorded 35 tackles and an interception in 2024, then moved to the star position out of necessity in 2025 and started all 14 games, earning honorable mention All-Big 12 recognition. His season included a fumble recovery returned for a touchdown against Kansas State. He projects as a returning starter in the Texas Tech front seven in 2026.

athletes.name: Jalen Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a junior wide receiver from Birmingham, Ala., who signed with Texas Tech in January 2026 after two seasons at Alabama State. He caught 51 passes for 1,167 yards in 2025, ranking fourth in the FCS in receiving yards and becoming the fifth Hornet to reach 1,000 in a season. He was a first team HBCU All-American and a second team AFCA selection, and he prepped at Ramsay.

athletes.name: Terrance Carter Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$700K; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Carter is Texas Tech's returning starting tight end, a Louisiana transfer who posted 552 receiving yards in 2025 and announced his return for a final season.

athletes.name: Brenden Jordan
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$650K; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Jordan is Texas Tech's returning starting free safety, moving into a full-time safety role after two seasons at the Star hybrid position.

athletes.name: Cameron Dickey
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$600K; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Dickey is Texas Tech's returning starting running back and a 2025 first-team All-Big 12 selection after rushing for 1,124 yards and 14 touchdowns on 209 carries for the Big 12 champions.

athletes.name: Jamond Mathis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mathis is a junior edge rusher from St. Louis who transferred to Texas Tech from Southern Illinois. He redshirted after four games in 2023, then recorded 30 tackles, 8.5 tackles for loss and three sacks as a part-time starter the following year. A three-star prospect out of Duchesne, he set the school record with 23 career sacks and was an all-state pick as a senior. He is listed at 6-1 and 250 pounds.

athletes.name: Donte Lee Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lee is a senior wide receiver from Baltimore who signed with Texas Tech in January 2026 after two seasons at Liberty and two at Shaw. He caught 32 passes for 589 yards and five touchdowns in 2025, averaging 18.4 yards per catch to rank third in Conference USA. Across 35 college games he has 69 receptions for 1,150 yards and nine scores. He won a Maryland state title at Dunbar in 2022.

athletes.name: Corey Platt Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Platt is a senior linebacker from Little Rock, Ark., spending his final season at Texas Tech after three years at Tulane and two at Houston. He posted 40 tackles, five tackles for loss and three sacks for a 10-3 Houston team in 2025, and he reunites in Lubbock with defensive coordinator Shiel Wood, who coached him at Tulane. He helped Little Rock Christian Academy win a Class 5A state title in 2018.

athletes.name: A.J. Holmes Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$1.21M; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Holmes is a returning interior defensive lineman and Houston transfer who recorded 4.5 sacks in 2025, third-most on Texas Tech's Big 12 championship defense.

athletes.name: Lloyd Jones III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a redshirt freshman quarterback from Hitchcock, Texas, and was a composite four-star prospect in Texas Tech's 2025 class, rated the No. 17 quarterback nationally by the On3 industry ranking. He committed over offers from Colorado State, North Texas, Texas State and UTSA. As a high school sophomore he completed 160 of 258 passes for 2,836 yards and 36 touchdowns with one interception. He is listed at 6-4 and 215 pounds.

athletes.name: Brock Golwas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Golwas is a sophomore linebacker from Flower Mound, Texas, and a consensus three-star member of Texas Tech's 2025 class out of Marcus High School. He recorded 90 tackles and six sacks as a senior and was a unanimous All-District 5-6A selection at inside linebacker. He committed over offers from Kansas State, Army, Memphis, North Texas and UTEP. Listed at 6-1 and 240 pounds, his father is a Texas Tech graduate.

athletes.name: Malcolm Simmons
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Simmons is a junior wide receiver from Montgomery, Alabama who transferred to Texas Tech from Auburn after two seasons in the SEC. He caught 40 passes for 451 yards and three touchdowns as a true freshman in 2024, then added 25 catches for 457 yards and three scores in 2025 while raising his average to 18.3 yards per reception. A Benjamin Russell High School product, he arrives with 65 career receptions and projects into the Red Raiders' starting receiver rotation in 2026.

athletes.name: Stephen Cannon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cannon is a freshman quarterback from Savannah, Georgia, who played at Benedictine Military School. He was Region 1-4A Offensive Player of the Year as a senior after passing for 1,908 yards and 22 touchdowns against four interceptions while rushing for 537 yards and seven scores. He also won two Georgia state track titles in relay events.

athletes.name: Tarrion Grant
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Grant is a redshirt sophomore cornerback from Sumter, S.C., who transferred to Texas Tech from Purdue in January 2025. He appeared in 13 games as a freshman for the Boilermakers and finished with 13 tackles, two passes defended and a forced fumble. A four-star prospect at Siegel High School in Murfreesboro, Tenn., he reclassified into the 2024 class. He is listed at 6-2 and 190 pounds.

athletes.name: Chase Campbell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Campbell is a freshman wide receiver from Lubbock who played at Frenship High School. He totaled more than 3,500 receiving yards in high school, including 81 catches for 1,497 yards and 18 touchdowns as a junior, when he earned first team All-District 2-6A honors and third team all-state recognition from the Texas Sports Writers Association.

athletes.name: Bryson Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a sophomore wide receiver from Frisco, Texas, and was a composite four-star signee in Texas Tech's 2025 class out of Lone Star High School. He caught 57 passes for 969 yards and 15 touchdowns as a junior and chose the Red Raiders over reported offers from Penn State, Texas A&M, Ole Miss, Tennessee and Michigan State. Listed at 6-3 and 195 pounds, he saw playing time as a freshman in 2025.

athletes.name: Brice Pollock
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$1.0M; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Pollock is Texas Tech's returning starting cornerback, a Mississippi State transfer who started all 14 games in 2025 and tied for the Big 12 lead with five interceptions before announcing his return.

athletes.name: Will Hammond
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$1.76M; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Hammond is Texas Tech's starting quarterback for 2026, named to the job in July after Brendan Sorsby's departure. He threw for 680 yards and seven touchdowns and ran for 299 yards and five scores in relief duty in 2025 before tearing his ACL in October.

athletes.name: Austin Romaine
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$600K; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Romaine is a Kansas State transfer linebacker who recorded 66 tackles and 7.0 tackles for loss in nine games in 2025 and 96 tackles with a 90.3 PFF grade in 2024.

athletes.name: Holden Phillips
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Phillips is a redshirt freshman quarterback from Lubbock and a Frenship High School product. He led Texas Class 6A with 4,438 passing yards and 57 touchdowns as a senior and was the Lubbock Avalanche-Journal big-school player of the year. He appeared in one game in 2025, completing his only pass attempt against Oklahoma State.

athletes.name: Noah Lewis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lewis is a freshman cornerback from Terrell, Texas, where he played both cornerback and wide receiver at Terrell High School. He was a unanimous first team All-District 6-5A pick as a senior with 40 tackles, six pass breakups and two blocked field goals. A consensus three-star recruit, he enrolled at Texas Tech in January 2026.

athletes.name: Leyton Stone
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stone is a sophomore wide receiver from Lubbock who stayed home to sign with Texas Tech in the 2025 class out of Frenship. He was District 2-6A Offensive MVP as a senior after catching 70 passes for 1,488 yards and 29 touchdowns, finishing his varsity career with more than 4,000 receiving yards and 66 scores. His father is a former Texas Tech soccer coach. He is listed at 6-3 and 200 pounds.

athletes.name: Kirk Francis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Francis is a junior quarterback from Tulsa, Okla., who signed with Texas Tech out of the portal in January 2026 after three seasons at Tulsa. He appeared in 18 games with 12 starts for the Golden Hurricane, completing 270 of 462 passes for 3,045 yards with 18 touchdowns and 13 interceptions. He threw for 9,959 yards and 115 touchdowns at Metro Christian Academy and is competing with Will Hammond in 2026.

athletes.name: S'Vioarean Martin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Martin is a freshman cornerback from Palestine, Texas, and a Palestine High School product. He earned first team all-district honors in each of his three varsity seasons and recorded 40 tackles and 15 pass breakups as a senior. A consensus four-star recruit, he was invited to the 2026 Navy All-American Bowl and enrolled in January 2026.

athletes.name: Michael Dever
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dever is a redshirt freshman wide receiver from Lubbock who played at Lubbock-Cooper. He set the school single-season receiving record with 1,206 yards on 68 catches as a senior and was named District 2-5A Offensive MVP. He appeared in four games in 2025 and made his first career catch against Kent State.

athletes.name: Cam Wyatt
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wyatt is a freshman cornerback from Houston who played at Langham Creek High School. He was a first team All-District 16-6A defensive back as a senior after recording 49 tackles, an interception and seven pass breakups. He was initially committed to Norfolk State before joining Texas Tech in the summer of 2026.

athletes.name: Adam Trick
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$1.47M; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Trick is a Miami (Ohio) transfer edge rusher who posted 59 tackles, 12.5 tackles for loss and 8.5 sacks in 2025 and projects as Texas Tech's starting rush end.

athletes.name: J'Koby Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a junior running back out of Beckville, Texas who led Texas Tech with 1,525 all-purpose yards in 2025. He carried 155 times for 868 yards and six touchdowns while catching 35 passes for 388 yards and two more scores, averaging 108.9 all-purpose yards per game. His outings included 135 rushing yards and a touchdown against Kansas State and 116 receiving yards versus Oregon State. He was named a semifinalist for the Paul Hornung Award and returns as the Red Raiders' lead back.

athletes.name: Miquel Dingle Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dingle is a junior safety from Charleston, S.C., who signed with Texas Tech in the 2023 class out of Byrnes High School, where he recorded 38 tackles and seven stops for loss as a senior linebacker. He is also a member of the Texas Tech track and field roster after winning a South Carolina state title in the 110-meter hurdles, running 13.56 as a junior. He is listed at 6-2 and 220 pounds.

athletes.name: Tristian Gentry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gentry is a sophomore wide receiver from Stephenville, Texas, and was the first commitment in Texas Tech's 2025 class. Rated a four-star prospect by On3, 247Sports and Rivals, he finished his Stephenville career with 228 catches for 4,416 yards and 51 touchdowns, clearing 1,000 receiving yards in all three varsity seasons. He also played in the secondary in high school and is listed at 6-0 and 180 pounds.

athletes.name: Marcus Ramon-Edwards
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ramon-Edwards is a junior safety from Lubbock who signed with Texas Tech out of Trinity Christian as a consensus three-star prospect. He appeared in 11 games in 2025, working mainly on special teams and as a regular on the punt return unit. In high school he rushed for 1,778 yards and 27 touchdowns as a junior and 1,541 yards and 31 scores as a senior. He is listed at 6-3 and 225 pounds.

athletes.name: Maddox Quiller
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Quiller is a freshman safety from Pflugerville, Texas, who played at Hendrickson High School. He earned second team All-District 12-5A honors as a senior with 74 tackles, two interceptions and two forced fumbles. A four-year varsity letterwinner and team captain, he graduated early to join the Red Raiders as a mid-year enrollee.

athletes.name: Malik Esquerra
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Esquerra is a sophomore safety from Killeen, Texas who signed with Texas Tech in the 2024 class out of Shoemaker High School. He was a first team All-District 4-5A Division I selection as a prep, posting 68 tackles and four interceptions, and recruiting services placed him around the top 100 in the state, with On3 listing him at No. 82 and 247Sports at No. 95. He chose the Red Raiders over Nebraska and also competed as a hurdler in track.

athletes.name: Donovan Webb
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Webb is a freshman safety from Frisco, Texas, and a Panther Creek High School product. He shared District 7-4A Division I Most Valuable Player honors as a senior after posting 82 tackles, an interception and three forced fumbles, and he recorded 120 tackles and five interceptions as a junior. He was a four-year letterwinner.

athletes.name: Aaron Bradshaw
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bradshaw is a freshman safety from Crowley, Texas, who played at North Crowley. He was a first team All-District 3-6A pick and a first team all-state selection by the Texas Sports Writers Association as a senior, finishing his career with 134 tackles and eight interceptions. He was part of North Crowley's 16-0 state title team as a junior.

athletes.name: Amier Boyd
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$715K; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Boyd is Texas Tech's projected starting field cornerback, a UTEP transfer who was ranked the No. 14 corner in the 2025 transfer class.

athletes.name: Braylan McDonald
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McDonald is a redshirt freshman safety who calls Terrell, Texas, home and played at Lancaster High School near Dallas. A consensus three-star recruit, he originally committed to Washington State before flipping to Texas Tech in June 2024. He appeared in two games as a true freshman in 2025 and served on the scout team.

athletes.name: Jordan Rogers
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rogers is a senior safety from Bellmead, Texas, who arrived from Pittsburg State in the summer of 2026 after being granted a sixth season. A three-time All-MIAA selection, he was a Division II All-American in 2025 with 85 tackles, five interceptions and four forced fumbles while helping the Gorillas to a share of the conference title.

athletes.name: Ashton Rowden
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rowden is a freshman running back from Texarkana, Texas, who played at New Boston High School. He rushed for 1,700 yards and 22 touchdowns as a junior and added 955 all-purpose yards in seven games as a senior. Rated a four-star prospect by Rivals and ESPN, he enrolled at Texas Tech in January 2026.

athletes.name: Jamarn Grant II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Grant is a sophomore cornerback from Fort Worth who played at Boswell High School. He recorded 82 tackles, five interceptions and two forced fumbles as a senior in 2023 and was a second team All-District 3-6A defensive back. He was a team captain at Boswell and is majoring in biology at Texas Tech.

athletes.name: Cord Nolan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nolan is a freshman linebacker from Bixby, Oklahoma, and a Bixby High School product. He was named all-state Defensive Player of the Year by The Oklahoman as a senior after 87 tackles, 19 tackles for loss and three sacks. He was part of four state championship football teams at Bixby, including an undefeated senior season.

athletes.name: Sawyer Wilkerson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilkerson is a redshirt freshman running back from Stephenville, Texas, who joined the program as a walk-on. He rushed for more than 5,600 yards across four varsity seasons, including 1,659 yards and 26 touchdowns as a senior at Stephenville after two years at Comanche, where he was District 5-3A Division II MVP as a sophomore.

athletes.name: Ansel Nedore
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nedore is a junior edge rusher from Round Rock, Texas, who signed with Texas Tech in the 2023 class out of Round Rock High School. He was rated a three-star prospect by 247Sports, Rivals and ESPN and a four-star by On3, and he committed over offers from Texas, TCU, Baylor, SMU, Houston and Colorado. He also threw the shot put and discus in high school and is listed at 6-3 and 260 pounds.

athletes.name: Loic Tshibangu
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tshibangu is a redshirt junior running back from Brussels, Belgium, who joined Texas Tech as a walk-on during the 2025 season. He attended IMI Secondaire and played for the Brussels Tigers club before moving to the United States in 2023 and attending Collin College. Two of his uncles played for the Red Raiders.

athletes.name: Kaegan Ash
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ash is a freshman linebacker from Mount Enterprise, Texas, who set the Texas high school career rushing record with 11,382 yards. He also set the state single-season rushing mark with 4,562 yards as a senior and the national single-season scoring record with 528 points, leading Mount Enterprise to the Class 2A Division II state semifinals.

athletes.name: Michael Henderson III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Henderson is a redshirt freshman running back from Dallas who played at Wylie East. He was District 9-6A Two-Way Player of the Year as both a junior and a senior, rushing for 1,150 yards as a senior. He moved to running back late in 2025 preseason camp and appeared in two games that season.

athletes.name: Adam Hill
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hill is a sophomore linebacker from Albany, Texas, who helped Albany win back to back Class 2A state championships and was named offensive MVP of the title game as a senior. He finished that year with 2,641 rushing yards and 51 touchdowns as a two-way player while adding 16.5 sacks and more than 90 tackles. He has since moved into Texas Tech's inside linebacker room and is listed at 6-1 and 230 pounds.

athletes.name: Demarcus Marks
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Marks is a freshman edge rusher from Houston who played at Westfield High School. He earned first team All-District 14-6A honors as a senior with 92 tackles, 23 tackles for loss and five sacks. A consensus three-star recruit ranked as high as No. 46 among edge rushers nationally by ESPN, he committed to Texas Tech in June 2025.

athletes.name: Ian Hershey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hershey is a senior specialist from Pocatello, Idaho, listed as a punter and kicker who came to Texas Tech from Arizona State, where he spent two seasons handling place kicking and punting duties. He began his career at Idaho State, making seven of 11 field goals and averaging 38.7 yards on 56 punts in 2022. A Highland High School product, he is listed at 5-11 and 185 pounds.

athletes.name: Jacob Hand
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hand is a junior kicker from Mansfield, Texas, who committed to Texas Tech from the transfer portal in January 2026 after signing with Stephen F. Austin in the 2023 class. He converted all three of his field goal attempts for the Lumberjacks from 54, 56 and 48 yards, and served mainly as their kickoff specialist with 87 touchbacks on 155 attempts over two seasons. He arrives with two years of eligibility.

athletes.name: Wesley Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a senior linebacker from Midland, Texas, who signed with Texas Tech out of Legacy High School, where he was named District 2-6A defensive most valuable player in each of his final two seasons after combining for 252 tackles and 30 tackles for loss. As a true freshman in 2022 he appeared in seven games, all on special teams, and became a regular on the kickoff and punt coverage units.

athletes.name: Chris Lemons
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lemons is a junior linebacker from Prosper, Texas, and a Prosper High School product whose father played linebacker for the Red Raiders. He redshirted in 2023, spent 2024 on the scout team and made his collegiate debut on kickoff coverage against Kent State in 2025. He is a sport management major.

athletes.name: Rylan Vagana
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Vagana is a sophomore long snapper from Huntington Beach, California who came to Texas Tech from Mater Dei High School in Santa Ana, where he was regarded as the top long snapper in the 2024 recruiting class and helped the Monarchs to a state title. As a redshirt freshman in 2025 he handled deep snapping duties in all 14 games, primarily on punts, without a failed snap across 45 punt attempts and 11 place kicks. He returns as a specialist starter in 2026.

athletes.name: Stone Harrington
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Harrington is a senior kicker from Colleyville, Texas who was a two-year varsity kicker and soccer player at Colleyville Heritage. He won the Texas Tech place-kicking job midway through the 2025 season and appeared in all 14 games, finishing 22 of 28 on field goals and 41 of 42 on extra points for 107 points. He made at least one field goal in nine games and did not miss from inside 40 yards. He completed a sports management degree in fall 2025.

athletes.name: Will Karoll
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Karoll is a senior punter from Mosman, New South Wales, Australia who attended The King's School and trained through Prokick Australia before beginning his college career. He punted for Tulane in 2023 and 2024, averaging 43.9 and 42.8 yards per kick, then started at UCLA in 2025 and averaged 43.48 yards with five punts over 50 yards, a long of 63 and 13 kicks downed inside the 20. He arrives at Texas Tech for his final season as one of the more experienced punters in the country.

athletes.name: Patrick McMath
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McMath is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Katy, Texas, who was a team captain and two-time first team all-district pick at Katy High School. He graduated early to join Texas Tech in the spring of 2025 and appeared in four games in 2025, logging 69 offensive snaps at center and right guard.

athletes.name: Jayden Cofield
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cofield is a junior defensive lineman from Austin who played at Manor High School. He appeared in all 14 games in 2025 as the primary backup at noseguard, recording 24 tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss and a shared sack. He recovered a fumble in the Big 12 Championship win over BYU.

athletes.name: Felix Ojo
athletes.source: Reported: Year 1 of a fully guaranteed 3-year, $5.1M revenue-share deal signed July 2025 ($1.2M/$1.6M/$2.1M escalator)
athletes.blurb: Ojo is Texas Tech's five-star freshman offensive tackle who signed a reported fully guaranteed three-year, $5.1 million revenue-share deal, the largest known contract in college football at the time. He opens 2026 behind returning starter Howard Sampson at left tackle.

athletes.name: Cash Cleveland
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cleveland is a junior offensive lineman from Rockwall, Texas, who signed with Texas Tech in April 2025 after one season at Colorado. He was named a freshman All-American by 247Sports, On3 and Pro Football Focus after playing six games with four starts as a true freshman walk-on, and he was the first true freshman walk-on to start at center for the Buffaloes. He finished high school at IMG Academy.

athletes.name: Holton Hendrix
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hendrix is a sophomore offensive lineman from Lubbock who stayed home to sign with Texas Tech in the 2024 class out of Lubbock Cooper, which gave him his first scholarship offer. He was a team captain and all-district selection as a senior and chose the Red Raiders over Baylor, Kansas and Houston. He appeared in two games as a freshman, against North Texas and West Virginia, and is listed at 6-4 and 310 pounds.

athletes.name: Jordan Church
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$679K; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Church is Texas Tech's returning starting right guard on an offensive line that brings back all five starters from the 2025 Big 12 championship team.

athletes.name: Amarie Fleming
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fleming is a junior edge rusher from Mayo, Florida, who joined Texas Tech in January 2026 after two seasons at Division II Allen University. He ranked third nationally in Division II with 14.5 sacks in 2025 and earned first team All-SIAC honors, setting Allen single-season and career records for sacks and tackles for loss.

athletes.name: Jerald Mays
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mays is a freshman offensive lineman from Pflugerville, Texas, who started every game at center as a senior at Weiss High School and was District 12-5A Offensive Lineman of the Year in each of his final two seasons. He was invited to the 2026 Navy All-American Bowl and enrolled at Texas Tech in January 2026.

athletes.name: Hunter Zambrano
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zambrano is a redshirt senior offensive lineman from Weston, Florida who joined Texas Tech from Illinois State, where he played 30 games with 26 starts, mostly at left tackle. He was a second team all-Missouri Valley Football Conference pick in 2023 and posted the Redbirds' highest blocking grade among offensive linemen. Listed at 6-foot-5 and 300 pounds, he was ranked the top interior offensive lineman available in the transfer portal and projects into the Red Raiders' starting front for 2026.

athletes.name: Connor Carty
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Carty is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Prosper, Texas, where he was a three-year starter and a two-time first team all-district selection. He appeared in four games in 2025, logging 44 offensive snaps, and was recognized as offensive scout team player of the week after the win over Houston.

athletes.name: D'Anthis Upshaw Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Upshaw is a sophomore offensive lineman from Dallas who signed with Texas Tech out of Irving High School, where he played both ways and earned first team All-District 7-6A honors on offense and second team recognition on defense as a senior. He chose the Red Raiders over interest from North Texas and Texas State, then redshirted in 2024 while working on the scout team. He is listed at 6-5 and 305 pounds.

athletes.name: Jackson Hildebrand
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hildebrand is a sophomore offensive lineman from San Antonio who was a team captain and two-time first team All-District 14-5A pick at Alamo Heights. He graduated early and joined Texas Tech in the spring of 2024, then appeared in two games in 2025 on the field goal protection unit. His father started at Air Force.

athletes.name: Ren Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Stanton, Nebraska, whose high school team went 25-1 across his junior and senior seasons and won the 2023 Class D1 state title. He was a first team all-state pick as both a junior and a senior and committed to Texas Tech in June 2024.

athletes.name: Jacob Ponton
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$1.12M; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Ponton is Texas Tech's returning starting right tackle and a 2025 FWAA Freshman All-American, the only Big 12 offensive lineman named to that team.

athletes.name: Bryce Gilmore
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gilmore is a freshman offensive lineman from Prosper, Texas, who allowed no sacks as a senior and earned first team All-District 6-6A honors in each of his final two seasons. A consensus four-star recruit ranked among the top offensive tackles nationally, he played in the Navy All-American Bowl and enrolled in January 2026.

athletes.name: Sheridan Wilson
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$800K; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Wilson is Texas Tech's returning starting center, who played 1,021 offensive snaps in 2025 -- second-most on the team and the second-highest total among FBS centers.

athletes.name: Danilo Guberinich
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Guberinich is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Ann Arbor, Michigan, who played both offensive and defensive tackle at Detroit Catholic Central. He was an all-region selection as a senior for a team that went 12-1 and reached the Michigan state semifinals. He appeared in the 2025 season opener against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.

athletes.name: Daniel Sill
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sill is a junior offensive lineman from College Station, Texas, and an A&M Consolidated product who started at both tackle spots in high school. He appeared in all 14 games in 2025 as a reserve lineman and special teams player, logging 114 offensive snaps across guard and right tackle.

athletes.name: Garin Maley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Maley is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Omaha, Nebraska, who played offensive tackle and defensive end at Papillion-La Vista. He recorded 45 pancake blocks and 43 tackles with four sacks as a senior. A consensus three-star recruit rated among Nebraska's top prospects, he appeared in the 2025 season opener.

athletes.name: Jacob Crow
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Crow is a freshman offensive lineman from Knoxville, Tennessee, who played at Alcoa High School. He was a team captain and a first team all-state selection by the Tennessee Sports Writers Association as both a junior and a senior, and was Region 2-4A Offensive Lineman of the Year for a state championship team.

athletes.name: Elias Gillen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gillen is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Rapid City, South Dakota, who was a Class 11AAA first team all-state tackle at Stevens High School after allowing no sacks and recording 65 pancake blocks. He also swept his class state titles in the shot put and discus as a senior.

athletes.name: Ellis Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davis is a sophomore offensive lineman from Prosper, Texas, and was a consensus four-star signee in Texas Tech's 2024 class. 247Sports ranked him the No. 190 overall prospect and the No. 16 offensive tackle nationally. He was a unanimous first team All-District 5-6A selection as a senior and played in the Under Armour All-America Game in Orlando. Listed at 6-7 and 305 pounds, he is among the Red Raiders' developing tackles.

athletes.name: Howard Sampson
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$1.5M; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Sampson is Texas Tech's returning starting left tackle, a 6-8, 330-pound North Carolina transfer who announced his return for the 2026 season rather than entering the NFL Draft.

athletes.name: Kai Powell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Powell is a junior wide receiver from Spring, Texas, who joined Texas Tech as a walk-on before the 2025 season. At Klein High School he caught 34 passes for 690 yards and eight touchdowns as a senior and 38 for 790 yards as a junior. He made his collegiate debut against Oklahoma State.

athletes.name: Jack Esparza
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Esparza is a senior tight end from Austin who caught 33 passes for 785 yards and 14 touchdowns as a senior at St. Michael's Catholic. After redshirting in 2022 and moving from wide receiver to tight end, he made his collegiate debut in 2025 and appeared in three games. He earned his communications degree in December 2025.

athletes.name: Imari Jehiel
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jehiel is a freshman wide receiver from Forney, Texas, who totaled close to 2,000 receiving yards at Forney High School, including 931 yards and 10 touchdowns as a senior. He was a first team All-District 10-6A selection and returned a kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown in the playoffs.

athletes.name: Jett Carpenter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Carpenter is a senior tight end from Medford, Ore., who joined Texas Tech from Nevada, where he led the Wolf Pack in receiving with 35 catches for 374 yards and two touchdowns. He spent five prior seasons at FCS Eastern Washington and earned second team all-state honors at North Medford High School. Listed at 6-3 and 255 pounds, he adds experience behind returning starter Terrance Carter.

athletes.name: Sean Robinson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Robinson is a redshirt freshman edge rusher listed from Greenbrae, California, who played at Steele High School in Cibolo, Texas. He earned second team All-District 29-6A honors as a senior, primarily as a receiver. He appeared in one game in 2025 and moved from tight end to outside linebacker after the season.

athletes.name: Quintaelyn Joyner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Joyner is a redshirt freshman wide receiver from Austin who joined Texas Tech as a walk-on defensive back before the 2025 season. He played quarterback at Bastrop High School and helped the Bears to a 7-0 district title run in 2024. His older brother Quinten is a running back on the same roster.

athletes.name: Jason Llewellyn
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Llewellyn is a senior tight end from Aledo, Texas, who transferred to Texas Tech from Oklahoma in January 2024. A four-star prospect in the 2022 class, he was rated the No. 12 tight end nationally and the No. 43 recruit in Texas. He played 13 games across two seasons with the Sooners, mostly on special teams and as a reserve, and he helped Aledo reach a Class 5A Division II state title as a junior.

athletes.name: Ayden Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a freshman defensive lineman from Sulfur Springs, Texas, who played at Mount Pleasant High School. He was a District 7-5A first team pick as a senior and helped Mount Pleasant win its first playoff game in 27 years. A consensus three-star recruit, he enrolled at Texas Tech in January 2026.

athletes.name: Krush Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a freshman defensive lineman from Amarillo who played at Tascosa High School. He earned first team All-District 2-5A honors as both a junior and a senior, recording 103 tackles as a junior, and was a two-time Amarillo Globe-News Texas Panhandle Super Team selection. He enrolled at Texas Tech in January 2026.

athletes.name: Bryce Butler
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$936K; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Butler is a Washington transfer nose tackle from Toronto who projects as a starter on Texas Tech's rebuilt 2026 defensive front.

athletes.name: Dylan Singleton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Singleton is a redshirt freshman defensive lineman from New Iberia, Louisiana, who played at Loreauville High School. He recorded 73 tackles, 27 tackles for loss and five sacks as a senior while helping his team reach the Division III state quarterfinals. He redshirted in 2025 as a scout team member.

athletes.name: Christian Bruce
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bruce is a freshman defensive lineman from Alpharetta, Georgia, who played defensive tackle, offensive tackle and defensive end at Alpharetta High School. He was an honorable mention All-Region 6-6A selection by the Georgia High School Sports Association in 2024 and chose Texas Tech over Western Kentucky. His father played basketball at Clemson.

athletes.name: Keyshawn Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a sophomore defensive lineman from Houston who signed with Texas Tech out of Dekaney High School as a three-star prospect, choosing the Red Raiders over Rice and Marshall. As a senior he was a first team All-District 14-6A pick on both lines after recording 32 tackles, 17.5 of them for loss, 4.5 sacks and six forced fumbles. A three-sport athlete in high school, he is listed at 6-3 and 315 pounds.

athletes.name: Charles Anderson Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anderson is a sophomore edge rusher from Houston who committed to Texas Tech in June 2023 out of Pearland Dawson. A three-star prospect across the major services, he held 18 offers including Nebraska, Missouri, Oklahoma State, Kansas and Kansas State. He recorded 66 tackles, seven tackles for loss and four sacks as a senior while also playing center for the Dawson basketball team. He is listed at 6-6 and 275 pounds.

athletes.name: Mateen Ibirogba
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ibirogba is a senior defensive lineman from Clarksburg, Maryland who transferred to Texas Tech from Wake Forest after beginning his college career at Georgetown. Listed at 6-foot-3 and 296 pounds, he recorded three sacks, 21 quarterback hurries and a forced fumble in his final season with the Demon Deacons and entered the portal ranked as the No. 1 defensive lineman available by On3. He was an All-Montgomery County first team honoree and county most valuable player in 2021 at Clarksburg High School.

athletes.name: Jojo Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a junior defensive lineman from Salt Lake City who signed with Texas Tech from Oregon State in January 2026. In his final season with the Beavers he recorded 18 tackles, 6.5 tackles for loss, an interception and a team-high eight quarterback hurries. He was a Utah Class 5A first team all-state selection at Olympus High School and arrives with two seasons of eligibility. He is listed at 6-2 and 290 pounds.

athletes.name: Ben Roberts
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Texas Tech roster valuation ~$558K; no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Roberts is Texas Tech's returning starting middle linebacker, who made 74 tackles in 2025 and was the 2023 Big 12 Defensive Freshman of the Year with a program freshman-record 107 stops.

athletes.name: Ashton Hampton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A sophomore cornerback out of Pearland, Texas, Hampton is competing for a spot in the Red Raiders' two-deep this fall.

athletes.name: Luke Hamilton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Delano Townsend
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Will Echoles
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Echoles anchors the Ole Miss defensive line entering 2026. The junior from Houston, Mississippi started all 15 games during the Rebels' 2025 College Football Playoff run, posting 68 tackles, 11.5 tackles for loss and five sacks. He represented Ole Miss at SEC Media Days, publicly confirmed his return for 2026, and is widely projected as one of the nation's top interior defensive linemen and a potential first round NFL draft pick.

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

Head coach Pete Golding has singled out the sophomore from Hyattsville, Maryland as a standout of spring and summer work, calling his play at left tackle as good as he can remember at the position.

athletes.name: Carius Curne
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Tommy Kinsler IV

He is in his first season with the Rebels and is one of several linemen the program added through the portal for 2026, joining arrivals from Oklahoma, LSU and Florida in the competition for snaps up front.

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He enters 2026 as one of three returning interior starters up front alongside guards Delano Townsend and Patrick Kutas.

athletes.name: Kamron Beavers
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Cam Clark
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A sophomore edge rusher out of Medina, Tenn., Clark is competing for a spot in the Rebels' two-deep this fall.

athletes.name: Evan Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation ~$650K; not a disclosed deal figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is BYU's returning starting cornerback and a preseason first-team All-Big 12 pick after leading the Cougars with five interceptions in 2025, including the pick that sealed the Pop-Tarts Bowl win over Georgia Tech.

athletes.name: Tei Nacua
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nacua is a projected starting wide receiver for BYU and the younger brother of NFL receivers Puka and Samson Nacua. The Provo native came to BYU out of Timpview High School.

athletes.name: Therrian Alexander III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alexander is BYU's returning starting cornerback opposite Evan Johnson and a preseason third-team All-Big 12 selection. The Ellenwood, Georgia native goes by 'Tre.'

athletes.name: Jonathan Kabeya
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kabeya is a redshirt sophomore cornerback from Euless, Texas, who played in nine games as a true freshman in 2024 and saw limited action in 2025. He profiles as one of the few natural slot corners on BYU's roster and has been flagged as a pivotal player entering 2026 fall camp. A three star recruit out of Byron Nelson High, he recorded 10 interceptions and 55 solo tackles in high school and was a first team all district pick. Three of his brothers played college football.

athletes.name: Roger Saleapaga II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Saleapaga is a projected co-starting tight end for BYU after transferring from Oregon. The Orem native gives the Cougars a second high-profile tight end alongside USC transfer Walker Lyons.

athletes.name: Raider Damuni
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Damuni is a returning starting safety for BYU who made 43 tackles in 2025. The Provo native and Timpview product starts alongside Faletau Satuala.

athletes.name: Kyler Kasper
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kasper is a projected starting wide receiver for BYU after transferring from Oregon. The 6-foot-6 Chandler, Arizona native was a top national recruit who chose the Ducks over Ohio State, Georgia and Notre Dame, and is the son of former NFL receiver Kevin Kasper.

athletes.name: LJ Martin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation ~$1.0M; not a disclosed deal figure)
athletes.blurb: Martin is BYU's returning feature back and the 2025 Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year after rushing for 1,305 yards and 12 touchdowns. The El Paso native bypassed the NFL Draft to return for 2026 and is a preseason third-team All-America pick.

athletes.name: Cade Uluave
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Uluave is BYU's projected starting linebacker after transferring from Cal, where he made 97 tackles in 2025. He was rated the top linebacker in the 2026 portal cycle and is a preseason fourth-team All-America and first-team All-Big 12 selection.

athletes.name: Cody Hagen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hagen came to BYU from Corner Canyon High in Draper, Utah, where he won 2021 Utah Gatorade Player of the Year honors after 89 catches for 1,805 yards and 23 touchdowns. The junior receiver caught 15 passes for 126 yards across two seasons in Provo and added two rushing touchdowns. He announced a medical retirement from football in May 2026 and no longer appears on the Cougars roster.

athletes.name: Nusi Taumoepeau
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taumoepeau is projected to start at defensive end for BYU in 2026 after flashing as a true freshman. A late addition to the Cougars' 2025 signing class out of Westlake High School in Saratoga Springs, he was rated Utah's third-best prospect by 247Sports and piled up 88 tackles, 12 sacks and 13 tackles for loss as a senior. He played roughly 130 snaps in 2025, finishing with 12 tackles and a sack, and made his first career start in the Pop-Tarts Bowl against Georgia Tech, where he led BYU in tackles and forced a fumble.

athletes.name: Walker Lyons
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lyons is a projected starting tight end for BYU after transferring from USC, where he caught 20 passes for 223 yards in 2025. The Folsom, California native is among the most-followed players on BYU's roster with more than 100,000 followers on both Instagram and TikTok.

athletes.name: Treyson Bourguet
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bourguet, a redshirt senior from Tucson, Arizona, transferred to BYU from Western Michigan in January 2024. He threw for 1,314 yards with six touchdowns and two interceptions over 10 games for the Broncos. At BYU he has appeared in one game, the 69-0 win over Portland State, and enters 2026 as the most experienced backup behind starter Bear Bachmeier.

athletes.name: Orion Maile-Kaufusi
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Maile-Kaufusi is a redshirt sophomore defensive end from Salt Lake City who prepped at East High. Listed at 6-3 and 242 pounds on BYU's 2026 roster, he is among the names in the mix for the two-deep at defensive end, a group that also includes Hunter Clegg, Bodie Schoonover, Nusi Taumoepeau and Tausili Akana. BYU coaches have said the rotation will be settled in fall camp.

athletes.name: Faletau Satuala
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Satuala is BYU's returning starting safety and led the Cougars with 83 tackles in 2025. He enters 2026 as a preseason fourth-team All-America and first-team All-Big 12 selection.

athletes.name: Preston Rex
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rex is a redshirt senior walk-on from San Clemente, California, who played slot receiver and safety at San Clemente High. He originally joined BYU as a safety before Kalani Sitake asked him to move to running back, and he was in line for carries behind LJ Martin late in 2025. His father Byron was an All-American tight end at BYU, and his brother Isaac also played tight end for the Cougars.

athletes.name: Jojo Phillips
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Phillips is a projected starting wide receiver for BYU and a preseason fourth-team All-Big 12 pick. The Sierra Canyon product missed roughly two months of the 2025 season with an injury before returning down the stretch.

athletes.name: Tausili Akana
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Akana is a BYU edge rusher and former Texas transfer who sits in the two-deep at defensive end for 2026. The Laie, Hawaii native was a four-star recruit out of Kahuku.

athletes.name: Jayven Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams, a redshirt senior from Mobile, Alabama, joined BYU in January 2026 after playing at Mississippi State. He appeared in all 13 games for the Bulldogs in 2025 and recorded 10 tackles, two forced fumbles and an interception against Arizona State. He began his career at Kennesaw State and brings 37 games of experience. He projects as a rotational outside corner with one year of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Isaiah Glasker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Glasker is a returning starting linebacker for BYU who recorded 66 tackles in 2025, second most on the team. He is a preseason second-team All-Big 12 pick.

athletes.name: Owen Geilman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Owen Geilman is a freshman quarterback on the BYU roster, wearing No. 16. He is from Bountiful, Utah, and played his high school football at Bountiful High School. BYU lists him at 6-foot-4 and 220 pounds.

athletes.name: Jarinn Kalama
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kalama is a redshirt sophomore safety listed out of Honolulu, Hawaii. He began high school at Mililani before moving to Utah and finishing at Wasatch High, where he totaled 124 catches for 1,504 yards along with 65 tackles and two interceptions. He served a mission in Mexico before enrolling. At 6-3 and 210 pounds he is in the rotation mix in a deep BYU safety room for 2026.

athletes.name: Enoch Watson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Ace Kaufusi
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kaufusi is a redshirt junior linebacker from Kahuku, Hawaii, who played at Kahuku High. He comes from an extensive BYU football family, including cousins Maika Kaufusi on the current roster and former Cougars Isaiah, Jackson, Bronson and Corbin Kaufusi. At 6-4 and 235 pounds he is a reserve behind a projected 2026 starting group of Cade Uluave, Isaiah Glasker and Siale Esera.

athletes.name: Reggie Frischknecht
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Frischknecht is a redshirt sophomore receiver listed out of Ephraim, Utah. He caught 38 passes for 740 yards and 14 touchdowns at Snow College in 2024, leading all NJCAA players in receiving scores and setting a school record. He signed with Weber State before transferring to BYU in spring 2025. At 6-4 and 207 pounds he offers a big target on the outside.

athletes.name: Fuller Shurtz
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

Listed at 5-11 and 185 pounds, the redshirt freshman served a mission in Veracruz, Mexico before enrolling. He prepped at Katy High School in Texas, where he was part of a 6A state championship team, earned academic all district honors and was also named a 6A all district goalkeeper of the year in soccer.

athletes.name: Tiger Bachmeier
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Max Barker

athletes.name: Miles Hall
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He was rated a three-star prospect and ranked around the top 15 in the state, and recorded 75 tackles and four tackles for loss as a senior while also playing tight end and running sprints in track. He is listed at 6-1 and 230 pounds.

athletes.name: Jaron Pula

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

A Heber City, Utah, native, he came to Provo from New Mexico State, committing in April 2025 with three seasons of eligibility remaining. Before that he played at Snow College, catching 13 passes for 163 yards and two touchdowns in 2023, and he did not appear in a game for the Aggies in 2024.

athletes.name: Devaughn Eka
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Eka is a true freshman running back from Lehi, Utah, who signed with BYU in the 2026 class out of Lehi High. A three-star prospect rated among the top recruits in the state, he rushed for more than 3,200 career yards, including 1,038 as a senior. He arrived alongside Lehi teammate Legend Glasker, and offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick has said an early contribution would not surprise him.

athletes.name: Kennan Pula
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pula is a true freshman safety from Highland, Utah, and a four-star Lone Peak High product who flipped his commitment from Utah to BYU.
