athletes.blurb: Luke Hutchinson is a freshman tight end at Mississippi State from Nashville, Tennessee. The official Bulldogs roster lists him as coming from Avon Old Farms School, a Connecticut prep program, and carries him at No. 85.

athletes.name: Sam West
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: West came to Mississippi State from Indiana ahead of the 2025 season. The redshirt junior from Greensburg, Indiana played in all 13 games for the Hoosiers in 2024, including their College Football Playoff appearance, catching one pass for 37 yards. A former high school quarterback at Greensburg, he was rated the nation's No. 25 tight end in the 2023 class by On3 and gives the Bulldogs an experienced blocker and depth target at tight end.

athletes.name: Tico Crittendon Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tico Crittendon Jr. is a freshman defensive lineman at Mississippi State from Lithonia, Georgia. He came to the Bulldogs out of Lithonia High School and is listed at No. 88 along the defensive front on the official roster.

athletes.name: Ethan Pulliam
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pulliam returns as Mississippi State's starting punter after a record-setting 2025. The Starkville native averaged 46.8 yards per punt, a single-season program record, with 18 punts of 50 yards or more, earning second team All-America honors from Sporting News and third team All-SEC recognition from Phil Steele. A redshirt junior, he began his college career as a Bulldog baseball player before committing full time to football.

athletes.name: Joeseph Skipworth
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Joeseph Skipworth is a redshirt freshman tight end at Mississippi State from Pace, Florida. He played his high school football at Pace High School and is listed at No. 88 in the Bulldogs tight end group.

athletes.name: Jessie Primer IV
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jessie Primer IV is a redshirt freshman wide receiver at Mississippi State from Canton, Mississippi. He played at Canton Academy before joining the Bulldogs and is listed at No. 89 in the receiver group on the official roster.

athletes.name: Davon Young
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davon Young is a freshman defensive lineman at Mississippi State from Mobile, Alabama. He came to Starkville out of Theodore High School and is listed at No. 90 along the Bulldogs defensive front on the official roster.

athletes.name: Kaleb Morris
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kaleb Morris is a freshman defensive lineman at Mississippi State from Mobile, Alabama. He played his high school football at Mary G. Montgomery High School and is listed at No. 92 on the official Bulldogs roster.

athletes.name: Jayson Jenkins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jenkins is a redshirt senior defensive lineman from Bordentown, New Jersey, who joined Mississippi State from Florida State in January 2026. He began his career at Tennessee, where he redshirted and then worked as a reserve tackle, posting 15 tackles and two sacks in 2024. He started five of 12 games for the Seminoles in 2025 and recorded 17 tackles and a sack. At 6-6 and 280 pounds he adds experienced depth.

athletes.name: Diesel Moye
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moye is a redshirt senior defensive lineman from Phenix City, Alabama, who came to Mississippi State from Tyler Junior College in Texas. He prepped at Smiths Station High School and played in 11 games in his first season with the Bulldogs, recording 10 tackles without a start. Listed at 6-5 and 345 pounds, he provides size on the interior and is competing for rotation snaps in 2026.

athletes.name: Douglas Adams III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Douglas Adams III is a junior defensive lineman at Mississippi State from San Francisco, California. He played at Menlo-Atherton High School and then at Foothill College before joining the Bulldogs, arriving in Starkville by way of the junior college route. The official Mississippi State roster lists him at No. 33.

athletes.name: Chris Addison
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chris Addison is a freshman edge rusher at Mississippi State from Winnsboro, Louisiana. He came to the Bulldogs out of Franklin Parish High School and is listed at No. 48 on the official roster for the 2026 season.

athletes.name: Lorenz Cammon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lorenz Cammon is a junior defensive lineman at Mississippi State from Upland, California. He played at Upland High School and then at Victor Valley College before joining the Bulldogs, reaching the Southeastern Conference by way of junior college. The official Mississippi State roster lists him at No. 91 along the defensive front.

athletes.name: Jayden Cration
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jayden Cration is a freshman wide receiver at Mississippi State from Canton, Mississippi. He stayed in state after playing at Canton High School and is listed at No. 16 in the Bulldogs receiver group on the official roster.

athletes.name: Zion Crumpton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zion Crumpton is a freshman wide receiver at Mississippi State from Montgomery, Alabama. He came to Starkville out of Carver High School and is listed at No. 81 in the Bulldogs receiver group on the official roster.

athletes.name: Oisin Flynn
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Oisin Flynn is a freshman kicker and punter at Mississippi State who is listed on the official Bulldogs roster as coming from Ireland. No high school is listed for him, and he wears No. 83 among the specialists.

athletes.name: Jamari Freeman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jamari Freeman is a redshirt senior offensive lineman at Mississippi State from Fairburn, Georgia. He played at Langston Hughes High School and spent time at Mercer before transferring to Starkville. The official Bulldogs roster lists him at No. 62 and places him among the more experienced players on the offensive line.

athletes.name: Shawn Gee
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Shawn Gee is a sophomore edge rusher at Mississippi State from Birmingham, Alabama. He played at Shades Valley High School and then at Mississippi Delta Community College before joining the Bulldogs. The official Mississippi State roster lists him at No. 49 among the players working on the defensive edge.

athletes.name: James Heard Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: James Heard Jr. is a redshirt junior linebacker at Mississippi State from Camden, New Jersey. He played at Camden High School and began his college career at Syracuse before transferring to Starkville. The official Bulldogs roster lists him at No. 45 in the linebacker group for the 2026 season.

athletes.name: Terrell Johnson Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Terrell Johnson Jr. is a freshman cornerback at Mississippi State from Lexington, Mississippi. He stayed in state after playing at Holmes County Central High School and is listed at No. 36 in the Bulldogs secondary.

athletes.name: Terrance Love
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Terrance Love is a redshirt junior safety at Mississippi State from Atlanta, Georgia. He played at Langston Hughes High School in Fairburn and spent time at Colorado before transferring to Starkville. The official Bulldogs roster lists him at No. 31 among the safeties for the 2026 season.

athletes.name: Dre Otey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dre Otey is a freshman cornerback at Mississippi State from Murfreesboro, Tennessee. He came to the Bulldogs out of Riverdale High School and is listed at No. 37 among the defensive backs on the official roster.

athletes.name: Kison Shepard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kison Shepard is a junior offensive tackle at Mississippi State from Memphis, Tennessee. He played at Germantown High School and then at East Mississippi Community College before joining the Bulldogs. The official Mississippi State roster lists him at No. 74 among the tackles for the 2026 season.

athletes.name: Fisher Southall
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fisher Southall is a freshman wide receiver at Mississippi State from Fairhope, Alabama. He came to Starkville out of Fairhope High School and is listed at No. 80 in the Bulldogs receiver group on the official roster.

athletes.name: Dylan Steen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dylan Steen is a freshman offensive lineman at Mississippi State from Doral, Florida. He played his high school football at St. Thomas Aquinas High School and is listed at No. 53 on the official Bulldogs roster.

athletes.name: Antavious Watts
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Antavious Watts is a freshman safety at Mississippi State from Columbus, Georgia. He came to the Bulldogs out of Carver High School and is listed at No. 27 in the Mississippi State secondary on the official roster.

athletes.name: Isaac Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard roster valuation, June 2026, lists $607,103; no publicly reported deal figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is Mississippi State's returning starting safety and the centerpiece of its defense, having led the SEC with 127 tackles in 2024. He announced he would return to Starkville for 2026 rather than leave the program.

athletes.name: Junior Sherrill
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sherrill is Vanderbilt's leading returning wide receiver after catching 54 passes for 784 yards and seven touchdowns in 2025. The Nashville native is ranked the Commodores' best player entering 2026 by Vanderbilt on SI.

athletes.name: Cobey Sellers
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sellers is a sophomore cornerback from Houston who transferred to Vanderbilt from Texas A&M. He came out of Shadow Creek High School as a 2024 signee ranked around No. 255 nationally in the 247Sports Composite, and he also carried an extensive track and field background. Length and press coverage are his calling cards, and he enters 2026 competing for a rotation role in a crowded Commodores secondary.

athletes.name: Blaze Berlowitz
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Berlowitz is a senior quarterback from Cushing, Oklahoma, who spent his first college season at New Mexico State before joining Vanderbilt. He made his collegiate debut in the Conference USA championship game, completing 10 of 19 passes for 134 yards and a touchdown. He threw 30 touchdowns in a season for a top-ranked Class 4A team at Cushing High School and reunited with offensive coordinator Tim Beck, his former New Mexico State play caller.

athletes.name: Dontae Carter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Carter is a junior safety from Cibolo, Texas, who has appeared in all 13 games in each of his first two seasons at Vanderbilt. He recorded 33 tackles in 2025, including a season-high six against Missouri, and added kickoff return work in the ReliaQuest Bowl against Iowa. As a freshman in 2024 he posted 11 tackles and two pass breakups. Carter was a four-star recruit rated among the nation's top 25 safeties by On3 and 247Sports, and he chose Vanderbilt over Missouri, Nebraska and Texas Tech.

athletes.name: Jared Curtis
athletes.source: Reported (On3's Pete Nakos reported Curtis is expected to earn roughly $2M in his first college season; On3 NIL valuation ~$1.7M)
athletes.blurb: Curtis is Vanderbilt's projected starting quarterback and the highest-rated signee in program history, a five-star from Nashville Christian who was the consensus No. 1 quarterback prospect in his class. He has yet to take a college snap after choosing Vanderbilt over Georgia.

athletes.name: Jaylin Lackey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lackey is a junior cornerback from Monroe, Georgia, who signed with Vanderbilt out of South Gwinnett High School as a unanimous three-star prospect ranked among the top 70 corners nationally. He played all 13 games as a freshman in 2024 with five starts, finishing with 14 tackles and two pass breakups. He remains in the mix for snaps on the boundary and on special teams in 2026.

athletes.name: Carson Lawrence
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lawrence is a sophomore safety from Chattanooga who signed out of the McCallie School as a four-star prospect and, by 247Sports rankings, one of the highest rated recruits in Vanderbilt history. He recorded 64 tackles and five interceptions over his final two high school seasons, returning one 42 yards for a touchdown in a state semifinal. He projects into the safety rotation in 2026.

athletes.name: Jamezell Lassiter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lassiter is a junior running back from Providence, Rhode Island, who played at La Salle Academy before a final prep season at Deerfield Academy in Massachusetts. He was a first team All-Rhode Island selection and ran for more than 2,000 yards with 25 touchdowns across two high school seasons. Listed at 5-8, he competes for change of pace carries in a deep Vanderbilt backfield in 2026.

athletes.name: Martel Hight
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hight is Vanderbilt's returning starting cornerback and intercepted four passes in 2025 after moving to defense full time. He is one of the Commodores' highest-graded returning defenders and also returns punts.

athletes.name: Tristen Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is a junior slot receiver from Houston who committed to Vanderbilt in July 2023 over Utah and Northwestern. He left Lamar High School as the program's all-time leader in receptions, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, finishing with 98 catches for 2,275 yards and 28 scores, and was a two-time district offensive most valuable player. He also offers value as a kick returner.

athletes.name: Issa Ouattara
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ouattara is Vanderbilt's projected starting nose tackle after missing most of 2025 with a shoulder injury. The Cologne, Germany native is among the Commodores' most physically gifted defensive linemen.

athletes.name: Ja'Cory Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a transfer wide receiver projected as Vanderbilt's vertical threat in 2026 after working as a downfield playmaker at Old Dominion.

athletes.name: Jordan Matthews
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Matthews is Vanderbilt's projected starting boundary cornerback entering his senior season.

athletes.name: Ricardo Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is Vanderbilt's projected starting strong safety after transferring from Clemson, where he was an All-ACC pick in 2025. His six interceptions led the ACC and were the most by a Clemson player since 2009.

athletes.name: Cole Adams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Adams is Vanderbilt's projected starting slot receiver after transferring from Alabama, where he caught five passes for 71 yards and a touchdown and served as the Crimson Tide's primary punt returner in 2025.

athletes.name: Jayvontay Conner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Conner is a junior tight end from Winston-Salem, North Carolina, who joins Vanderbilt after stops at Ole Miss and East Carolina. He played 12 games with six starts for the Pirates in 2025, collecting 98 receiving yards highlighted by a 79-yard catch against NC State and a touchdown reception against UTSA. He caught his first career touchdown in 2024 against Florida Atlantic and appeared in three games at Ole Miss in 2023. A consensus three-star recruit, Conner was ranked the No. 17 tight end nationally by ESPN out of East Forsyth High School.

athletes.name: CJ Heard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Heard led Vanderbilt in tackles in 2025 and returns as a starter in the secondary, adding three pass breakups, an interception and a forced fumble. He joined the Commodores from FAU via the transfer portal.

athletes.name: Brycen Coleman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Coleman is projected as Vanderbilt's starting outside receiver in 2026 after contributing in the Commodores' rotation in 2025.

athletes.name: Jalen Gilbert
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gilbert is a senior safety from Round Rock, Texas, who committed to Vanderbilt in December 2022 as a unanimous three-star prospect rated the No. 41 safety in his class by On3. He chose the Commodores over offers from Arizona State, Washington State, West Virginia and UNLV. Entering 2026, he is a veteran depth piece in a safety room that returns experience ahead of him.

athletes.name: Whit Muschamp
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Whit Muschamp is a junior quarterback on the Vanderbilt Commodores roster. He is from Columbia, South Carolina, and played his high school football at the Baylor School. He wears No. 10 and is listed at 6-1 and 195 pounds.

athletes.name: Brian Allen Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Allen is projected to start at defensive end for Vanderbilt opposite Miles Capers in 2026.

athletes.name: Jack Elliott
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jack Elliott is a sophomore quarterback at Vanderbilt. He comes from Orland Park, Illinois, where he played at Mount Carmel High School. Elliott wears No. 11 for the Commodores and is listed at 6-0 and 205 pounds.

athletes.name: Bryan Longwell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Longwell is Vanderbilt's returning starting linebacker and the team's leading returning tackler, finishing second on the roster in tackles with 18 tackles for loss in 2025 after leading the Commodores in tackles in 2024.

athletes.name: Walter Taylor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taylor is a senior tight end from Jackson, Alabama, who originally signed with Vanderbilt as a three-star quarterback in the 2022 class. He appeared in five games in 2023, passing for 44 yards and rushing 30 times for 103 yards and a touchdown, then transferred to Colorado and later Ball State before returning to Nashville. He is making the move to tight end with one season of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Vanzale Hinton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Vanzale Hinton is a sophomore safety for Vanderbilt. His hometown is Chattanooga, Tennessee, and the official roster lists him out of Paducah Tilghman High School. He wears No. 12 and is listed at 6-0 and 196 pounds.

athletes.name: Kayleb Barnett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Barnett is a sophomore receiver from Tulsa who caught 30 passes for 607 yards and eight touchdowns in his lone season at Jenks after two years at Broken Arrow. He was an Oklahoma Class 6A state champion in the 100 meters and the long jump as a junior. Vanderbilt flipped him from Central Arkansas, and his speed projects him as a gadget and return option.

athletes.name: Tate Hamby
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tate Hamby is a junior linebacker on the Vanderbilt roster. He is from West Monroe, Louisiana, and played high school football at Ouachita Christian. Hamby wears No. 13 for the Commodores and is listed at 6-2 and 208 pounds.

athletes.name: Jailen Ruth
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ruth is a junior listed at safety who enrolled at Vanderbilt in January 2023 from Hawthorne, Florida, as a unanimous three-star prospect who chose the Commodores over Iowa State and Washington State. He was the Gainesville Sun small school defensive player of the year in 2021 and finished his Hawthorne career with 49 sacks while helping the school reach three straight state title games.

athletes.name: Drew Cowart
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Drew Cowart is a sophomore quarterback at Vanderbilt. He comes from Queen Creek, Arizona, where he played at ALA Queen Creek. Cowart wears No. 14 for the Commodores and is listed on the roster at 6-2 and 208 pounds.

athletes.name: Joseph McVay
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McVay is a junior receiver from Earle, Arkansas, who signed with Vanderbilt in the 2024 class after back to back Arkansas 2A all-state selections and a junior season of 69 catches for 1,573 yards and 22 touchdowns. He scored on his first career reception, a 65 yard touchdown against Missouri in 2024, and added a second career touchdown catch in the ReliaQuest Bowl.

athletes.name: Mike Diatta
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Diatta is a graduate defensive lineman from Antioch, Tennessee, who returned home in January 2026 through the transfer portal. A three-star prospect out of Cane Ridge High School, he spent four seasons at Virginia and one at Oklahoma State before choosing Vanderbilt. Listed at 6-5 and 295 pounds, he enters his sixth college season as an experienced interior body in the defensive line rotation.

athletes.name: Cole Spence
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Spence is Vanderbilt's projected starting tight end following Eli Stowers' departure, catching 15 passes for 233 yards and two touchdowns in a primarily blocking role in 2025.

athletes.name: Jaylin Davies
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davies is a graduate cornerback from Rancho Cucamonga, California, and a former four-star Mater Dei recruit who arrives at Vanderbilt after stops at Oregon, UCLA and Oklahoma State. His most productive season came at UCLA, where he recorded 32 tackles and three interceptions, including one returned for a touchdown. He gives the Commodores an experienced option in a reworked secondary in 2026.

athletes.name: Edwin Kolenge
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kolenge is a graduate edge rusher from Montreal, Quebec, who committed to Vanderbilt in January 2026 after four seasons at Boston College. He played all 12 games in 2025 with 10 starts, recording 31 tackles, one tackle for loss and one sack. He prepped at the Loomis Chaffee School in Connecticut and brings one year of eligibility to a rebuilt Commodores edge group.

athletes.name: Maurice Veney
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Veney is a junior tight end from Philadelphia who transferred to Vanderbilt from Division II Morehouse College in November. He caught 32 passes for 381 yards and three touchdowns in 2025 and earned first team All-SIAC honors. Originally an Army offensive tackle commit out of Roman Catholic High School, he moved to tight end in college and has at least two seasons of eligibility left.

athletes.name: Josiah Broxton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Josiah Broxton is a sophomore linebacker for Vanderbilt. He is from Tallahassee, Florida, and the official Commodores roster lists him as coming to the program from Florida State. Broxton wears No. 18 and is listed at 5-10 and 220 pounds.

athletes.name: CJ Jackson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson is a junior edge rusher from Tucker, Georgia, who committed to Vanderbilt in January 2026 after two seasons at LSU. A four-star recruit who backed off a Georgia Tech pledge before signing with the Tigers, he appeared in one game in 2024 and five in 2025, finishing with three tackles and two tackles for loss. He has three years of eligibility and figures into the edge rotation.

athletes.name: Izayah Lee
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Izayah Lee is a freshman running back at Vanderbilt. He is from Lancaster, Texas, and played his high school football at Lancaster High School. Lee wears No. 20 for the Commodores and is listed at 5-11 and 215 pounds.

athletes.name: Jamison Curtis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Curtis is a junior linebacker from Mobile, Alabama, who signed with Vanderbilt in November 2023 out of Saraland High School. He totaled 107 tackles, 3.5 sacks and two interceptions in high school and helped Saraland win the Alabama Class 6A state championship in 2022. Rivals ranked him the No. 44 linebacker nationally. He competes for rotation snaps and special teams work in 2026.

athletes.name: Davin Chandler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davin Chandler is a sophomore safety on the Vanderbilt roster. He comes from Berlin, Maryland, where he played at Stephen Decatur High School. Chandler wears No. 21 for the Commodores and is listed at 6-0 and 190 pounds.

athletes.name: Makhilyn Young
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Young is Vanderbilt's No. 2 running back and averaged 9.0 yards per carry in 2025 after missing the entire 2024 season.

athletes.name: Bryce Cowan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cowan is a senior linebacker from Tallahassee who committed to Vanderbilt in July 2021 as a three-star prospect out of Amos P. Godby High School. He led Godby with 102 tackles as a senior while playing mostly safety, and the Commodores projected him as a versatile outside linebacker. A multi-sport athlete in high school, he enters 2026 as veteran depth in the linebacker room.

athletes.name: Evan Hampton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hampton is a freshman running back from Owensboro, Kentucky, who was named the 2025-26 Kentucky Gatorade Football Player of the Year. He rushed for 1,835 yards and 28 touchdowns as a senior, including a 326 yard state quarterfinal that broke a program record standing since 1982, and led Owensboro to the Class 5A title game. He flipped his commitment from Louisville to Vanderbilt.

athletes.name: Bishop Starling
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bishop Starling is a freshman cornerback at Vanderbilt and a Nashville, Tennessee, native. He played his high school football at the Ensworth School. Starling wears No. 23 for the Commodores and is listed at 5-9 and 170 pounds.

athletes.name: Gabe Fields
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gabe Fields is a sophomore running back for Vanderbilt. He is from Saint Joseph, Missouri, and played at Central High School. Fields wears No. 24 for the Commodores and is listed on the official roster at 6-0 and 217 pounds.

athletes.name: Nick Rinaldi
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rinaldi is projected to start at linebacker alongside Bryan Longwell after posting 47 tackles, seven tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks and nine quarterback hurries in 2025.

athletes.name: Mason Lewis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mason Lewis is a freshman safety on the Vanderbilt roster. He comes from Queen Creek, Arizona, where he played his high school football at Basha. Lewis wears No. 25 for the Commodores and is listed at 6-0 and 195 pounds.

athletes.name: Cayden Daniels
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Daniels is a sophomore cornerback from Cordele, Georgia, who enrolled at Vanderbilt in January 2025 out of Crisp County High School. A unanimous three-star prospect rated the No. 46 cornerback in his class by Rivals, he made 40 tackles with two interceptions as a senior, returning both for touchdowns, after posting three picks and five tackles for loss as a junior.

athletes.name: Bradley Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bradley Brown is a freshman safety at Vanderbilt. He is from Plano, Texas, and played his high school football at Plano High School. Brown wears No. 27 for the Commodores and is listed on the roster at 6-0 and 185 pounds.

athletes.name: Sedrick Alexander
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alexander is Vanderbilt's returning starting running back, rushing for a team-high 567 yards and 11 touchdowns and adding 19 catches for 200 yards and four scores in 2025. He started all 13 games of the Commodores' 10-3 season.

athletes.name: Thomas Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas Jones is a sophomore safety for Vanderbilt. He comes from Smyrna, Tennessee, where he played at Smyrna High School. Jones wears No. 28 for the Commodores and is listed on the official roster at 5-11 and 195 pounds.

athletes.name: Miles Capers
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Capers is Vanderbilt's veteran starting edge rusher entering a sixth season, recording 4.5 sacks with a forced fumble and a fumble recovery in 2025. He is the only player remaining from the start of Clark Lea's tenure.

athletes.name: Austin Howard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Austin Howard is a sophomore linebacker on the Vanderbilt roster. He is from Memphis, Tennessee, and played his high school football at Bartlett. Howard wears No. 30 for the Commodores and is listed at 6-2 and 245 pounds.

athletes.name: Jeremy Garner II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jeremy Garner II is a freshman cornerback at Vanderbilt. He comes from Rosharon, Texas, where he played at Iowa Colony High School. Garner wears No. 31 for the Commodores and is listed on the roster at 6-2 and 155 pounds.

athletes.name: Mason Carter
