athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Saint Paul is a junior wide receiver for UCLA who came to the program from Oregon. He played his high school football at Carlsbad High School in his hometown of Carlsbad, California. Listed at 5-11 and 185 pounds, he wears No. 86 in a Bruins receiver room stocked largely with transfers from other programs.

athletes.name: Julian Armella
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Armella joined UCLA from Florida State after signing with the Seminoles out of St. Thomas Aquinas High School in Fort Lauderdale, one of the nation's top programs. The Miami native is a fifth-year senior listed at 6-6 and 333 pounds and wears No. 74. He is among the most experienced additions to a Bruins offensive line remade through the portal.

athletes.name: Dylan Sims
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sims is a sophomore tight end for the Bruins from Queen Creek, Arizona, where he played at Queen Creek High School. He is listed at 6-5 and 232 pounds and wears No. 87.

athletes.name: Aiden Gobaira
athletes.source: Estimate (aggregated 2026 NIL valuation reported as 'over $1 million'; no deal terms publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Gobaira is projected to start at edge opposite Sahir West after transferring from James Madison. The former Notre Dame signee recorded 38 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss and four sacks in 2025 and earned third-team All-Sun Belt honors.

athletes.name: Peter Bario
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bario is a senior tight end for UCLA from Sherman Oaks, California, who played his high school football at Campbell Hall School in Studio City. He wears No. 44 and is listed at 6-2 and 241 pounds.

athletes.name: Noah Fox-Flores
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fox-Flores is a sophomore tight end for UCLA from Tacoma, Washington, where he played at Graham-Kapowsin High School. He is listed at 6-3 and 244 pounds and wears No. 82.

athletes.name: Russell Weir
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Weir is a junior wide receiver for the Bruins from Corona del Mar, California, who played at Corona del Mar High School. He wears No. 83 and is listed at 6-1 and 201 pounds.

athletes.name: Grant Buckey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Buckey is a senior defensive lineman for UCLA out of Bakersfield, California, and Liberty High School. He is listed at 6-5 and 266 pounds and wears No. 88. UCLA's roster also carries freshman offensive lineman Quinn Buckey from the same high school.

athletes.name: Hall Schmidt
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Schmidt transferred to UCLA from Boise State for his final season of eligibility. The redshirt senior from Gig Harbor, Washington, started 12 games at right tackle in 2024, when the Broncos went 12-2 and reached the College Football Playoff for the first time in program history. A three-star recruit out of Peninsula High School, the 6-foot-6, 317-pound tackle is expected to compete for a starting job on the Bruins' rebuilt offensive line in 2026.

athletes.name: Salem Abdul-Wahab
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Abdul-Wahab enters 2026 on the Patrick Mannelly Award watch list, which honors the nation's top long snapper. The redshirt senior from Fontana, California, handled 100 percent of UCLA's long snaps in 2025, appearing in all 12 games on field goals, punts and extra points. A Summit High School product, he began his college career at Northern Colorado before transferring to UCLA in 2023 and has been the Bruins' primary snapper for the past two seasons.

athletes.name: Jewelous "JuJu" Walls
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Walls signed with UCLA out of Pittsburg High School in Northern California, where he was a two-time Bay Valley Athletic League defensive lineman of the year and posted 83 tackles, 13 tackles for loss and five sacks as a senior. Rated a three-star edge, he committed to the Bruins in August 2024. The sophomore wears No. 41 at 6-2 and 191 pounds.

athletes.name: Quinn Buckey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Buckey is a freshman offensive lineman for UCLA out of Bakersfield, California, and Liberty High School. He is listed at 6-6 and 306 pounds and wears No. 73. Senior defensive lineman Grant Buckey is also on the roster from the same high school.

athletes.name: Sam Yoon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Yoon chose UCLA in the 2022 class out of Loyola High School in Los Angeles, picking the Bruins over USC, California and Notre Dame. The Pasadena native has appeared in 24 games with 20 starts, all at center, and enters 2026 as a fifth-year senior wearing No. 64 at 6-5 and 315 pounds. He is among the few returning linemen on a heavily rebuilt front.

athletes.name: Harry Lodge
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lodge transferred to UCLA from Wake Forest after prepping at Belmont Hill School near his Cambridge, Massachusetts home. At 6-7 and 247 pounds, the fifth-year senior is the tallest tight end on the 2026 Bruins roster and wears No. 47. He joins Kansas State transfer Brayden Loftin among the portal additions at the position.

athletes.name: DJ Bordeaux
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bordeaux is a freshman quarterback for UCLA from Aurora, Colorado, where he played at Legend High School. He is listed at 6-2 and 200 pounds and wears No. 18.

athletes.name: Mason Rivera
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rivera is a fifth-year defensive back for UCLA who came to the program from Cal Poly. He played his high school football at Kimball High School in his hometown of Tracy, California. Listed at 6-0 and 190 pounds, he wears No. 28 and is one of the more experienced players in the Bruins secondary.

athletes.name: Jayden Fox
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fox is listed as a freshman running back for UCLA from Denver, Colorado, wearing No. 29. He does not appear on the Bruins published online roster, so details beyond his listed position, class and hometown could not be confirmed.

athletes.name: Markus Kier
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kier is a freshman wide receiver for the Bruins from Mission Viejo, California, who played at Orange Lutheran High School. He is listed at 6-2 and 190 pounds and wears No. 46.

athletes.name: Lucas Hickey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hickey is a freshman offensive lineman for UCLA from Prosper, Texas, where he played at Walnut Grove High School. He is listed at 6-3 and 290 pounds and wears No. 61.

athletes.name: Zaheer Young
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Young is a junior offensive lineman for UCLA who reached the Bruins through junior college, playing at Diablo Valley College after Sacred Heart High School in his hometown of San Francisco. He is listed at 6-5 and 290 pounds and wears No. 63, adding to a line that leans heavily on transfer additions.

athletes.name: James Moffat
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moffat is a freshman defensive lineman for UCLA from Los Angeles, where he played at Crespi Carmelite High School in Encino. He is listed at 6-4 and 260 pounds and wears No. 96.

athletes.name: Aaron Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A redshirt junior defensive back out of Moreno Valley, Calif., Williams is competing for a spot in the Bruins' two-deep this fall after transferring from Louisville.

athletes.name: Nas Rankin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rankin is a freshman wide receiver from Chicago who played at Morgan Park for head coach Chris James, a former Illini player. He totaled 1,512 receiving yards and 21 receiving touchdowns across a two-year varsity career and was a two-time Academic All-State selection. A two-sport athlete, he also committed to play basketball at Illinois and once scored 54 points in a high school game.

athletes.name: Mac Resetich
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Resetich is a senior safety who wears No. 0 for Illinois and came to Champaign from Spring Valley Hall High School, signing with the Illini during the February 2023 signing period as part of their 2023 recruiting class. He was a 2022 IHSFCA Class 4A all-state pick and a three-time all-Three Rivers Conference selection, and he set Hall's single-season rushing record while posting a 429-yard, seven-touchdown game against Mendota. The Spring Valley, Ill. native is listed at 6-0 and 210 pounds on the 2026 roster.

athletes.name: Jayshon Platt
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Platt is a senior receiver who transferred from Florida Atlantic and is projected to start at Z receiver for Illinois in 2026. He also figures into the Illini's kick return plans.

athletes.name: Xavier Scott
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Scott is Illinois' veteran nickel back and chose to return for 2026 rather than turn pro after an ankle injury limited him to three games in 2025. He was a preseason second-team All-Big Ten pick by The Athletic.

athletes.name: Carson Boyd
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Boyd is a sophomore quarterback from St. Louis, Mo., who did not play and redshirted the 2025 season. He was a three-star recruit rated the No. 14 quarterback nationally by Rivals out of Cardinal Ritter, where he passed for 7,148 yards and 88 touchdowns and rushed for 2,350 more while leading the program to a 48-5 record. He was Missouri's 2023 Class 5 All-State Player of the Year and enters fall camp working in the quarterback room behind the veterans.

athletes.name: RJ Jones III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a sophomore defensive back from Fort Pierce, Florida, who played at Vero Beach for head coach Lenny Jankowski. He appeared in two games as a freshman in 2025, primarily on special teams, before redshirting the season. Rated a three-star recruit by 247Sports, ESPN, On3 and Rivals, he chose Illinois over offers that included Auburn, Florida, Miami and Louisville.

athletes.name: Kenyon Alston
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alston is a freshman wide receiver from Orlando who was a four-year letterwinner at Bishop Moore Catholic. He finished his high school career with 155 receptions for 2,883 yards and 39 touchdowns and earned all-district honors three times. As a senior he helped the Hornets to a 12-1 record and the Florida 3A state semifinals. His father played college football at Western Michigan.

athletes.name: Nick Hankins Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hankins is a true freshman defensive back from Belleville, Ill., who arrives as one of the higher-rated signees in Illinois' class. Rivals graded him a four-star, the No. 92 player nationally and the No. 2 prospect in Illinois, and 247Sports and ESPN also listed him among the top cornerbacks in the country. He earned 2025 IHSFCA Class 7A All-State first team honors at Belleville West and picked the Illini over offers including USC, Tennessee and Auburn.

athletes.name: Daniel Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is a senior edge rusher who arrived from Hutchinson Community College and is projected to start at Illinois' JACK outside linebacker spot in 2026.

athletes.name: Katin Houser
athletes.source: Estimate (unofficial Big Ten roster-pay list circulated May 2026 and cited by the News-Gazette put Illinois' QB1 near $1.5M; not officially disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Houser is Illinois' starting quarterback in 2026 after transferring from East Carolina, where he threw for 3,300 yards and 19 touchdowns. He has passed for 6,438 yards and 43 touchdowns across four seasons at Michigan State and ECU.

athletes.name: Jakwon Morris
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Morris is a junior college transfer cornerback who was rated the No. 1 JUCO cornerback in the 2026 class and flipped his commitment from USC to Illinois. He projects as a starting cornerback.

athletes.name: Ca'Lil Valentine
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Valentine led Illinois in rushing in 2025 and is projected as the Illini's starting running back in 2026 after returning from a knee injury.

athletes.name: Juice Clarke
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clarke is Illinois' projected starting boundary cornerback and one of three Illini chosen to represent the program at 2026 Big Ten Media Days. Orange and Blue News ranked him the No. 5 Illinois player for 2026.

athletes.name: Jershaun Newton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Newton is a sophomore from St. Petersburg, Florida, who moved from quarterback to wide receiver in June 2026 after redshirting the 2025 season. He played at Clearwater Central Catholic, where he was a two-time team MVP. His brother Jer'Zhan Newton was an All-American defensive tackle and Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year at Illinois, and another brother, Jerjuan, was a three-time All-MAC receiver at Toledo.

athletes.name: Matthew Bailey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bailey is Illinois' returning starting safety and led the Illini with 76 tackles in 2025. He is a two-time All-Big Ten honoree and one of three Illinois players sent to Big Ten Media Days in 2026.

athletes.name: Michael Clayton II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clayton is a freshman quarterback from Orlando who started three seasons at Miami Edison under head coach Luther Campbell. He threw for more than 6,000 yards and 72 touchdowns and led the program to a 30-6 record as its starter, earning all-district honors twice and serving as a two-time team captain. He also won the 2025 Elite 11 accuracy challenge.

athletes.name: Davon Grant
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Grant is a freshman wide receiver on the Illinois roster from DeKalb, Illinois, listed at jersey number 8. He does not currently appear on the school's published football roster, so no additional verified background details are available for him at this time.

athletes.name: Cameron Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a freshman linebacker from Cincinnati and a four-year letterwinner at Lakota West, where he helped the program to two Greater Miami Conference championships. He recorded 211 tackles, 40 tackles for loss and 16 sacks in his high school career and earned All-Ohio honors three times. He was a 2026 U.S. Army All-American Bowl selection and a high school teammate of Illini linebacker Grant Beerman.

athletes.name: Alex Perry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Perry is a fifth-year wide receiver from Port Charlotte, Fla., who transferred to Illinois after a productive 2025 at FIU. He started all 13 games there and led the team with 56 receptions, 840 yards and nine touchdowns, earning All-Conference USA first team recognition. He spent his first three college seasons at Hawaii, catching 46 passes across 2023 and 2024. A three-star recruit out of Port Charlotte, he adds size at 6-5 and competes for snaps in a crowded receiver group.

athletes.name: Lavon Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a fifth-year defensive back from San Antonio, Texas, who joined Illinois from East Texas A&M. He started 10 games there in 2025 and finished third on the team with 74 tackles, adding 3.0 tackles for loss, an interception, a forced fumble and eight passes defensed. He posted 55 tackles and 6.0 tackles for loss the prior year. A San Antonio Express-News all-area selection at Roosevelt, he brings experienced depth to the secondary.

athletes.name: James Kreutz
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kreutz is Illinois' projected starting middle linebacker and the son of six-time Pro Bowl Chicago Bears center Olin Kreutz.

athletes.name: Ty Robinson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Robinson is a sixth-year wide receiver from Aurora, Colo., who came to Illinois from Ball State. He caught 11 passes for 113 yards across 10 games in 2025 and began his career at Colorado, where he appeared in 22 games over two seasons. A three-star recruit rated the No. 68 athlete nationally by 247Sports out of Eaglecrest, he totaled 89 catches for 1,692 yards in high school. He provides veteran depth on the perimeter.

athletes.name: Jacob Alexander
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alexander is a freshman linebacker from Frankfort, Illinois, who played for head coach Rob Zvonar at Lincoln-Way East. He posted 80 tackles, 16 tackles for loss and 11 sacks along with three forced fumbles, and was a two-time all-conference selection. Rated a three-star recruit by 247Sports, ESPN and Rivals, he also played basketball through his sophomore year of high school.

athletes.name: Brayden Trimble
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Trimble is a sophomore wide receiver from Mt. Zion, Ill., who played three games and redshirted in 2025. He was a three-star recruit ranked among the top 15 prospects in Illinois by every major service and chose the Illini over offers from Auburn, Iowa, Nebraska and Wisconsin. He finished ninth in Illinois high school history with 215 career receptions and 16th with 3,036 receiving yards, leading Mt. Zion to the Class 4A state title game as a senior.

athletes.name: Dane Eisenmenger
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Eisenmenger is a freshman quarterback and walk-on from Tolono, Illinois, who set Unity records with 8,801 career passing yards and 111 touchdown passes. He led the Rockets to a 30-9 record as a three-year starter and a berth in the 2025 state championship game, where he set title game records with 545 passing yards and seven touchdowns. His father served as his offensive coordinator.

athletes.name: Isaiah Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a freshman defensive back from Houston and a four-year letterwinner at Fort Bend Marshall. He compiled 194 tackles, including 114 solo stops and 18 tackles for loss, to go with six interceptions and five sacks during his high school career. He earned first team all-district recognition and a spot on the 2025 Whataburger Super Team before signing with Illinois.

athletes.name: Hudson Clement
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clement is Illinois' top returning receiver, catching 22 passes for 480 yards and four touchdowns in 11 games in 2025 after transferring in from West Virginia. He projects as the Illini's starting slot receiver.

athletes.name: Xanai Scott
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Scott is a sophomore defensive back from Riviera Beach, Fla., who played four games and redshirted in 2025, contributing on special teams in each and taking defensive snaps in two. He was a three-star recruit out of Cardinal Newman, where he also helped the basketball program to a 2023 state title and qualified for the state track meet in the long jump. His brother Xavier Scott is also on the Illinois roster.

athletes.name: Andre Lovett Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lovett is a sophomore defensive back from Blue Island, Illinois, who played in each of the Illini's final nine games in 2025, including the Music City Bowl win over Tennessee, and finished with three solo tackles. At Eisenhower he was a 2024 News-Gazette All-State pick after recording 62 tackles and 3.0 sacks while also rushing for 932 yards as a senior.

athletes.name: Maurice Smith Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a fifth-year tight end from Fort Pierce, Florida, who arrived after playing quarterback at Chowan and Long Island. He was a team captain at Chowan and threw for 1,088 yards and seven touchdowns in 2025. At Vero Beach he was Florida 8A Player of the Year and a two-time all-state selection. His brother Micah also plays football at Illinois.

athletes.name: Kingston Shaw
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Shaw is a freshman defensive lineman from Apopka, Florida, who finished high school at The First Academy under head coach Jeff Conaway. He recorded 42 tackles, 11 tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks as a junior at Apopka and was a two-time Academic All-America selection. His father, Jeff, played quarterback at Southeast Missouri State.

athletes.name: Logan Farrell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Farrell is a sophomore tight end from Arlington Heights, Illinois, who played at John Hersey and redshirted in 2025. He caught 63 passes for 828 yards and 19 touchdowns over his sophomore and junior seasons and was a two-time all-conference pick. He also won the IHSA state discus title as a senior with a throw of 196 feet, 10.5 inches.

athletes.name: Tanner Heckel
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Heckel is a junior defensive back from Lyndon, Kan., who played all 13 games with nine starts in 2025 and recorded 37 tackles, 3.0 tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks, an interception, a forced fumble and two pass breakups. He earned Academic All-Big Ten and Big Ten Distinguished Scholar honors. At Lyndon he was the 2023 Kansas eight-man Offensive Player of the Year and led the school to a 13-0 record and its first state championship.

athletes.name: Collin Dixon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dixon is a returning Illinois receiver from Tallmadge, Ohio, projected to start at X receiver in 2026. He and Hudson Clement combined for 71 catches and eight touchdowns in 2025.

athletes.name: Isaiah Thomison
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomison is a senior defensive lineman from Fayetteville, Tenn., who transferred in from Bowling Green. He played 10 games there in 2025 and posted 12 tackles, 4.0 tackles for loss, two fumble recoveries and three quarterback hurries. He spent 2023 and 2024 at Memphis without appearing in a game. A three-star recruit at Fayetteville, he was a finalist for Tennessee's 2022 Mr. Football award and adds rotational depth to the interior line.

athletes.name: Jack Gray
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gray is a freshman punter from Adelaide, South Australia, who came to Illinois through the ProKick Australia program in Melbourne. He began playing American football in January 2025 after a background in Australian Rules football and cricket at Immanuel College, where he led the Sports Association of Adelaide Schools in goals scored in 2024. He was rated a three-star prospect by 247Sports and Rivals and the No. 31 punter nationally by ESPN.

athletes.name: Mason Muragin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Muragin is a senior linebacker and edge player from Macomb, Mich., who has appeared in two career games, both in 2025, and has twice earned Academic All-Big Ten recognition. He was a three-star recruit out of De La Salle, where he set program records with 70.5 career tackles for loss and 29.5 career sacks, was named 2022 Metro Detroit Defensive Player of the Year and won two Division 2 state championships.

athletes.name: Nate Cichy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cichy is a freshman wide receiver and walk-on from Mount Prospect, Illinois, who caught 142 passes for 2,313 yards and 28 touchdowns at Prospect High School. He was a first team All-State selection as both a junior and senior and shared Mid-Suburban League Offensive Player of the Year honors in 2025. He also holds school records in the 55 and 60 meter hurdles.

athletes.name: Jacob Eberhart
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Eberhart is a freshman defensive back from St. Louis who played for head coach Jeremy Maclin at Kirkwood. He was a two-time all-state selection who accounted for 912 total yards, 50 tackles and six pass breakups, and he also ran on state finalist relays in track. His father, Jason, was a four-year letterwinner in football at Illinois from 1997 to 2000.

athletes.name: John Forster
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Forster is a sophomore running back from Montvale, New Jersey, who played at St. Joseph Regional and redshirted in 2025. He rushed for 618 yards and four touchdowns as a senior. Following his junior season Rivals rated him a four-star recruit and the nation's fifth-best all-purpose back. His offer list included Penn State, Nebraska, Rutgers, Wisconsin and Tennessee.

athletes.name: Almirian Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a freshman defensive back from Fort Myers, Florida, and a four-year letterman at Cape Coral. He finished his high school career with 50 total tackles, 38 of them solo, along with three interceptions, three forced fumbles and three fumble recoveries. Rated a three-star recruit by 247Sports, ESPN and Rivals, he picked Illinois over offers from Indiana, Michigan State and Minnesota.

athletes.name: Ben Clawson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clawson is a fifth-year defensive back and walk-on from Arlington Heights, Illinois, who has appeared mainly on special teams since 2023. He has earned Academic All-Big Ten honors three times and was named a Big Ten Distinguished Scholar twice. He graduated from Illinois in December 2025 with a degree in agribusiness, markets and management and is now pursuing a master's in management.

athletes.name: Aidan Laughery
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Laughery is a senior running back from Gibson City, Ill., who returns as a key part of Illinois' backfield rotation. He ran for 109 yards and two touchdowns against Western Illinois in 2025.

athletes.name: Deuce Fillmore
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fillmore is a senior defensive back from Biloxi, Miss., who arrived from Georgia State. He started all 12 games there in 2025, recording 39 tackles and three pass breakups while allowing only two touchdowns across 498 defensive snaps according to Pro Football Focus. He spent two seasons at Mississippi Gulf Coast Community College, where he had 37 tackles and three interceptions in 2024. He adds experienced depth at cornerback.

athletes.name: Cedric Wyche II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wyche is a sophomore running back from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, who redshirted the 2025 season. At St. Thomas Aquinas he ran for 1,284 yards and 18 touchdowns as a three-year letterwinner and helped the Raiders win the FHSAA Class 5A state title as a senior, the program's sixth straight championship. He was rated a three-star recruit by all four major services.

athletes.name: Jordan Anderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anderson is a fifth-year running back from Naperville, Ill., who played all 13 games in 2025, working at tight end and carrying nine times for 41 yards with his first career rushing touchdown. He converted a critical first down late in the Music City Bowl win over Tennessee. At Joliet Catholic he ran for 306 yards in the 2021 IHSA Class 4A championship game, a state record, and he graduated from Illinois in December 2025.

athletes.name: Jaylen Stewart
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stewart is a freshman linebacker from Houston who was a four-year varsity letterwinner and two-year captain at Pearland. He totaled 132 tackles, including 18 tackles for loss, along with 17 sacks during his high school career. He earned first team all-district honors in 2024 and second team recognition in 2025, and he also competed in basketball and track.

athletes.name: Javari Barnett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Barnett is a freshman running back from Tampa who spent his final two high school seasons at Tampa Bay Tech after transferring from Carrollwood Day. He opened his senior year with a 160-yard rushing game against the defending Florida 7A state champions. Rated a three-star recruit, he chose Illinois over offers that included Alabama, Penn State, Miami and Tennessee.

athletes.name: Will Holmes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Holmes is a junior defensive lineman from Detroit who transferred from Utah State, where he started seven of 10 games in 2025 and posted 45 tackles, 6.5 tackles for loss, 2.0 sacks and an interception. He came to football late, having been selected by the Los Angeles Angels in the fifth round of the 2018 MLB Draft and playing in their system through 2021.

athletes.name: Des Straughton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Straughton is a sophomore defensive back from Detroit who redshirted the 2025 season. A four-year letterwinner at Roseville, he was named MAC White Conference Player of the Year and an All-MAC White first team selection after rushing for 1,623 yards and 25 touchdowns and adding 356 receiving yards in high school. He also ran track and played basketball for the Panthers.

athletes.name: Nelsyn Wheeler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wheeler is a freshman running back and walk-on from Grand Island, Nebraska, who played at Millard South for head coach Taylor Mendenhall. He helped the program to a 2025 Nebraska state title while rushing for 746 yards and 14 touchdowns at 8.5 yards per carry as a senior. He also ran track, placing sixth in the Class A 100 and 200 meters as a sophomore.

athletes.name: Ismael Kante
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kante is a fifth-year linebacker from Brooklyn Park, Minn., who played all 13 games in 2025, mostly on special teams with defensive snaps in 10 regular season contests. He finished with eight tackles, a half tackle for loss and a pass breakup. He came to Illinois from Iowa Central Community College, where 247Sports rated him the top junior college linebacker in the country after a 71-tackle season, and he also played at Northern State.

athletes.name: Lucas Osada
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Osada is a junior kicker from Charlottesville, Va., who transferred from North Carolina with three years of eligibility. He served as the Tar Heels' kickoff specialist as a true freshman in 2024, handling 59 kickoffs for 3,709 yards with 39 touchbacks. He played two games and redshirted at Illinois in 2025. Out of Woodberry Forest he was rated the No. 7 punter nationally by 247Sports and was a two-time Kohl's All-America honoree.

athletes.name: Corey Rashad
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rashad is a junior running back and walk-on from Chicago who played at Marist under head coach Ron Dawczak. He was a three-year letterwinner and two-year starter who recorded 98 tackles, 4.5 tackles for loss and 2.0 sacks while helping Marist to two IHSA playoff berths, including a semifinal run in 2021. He earned Academic All-Big Ten honors in 2024 and studies civil engineering.

athletes.name: Kayden Bennett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bennett is a freshman linebacker from Windsor, Connecticut, who was a three-sport letterman in football, wrestling and track at Suffield Academy. He captained the football team as a senior and earned All-NEPSAC first team honors three times, along with two-time All-NEPSAC recognition in both wrestling and track. His brother Kechaun played football at Michigan from 2021 to 2024 and at UCLA in 2025.

athletes.name: Karson Kaiser
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kaiser is a junior wide receiver and walk-on listed from Weston, Florida, who played his high school football at Champaign Centennial. He was a three-year letterwinner there and earned the program's Special Teams Player of the Year award. He redshirted in 2024 and did not appear in a game in 2025. His father, Jay, is assistant to the head coach for the Jacksonville Jaguars.

athletes.name: James Finley IV
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Finley is a sophomore defensive back wearing No. 29 for Illinois after transferring in from Northern Illinois, where he started four games at safety as a true freshman and lined up at cornerback, boundary safety, free safety and nickel. A four-star prospect in the 2025 class out of Andrean High School, he earned all-state honors in each of his final three high school seasons and was a team captain and team MVP as a senior. The Portage, Ind. product is listed at 6-2 and 195 pounds.

athletes.name: Tony Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a freshman linebacker from Jacksonville, Florida, who played for head coach Donovan Maseline at Raines. He recorded 152 total tackles across his junior and senior seasons, including 22 tackles for loss, and added nine career sacks with three forced fumbles. He was a 2024 first team All-State selection and a two-time All-Gateway Conference honoree.

athletes.name: Murphy Clement
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clement is a junior running back from Martinsburg, West Virginia, who transferred to Illinois after redshirting at West Virginia in 2024. As a high school senior he was the 2023 West Virginia Gatorade Player of the Year, rushing for 1,110 yards and 20 touchdowns while passing for 1,673 more, and he was named MVP of the Class AAA state championship game that Martinsburg won.

athletes.name: Tywan Cox
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cox is a sophomore defensive back from Miami who redshirted the 2025 season. He played at Miami Northwestern for head coach Teddy Bridgewater and was rated a three-star recruit by all four major services. His brother, Torrie Jr., also plays football at Illinois, and his father, Torrie Sr., was a sixth-round pick in the 2003 NFL Draft who spent five seasons with Tampa Bay.

athletes.name: Grant Beerman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Beerman is a sophomore linebacker wearing No. 33 for Illinois and comes out of Lakota West High School in West Chester, Ohio. Rated a four-star recruit, he flipped his commitment from Purdue and signed with the Illini in November 2024 after a senior season of 103 tackles, 15 tackles for loss and Greater Miami Conference Defensive Player of the Year honors. As a freshman in 2025 he appeared in the final 11 games, mostly on special teams, and recorded his first career tackle at Washington. He is listed at 6-5, 240 pounds.

athletes.name: Erik Gayle
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gayle is a sophomore linebacker from Cincinnati who redshirted the 2025 season. He played for head coach Anthony Berry at Withrow, where he was a 2024 All-CMAC first team selection, a 2023 All-CMAC second team pick and a two-time all-district honoree. ESPN rated him a four-star recruit, and his offers included Boston College, Cincinnati, Indiana, Kentucky and Louisville.

athletes.name: Kaedyn Cobbs
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cobbs is a freshman defensive back from Denton, Texas, and a four-year letterwinner at Guyer. He was named the 2025 District 5 6A Offensive MVP after rushing for 1,435 yards and 28 touchdowns as a senior, and he finished with 129 tackles in his high school career. His brother Kaedric played at UTSA from 2020 to 2024 and his father played at Oklahoma Panhandle State.

athletes.name: Caden Considine
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Considine is a freshman defensive back and walk-on from Byron, Illinois, who ran for 5,104 yards and scored 78 touchdowns in high school while adding 284 tackles. He helped Byron win IHSA Class 3A state titles in 2023 and 2025, setting a title game record with 367 rushing yards in the 2025 final. His father, Sean, played at Iowa and eight seasons in the NFL.

athletes.name: Ethan Moczulski
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moczulski is a fifth-year kicker wearing No. 37 for Illinois and returns to the program after a season at Washington, where he handled kickoffs and recorded 51 touchbacks on 74 attempts. He first joined the Illini in 2024 as a Texas A&M transfer and set a school record with a 59-yard field goal against Central Michigan that September. A three-star recruit from Mt. Spokane High School in Spokane, Wash., he was ranked the No. 6 kicker in his class by 247Sports and has one year of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Jack Paris
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Paris is a sophomore linebacker from River Forest, Illinois, who made his Illinois debut in the Music City Bowl win over Tennessee after redshirting the 2025 regular season. At Fenwick he was the 2024 Chicago Catholic League White Defensive Player of the Year, posting 107 tackles and 27.5 tackles for loss as a senior and 35.0 tackles for loss as a junior.

athletes.name: Joe Barna
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Barna is a junior defensive lineman wearing No. 43 for Illinois and stayed in state after a career at Wheaton North High School in Wheaton, Ill. A three-star recruit who held roughly 19 scholarship offers, he was the second commitment in the Illini's 2024 signing class and was recruited by Illinois assistant Charlie Bullen. He has added weight through his first two years in the program and is listed at 6-4 and 280 pounds on the 2026 roster after playing at 265 pounds a season earlier.

athletes.name: Patrick Mahoney III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mahoney handled long snapping duties on field goals and extra points in all 13 games for Illinois in 2025, his first season of game action after redshirting in 2023 and sitting out 2024. The Northbrook native and Glenbrook North product was named Academic All-Big Ten and an Illinois Big Ten Distinguished Scholar. He drew recruiting interest from Iowa, Michigan, Notre Dame and Wisconsin and returns as a senior on the Illini roster in 2026.

athletes.name: Robert Edmonson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Edmonson is a senior linebacker from Houston, Texas, who came to Illinois from Colorado State. He played 11 games with four starts there in 2025, finishing fifth on the team with 49 tackles while adding 4.0 tackles for loss, a sack, an interception and six quarterback hurries. He spent his first two college seasons at Prairie View A&M, where he had 37 tackles in 2024. He was an all-district selection at Shadow Creek.

athletes.name: Zach Haber
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Haber is a senior long snapper from Durango, Colo., who joined Illinois after a year at Arkansas. He handled long snapping duties in eight games at Butler Community College in 2024, adding nine tackles and a fumble recovery, and he also spent time at New Mexico State. At Durango he played running back, rushing for 1,358 yards and 19 touchdowns as a junior and 979 yards and 18 scores as a senior.

athletes.name: Parker Crim
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Crim is a freshman defensive lineman from Lima, Ohio, and a four-year letterwinner at Elida. He finished his high school career with 320 tackles, 75 tackles for loss and 42 sacks, earning first team All-Western Buckeye League honors three times and league Defensive Lineman of the Year twice. He also lettered in basketball and track and holds the school bench press record.

athletes.name: Alfred Washington
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Washington is a senior offensive lineman from Pensacola, Florida, who joins Illinois from Northeast Mississippi Community College, where he played nine games in 2025 and was rated the nation's fourth-best junior college offensive tackle by 247Sports. He began his college career at Arkansas Tech. At Escambia he earned 2023 FHSAA Class 3S All-State honorable mention recognition.

athletes.name: Pat Farrell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Farrell is a senior defensive lineman from Oak Lawn, Ill., who has played all 13 games in each of the last two seasons. He recorded 11 tackles, 2.0 tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks and two pass breakups in 2025, tying for sixth on the team in sacks, and he has earned Academic All-Big Ten honors in each of the last two seasons. A three-star recruit at St. Rita, he was the 2022 Chicago Catholic League Green Division Defensive MVP.

athletes.name: Champ Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a true freshman offensive lineman from Fort Pierce, Fla., who signed with Illinois in the 2026 class. ESPN rated him a four-star prospect and the No. 81 overall recruit in the ESPN 300, and he was selected to the Under Armour All-American Game as a junior at Vero Beach. He chose Illinois over offers from Alabama, Georgia, Ohio State and Texas among many others.

athletes.name: Kai Pritchard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pritchard is a freshman offensive lineman from Little Egg Harbor, New Jersey, who played for head coach Dan Curcione at Donovan Catholic. Rated a four-star recruit by both 247Sports and ESPN, he is the highest-rated recruit ever to come out of that program. He also played basketball and served as a Shore Conference student ambassador. His uncle Greg played football at Duke.

athletes.name: Demetrius John
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: John is a junior defensive lineman from Columbus, Ohio, who played six games in 2025 and earned Academic All-Big Ten honors after redshirting the previous season. He was a three-star recruit ranked among the top defensive linemen in his class by On3 and ESPN, and he totaled 125 tackles and 16.0 sacks in high school between Westerville North and Dublin Coffman. He earned All-Ohio second team recognition in 2023 and competes for interior rotation snaps.

athletes.name: Griffin Rousseau
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rousseau is a sophomore offensive lineman from Stoughton, Wisconsin, who redshirted the 2025 season. A four-year letterwinner at Stoughton, he was named the 2024 Badger Small Conference Offensive Lineman of the Year, earned all-conference honors twice and was a Joe Thomas Award finalist. He also won a conference shot put title as a junior. His brother Gabe plays at Minnesota State Mankato.

athletes.name: Tony Balanganayi
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Balanganayi is a freshman defensive lineman from Palatine, Illinois, who played for head coach Corey Olson at his hometown high school. He earned 2025 All-Mid-Suburban League recognition in football and was also a two-time all-conference selection in basketball. Rated a three-star recruit by 247Sports, ESPN and Rivals, he chose Illinois over offers from Michigan, Auburn, Nebraska and Purdue.

athletes.name: TJ McMillen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McMillen is a senior offensive lineman from Naperville, Ill., who played all 13 games in 2025 and made his first career start at center against Purdue. He appeared in all 13 games in 2024 as well and earned Academic All-Big Ten honors. A three-star recruit at St. Francis, where he played for his father Bob McMillen, he was a three-time academic all-state selection and graduated from Illinois in August 2026.

athletes.name: Guillermo Gallardo
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gallardo is a fifth-year defensive lineman from Bloomington, Illinois, who came to Champaign from New Mexico Military Institute, where he played nine games and made 25 tackles in 2023. He earned Academic All-Big Ten honors in 2025 and graduated from Illinois in August 2026 with a degree in kinesiology. He played high school football at Normal Community.

athletes.name: JJ Hirdes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hirdes is a sophomore offensive lineman from Coopersville, Michigan, who redshirted the 2025 season. He was a three-year letterwinner at Coopersville High School and earned all-conference and all-region honors in 2024. He also competed in track and field, winning a conference championship in the discus. He was rated a three-star recruit by 247Sports, ESPN and On3.

athletes.name: Zach Barrett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Barrett is a junior offensive lineman and walk-on from Orland Park, Illinois, who played at Carl Sandburg for head coach Troy McAllister. He was a four-year letterwinner, a two-time All-Southwest Suburban Conference selection and a two-time team captain, and he earned Academic All-State honors in 2023. He redshirted in 2024 and studies political science at Illinois.

athletes.name: Landen Von Seggern
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Von Seggern is a freshman offensive lineman and walk-on from Omaha who was a four-year varsity letterwinner at Millard South. He earned all-state honors three times and won two Nebraska state championships with the Patriots, including an undefeated 2025 season. He signed with Illinois alongside high school teammate Nelsyn Wheeler and also competed in basketball and track.

athletes.name: Jake Renfro
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Renfro is Illinois' projected starting center after transferring from Wisconsin with more than 2,000 career snaps. He was a first-team All-AAC selection at Cincinnati in 2021 and was a Top247 transfer in the 2026 cycle.

athletes.name: Casey Thomann
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomann is a freshman offensive lineman from Olney, Illinois, who played for head coach Luke Carmody at Richland County. He was a three-year letterwinner who earned first team All-Little Illini Conference honors three times after making the second team as a freshman, and he recorded 80 pancake blocks as a senior. He also played basketball and competed in track for four years.

athletes.name: Brandon Hansen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hansen is a junior offensive lineman from Mundelein, Ill., who played 13 games in 2025 and made his first career start at right guard in the season opener against Western Illinois. He appeared in 10 games as a redshirt freshman, primarily on special teams. He was the first commitment in Illinois' 2024 class and a three-star recruit by all four major services, earning News-Gazette All-State first team honors in 2023.

athletes.name: Michael McDonough
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McDonough is a sophomore offensive lineman from Tinley Park, Illinois, who redshirted the 2025 season. A four-year letterwinner at Andrew, he was a 2024 IHSFCA Class 8A All-State honorable mention selection and a 2024 News-Gazette All-State pick, along with two-time All-Southwest Valley Conference honors. He was also a state-qualifying wrestler and studies mechanical engineering at Illinois.

athletes.name: Maika Matelau
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Matelau is a sophomore offensive lineman wearing No. 70 for Illinois and arrived as a junior college transfer from Mt. San Antonio College in California. He was rated the No. 16 junior college prospect in the 2026 class and the top JUCO interior offensive lineman in the country, and he chose Illinois over offers from Cal, NC State, Nebraska, Oklahoma State and Washington State. A product of Upland High School in his hometown of Upland, Calif., he is listed at 6-3 and 305 pounds.

athletes.name: Nathan Knapik
athletes.source: Estimate (unofficial roster-pay list cited by the News-Gazette listed Illinois' starting right tackle near $469K; not officially disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Knapik is Illinois' projected starting right tackle, a 6-foot-7 lineman from Kennewick, Wash., who came to the Illini from Idaho.

athletes.name: Christian Martin
athletes.source: Estimate (unofficial roster-pay list cited by the News-Gazette listed Illinois' Colorado State transfer tackle above $500K; not officially disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Martin is Illinois' projected starting left tackle after transferring from Colorado State, where the 6-foot-7 Louisiana native started every game in 2025.

athletes.name: Zafir Stewart
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stewart is a junior offensive lineman from Philadelphia who played in one game in 2025 after redshirting the 2024 season. He played at Imhotep Charter for head coach Devon Johnson and earned PFN Coaches Select 5A All-State honors. Rated a three-star recruit by all four major services, he chose Illinois over offers that included Penn State, Rutgers, Maryland and Nebraska.

athletes.name: Brandon Henderson
athletes.source: Estimate (unofficial roster-pay list cited by the News-Gazette listed the senior Illinois lineman above $500K; not officially disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Henderson is a senior offensive lineman from East St. Louis who has started at both tackle and guard for Illinois and is projected at right guard in 2026.

athletes.name: Dylan Frechette
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Frechette is a sophomore offensive lineman listed from Central Falls, Rhode Island, who played his high school football at Cardinal Newman in Florida. He was rated a three-star recruit and redshirted the 2025 season without appearing in a game for Illinois.

athletes.name: Eddie Tuerk
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tuerk is a junior offensive lineman from La Grange, Ill., who played all 13 games in 2025, primarily on special teams, after making his debut against Northwestern at Wrigley Field in 2024. Rivals rated him a four-star recruit at Lyons Township, where he played defensive line and posted 19.0 career sacks and 30.0 tackles for loss. He picked Illinois over offers from Michigan, Nebraska, Wisconsin and Tennessee.

athletes.name: TJ Taylor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taylor is a junior offensive lineman from Santa Clarita, Calif., who joined Illinois from College of the Canyons. ESPN rated him the No. 2 junior college offensive lineman in the country and Rivals listed him as the No. 9 overall junior college player. He earned Southern California Football Association All-Central League first team honors in 2025 and chose the Illini over offers including UCLA, North Carolina and Kentucky. He adds size at 6-5 and 340 pounds.

athletes.name: Eddie Kasper
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kasper is a fifth-year wide receiver from Burlington, Wis., who transferred from Illinois State. He played 17 games with seven starts in 2025, catching 36 passes for 322 yards and a touchdown while helping the Redbirds reach the FCS national championship game. He caught 52 passes for 440 yards in 2024 and also handled punt return duties. He graduated from Illinois State in May 2026 and gives the Illini an experienced slot option.

athletes.name: Leslie Mosley Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mosley is a freshman wide receiver from Belle Glade, Florida, who played at Cardinal Newman for head coach Jack Daniels. As a senior he caught 52 passes for 1,001 yards and 10 touchdowns while leading the Crusaders to the FHSAA Class 1A state championship, the first title in program history. He also set the school record with 205 receiving yards in a game.

athletes.name: Lars Rau
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rau is a junior punter wearing No. 81 for Illinois and joined the program as a transfer from Texas State. The Novato, Calif. native came out of San Marin High School and is in his second season on the Illini roster after being listed as a sophomore in 2025. He is listed at 6-3 and 195 pounds on the 2026 roster, down from 215 pounds a year earlier.

athletes.name: Jacob Harvey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Harvey is a freshman wide receiver and walk-on from Mt. Zion, Illinois, who caught 180 passes for 2,769 yards and 32 touchdowns during his high school career. He earned 2025 IHSFCA All-State first team honors and was a three-time all-conference selection. He was also a two-time Academic All-State pick and an Illinois State Scholar who plans to study engineering.

athletes.name: Kaden Feagin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Feagin is an in-state fan favorite from Atwood, Ill., who moved from running back to tight end for 2026. He rushed for 507 yards and seven touchdowns on 122 carries in 2025 and added 16 catches for 188 yards and two scores.

athletes.name: Grant Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a sophomore tight end and walk-on from Forsyth, Illinois, who redshirted the 2025 season. At Maroa-Forsyth he caught 91 passes for 1,594 yards and 27 touchdowns and set the school single-season tackles record as a senior. He was a 2024 IHSFCA Class 2A All-State selection and a two-time Academic All-State honoree. His father played basketball and football at Millikin.

athletes.name: Will Vala III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Vala is a freshman tight end and walk-on from Downers Grove, Illinois, who played for head coach Joe Horeni at Downers Grove North. He caught 57 passes for 851 yards and eight touchdowns and earned 2025 all-state honors along with two all-conference selections. He was also an Academic All-State pick and played basketball and baseball for two years.

athletes.name: Christian Abney
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Abney is a senior tight end who transferred from Ball State and is projected as Illinois' starting tight end in 2026.

athletes.name: BJ Thurman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thurman is a sophomore tight end from Berkeley, California, who arrives from College of San Mateo, where he caught 16 passes for 322 yards and six touchdowns in 11 games. He helped the Bulldogs to a 12-1 record and the 3C2A state championship and was rated the nation's top junior college tight end by 247Sports.

athletes.name: Davin Stoffel
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stoffel is a senior tight end from Mosinee, Wis., who played all 13 games for Illinois in 2025 and caught one pass for 24 yards at Wisconsin. He signed with the Illini in January 2025 after two years at South Dakota State, where he started 14 games in 2024, caught 14 passes for 177 yards and made the MVFC All-Newcomer Team. He was on the Jackrabbits' 15-0 FCS championship team in 2023.

athletes.name: Tanner Hollinger
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hollinger is a junior tight end and walk-on from Stromsburg, Nebraska, who played eight-man football at Cross County. He caught 23 passes for 408 yards and 12 touchdowns as a senior and was a two-time all-state and two-time all-district selection. He appeared in one game for Illinois in 2025 after redshirting in 2024, and he studies agricultural communications.

athletes.name: Carter Janki
athletes.source: Estimate (unofficial roster-pay list cited by the News-Gazette listed the Penn transfer defensive lineman near $490K; not officially disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Janki is a graduate transfer defensive tackle from Penn, where the 6-foot-5, 295-pounder earned All-Ivy honors with 13 tackles for loss and 7.5 sacks over his final two seasons.

athletes.name: Cameron Brooks
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brooks is a sophomore defensive lineman from Chicago who played in one game and redshirted in 2025. At Homewood-Flossmoor he totaled 127 tackles, 38.0 tackles for loss and 13.0 sacks and earned 2023 All-Southwest Suburban Blue honors. He was rated a three-star recruit by all four major services. His brother Charlie played college football at Eastern Illinois.

athletes.name: Deon Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a sophomore defensive lineman from Las Vegas who joins Illinois from City College of San Francisco, where he played 10 games in 2025 and recorded 25 total tackles with 3.0 tackles for loss while helping the Rams win a Bay 6 League championship. At Liberty High School he starred on both lines and reached the Nevada 5A Division I state semifinals as a senior.

athletes.name: Ean Rhea
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rhea is a fifth-year defensive lineman from Glade Spring, Virginia, who transferred from Emory and Henry. In 2025 he was a Division II first team All-American and South Atlantic Conference Defensive Player of the Year after posting 50 tackles, 17.5 tackles for loss, 12.0 sacks and three forced fumbles. His sack total led the conference and ranked second nationally in Division II.

athletes.name: Connor Sullivan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sullivan is a sophomore defensive lineman from Glenview, Illinois, who transferred from Washington State, where he played three games and redshirted in 2025. He was a team captain at Loyola Academy, which won three straight Illinois state titles during his time there, and he recorded 54 tackles, 12.0 tackles for loss and 5.0 sacks as a junior.

athletes.name: Isaiah White
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: White is a sophomore defensive lineman from Indianapolis who made his Illinois debut in the 2025 season opener against Western Illinois and redshirted the year. A four-year letterwinner at Ben Davis, he helped the Giants win a state title as a junior and earned 2024 All-Marion County and All-MIC honors along with a preseason IndyStar Super Team selection.

athletes.name: Darrell Prater
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Prater is a graduate transfer nose tackle from Jacksonville State, where he recorded 63 tackles, 8.0 tackles for loss and 5.5 sacks in 39 games over three seasons.

athletes.name: Joshua Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davis is a sophomore defensive lineman from Mendenhall, Mississippi, who comes to Illinois from Copiah-Lincoln Community College. He played nine games there in 2025 and recorded 21 tackles, 7.0 tackles for loss, 3.0 sacks and a forced fumble. At Mendenhall High School he was a 2024 All-State first team selection and a Mississippi Association of Coaches South All-Star.

athletes.name: King Liggins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Liggins is a freshman defensive lineman from Crete, Illinois, who was a three-year letterwinner at Brother Rice. He recorded 120 tackles, 20 tackles for loss and 10 sacks in high school, earned All-Chicago Catholic League Blue honors twice and helped the Crusaders to a 12-1 record and a berth in the IHSA Class 7A title game. He was also a two-time Catholic League wrestling champion.

athletes.name: Carter Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a sophomore linebacker for the Illinois Fighting Illini out of Rolling Meadows, Ill.

athletes.blurb: Jordan Cree is a senior defensive lineman from Remington, Indiana, listed as a walk-on with the 2026 Purdue Boilermakers. The official roster measures him at 6-1 and 305 pounds wearing No. 96.

athletes.name: Wisdom Simms
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Simms is a senior defensive lineman from Kannapolis, North Carolina, who was Purdue's first transfer portal signing of the offseason after playing at North Carolina Central. He recorded 22 tackles, 5.5 tackles for loss and three sacks in 2025 at the FCS level. Listed at 6-4 and 320 pounds, he is expected to fill a rotation role in 2026, particularly against run heavy opponents.

athletes.name: Drake Carlson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Hayden Timosciek
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hayden Timosciek is a senior offensive lineman from Lockport, Illinois, listed as a walk-on with the 2026 Purdue Boilermakers. The roster measures him at 6-8 and 265 pounds wearing No. 99.

athletes.name: Josiah Hope
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Josiah Hope is a freshman defensive lineman from Radcliff, Kentucky, on the 2026 Purdue Boilermakers roster. He is listed at 6-3 and 308 pounds wearing No. 99 as he begins his college career.

athletes.name: Jojo Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jojo Johnson is a freshman wide receiver from Goochland, Virginia, on the 2026 Purdue Boilermakers roster. He is listed at 6-4 and 185 pounds wearing No. 88, giving Purdue another tall, lean target on the outside.

athletes.name: DeAndre Moore Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (reported as Colorado's highest-valued incoming transfer at ~$1M On3 valuation; On3 NIL value component listed at ~$546K, no deal terms disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Moore is a projected starting receiver for Colorado after three seasons at Texas, where he totaled 77 catches for 988 yards and 11 touchdowns across 2024 and 2025. He reunites in Boulder with offensive coordinator Brennan Marion.

athletes.name: Ernest Campbell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Campbell is a third-year receiver from Refugio, Texas who arrived in Boulder by way of Texas A&M and Sacramento State. He led the Hornets in 2025 with 37 catches for 755 yards and eight touchdowns, averaging better than 20 yards a reception. At Refugio he won four straight Class 2A 100-meter state titles. Listed at 5-9 and 145 pounds, he projects as a rotational vertical threat in 2026.

athletes.name: Naeten Mitchell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mitchell is a projected starting safety for Colorado after transferring from New Mexico State, where he tallied 52 tackles and six pass breakups in 2025. He is a versatile defender who has lined up at box safety, slot corner and linebacker.

athletes.name: RJ Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a fourth-year cornerback from McDonough, Georgia who signed with Colorado out of Eagle's Landing Christian Academy, where he played both ways and posted 56 tackles, two interceptions and 32 receptions for 486 yards as a senior. He appeared in four games in 2025, starting three, and finished with eight tackles and an interception. At 6-2 and 185 pounds he is in the mix for rotation snaps on the boundary.

athletes.name: Hykeem Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a rotation receiver for Colorado and a former five-star recruit who caught 21 passes for 267 yards and two touchdowns in two seasons at Florida State. He transferred to Boulder ahead of the 2025 season.

athletes.name: Boo Carter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation ~$700K on its 2026 Colorado transfer board; not exactly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Carter is Colorado's projected starting nickel back after transferring from Tennessee, where he posted 25 tackles, 4.5 tackles for loss and three forced fumbles in 2025 while returning punts. He was the Buffaloes' highest-rated transfer addition of the 2026 cycle.

athletes.name: Quentin Gibson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gibson is a second-year receiver from Fort Worth, Texas who was named the 2025 FWAA Freshman Special Teams Player of the Year. He played all 12 games with two starts, catching 15 passes and returning 25 kickoffs for 597 yards. At North Crowley he was the 2024 MaxPreps National Player of the Year, with 93 receptions for 2,009 yards and 36 touchdowns on an unbeaten Class 6A state title team.

athletes.name: Randon Fontenette
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fontenette is a projected starting safety for Colorado after transferring from Vanderbilt. Across three college seasons that began at TCU he recorded 60 tackles with 14.5 for loss, 3.5 sacks and 14 pass breakups.

athletes.name: Kam Perry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kam Perry is a fifth-year wide receiver from Marietta, Georgia, who joined Colorado in January 2026 with two seasons of eligibility. He broke out at Miami (Ohio) in 2025, catching 43 passes for 976 yards and six touchdowns to earn first team All-MAC honors and the RedHawks' team offensive MVP award. He began his career at Indiana in 2022 and was rated a three-star transfer prospect by 247Sports. He projects as one of the Buffaloes' top receiving options in 2026.

athletes.name: Dominiq Ponder
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ponder is a fourth-year quarterback on Colorado's roster, listed at 6-5 and 200 pounds and wearing No. 7. He is from Opa Locka, Florida, and played high school football at Carol City. The Buffaloes list his previous schools as Bethune-Cookman and Georgia Tech, making Boulder his third college stop.

athletes.name: Emory Floyd
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Floyd is a fifth-year cornerback from Powder Springs, Georgia in his final season of eligibility. He came out of Hillgrove High School and spent time at South Carolina and Appalachian State before joining the Buffaloes. Listed at 6-1 and 195 pounds, he brings length and experience from two prior Football Bowl Subdivision programs to a Colorado secondary that will lean on veterans for rotation snaps in 2026.

athletes.name: Joseph Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a projected starting receiver for Colorado after finishing second on the team with 37 catches for 489 yards and four touchdowns in 2025. He came to Boulder from Tulsa.

athletes.name: Jaydan Hardy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hardy is a third-year cornerback from Lewisville, Texas who transferred to Colorado from Oklahoma. He played his high school football at Lewisville High School and is listed at 5-10 and 180 pounds. With the Buffaloes replacing production in the secondary, Hardy is competing for nickel and outside cornerback rotation snaps in 2026 along with a role in the kicking game.

athletes.name: Richard Young
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Young is a projected rotation running back for Colorado after transferring from Alabama, where the former top-five national running back recruit carried 59 times across 15 games. He competes with Damian Henderson II for lead-back work in 2026.

athletes.name: Makari Vickers
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Vickers is a projected starting cornerback for Colorado who played eight games with two starts in 2025, finishing with 13 tackles and three pass breakups. The former four-star recruit began his career at Oklahoma and returned to activity after offseason heart surgery.

athletes.name: Kaleb Mathis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mathis is a fourth-year wide receiver from Arlington, Texas, who wears No. 13 for Colorado. He came to the Buffaloes out of Grace Prep and is listed at 5-9 and 165 pounds on the 2026 roster.

athletes.name: Jason Stokes Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stokes is a third-year safety on Colorado's roster, listed at 6-2 and 185 pounds and wearing No. 13. He is from Pflugerville, Texas, and played high school football at Weiss. Before arriving in Boulder he spent time at Utah, and the Buffaloes list him among their defensive backs.

athletes.name: Quanell Farrakhan Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Farrakhan is a second-year Colorado receiver competing for rotation snaps after catching one pass for 17 yards as a freshman in 2025. He ranks among the Buffaloes' highest NIL valuations largely on the strength of his social following.

athletes.name: Kaneal Sweetwyne
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sweetwyne is a first-year quarterback from Lehi, Utah, who wears No. 14 for Colorado. He came to the Buffaloes out of Skyridge High School and is listed at 6-3 and 195 pounds.

athletes.name: Jah Jah Boyd
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Boyd is a third-year safety from Philadelphia who transferred to Colorado from Indiana. He played at Roman Catholic High School in Philadelphia and is listed at 5-11 and 190 pounds. He arrives with Big Ten experience behind him and enters 2026 competing for rotation snaps in a Colorado safety group that returns several veterans, with special teams the likeliest early path to playing time.

athletes.name: Isaac Wilson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilson is Colorado's veteran backup quarterback after transferring from Utah, where he started seven games as a freshman in 2024 and threw for 1,510 yards with 10 touchdowns. He is the younger brother of NFL quarterback Zach Wilson.

athletes.name: Liona Lefau
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lefau is a projected starting linebacker for Colorado after transferring from Texas, where he recorded 69 tackles, 10 tackles for loss and a sack in 2025. He ranked as On3's No. 8 linebacker in the 2026 transfer class.

athletes.name: Christian Ward
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ward is a first-year wide receiver from Carrollton, Georgia, who wears No. 17 for Colorado. He played his high school football at IMG Academy in Florida and is listed at 6-3 and 205 pounds.

athletes.name: Paul Omodia
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Omodia is a fourth-year cornerback from Richmond, Texas who reached Boulder after stops at Illinois State and Lamar. He played at Fort Bend Bush High School and is listed at 6-2 and 200 pounds, giving Colorado a long-framed option on the perimeter. He is competing for rotation snaps at cornerback in 2026 and figures to contribute in the kicking game.

athletes.name: Danny Scudero
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Scudero is Colorado's projected No. 1 receiver after transferring from San Jose State, where he led the nation with 1,291 receiving yards on 88 catches with 10 touchdowns in 2025. He was an AP second-team All-American and a Biletnikoff Award semifinalist.

athletes.name: DeKalon Taylor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taylor is a fifth-year running back from Longview, Texas who transferred to Colorado from Incarnate Word. He played at Longview High School and is listed at 5-9 and 165 pounds, profiling as a change-of-pace back and return option. He joins a running back room that added several veterans for 2026, so his path to snaps runs through third-down work and special teams.

athletes.name: Cree Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cree Thomas, a sophomore cornerback from Phoenix, transferred to Colorado from Notre Dame with four years of eligibility remaining. He played three games as a true freshman in 2025, recording a tackle and a pass breakup. A three-star recruit and team captain at Brophy College Prep, he was rated the No. 5 player in Arizona by ESPN and earned first team all-state honors in 2023 and 2024. He is competing for a starting cornerback spot in 2026.

athletes.name: Tagert Bardin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bardin is a fourth-year wide receiver from Durango, Colorado, who wears No. 22 for the Buffaloes. He came to the program out of Durango High School and is listed at 6-0 and 160 pounds.

athletes.name: JaQuail Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a second-year running back from Orlando who came to Colorado from Sacramento State. He played at Jones High School in Orlando and is listed at 5-11 and 170 pounds. With Colorado remaking its backfield for 2026 under a run-heavy offensive scheme, Smith is competing for rotation carries behind the veterans in the room and should see early work on special teams.

athletes.name: Mojo Williams Jr.

athletes.name: Braylon Edwards
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Edwards is a first-year defensive back from Duncanville, Texas, who wears No. 26 for Colorado. He played his high school football at Duncanville and is listed at 5-11 and 180 pounds on the roster.

athletes.name: Damian Henderson II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Henderson is Colorado's projected starting running back after rushing for 565 yards and five touchdowns on 91 carries at Sacramento State in 2025. He began his career at Colorado State.

athletes.name: Bryce Hicks
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hicks is a third-year running back at Colorado, listed at 5-9 and 185 pounds and wearing No. 27. He is from Atlanta and played high school football at Carrollton in Georgia. The Buffaloes list West Georgia as his previous school, so Boulder is his second college program.

athletes.name: Domata Peko Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Peko is a junior-college edge transfer competing for rotation snaps on Colorado's rebuilt defensive line. He is the son of Buffaloes defensive line coach and 14-year NFL veteran Domata Peko.

athletes.name: Ben Finneseth
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Finneseth is a sixth-year safety from Durango, Colorado and one of the few in-state players on the roster. A former walk-on out of Durango High School, he has built his role largely on special teams over five seasons in Boulder and is regarded as a leader in the secondary. He enters his final year listed at 6-2 and 205 pounds, competing for defensive rotation snaps.

athletes.name: Cam Newton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Newton is a first-year running back from Prosper, Texas, listed at No. 28 on Colorado's 2026 football roster. He is one of several first-year backs the Buffaloes carry in the running back room.

athletes.name: Micah Welch
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Welch is a third-year running back from Milledgeville, Georgia who has appeared in 21 games with 11 starts for Colorado. He carried 96 times for 384 yards and four touchdowns across 12 appearances in 2025. At Baldwin High School he finished with more than 4,000 all-purpose yards and 47 touchdowns. Listed at 5-9 and 215 pounds, he is a leading candidate for early-down work in 2026.

athletes.name: Justin Eaglin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
