In 2025 he started 11 of 14 games and tied for second in the Sun Belt with five interceptions, adding eight pass breakups and a blocked kick to earn second team All-Sun Belt honors. His four-year James Madison career included 26 games, 14 starts and six interceptions. He is projected to start in the Buffaloes' secondary.

athletes.name: Preston Ashley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ashley is a first-year cornerback from Brandon, Mississippi, who wears No. 31 for Colorado. He came to the Buffaloes out of Brandon High School and is listed at 5-11 and 185 pounds.

athletes.name: Alex Ward

The Buffaloes list Mercer as his previous school, making Boulder his second college stop as a graduate-level defensive back.

athletes.name: Kole Mathis

athletes.name: Drew Molinari
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Molinari is a third-year defensive back at Colorado, listed at 6-1 and 195 pounds and wearing No. 34. He is from Salinas, California, and played high school football at Palma. The Buffaloes list Monterey Peninsula College as his previous school, so he reached Boulder by way of the California junior college ranks.

athletes.name: Damon Greaves
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Damon Greaves returns as Colorado's punter for 2026 after earning All-Big 12 honorable mention in 2025, when he averaged 42.4 yards on 67 punts with 15 downed inside the 20. His 67-yarder against Delaware was the third longest in program history. A senior from Busselton, Australia, he spent two seasons as Kansas' primary punter, trained with Prokick Australia, and previously played Australian rules football for Hawthorn after going No. 14 in the 2019 AFL rookie draft.

athletes.name: Tyler Martinez
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Martinez is a fifth-year linebacker from Albuquerque, New Mexico who reached Boulder after stops at New Mexico Military Institute and New Mexico State. He played at Volcano Vista High School and is listed at 6-1 and 220 pounds. He joins a Colorado linebacker room blending returning starters with newcomers, and he is competing for rotation snaps and a special teams role in 2026.

athletes.name: Carson Westbrook
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Westbrook is a third-year wide receiver from Ellaville, Georgia, who wears No. 36 for Colorado. He came to the Buffaloes out of Schley County High School and is listed at 5-11 and 170 pounds.

athletes.name: Leonardo Valle
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Valle is a second-year running back from Richmond Hill, Georgia, who wears No. 37 for Colorado. He played his high school football at Richmond Hill and is listed at 6-1 and 210 pounds.

athletes.name: Daniel Gerlach
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gerlach is a fourth-year punter at Colorado, listed at 6-0 and 160 pounds and wearing No. 38. He is a Boulder native who played his high school football at Boulder High School. The Buffaloes list Colby College in Maine as his previous school, so he came home to Boulder after starting his college career in Division III.

athletes.name: Cadel Ayala
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ayala is a second-year kicker and punter at Colorado, listed at 6-1 and 185 pounds and wearing No. 39. He is from Reno, Nevada, and played high school football at McQueen. The Buffaloes list Saddleback College as his previous school, so he arrived in Boulder from the California junior college ranks.

athletes.name: Donavon Stephens
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stephens is a second-year defensive back at Colorado, listed at 5-10 and 170 pounds and wearing No. 39. He is from Alpharetta, Georgia, and played high school football at Collins Hill. The Buffaloes list Georgia Military as his previous school, so he reached Boulder through the junior college route.

athletes.name: Colby Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a first-year linebacker from Sammamish, Washington, who wears No. 40 for Colorado. He came to the Buffaloes out of Eastlake High School and is listed at 6-2 and 195 pounds.

athletes.name: Kylan Salter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Salter is a fourth-year edge rusher from Cedar Hill, Texas who transferred to Colorado from TCU and is the younger brother of former Buffaloes quarterback Kaidon Salter. He played 10 games in 2025 with six tackles while logging 162 special teams snaps across four units. Coaches moved him from linebacker to the edge this offseason, and at 6-2 and 230 pounds he is competing for pass-rush rotation snaps.

athletes.name: Gideon Lampron
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lampron is a projected starting linebacker for Colorado after leading Bowling Green with 119 tackles and 17.5 tackles for loss as a team captain in 2025. He was a first-team FCS All-American at Dayton in 2024.

athletes.name: Vili Taufatofua
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Vili Taufatofua is a fifth-year defensive lineman from Auckland, New Zealand, who joined Colorado from San Jose State, where he started 11 games in 2025 and posted 34 tackles, seven tackles for loss and three sacks to earn All-Mountain West honorable mention. He previously spent 2023 and 2024 at Utah and starred at New Mexico Military Institute, where the 247Sports Composite rated him the No. 11 junior college player nationally. He projects into Colorado's defensive line rotation with two years to play.

athletes.name: Luke Whiting
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Luke Whiting, a fourth-year long snapper who prepped at Olympus High School in suburban Salt Lake City, is in line to handle snapping duties for Colorado in 2026. The Buffaloes are his fourth program: he appeared in four games at Idaho State in 2023 before redshirting, spent time at Florida Atlantic, and was at Georgia Tech in spring 2025 before arriving in Boulder with three years of eligibility. Rubio Long Snapping rated him the No. 30 long snapper in the class of 2023.

athletes.name: Elliot Arnold
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Elliot Arnold, a redshirt freshman from Chattanooga, Tennessee, is positioned to take over placekicking duties at Colorado after redshirting in 2025. At the McCallie School he made 15 of 17 field goals and 41 of 43 extra points as a senior while helping win a Tennessee Division II Class AAA championship, and he sent 34 of 40 kickoffs for touchbacks. His career long was a 52-yard field goal as a junior. 247Sports rated him the No. 28 kicker in his recruiting class.

athletes.name: Cody Jordan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jordan is a first-year running back from The Woodlands, Texas, who wears No. 47 for Colorado. He played his high school football at The Woodlands and is listed at 5-9 and 185 pounds.

athletes.name: Quency Wiggins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wiggins is a projected starting interior defensive lineman for Colorado after moving inside from defensive end. The former LSU signee played all 12 games in 2025, recording nine tackles and six quarterback hurries.

athletes.name: Rodney Colton Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Colton is a first-year linebacker from Newnan, Georgia, who wears No. 50 for Colorado. He came to the Buffaloes out of Newnan High School and is listed at 6-1 and 225 pounds on the roster.

athletes.name: Trey Young
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Young is a second-year long snapper at Colorado, listed at 5-10 and 195 pounds and wearing No. 50. He is from San Juan Capistrano, California, and played high school football at San Juan Hills. The Buffaloes list Saddleback College as his previous school, so he came to Boulder from the California junior college ranks.

athletes.name: Carson Crawford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Crawford is a first-year linebacker from Carthage, Texas and one of the higher-rated signees in Colorado's 2026 class. He committed to Texas State before flipping to the Buffaloes after a visit to Boulder, then enrolled early in January. Carthage won back-to-back Texas state championships during his career, and he posted seven tackles and a receiving touchdown in the title game. He is listed at 6-4 and 220 pounds.

athletes.name: Chauncey Gooden
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gooden is a second-year offensive lineman from Nashville who signed with Colorado in the 2025 class as one of the country's top-rated interior linemen, choosing the Buffaloes over Clemson, Georgia, Michigan and Oregon among others. He started three seasons at Lipscomb Academy and helped the Mustangs win consecutive state titles. Listed at 6-3 and 380 pounds, he is competing for interior rotation snaps in 2026.

athletes.name: Immanuel Ezeogu
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ezeogu is a third-year edge rusher from Suffolk, Virginia who transferred to Colorado from James Madison. He played at Nansemond River High School and is listed at 6-2 and 240 pounds. He joins a Buffaloes defensive front that added several transfers for 2026 and is competing for rotation snaps on the edge, with special teams offering an additional path to the field.

athletes.name: Andre Roye Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Roye is a fifth-year offensive lineman at Colorado, listed at 6-6 and 295 pounds and wearing No. 52. He is from District Heights, Maryland, and played high school football at St. Frances Academy in Baltimore. The Buffaloes list Maryland as his previous school, so he joined Colorado after beginning his career in his home state.

athletes.name: Toby Anene
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Toby Anene is a fifth-year edge rusher from St. Paul, Minnesota, who transferred to Colorado from North Dakota State with one season to play. He appeared in 40 games with 22 starts for the Bison, totaling 10.5 career sacks, and started all 13 games in 2025 with seven sacks and 8.5 tackles for loss. He led the Missouri Valley Football Conference with four forced fumbles in 2024 and played on an FCS national championship team. 247Sports listed him as the No. 26 edge in the transfer portal.

athletes.name: Larry Johnson III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a fifth-year offensive lineman from Savannah, Georgia who reached Boulder by way of Hutchinson Community College and Tennessee. He played at Jenkins High School and is listed at 6-7 and 350 pounds, among the largest linemen on the roster. He gives Colorado an experienced tackle option and is competing for rotation snaps on an offensive line built around size and veteran depth.

athletes.name: Bo LaPenna
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: LaPenna is a fifth-year linebacker from Commerce City, Colorado and a product of Adams City High School, where he ran for 1,104 yards and 10 touchdowns while adding 88 tackles as a senior. He has spent his career in Boulder contributing mainly on special teams. Listed at 6-1 and 235 pounds, he is competing for defensive rotation snaps in 2026 while remaining a core kicking game contributor.

athletes.name: Taj White
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: White is Colorado's projected starting right tackle after transferring from Rutgers. He is one of three portal tackles the Buffaloes added to rebuild an offensive line that lost its entire starting front.

athletes.name: Gage Goldberg
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Goldberg is a third-year linebacker from Boerne, Texas, who wears No. 55 for Colorado. He came to the Buffaloes out of Boerne Champion High School and is listed at 6-0 and 210 pounds.

athletes.name: Bo Hughley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hughley is Colorado's projected starting left tackle after transferring from Georgia, where he played 10 games with two starts in 2025 at both tackle spots. He is tasked with replacing departed left tackle Jordan Seaton.

athletes.name: Phillip Houston
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Houston is a sixth-year offensive lineman from McKinney, Texas who arrived in Boulder after stops at Navarro College and Florida International. athletes.blurb: Brown is a sophomore cornerback from Cypress, Texas who joins Utah after two seasons at Lamar. He played in seven games in 2025 and recorded nine tackles, with a season best of two stops in three separate games. At Cy Springs High he was a two-year letterwinner and first-team all-conference selection who caught 35 passes for 638 yards and three touchdowns on offense. He is competing for depth snaps in the Utah secondary.

athletes.name: Brandon Holmes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brandon Holmes is a sophomore cornerback for Utah who reached Salt Lake City by way of the junior college ranks. Listed as a San Diego, California, native, he played high school football at Corona Del Sol High School and then spent time at Fresno City College before joining the Utes. Utah lists him at 6-foot-1 and 180 pounds.

athletes.name: Luke Bryant
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Luke Bryant is a freshman safety on Utah's 2026 roster and one of several Utes from nearby Olympus High School. He is from Holladay, Utah, and is listed at 6-foot-2 and 200 pounds.

athletes.name: Major Hinchen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Major Hinchen is a freshman cornerback for Utah out of La Quinta, California, where he played at La Quinta High School. The Utes list the long defensive back at 6-foot-2 and 175 pounds for 2026.

athletes.name: Matt Clark
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Matt Clark is a junior wide receiver on Utah's 2026 roster, listed with jersey number 30. He is from Mesa, Arizona, and played at Mountain View High School. The Utes list him at 5-foot-11 and 181 pounds.

athletes.name: Jack Evans
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jack Evans is a sophomore safety for Utah out of Salt Lake City, where he played his high school football at Olympus High School. The Utes list the local defensive back at 6-foot-0 and 192 pounds.

athletes.name: Josh Sovereign
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Josh Sovereign is a sophomore safety on the Utah roster. He is from Chandler, Arizona, and played at Williams Field High School. The Utes list him at 5-foot-11 and 198 pounds in the secondary for 2026.

athletes.name: Kana'i Lopes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lopes is a junior tight end from Las Vegas who played in all 13 games in 2025, primarily on special teams, and made two tackles against Colorado. He was a three-star recruit at St. John Bosco High in California, part of a squad ranked No. 5 nationally by MaxPreps, and made 45 tackles and a fumble recovery as a senior. He began his prep career at Liberty High in Nevada, where he totaled 85 tackles in two seasons.

athletes.name: Ashton Olevao
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ashton Olevao is a sophomore safety for Utah and a Salt Lake City native who played at Highland High School. He stayed home for college, and the Utes list him at 6-foot-0 and 200 pounds.

athletes.name: Preston Pitts
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Preston Pitts is a freshman linebacker on Utah's 2026 roster out of League City, Texas. He played his high school football at Clear Falls High School, and the Utes list him at 6-foot-4 and 225 pounds.

athletes.name: Brock Fonoimoana
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fonoimoana is a sophomore linebacker from Laie, Hawaii who appeared in 11 games in 2025 on defense and special teams, including four tackles and an assisted stop behind the line against Cal Poly. A four-star recruit rated the No. 3 player in Hawaii, he was a co-winner of the Cover 2 defensive player of the year award as a senior, helped Kahuku High to back-to-back state titles in 2021 and 2022 and was invited to the Polynesian Bowl.

athletes.name: Anthony Hernandez
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anthony Hernandez is a junior linebacker for Utah and one of the few Utes from Park City, Utah, where he played at Park City High School. He spent time at Northern Colorado before joining the Utah program, and the Utes list him at 5-foot-10 and 192 pounds with jersey number 28 on the 2026 roster.

athletes.name: Peyton Rice
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Peyton Rice is a senior wide receiver for Utah out of Salt Lake City. He played at Olympus High School, is listed at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds, and the roster lists his major as intermediate business.

athletes.name: Junior Coughlin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Junior Coughlin is a sophomore wide receiver on Utah's 2026 roster. He is from Lehi, Utah, and played his high school football at Skyridge High School. The Utes list him at 6-foot-0 and 176 pounds.

athletes.name: Tommy Nelson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tommy Nelson is a sophomore safety for Utah out of Salt Lake City, where he played at Olympus High School. He is listed at 6-foot-3 and 193 pounds, and the roster lists his major as biology.

athletes.name: Paul Fitzgerald
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fitzgerald is a fifth-year edge rusher from Idaho Falls, Idaho who played four games in 2025 and contributed 11 tackles with 1.5 for loss, including a season-high six stops against Cal Poly. He appeared in nine games the prior season. Before Utah he made 13 starts at Utah State, posting 46 tackles, 9.0 tackles for loss and 8.0 sacks in 2023 and tying the school bowl record with 3.0 sacks in the Idaho Potato Bowl.

athletes.name: LaGary Mitchell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: LaGary Mitchell is a freshman linebacker on the Utah roster out of Meridian, Idaho, where he played at Meridian High School. The Utes list him at 6-foot-2 and 212 pounds heading into the 2026 season.

athletes.name: Tayson Reid
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reid is a sophomore linebacker from Spanish Fork, Utah who spent 2025 at Snow College, leading that team with 69 tackles in eight games despite missing two, adding 4.0 tackles for loss, two interceptions including a pick six and a fumble recovery. He was rated a three-star junior college prospect and the nation's No. 4 juco linebacker by 247Sports. He played at Spanish Fork High and served a two-year church mission in New Zealand.

athletes.name: Grady Mareko
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Grady Mareko is a junior linebacker for Utah and one of the more distant recruits on the roster, coming from Leone, American Samoa, where he played at Leone High School. He is listed at 6-foot-1 and 231 pounds.

athletes.name: Logan Castor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Logan Castor is Utah's veteran long snapper, a fifth-year player from Cottonwood Heights, Utah, who handled 113 snaps across the 2025 season on extra points, punts and field goals after making his collegiate debut against Southern Utah in 2024. A Brighton High School product, he also lettered four years as the baseball team's starting catcher, and both of his parents attended Utah. He is set to continue as the Utes' primary snapper in 2026.

athletes.name: Sione Motuapuaka
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sione Motuapuaka is a sophomore tight end on Utah's 2026 roster. He is from Las Vegas and played at Bishop Gorman High School. The Utes list the heavy-set blocker at 5-foot-11 and 276 pounds.

athletes.name: Pupu Sepulona
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pupu Sepulona is a sophomore defensive tackle from Kalihi, Hawaii, who played in 11 games on defense and special teams as a true freshman in 2025, recording 13 tackles with career highs of four against both West Virginia and Colorado. A three-star recruit and Polynesian Bowl invitee out of Saint Louis School, he was rated the No. 7 prospect in Hawaii and was a two-time Gatorade Hawaii Basketball Player of the Year. He is in line for an expanded role on Utah's interior defensive line in 2026.

athletes.name: Mauka Bernard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mauka Bernard is a freshman edge rusher for Utah out of Salt Lake City, where he played his high school football at Granger High School. The Utes list the local defensive end at 6-foot-4 and 215 pounds.

athletes.name: Jared Fredrick
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jared Fredrick is a freshman edge rusher on Utah's 2026 roster and a Salt Lake City native who played at East High School. He stayed home for college and is listed at 6-foot-3 and 220 pounds.

athletes.name: Alex Cloward
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alex Cloward is a freshman edge rusher for Utah out of Salem, Utah, where he played at Salem Hills High School. The Utes list the in-state defensive end at 6-foot-3 and 247 pounds for 2026.

athletes.name: Karson Kaufusi
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kaufusi is Utah's projected starting defensive tackle for 2026, a former four-star Salt Lake City recruit who was rated the No. 1 defensive tackle in the state out of Skyline High School.

athletes.name: Milz Asiata
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Milz Asiata is a freshman offensive lineman for Utah and one of the roster's international players, listed out of Melbourne, Australia, where he attended Aquinas High School. The Utes list him at 6-foot-5 and 331 pounds.

athletes.name: Mataalii Benjamin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mataalii Benjamin is a freshman offensive lineman on Utah's 2026 roster, wearing jersey number 70. He is from Lehi, Utah, and played at Lehi High School. The Utes list him at 6-foot-7 and 340 pounds.

athletes.name: Kelvin Obot
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Obot is a freshman offensive lineman from Fruitland, Idaho and one of Utah's most decorated recent signees. He was named the 2025 MaxPreps Idaho Player of the Year, listed as the top player in the state and the No. 4 offensive tackle nationally, and slotted No. 74 in the 2026 ESPN 300. He was first-team All-Idaho as a junior on both lines and won Idaho 4A state titles in the shot put and discus.

athletes.name: Isaiah Kema
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kema is a freshman offensive lineman from Lubbock, Texas who comes to Utah after appearing in four games at Ohio State in 2025. He originally signed with Oklahoma State in 2023 and served a two-year mission in New Zealand before joining the Buckeyes. At Frenship High he was a District 2-6A first-team center as a senior and a Class 6A first-team all-state guard as a junior, and he played in the 2023 Polynesian Bowl.

athletes.name: Stanley Raass
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stanley Raass is a freshman defensive lineman for Utah out of Laie, Hawaii, where he played at Kahuku High School. The Utes list the interior lineman at 6-foot-0 and 290 pounds on the 2026 roster.

athletes.name: Moses Sparks
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moses Sparks is a freshman offensive lineman on the Utah roster. He comes from Rio Rancho, New Mexico, and played his high school football at Cleveland High School. The Utes list him at 6-foot-4 and 305 pounds.

athletes.name: Fameitau Siale
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fameitau Siale is a freshman edge rusher for Utah out of Seattle, where he played at O'Dea High School. The Utes list him at 6-foot-3 and 265 pounds among their younger defensive linemen for 2026.

athletes.name: Solatoa Moea'i
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moea'i is Utah's projected starting left guard for 2026, a senior from Laie, Hawaii, and Punahou School.

athletes.name: Tanner Cragun
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cragun is a junior kicker from Frisco, Texas who has returned to Utah, where he walked on from 2020 to 2023. He spent 2025 at UTEP, making 6 of 8 field goals with a long of 38 and handling 22 kickoffs, after connecting on 7 of 9 field goals with a long of 40 in one season at Utah State. He played football and soccer at Wakeland High and was a five-star Chris Sailer Kicking prospect.

athletes.name: Reece Parmenter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Parmenter is a junior offensive lineman from St. George, Utah who appeared in all 13 games in 2025 on special teams and as a reserve lineman. He logged 83 snaps at left guard across eight games, the majority of them run blocking opportunities. A Crimson Cliffs High product, he returns as interior line depth and a special teams contributor as Utah sorts out its 2026 rotation up front.

athletes.name: Soren Shinofield
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Soren Shinofield is a sophomore offensive lineman on Utah's 2026 roster. He is from Greenwood Village, Colorado, and played at Cherry Creek High School. The Utes list the tall lineman at 6-foot-6 and 304 pounds.

athletes.name: Rowdy Pearce
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rowdy Pearce is a freshman offensive lineman for Utah out of Midland, Texas, where he played at Midland Christian School. The Utes list him at 6-foot-3 and 295 pounds heading into the 2026 season.

athletes.name: Isaiah Garcia
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Garcia is a junior offensive lineman from Magna, Utah who appeared in two games in 2025, against Iowa State and UCF. He signed with the Utes as a four-star recruit out of Corner Canyon High, rated the No. 1 prospect in the state by 247Sports and the No. 20 offensive tackle nationally. He was a two-time first-team all-state selection who finished as the highest graded lineman in Utah and drew an Under Armour All-America invitation.

athletes.name: Cedric Jefferson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jefferson is Utah's projected starting right tackle after transferring from Montana State, where he logged more than 1,200 career snaps.

athletes.name: Keith Olson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Keith Olson is a fifth-year offensive lineman from Napavine, Washington, who gives Utah versatility up front after playing in all 13 games in 2025 at right guard, left guard and right tackle, plus 97 snaps as a blocking tight end according to PFF. He did not allow a sack in 98 pass-blocking opportunities. Olson made his first two career starts in 2024 and earned Academic All-Big 12 honors. A three-star recruit from Napavine High School, he was rated the No. 20 player in Washington by 247Sports.

athletes.name: Roger Alderman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alderman is a senior offensive lineman from Sonora, California who played in each of Utah's 13 games in 2025, mainly at right guard and on special teams, taking 134 offensive snaps. He was a three-star recruit out of Sonora High and a first-team all-league offensive lineman as a senior, blocking for an offense that averaged 29.2 points per game on the way to a 10-3 record. He returns as interior line depth.

athletes.name: Zereoue Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is Utah's projected starting left tackle for 2026 after backing up first-round NFL draft pick Caleb Lomu, and he received an additional year of NCAA eligibility.

athletes.name: Nick Hallock
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nick Hallock is a sophomore offensive lineman on Utah's roster and a South Jordan, Utah, product who played at Bingham High School. He stayed in state for college and is listed at 6-foot-4 and 275 pounds.

athletes.name: Taniela Pepa
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taniela Pepa is a sophomore defensive lineman for Utah out of South Jordan, Utah, where he played at Bingham High School. The Utes list the interior defender at 6-foot-1 and 297 pounds for the 2026 season.

athletes.name: Alex Harrison
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Harrison is Utah's projected starting center for 2026, a fifth-year Bountiful, Utah, native who received extra NCAA eligibility as the Utes rebuild an offensive line that lost all five 2025 starters.

athletes.name: Bryson Baker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bryson Baker is a sophomore wide receiver on Utah's 2026 roster. He comes from Fresno, California, and played his high school football at Sanger High School. The Utes list him at 6-foot-1 and 185 pounds.

athletes.name: Bear Fisher
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bear Fisher is a freshman tight end for Utah out of Queen Creek, Arizona, where he played at Queen Creek High School. The Utes list the tall target at 6-foot-5 and 240 pounds on the 2026 roster.

athletes.name: Max Ausmus
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Max Ausmus is a sophomore wide receiver for Utah out of Redondo Beach, California, where he played at Redondo Union High School. The Utes list him at 6-foot-1 and 185 pounds in a deep receiver room.

athletes.name: Elijah Elliss
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Elliss is a junior linebacker from Farmington, Utah who played in all 13 games in 2025 and totaled 18 tackles with 3.0 for loss and 2.0 sacks. His career best five stops against Colorado included two tackles for loss and a sack, and he added a seven-yard sack in the Las Vegas Bowl win over Nebraska. He was first-team all-state at Layton Christian High. His father Luther coaches Utah's defensive tackles.

athletes.name: Broderick Redden
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Broderick Redden is a sophomore tight end on Utah's 2026 roster. He is from San Clemente, California, and played at San Clemente High School. The Utes list him at 6-foot-4 and 233 pounds.

athletes.name: Will Monney
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Monney is a junior tight end from Springville, Utah who joins the Utes after a season at Oklahoma State, where he played four games and caught three passes for 39 yards. He began at Utah State, hauling in 11 receptions for 138 yards and a touchdown in 2024 and starting against Idaho State in 2023, and earned Academic All-Mountain West honors twice. He caught 31 passes for 443 yards as a prep senior.

athletes.name: Mitch Nielsen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mitch Nielsen is a sophomore tight end for Utah out of Farmington, Utah, where he played at Farmington High School. He stayed close to home for college and is listed at 6-foot-1 and 232 pounds.

athletes.name: Noah Bennee
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Noah Bennee is a senior tight end from Holladay, Utah, back with the Utes after two seasons at Weber State, where he caught 23 passes for 264 yards in 2025 and earned Big Sky Academic All-Conference honors in 2024. He originally spent 2021 through 2023 at Utah. At Olympus High School he was named Utah 5A Defensive Player of the Year and earned all-state honors at both safety and receiver. His brother Jackson starts at safety for the Utes.

athletes.name: Jireh Moe
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moe is a sophomore defensive lineman from Westminster, California who transfers in from San Jose State, where he played 11 games in 2025 and finished with 28 tackles, two tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks. He made his collegiate debut with two stops at Texas and had five tackles against Fresno State. A three-star recruit, he played three years at Orange Lutheran High and one at Reed High and blocked three field goals as a senior.

athletes.name: Nicholas Igwe
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nicholas Igwe is a sophomore edge rusher on the Utah roster out of Houston, where he played his high school football at Cypress Creek High School. The Utes list him at 6-foot-4 and 255 pounds.

athletes.name: Orion Phillips
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Orion Phillips returns as Utah's punter and holder for 2026. The junior from Sandringham, Australia, appeared in all 12 games in 2025, allowing only six returns on 33 punts while dropping 13 inside the 20 and booming eight kicks of 50 or more yards, including a season-long 67-yarder against Colorado. He also completed a 25-yard fourth-down pass against the Buffaloes. Phillips began his career at Murray State, where his 71-yard punt in 2023 was the second longest in Missouri Valley Football Conference history, and spent 2024 at Missouri.

athletes.name: Kash Dillon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kash Dillon is a junior edge rusher from Draper, Utah, who broke into the rotation in 2025 with 35 tackles, 4.5 tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks while playing in all 13 games with three starts. He forced his first career fumble against Cincinnati and was named to the Academic All-Big 12 Rookie Team in 2024. A three-star recruit rated the No. 6 prospect in Utah by 247Sports, he helped Corner Canyon High School to region and state championships in 2023. He is projected to move into a starting role in 2026.

athletes.name: Mike Tauteoli
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tauteoli is a junior defensive lineman from Midvale, Utah who appeared in five games in 2025 on defense and special teams and is competing for interior rotation snaps this fall. He played football and rugby and competed in track at Brighton High, recording 32 total tackles as a senior and serving as a rugby team captain. His father Moses played football at Utah in 1989 and his brother Zach played at Snow College.

athletes.name: Dilan Battle
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Battle is a sophomore defensive lineman from Arlington, Texas who was on Utah's active roster in 2025 but did not see game action, leaving him in the mix for rotation snaps in 2026. He signed as a consensus three-star recruit out of Mansfield Timberview High, rated the nation's No. 59 defensive tackle and No. 83 overall in Texas for the 2025 class. As a junior he recorded 27 tackles, eight for loss and four sacks.

athletes.name: Lucas Samsula
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Samsula is a sophomore defensive lineman from Plano, Texas who arrives from Wyoming, where he played in all 12 games in 2025 and recorded 15 tackles with 1.5 for loss and 1.5 sacks. He arrived in Laramie as a tight end and caught 14 passes for 284 yards and two touchdowns in 2023, including a 75-yard reception. He was a first-team All-District 6-6A tight end at Plano West High before moving to the defensive front.

athletes.name: Semi Taulanga
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taulanga is a sophomore from Santa Ana, California listed as a tight end who made his first start on the road at BYU, catching two passes including a 10-yard grab. He came to Utah from Mater Dei High, where he helped win the CIF-SS Division I title in 2024 and a CIF Open Division state title in 2023. He played on the defensive line as a prep, posting 38 stops and 7.0 sacks as a junior.

athletes.name: Jamal Wallace
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wallace is a senior defensive lineman from Kansas City, Missouri who joins Utah after two seasons at Tennessee. He appeared in six games for the Volunteers in 2025 with four tackles, made his SEC debut against Georgia and had two tackles in the season opener versus Syracuse. He began at Sierra College, where he totaled 45 tackles, 11 tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks and earned 2023 NorCal all-state honors as a consensus three-star juco prospect.

athletes.name: Nate Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A fifth-year athlete out of Clovis, Calif., Johnson is competing for a spot in the Utes' two-deep this fall.

athletes.name: Malik Charles
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A redshirt senior edge rusher from Tempe, Arizona, Charles came to Stillwater from Division II West Georgia in 2025 and ranked second on Oklahoma State with 3.0 sacks in his first FBS season, playing 11 games with four starts and 28 tackles. He was a unanimous All-United Athletic Conference first team pick at West Georgia in 2024 with 7.0 sacks. He projects as a rotational edge again in 2026.

athletes.name: Justin Bowick
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bowick is a projected starting outside receiver for Oklahoma State, arriving from Illinois after earlier stops at Ball State and Eastern Illinois. The 6-foot-5 target led the Illini with five receiving touchdowns in 2025.

athletes.name: Miles Coleman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Coleman, a junior wide receiver from Austin, Texas, followed head coach Eric Morris from North Texas in the 2026 portal cycle. He started six of 12 games for the Mean Green in 2025 and caught 47 passes for 550 yards and three touchdowns while handling punt returns, with a seven-catch, 125-yard game in the American Conference title game. He was the 2023 District 25-6A MVP at Vandegrift.

athletes.name: Chris Barnes
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard valuation $660,000; not among On3's Top 100)
athletes.blurb: Barnes is a projected starting slot receiver and return man for Oklahoma State after transferring from Wake Forest. He led the Demon Deacons with 39 catches for 547 yards and three touchdowns in 2025, added 143 rushing yards and a 98-yard kickoff return touchdown, and earned third-team All-ACC special teams honors.

athletes.name: Isaiah Chisom
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chisom is a projected starting linebacker for Oklahoma State after transferring from UCLA, where he posted 84 tackles with 2.5 tackles for loss and two forced fumbles in 2025. He was a freshman All-American at Oregon State before that.

athletes.name: Tate Romney
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Romney is a redshirt senior linebacker from Chandler, Arizona, who began at BYU and spent three seasons at Arizona State before transferring to Oklahoma State for 2026. He started 11 games as a freshman in 2023 and tied for fourth on the Sun Devils with 52 tackles, then appeared in 10 games in 2025. A two-time Academic All-Big 12 honoree, he was named Arizona 6A linebacker of the year in 2019.

athletes.name: Mo Horn
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Horn is a projected starting cornerback for Oklahoma State after four years at Texas Tech, where he totaled 64 tackles and eight pass breakups. The Tulsa native was a full-time starter in 2024 with 56 tackles, three tackles for loss and five pass breakups.

athletes.name: Saadiq Clements
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Clements is a projected starting nose tackle for Oklahoma State, the 6-foot-4, 310-pound transfer arriving by way of North Texas after beginning his career at Louisville. He is one of 10 defensive linemen the Cowboys added through the transfer portal.

athletes.name: Israel Polk
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A redshirt junior wide receiver from Richmond, California, Polk arrived in 2026 after stops at Pittsburgh and Akron. He earned All-MAC second team honors in 2025, starting 11 games and catching 33 passes for 525 yards with eight touchdowns, which led Akron and ranked second in the league. He played at national power St. John Bosco and was rated among California's top 100 prospects. He should compete for rotation snaps.

athletes.name: Christian Bodnar
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bodnar is a redshirt junior safety from Tampa, Florida, who transferred to Oklahoma State in 2026 after three years at Liberty. He started nine of 12 games in 2025 and finished fourth on the team with 44 tackles, adding two sacks and two pass breakups, and was one of three national winners of the 2025 Comeback Player of the Year award. He should factor into the safety rotation.

athletes.name: Tre Page III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Page, a redshirt sophomore running back from Atlanta, joined Oklahoma State from Tarleton State in the 2026 portal cycle. He led the Texans with 839 rushing yards on 112 carries and seven touchdowns in 2025 despite playing only nine of 14 games, including 198 yards against Southern Utah and 170 against Portland State. He was a four-year varsity starter and state relay champion sprinter at Langston Hughes.

athletes.name: Quinton Hammonds
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hammonds is a projected starting safety and nickel for Oklahoma State after transferring from North Texas. He recorded 53 tackles with five tackles for loss, a sack and two interceptions in 2025.

athletes.name: Kollin Lewis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lewis is a redshirt junior cornerback from Gladewater, Texas, who followed the North Texas staff to Stillwater for 2026. He appeared in 13 games with one start for the Mean Green in 2025, recording 15 tackles, two interceptions, a pass breakup and a fumble recovery. He was an honorable mention all-state pick at Gladewater, where he played both ways and totaled 1,541 all-purpose yards as a senior.

athletes.name: Broderick Vehrs
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Vehrs is a true freshman quarterback from Gilbert, Arizona, who enrolled at Oklahoma State in the spring of 2026 and profiles as a developmental option behind the veterans on the depth chart. He threw for nearly 3,000 yards with 27 touchdowns and two interceptions as a junior at Basha and was the 2025 Southern Region offensive player of the year. Rivals rated him the No. 65 quarterback nationally.

athletes.name: LaDainian Fields
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard valuation $452,000; no disclosed deal)
athletes.blurb: Fields is Oklahoma State's returning starting cornerback after playing all 12 games and starting the final six as a freshman in 2025. He tied for the team lead with two interceptions, including a 55-yard pick-six at Arizona that was the Cowboys' only non-offensive touchdown of the season.

athletes.name: Grant Jordan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A redshirt senior quarterback from New Orleans, Jordan reached Oklahoma State in 2026 after playing at Yale and UMass. He was an All-Ivy honorable mention in 2024, leading Yale with 1,938 passing yards and 22 touchdowns while completing 66.4 percent of his throws, then started twice at UMass in 2025 and passed for 595 yards. He prepped at Jesuit and adds experienced depth to the quarterback room.

athletes.name: Wyatt Young
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard valuation $848,125; not among On3's Top 100, no disclosed deal)
athletes.blurb: Young is Oklahoma State's projected No. 1 receiver and Drew Mestemaker's top target, reuniting with both at Stillwater after North Texas. He caught 70 passes for 1,264 yards and 10 touchdowns in 2025, third in FBS in receiving yards, and set an American Conference record with 295 receiving yards against Rice.

athletes.name: James Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a projected starting defensive end for Oklahoma State after transferring from Florida State, with earlier stops at Nebraska and Iowa Central Community College. The Kansas City native adds Power Four edge experience to a rebuilt Cowboys front.

athletes.name: Keviyan Huddleston
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Huddleston arrives at Oklahoma State for 2026 as a transfer portal addition and projects into the edge rotation as a redshirt junior. The Tyler, Texas native spent 2025 at North Texas, appearing in all 14 games with two starts and leading the Mean Green with 9.5 tackles for loss and 5.0 sacks while adding 31 tackles and two fumble recoveries. He began his college career at TCU in 2023 and 2024. Out of Chapel Hill High School, 247Sports rated him the No. 55 edge rusher nationally.

athletes.name: Rodney Harris II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Harris is a redshirt senior wide receiver from Cincinnati who spent four seasons at Ohio before transferring in 2026. He started 11 of 13 games for the Bobcats in 2025 and posted 419 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including a six-catch, 103-yard game against Eastern Michigan, after 289 yards in 2024. He caught 20 touchdowns as a senior at Princeton High School and is a computer science major.

athletes.name: Cameron Epps
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Epps is a redshirt senior safety from St. Louis and one of the few holdovers in the Oklahoma State secondary. As a freshman in 2023 he started 10 games, led the Cowboys with three interceptions, returned one for a touchdown against Kansas State and earned honorable mention All-Big 12 recognition. He played limited snaps the past two seasons. He was a first team all-state defensive back at Chaminade.

athletes.name: Luke Tepas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tepas is a freshman quarterback on the Oklahoma State roster, listed at 6-3 and 207 pounds. He comes from Barrington, Illinois, where he played at Barrington High School, and he wears No. 12 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Trudell Berry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Berry is a redshirt senior cornerback from Baytown, Texas, who reached Oklahoma State after beginning his college career at Vanderbilt in the SEC. He played his high school football at Lee High School in Baytown. The Cowboys list him at 6-1 and 196 pounds, and he wears No. 13, bringing Power Four secondary experience to the defensive back rotation.

athletes.name: Jeremy Cook Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cook is a redshirt sophomore safety from Hoover, Alabama, who took the junior college route to Oklahoma State, arriving from East Mississippi Community College. He played at Hoover High School, one of the best known programs in Alabama. The roster lists him at 6-2 and 205 pounds, and he wears No. 14 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Jabarie Thornton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thornton is a freshman wide receiver from Waco, Texas, who played his high school football at La Vega. Oklahoma State lists him at 5-11 and 185 pounds, and he wears No. 14 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Kam Powell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Powell is a redshirt freshman wide receiver from Dallas who came to Oklahoma State out of McKinney North High School. The Cowboys list him at 6-2 and 202 pounds, and he wears No. 15.

athletes.name: Fatafehi Vailea II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Vailea is a redshirt senior defensive tackle from Oakland, California, who came with the North Texas staff in 2026. He started 22 games across four seasons for the Mean Green, including seven in 2024 when he had 34 tackles, 4.0 tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks. He was a Conference USA All-Freshman selection in 2022 and adds interior depth to the Cowboys' front.

athletes.name: Dallas Winner-Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Winner-Johnson is a redshirt junior linebacker from St. Louis whose path to Oklahoma State ran through Missouri State and Tulane. He played high school football at Cardinal Ritter College Prep in St. Louis. At 6-5 and 225 pounds he is unusually long for the position, and he wears No. 16 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Sam Keltner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Keltner transferred to Oklahoma State ahead of 2026 and joins the Cowboys as a redshirt sophomore placekicker. He spent 2025 at SMU, appearing in all 13 games and leading the team in scoring with 78 points, converting 36 of 38 extra points and 14 of 20 field goals with six makes from beyond 40 yards. He was named ACC Specialist of the Week after a three field goal performance at Clemson that included a season long 51 yarder. The Keller, Texas product was an honorable mention 6A all state pick in high school.

athletes.name: Drew Mestemaker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation $3.5M, top-10 nationally in the 2026 cycle; actual contract not disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Mestemaker is Oklahoma State's starting quarterback after following head coach Eric Morris from North Texas, where in 2025 he led all of FBS in passing yards (4,379), passing yards per game (312.8) and total offense while throwing 34 touchdowns. He won the 2025 Burlsworth Trophy and was one of four Cowboys sent to Big 12 Media Days.

athletes.name: Terrence Lewis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lewis, a sophomore wide receiver from Brenham, Texas, transferred from North Texas with the new coaching staff. He played 12 games as a freshman in 2025 and averaged 16.7 yards on 11 catches for 184 yards and three touchdowns, including a 37-yard score against UTSA. He was the District 12-6A MVP at Bryan after 54 catches for 1,273 yards and 13 touchdowns as a senior.

athletes.name: Mose Phillips III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Phillips is a projected starting free safety for Oklahoma State after transferring from Missouri, where he landed following his time at Virginia Tech. The Nashville native brings two Power Four programs' worth of secondary experience.

athletes.name: DJ Jackson Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson is a senior edge rusher from Atlanta with one of the more well traveled paths on the roster, having stopped at Carson-Newman, Coffeyville Community College and Troy before Oklahoma State. He played at Mundy's Mill High School in the Atlanta area. The Cowboys list him at 6-4 and 243 pounds, and he wears No. 19.

athletes.name: Dayvon Standard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Standard is a freshman wide receiver from Goodyear, Arizona, who played at Desert Edge High School. Oklahoma State lists him at 6-4 and 185 pounds, giving him notable height on the outside, and he wears No. 19.

athletes.name: Taurean Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davis is a junior linebacker from Quitman County, Mississippi, who came to Oklahoma State from Mississippi Gulf Coast Community College. He played his high school football at DeSoto Central in Mississippi. The Cowboys list him at 6-1 and 231 pounds, and he wears No. 20 as part of the linebacker group.

athletes.name: KD Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a freshman running back from Jenks, Oklahoma, who stayed in state after playing at Jenks High School. Oklahoma State lists him at 5-11 and 186 pounds, and he wears No. 20 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Kobi Foreman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Foreman is a sophomore cornerback from Dallas who enrolled early in 2025 and played nine games as a true freshman, handling six kickoff returns for 114 yards and making two assisted tackles at UCF. ESPN rated him the No. 74 cornerback in his class and Rivals listed him among the top 70 prospects in Texas. He was a Dallas Morning News All-Metro pick at Berkner.

athletes.name: William Mason
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mason is a senior running back listed as a walk-on who arrived at Oklahoma State from Central Oklahoma, a Division II program in Edmond. Though his hometown is Detroit, he played his high school football at Coweta in Oklahoma. The Cowboys list him at 5-11 and 226 pounds, a thick frame for the position, and he wears No. 22.

athletes.name: Oscar Hammond
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hammond is a redshirt senior tight end from Collinsville, Oklahoma, who joined the Cowboys in 2025 after North Texas and Central Oklahoma. He started six of 10 games at UNT in 2024 with 19 catches for 238 yards and a touchdown, and earned third team All-MIAA honors in both seasons at UCO, where he had 33 receptions for 463 yards in 2023. He won a state title at Collinsville.

athletes.name: Braeden Presley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Presley is a freshman safety and walk-on from Bixby, Oklahoma, who played at Bixby High School. Oklahoma State lists him at 6-0 and 190 pounds, and he wears No. 23 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Caleb Hawkins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation ~$1M; The NIL Standard ~$750K; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Hawkins is Oklahoma State's projected starting running back after transferring in from North Texas with Eric Morris. As a true freshman in 2025 he ran for 1,434 yards and 25 touchdowns, added 32 catches for 370 yards, set the FBS freshman record for touchdowns scored and was a Walter Camp second-team All-American.

athletes.name: Ayo Adeyi
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Adeyi is a redshirt senior running back from Mansfield, Texas, in his final year of eligibility after stops at Harding, North Texas and James Madison. He was a second team All-AAC pick in 2023, rushing for 1,017 yards and six touchdowns at 7.1 yards per carry, which ranked fourth nationally. He also made the Conference USA All-Freshman team in 2021 and carries strong academic honors.

athletes.name: Markeith Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a redshirt senior safety from Orlando who came to Oklahoma State after beginning his career at Miami. He played his high school football at Evans High School in Orlando. The Cowboys list him at 6-2 and 175 pounds, a long and lean build for the back end, and he wears No. 25.

athletes.name: Maliek Bracy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bracy is a freshman cornerback from Argyle, Texas, who played his high school football at Argyle. Oklahoma State lists him at 6-0 and 171 pounds, and he wears No. 26 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Dennis Moody III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moody is a redshirt junior running back whose hometown is listed as Staten Island, New York, though he played his high school football at Reedy in Texas. He reached Oklahoma State by way of North Alabama and North Texas. The Cowboys list him at 5-10 and 178 pounds, and he wears No. 26.

athletes.name: Vincent Holmes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Holmes is a redshirt junior safety from San Jacinto, California, who transferred from Washington in the spring of 2026. He played all 13 games for the Huskies in 2025 and started the finale against Oregon, and he made his first career start against USC in 2024 with four tackles. He was a consensus top-30 California recruit and a Polynesian Bowl invitee out of San Jacinto High School.

athletes.name: Marrel Davis III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davis is a freshman cornerback from Houston who played at Summer Creek High School. Oklahoma State lists him at 6-2 and 196 pounds, giving him size on the perimeter, and he wears No. 28 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Cooper Lai
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lai is a redshirt junior safety and walk-on from Tulsa who played his high school football at Cascia Hall Preparatory School. Oklahoma State lists him at 6-0 and 199 pounds, and he wears No. 29.

athletes.name: Trip White
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: White is a redshirt senior linebacker from Little Rock, Arkansas, who arrived from Ole Miss in 2025 and played all 12 games in his first season in Stillwater, starting against Cincinnati. He tied for sixth on the team with 33 tackles, adding 2.0 tackles for loss, a sack against Iowa State and a forced fumble at UCF. He was a top-15 Arkansas recruit and a two-time captain at Parkview.

athletes.name: Billy Walton III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Walton is a redshirt sophomore edge rusher from Dallas who signed with Texas out of high school, spent two seasons at SMU and transferred to Oklahoma State in 2026. He appeared in all 13 games for the Mustangs in 2025 and recorded two sacks, tied for fifth on the team. At South Oak Cliff he won two state championships and was ranked the No. 41 edge prospect nationally by 247Sports.

athletes.name: Ethan Wesloski
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wesloski is a projected starting linebacker for Oklahoma State after following Eric Morris and coordinator Skyler Cassity from North Texas. He led the Mean Green with 113 tackles in 2025 with nine tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks, two forced fumbles and an interception, and was one of four Cowboys at Big 12 Media Days.

athletes.name: Jack Puckett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Puckett is a redshirt senior linebacker from Bixby, Oklahoma, who joined the Cowboys in 2026 after three seasons and three captaincies at Division II Central Oklahoma. He was a D2CCA first team All-American in 2024 with 102 tackles, 15.0 tackles for loss and 7.0 sacks, then made first team All-MIAA again in 2025 with 63 tackles and a team-high 13 tackles for loss. He won four state titles at Bixby.

athletes.name: Ayden Webb
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Webb is a redshirt freshman safety and walk-on from Dallas who played at Lake Highlands High School. Oklahoma State lists him at 6-2 and 174 pounds, and he wears No. 35 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Javen Hall
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hall is a freshman running back and walk-on whose hometown is listed as Cleveland, Tennessee, though he played his high school football at Washington in Oklahoma. The Cowboys list him at 6-0 and 214 pounds, and he wears No. 36.

athletes.name: Lachie Pozzobon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pozzobon is a sophomore punter from Melbourne, Australia, who transferred from Stephen F. Austin for 2026 and is in line to handle punting duties. He was named FCS Football Central Freshman All-America in 2025 after punting 53 times for a 41.8-yard average, with 17 punts downed inside the 20. He trained with Prokick Australia and had never played American football before college.

athletes.name: Carl'veon Young
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Young is a redshirt freshman defensive end from Oklahoma City who was a four-star recruit in the 2025 class, rated the No. 219 overall prospect nationally and the No. 4 player in Oklahoma by 247Sports. He played the final four games of 2025 while redshirting and made a tackle at UCF. He recorded more than 250 tackles in his career at Carl Albert and should push for rotation snaps.

athletes.name: Jeremiah Piper
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Piper is a redshirt senior cornerback from Detroit and one of the most traveled players on the roster, having spent time at Western Michigan, Western Illinois and Youngstown State before Oklahoma State. He played his high school football at Southfield in Michigan. The Cowboys list him at 5-10 and 175 pounds, and he wears No. 39.

athletes.name: Cooper Mailand
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mailand is a redshirt junior linebacker from Dallas who transferred to Oklahoma State from Wyoming. He played his high school football at Parish Episcopal School in Dallas, a program known for producing college talent. The Cowboys list him at 6-0 and 232 pounds, and he wears No. 40 in the linebacker room.

athletes.name: Gabe Pendyala
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pendyala is a freshman kicker and walk-on from Sunnyvale, Texas, who played at Sunnyvale High School. Oklahoma State lists him at 5-10 and 166 pounds, and he wears No. 41 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Caden Yates
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Yates joined Oklahoma State from the transfer portal and brings multiple seasons of FBS starting experience at long snapper as a redshirt junior. The Argyle, Texas native handled the role at North Texas, appearing in all 14 games as the primary long snapper in 2025 for a unit that made 11 of 12 field goals and all 70 extra points. He snapped in 11 games in 2024 after redshirting in 2023. At Argyle High School he recorded 94 tackles, 12 tackles for loss and 6.0 sacks.

athletes.name: Rashod Bradley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bradley is a redshirt junior edge rusher from Lake City, Florida, who came to Oklahoma State through the junior college ranks at East Mississippi Community College. He played his high school football at Columbia in Lake City. The Cowboys list him at 6-3 and 279 pounds, heavy enough to slide inside, and he wears No. 44.

athletes.name: Carson Kolb
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kolb is a redshirt sophomore tight end from Scottsdale, Arizona, who transferred from Oregon State in 2026. He played all 12 games for the Beavers in 2025 and made six tackles, all on special teams, after redshirting in 2024. He lettered in 29 games at Horizon High School and also competed in track and field. He projects primarily as a special teams contributor and depth tight end.

athletes.name: Enai White
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: White is a redshirt senior defensive lineman from Philadelphia who came to Oklahoma State in 2026 after three seasons at Texas A&M and one at Penn State. He played eight games for the Nittany Lions in 2025 with three tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss and a sack, and had eight tackles as an Aggies freshman in 2022. He was a consensus four-star recruit out of Imhotep Charter.

athletes.name: Morgan McPhaul
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McPhaul is a redshirt senior tight end from Kinston, North Carolina, who joined Oklahoma State after playing at VMI. He attended Arendell-Parrott Academy in Kinston. The Cowboys list him at 6-2 and 265 pounds, closer to a lineman's build than a typical pass catching tight end, and he wears No. 45.

athletes.name: Hunter Trusler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Trusler is a freshman safety and walk-on from Dalhart, Texas, in the Panhandle, who played at Dalhart High School. Oklahoma State lists him at 6-1 and 201 pounds, and he wears No. 46 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Harrison Dempsey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dempsey is a redshirt senior safety from Gainesville, Texas, who began as an Oklahoma State walk-on in 2022, spent three seasons at North Texas and returned to Stillwater with the new staff in 2026. He played five games for the Mean Green in 2025, mostly on special teams, and recorded his first career tackle on a kickoff at Charlotte. He was a district defensive utility player of the year in high school.

athletes.name: Nolan Akins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Akins is a redshirt freshman long snapper from Flower Mound, Texas, who came to Oklahoma State after time at SMU. He played his high school football at Marcus in Flower Mound. The Cowboys list him at 6-1 and 198 pounds, and he wears No. 48 as part of the specialist group.

athletes.name: Joseph Kim
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kim is a redshirt junior kicker from Lawton, Oklahoma, who arrived in the spring of 2026 after seasons at Houston and Central Oklahoma. He made 11 of 17 field goals with a long of 51 yards and went 40 for 43 on extra points at UCO in 2025, earning MIAA special teams athlete of the week honors. He was an Academic All-Big 12 selection at Houston in 2024.

athletes.name: Gunnar Wilson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilson is a redshirt sophomore linebacker and walk-on from Melissa, Texas, who played at Melissa High School. Oklahoma State lists him at 6-2 and 217 pounds, and he wears No. 50 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Kole Seaton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Seaton is a freshman offensive lineman from Mesquite, Texas, who played his high school football at Horn. Oklahoma State lists him at 6-5 and 299 pounds, and he wears No. 50 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Beau Wendel
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wendel is a freshman linebacker and walk-on from Midlothian, Texas, who played at Midlothian High School. Oklahoma State lists him at 5-11 and 197 pounds, and he wears No. 52 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Johnny Dickson III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dickson arrived at Oklahoma State in the spring of 2026 and projects along the interior offensive line as a redshirt senior. The Corpus Christi, Texas native started 13 games at right guard for North Texas in 2025, playing more than 750 snaps and earning third team All-American Conference honors from the coaches on a team that produced the nation's top scoring offense. He began his career at Virginia Tech, appearing in 10 games in 2023. Out of Flour Bluff, he ranked among the top 25 interior offensive linemen in the 247Sports Composite.

athletes.name: Tyler Mercer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mercer is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman who joined Oklahoma State through the transfer portal for 2026 and figures into the interior line picture. The Prosper, Texas product started six of the eight games he played as a true freshman at North Texas in 2024, earning ESPN and On3 Freshman All-America recognition along with Dave Campbell's Texas Football Offensive Freshman of the Year honors. He spent 2025 at Kansas, playing in three games. ESPN ranked him the No. 11 center in the country coming out of Prosper High School.

athletes.name: Simona Fuailetolo
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fuailetolo is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from St. George, Utah, who played his high school football at Desert Hills. Oklahoma State lists him at 6-6 and 315 pounds, and he wears No. 57 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Isaiah Bowman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bowman is a freshman offensive lineman from Conway, Arkansas, who played at Conway High School. Oklahoma State lists him at 6-3 and 296 pounds, and he wears No. 58 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Jamison Mejia
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mejia is a redshirt junior offensive lineman and walk-on from Broken Arrow, Oklahoma, who played at Broken Arrow High School. The Cowboys list him at 6-3 and 302 pounds, and he wears No. 62.

athletes.name: Caleb Hackleman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hackleman is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Texarkana, Texas, who played his high school football at Pleasant Grove. Oklahoma State lists him at 6-6 and 298 pounds, and he wears No. 63 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Louie Canepa
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Canepa is a redshirt senior offensive lineman from Napa, California, who joined the Cowboys in 2025 after three years at New Mexico State. He made 10 starts as a freshman in 2023 for an Aggies team that won 10 games and reached the Conference USA title game, then started four times at right guard in 2024. He was rated the No. 15 offensive lineman in California out of Vintage High School.

athletes.name: Braydon Nelson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nelson is a projected starting offensive tackle for Oklahoma State after following Eric Morris from North Texas, where he was one of the American Conference's highest-graded linemen and played both left and right tackle.

athletes.name: Joseph Hanson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hanson is a projected starting offensive tackle for Oklahoma State after transferring from Coastal Carolina. The Niceville, Florida, native is part of a nearly entirely rebuilt Cowboys offensive line.

athletes.name: Shaun Torgeson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Torgeson is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Ventura, California, who transferred from Portland State in 2026. He started all 12 games at left tackle for the Vikings in 2025 and played 788 offensive snaps, the most on the team. At St. Bonaventure he was the Ventura County and Marmonte League offensive lineman of the year and a Los Angeles Times All-Star selection. He adds tackle depth.

athletes.name: Miguel Chavez
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chavez is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman and walk-on from Muskogee, Oklahoma, who played at Muskogee High School. The Cowboys list him at 6-3 and 314 pounds, and he wears No. 71.

athletes.name: O’Ryan Mosley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Ja’Qwon Evans
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Eli Holbrook
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Holbrook is a freshman offensive lineman from Arlington, Texas, who played at Arlington High School. Oklahoma State lists him at 6-3 and 290 pounds, and he wears No. 74 for the Cowboys.

athletes.name: Jakobe Sanders
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sanders is the only Oklahoma State offensive letterwinner from 2025 to return in 2026, and the redshirt junior projects to start up front. A Stillwater, Oklahoma native who played at Stillwater High School, he appeared in all 12 games last season and started the final six, logging close to 400 snaps. He has earned Academic All-Big 12 honors in each of the past two seasons. 247Sports rated him the No. 17 overall prospect in Oklahoma in the 2023 class, and his grandfather Robert Turner played at Oklahoma State.

athletes.name: Desmond Magiya
