Listed at 205 pounds, he is one of the more experienced homegrown defensive backs on a 2026 roster that added several veteran safeties through the transfer portal, and he projects as a depth and special teams contributor.

athletes.name: Ryelan Morris
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Morris is a freshman running back from Honey Grove, Texas, who signed with Baylor in December 2025 out of Honey Grove High School. He ran for 1,754 yards and 32 touchdowns as a sophomore and added 1,200 yards and 26 touchdowns as a junior, leaving the school as its all-time leader in most major rushing and scoring categories.

athletes.name: LeVar Thornton Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Baylor roster valuation $500,000; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Thornton is Baylor's projected No. 1 cornerback for 2026 after two seasons of playing time in Waco. Sports Illustrated ranked him seventh among the Bears' most important players for 2026.

athletes.name: Colin Peacock
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Peacock is a sophomore safety for Baylor out of Gunter, Texas, where he played at Gunter High School. He is listed at 6-1 and 206 pounds and is in his second year in the program.

athletes.name: Jayden Rowe
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jayden Rowe is a fifth-year cornerback from Tulsa, Oklahoma, who played at Union High School and signed with Oklahoma as a four-star recruit before transferring to Kansas State. He appeared in nine games for the Wildcats in 2025, working mostly on special teams. Now in his first year at Baylor and listed at 227 pounds, Rowe projects into the two-deep at cornerback for 2026.

athletes.name: Calvin Simpson-Hunt
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Calvin Simpson-Hunt is a senior cornerback from Waxahachie, Texas, who played at Waxahachie High School and spent two seasons at Ohio State, where he was part of the 2024 national championship team. He transferred to Baylor and played in seven games in 2025 as a reserve, recording two tackles. Post-spring projections place him behind LeVar Thornton Jr. at one cornerback spot.

athletes.name: Michael Allen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Allen is a fifth-year safety for Baylor from Stilwell, Kansas, and a graduate of Blue Valley High School. The roster lists him at 5-7 and 180 pounds, one of the smallest listed heights on the team.

athletes.name: Anthony Crenshaw Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anthony Crenshaw Jr. is a senior linebacker from Arlington, Texas, who played at Martin High School and came to Baylor from Delaware ahead of the 2026 season. He is in his first year with the Bears and is listed at 218 pounds. Coaches have discussed the possibility of using him in the secondary as well as at linebacker, adding depth to a defense rebuilt through the portal.

athletes.name: DeBraun Hampton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: DeBraun Hampton is a junior wide receiver from Montgomery, Texas, who played at Willis High School alongside quarterback DJ Lagway. He spent his early career at Florida before following Lagway to Baylor, arriving with three years of eligibility remaining. Listed at 184 pounds and in his first year with the Bears, Hampton adds a receiver with existing chemistry with the starting quarterback.

athletes.name: Austin Ausberry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Austin Ausberry is a fifth-year safety from Baton Rouge, Louisiana, who played at University Lab High School. A four-star prospect ranked among the top 200 nationally in the 2022 class, he signed with Auburn and later transferred to LSU before joining Baylor with one year of eligibility left. Listed at 193 pounds, he can line up at either safety or cornerback for the Bears.

athletes.name: Brody Day
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Day is a sophomore wide receiver for Baylor out of Spring Branch, Texas, where he played at Smithson Valley High School. He is listed at 5-11 and 188 pounds in his second year with the Bears.

athletes.name: HD Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Davis is a freshman running back from Wolfe City, Texas, who signed with Baylor after flipping his commitment from Kansas State. He rushed for 2,429 yards and 30 touchdowns on 253 carries as a senior at Wolfe City High School and 2,789 yards with 31 scores as a junior, finishing with 6,306 career rushing yards and 73 touchdowns. He set a school single game record with 503 yards.

athletes.name: Daniel Edeni
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Edeni is a junior cornerback for Baylor out of San Antonio, where he played at O'Connor High School. The Bears list him at 6-2 and 203 pounds and he is in his third year in the program.

athletes.name: Dawson Pendergrass
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Baylor roster valuation $530,419; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Pendergrass is Baylor's projected lead running back after redshirting 2025 with a preseason injury. He ran for 671 yards and six touchdowns on 121 carries in 2024.

athletes.name: Travion Barnes
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Baylor roster valuation $376,811; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Barnes is Baylor's returning starting middle linebacker after a season-ending injury four games into 2025. He was the 2024 Conference USA Defensive Player of the Year at FIU, where he ranked fifth nationally in total tackles.

athletes.name: Ryne Shackelford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Shackelford is a senior wide receiver from Elyria, Ohio, who transferred to Baylor after two seasons at Purdue. At Keystone High School he was a two time first team All-Ohio selection in Division V and produced 597 receiving yards with 10 touchdowns plus 666 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns as a senior.

athletes.name: Demetrius Brisbon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brisbon is a sophomore safety for Baylor from Tyler, Texas, and a graduate of Chapel Hill High School. He is listed at 5-11 and 181 pounds in his second year with the Bears.

athletes.name: Jacob Redding
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Baylor roster valuation $450,000; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Redding is Baylor's returning starting free safety, who made 53 tackles with three interceptions in 2025 and graded as the Bears' top defender per PFF. He went from walk-on to full-time starter during the season.

athletes.name: Cole Redding
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Redding is a sophomore safety from New Braunfels, Texas, who came to Baylor after a redshirt season at Harding University. At New Braunfels High School he played defensive back and receiver, earned first team all district honors twice along with first team all region recognition, and totaled 112 tackles with three interceptions. His older brother, Jacob Redding, also plays defensive back for the Bears.

athletes.name: Kyler Jordan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kyler Jordan is a fifth-year defensive end from Lubbock, Texas, who came to Baylor from Cooper High School and has spent his entire career in the program. He recorded 18 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss and a sack in 2025 while working in the edge rotation. Listed at 251 pounds, Jordan has been cited as one of Baylor's more important veteran presences entering 2026.

athletes.name: Kaleb Burns
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kaleb Burns is a sophomore linebacker from Houston, Texas, who signed with Baylor out of Cy Falls High School and is in his second year in the program. He is listed at 224 pounds. Post-spring projections place him behind Kyland Reed at weakside linebacker, giving Burns a two-deep role and rotational snaps in a linebacker group that added transfer help for 2026.

athletes.name: Jamarion Phillips
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Phillips is a freshman linebacker from Dallas who signed with Baylor out of South Oak Cliff High School. As a senior he was the District 5-5A Division II defensive MVP with 90 tackles, 14 tackles for loss, three sacks and five blocked kicks, and the Dallas Morning News named him its 2025 defensive player of the year. He chose Baylor from 29 offers.

athletes.name: Brody Wilhelm
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brody Wilhelm is a sophomore tight end from Austin, Texas, in his second year at Baylor after signing out of Westlake High School. He committed to the Bears following a summer camp workout in Waco and opened his senior high school season with 15 receptions for 208 yards and four touchdowns. Now listed at 236 pounds, he sits behind veterans Tony Livingston and Matthew Klopfenstein.

athletes.name: JJ Shelton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: JJ Shelton is a sophomore linebacker from Dallas, Texas, who played at South Oak Cliff High School and spent one season at Arkansas before transferring to Baylor. He is in his first year with the Bears and is listed at 204 pounds. Shelton joins a linebacker room that also added Georgia State transfer Kedrick Walker, giving Baylor added depth behind its projected starters.

athletes.name: Kyland Reed
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reed signed with Baylor as a three-star recruit ranked the 123rd linebacker nationally by 247Sports out of Arlington, Texas. He appeared in all 12 games last season with nine starts, playing roughly 606 snaps and finishing with 50 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. Now a junior wearing No. 45, he projects as a starting linebacker in 2026 and is expected to share leadership of the unit with Travion Barnes.

athletes.name: Parker Almanza
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Almanza is a freshman tight end from Trophy Club, Texas, and a Byron Nelson High School product. He caught 57 passes for 758 yards and nine touchdowns as a junior, then moved to quarterback as a senior and threw for 2,681 yards and 31 touchdowns while rushing for 560 yards. His older brother, Leo Almanza, is also on the Baylor roster.

athletes.name: Kai Wesley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wesley is a freshman tight end from Orem, Utah, listed by Baylor at 6-7 and 252 pounds. He won a state championship at Orem High School and was a three sport athlete who also played baseball and basketball. Rated a three-star recruit, he committed to Baylor in June 2025 over offers that included Washington, Florida State, Utah and BYU.

athletes.name: Jad Darkazalli
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Darkazalli is a junior safety for Baylor from Arlington, Texas, where he played at Lamar High School. The roster lists him at 6-0 and 190 pounds in his second year with the program.

athletes.name: Trey Laurence
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Laurence is a senior linebacker for Baylor out of San Antonio, where he played at Reagan High School. He is listed at 6-0 and 220 pounds and is in his fourth year with the Bears.

athletes.name: Kedrick Walker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kedrick Walker is a senior linebacker from Adamsville, Alabama, who played at Minor High School and took a junior college route through Bethel and Hutchinson before landing at Georgia State. He was the Panthers' third-leading tackler in 2025 and transferred to Baylor for 2026. Listed at 236 pounds, he is projected behind Travion Barnes at middle linebacker in his first year with the Bears.

athletes.name: Garrick Ponder
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Baylor roster valuation $965,999; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Ponder is Baylor's projected starting Jack edge rusher after transferring from Southern Miss, where he was the Golden Eagles' primary pass rusher. He carries the second-highest NIL valuation on Baylor's 2026 roster.

athletes.name: Ryan Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ryan Davis is a senior edge rusher from Phoenix, Arizona, who played at O'Connor High School and spent two seasons at Kansas State, where he was among the Wildcats' most productive pass rushers with seven sacks and eight tackles for loss. He followed defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman to Waco and is listed at 251 pounds, projecting into the defensive end rotation in his first Baylor season.

athletes.name: Daemian Wimberly
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Daemian Wimberly is a senior defensive end from Austin, Texas, who played at Vandegrift High School and began his career at SMU before spending two seasons at UTSA. He appeared in 24 games for the Roadrunners and posted 11 tackles, four tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks in 2025. Now in his first year at Baylor and listed at 263 pounds, he adds interior and edge flexibility.

athletes.name: Jae'Lin Battle
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Battle is a freshman defensive lineman from Oklahoma City who signed with Baylor out of Edmond Santa Fe High School. He recorded 62 tackles with 17 for loss, 9.5 sacks and six pass breakups as a senior after posting 57 tackles, eight for loss and four sacks as a junior. He was Baylor's first defensive line commitment in the 2026 class.

athletes.name: Jaylin Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a junior edge rusher from Beaumont, Texas, who transferred to Baylor after a season at UTEP. He appeared in 12 games for the Miners in 2024, made 12 tackles with one for loss and earned a spot on the Conference USA All-Freshman team. He played at West Brook High School and was an honorable mention all-state pick in 2023.

athletes.name: Kaleb Arterberry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Arterberry is a sophomore linebacker from Pearl, Mississippi, who joined Baylor from Mississippi Gulf Coast Community College. He made 61 tackles and two sacks in 10 junior college games and earned All-MACCC South honorable mention recognition. He played high school football at Pearl and is listed by the Bears at 6-3 and 246 pounds.

athletes.name: Christopher Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a sophomore defensive end for Baylor out of Rosharon, Texas, where he played at Iowa Colony High School. He is listed at 6-3 and 265 pounds in his second year with the program.

athletes.name: Devonte Tezino
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Devonte Tezino is a fifth-year defensive lineman from Killeen, Texas, who came to Baylor out of Ellison High School and has spent his entire career in the program. Listed at 284 pounds, he is projected after spring practice as the backup nose tackle behind Hosea Wheeler. That gives Tezino a rotational role on the interior of a defensive front rebuilt largely through the transfer portal.

athletes.name: Brady Hibbard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hibbard is a junior long snapper from Marshville, North Carolina, who came to Baylor after time at Wofford. He was a four year letterman and three year starting quarterback at Forest Hills High School, where he finished as the school's all-time leader in passing yards and touchdowns and helped a 12-2 team reach the fourth round of the state playoffs.

athletes.name: Cayden Tone
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tone is a senior offensive lineman for Baylor from Pacifica, California, and a graduate of Junipero Serra High School. The Bears list him at 6-5 and 295 pounds in his fourth year with the program.

athletes.name: Alessandro Lorenzetti
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lorenzetti is a fifth-year offensive lineman from Montreal, Quebec, who transferred to Baylor from Michigan after joining the Wolverines in the 2022 recruiting class. He was named a Michigan scout team offensive player of the week during the 2022 season. He prepped at The Loomis Chaffee School in Connecticut and is listed at 6-5 and 314 pounds.

athletes.name: Wyatt Swaner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Swaner is a junior offensive lineman for Baylor from Dallas, where he played at Highland Park High School. He is listed at 6-1 and 287 pounds and is in his third year with the Bears.

athletes.name: Braylen Jackson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Braylen Jackson is a fifth-year defensive lineman from Mansfield, Texas, who played at Lake Ridge High School and began his college career at SMU before transferring to Baylor. He is in his second year with the Bears and is listed at 289 pounds, giving Baylor an experienced interior body in a defensive line room that added several portal additions ahead of the 2026 season.

athletes.name: Lawson Petty
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lawson Petty is a senior offensive lineman from Dallas, Texas, who played at Highland Park High School and transferred to Baylor from Incarnate Word, where he started at both left and right guard. Listed at 305 pounds in his first year with the Bears, he is projected after spring practice as the backup at left guard behind South Alabama transfer Asher Hale.

athletes.name: Koltin Sieracki
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A redshirt sophomore from The Woodlands, Texas, Sieracki was a three-star signee rated by 247Sports, Rivals and ESPN and earned first-team all-district honors as a high school junior. He redshirted in 2024 while serving as the primary backup center behind Coleton Price. Baylor coaches have projected him as a center in the program's wide zone scheme, putting him in contention for the interior starting job in 2026. He plays alongside his brother Kaden in the Baylor offensive line room.

athletes.name: Aleki Manutai
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Manutai is a junior defensive lineman from Mission Viejo, California, who joined Baylor from Saddleback College in August 2025. He was a second team All-Trinity League selection at Santa Margarita Catholic High School, where he lettered in football and track. Baylor lists him at 6-2 and 280 pounds.

athletes.name: Yakiri Walker
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Baylor roster valuation $399,000; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Walker is Baylor's projected starting center, arriving from Memphis after earlier stops at UConn and Colorado. His 2026 availability came into question after a court denied his request for a temporary injunction on eligibility.

athletes.name: Nate Kibble
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kibble transferred to Baylor from Texas in January 2026 after redshirting in 2024 and appearing in three games at right guard in 2025, playing 38 snaps without allowing a pressure or sack according to Pro Football Focus. The redshirt sophomore was a four-star recruit and four-year varsity starter at Atascocita High School in Humble, Texas, where he was a three-time all-district selection. He joins a rebuilt Baylor offensive line and figures into the interior rotation in 2026.

athletes.name: Asher Hale
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hale arrived at Baylor from South Alabama, where he started 11 games at right guard in 2025 and appeared in 12 games as a true freshman in 2024, including a start in the Salute to Veterans Bowl. He has logged more than 1,000 career snaps. A three-star prospect at St. Paul's Episcopal School in Mobile, Alabama, he was a second-team all-state pick and played in the Alabama versus Mississippi All-Star Game. The junior projects into Baylor's interior line rotation.

athletes.name: Keystone Allison
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Allison is a senior offensive lineman from Carthage, Texas, who signed with Baylor out of the transfer portal after two seasons at Louisiana Tech. He won a state championship as a senior at Carthage High School and was a three-star recruit in the 2023 class, choosing Louisiana Tech over Oklahoma State, Tulane and UTSA.

athletes.name: Kaden Sieracki
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Baylor roster valuation $880,764; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Sieracki is Baylor's returning starting right tackle, having started all 12 games there in 2025. He allowed no sacks and only two quarterback hits across 583 pass-blocking snaps, per PFF.

athletes.name: Harrison Cluff
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Harrison Cluff is a sophomore offensive lineman from Columbia, Mississippi, who signed with Baylor out of Columbia High School and is in his second year in the program. Listed at 315 pounds, he is projected after spring practice as the backup center behind Memphis transfer Yakiri Walker, who started every game at the position in 2025. That puts Cluff in the interior two-deep for 2026.

athletes.name: Logan Moore
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Logan Moore is a senior offensive lineman from San Diego, California, who played at Lincoln High School and transferred to Baylor from UAB, where he started at right tackle. He arrived with two years of eligibility remaining and is listed at 296 pounds. Post-spring projections place him second at right tackle behind Kaden Sieracki in his first season with the Bears.

athletes.name: Cole Rhett
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Baylor roster valuation $616,000; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Rhett is Baylor's projected starting left tackle after transferring from Toledo, where he made 11 career starts, mostly at right tackle.

athletes.name: Connor Cameron
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cameron is a junior offensive lineman from Gilbert, Arizona, who transferred to Baylor from Arizona State, where he redshirted after arriving in the 2024 class. He was a first team all-region selection in 2023 at Campo Verde High School. Baylor lists the tackle at 6-7 and 306 pounds.

athletes.name: Jackson Baird
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Baird is a junior wide receiver for Baylor from Waco, where he played at Midway High School. The roster lists him at 6-4 and 198 pounds and he is in his third year with the program.

athletes.name: Tony Livingston
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Baylor roster valuation $396,776; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Livingston is a projected starting tight end for Baylor, reuniting with quarterback DJ Lagway after both transferred from Florida.

athletes.name: London Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a freshman wide receiver from Waco who played at University High School and was a four-star recruit with more than 20 offers before choosing Baylor. He caught 132 passes for 2,102 yards and 22 touchdowns from 2022 through 2024. His father, Rodney Smith, started at safety for Baylor in the late 1990s, and his mother, Stacey, is an associate head coach with Baylor track and field.

athletes.name: Jadon Porter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jadon Porter is a junior wide receiver from Lorena, Texas, who signed with Baylor out of Lorena High School and is in his third year in the program. Listed at 192 pounds, he is projected after spring practice as the backup in the slot behind Oklahoma State transfer Gavin Freeman, keeping Porter in the receiver two-deep on a roster that added several portal pass catchers.

athletes.name: Chase Collier
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Collier is a sophomore wide receiver for Baylor out of Jacksonville, Florida, where he played at The Bolles School. He is listed at 6-1 and 181 pounds in his second year with the Bears.

athletes.name: Matthew Klopfenstein
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Klopfenstein is a senior tight end from Scottsdale, Arizona, who chose Baylor over Arizona, Arizona State and California. Rated a four-star prospect by 247Sports and ESPN, he caught 42 passes for 652 yards and six touchdowns as a senior at Horizon High School and was named team MVP. He played 11 games as a freshman in 2023 and appeared in 12 games with a start against Houston in 2024. He remains a fixture in Baylor's tight end rotation entering 2026.

athletes.name: Hawkins Polley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Polley is a senior tight end for Baylor from Houston, where he played at Stratford High School. The roster lists him at 6-4 and 256 pounds and he is in his fourth year with the program.

athletes.name: Ashton Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ashton Jones is a sophomore wide receiver from Pearland, Texas, who came to Baylor out of Shadow Creek High School and is in his second year in the program. Listed at 202 pounds, he is projected after spring practice as the backup at the X receiver spot behind fifth-year veteran Louis Brown IV, positioning him for rotational snaps in the 2026 passing game.

athletes.name: Taz Williams Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taz Williams Jr. is a sophomore wide receiver from Red Oak, Texas, who signed with Baylor out of Red Oak High School and is in his second year in the program. Listed at 192 pounds, he is projected after spring practice as the backup at the Z receiver spot behind Colorado transfer Dre'lon Miller, giving him a place in the two-deep for 2026.

athletes.name: Michael Johnson Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Michael Johnson Jr. is a junior wide receiver from Batesville, Mississippi, who played at South Panola High School and came to Baylor by way of East Mississippi Community College. He is in his second year in the program and is listed at 207 pounds. Johnson competes in a receiver room that Baylor restocked with portal additions from Colorado, Kentucky and Oklahoma State for 2026.

athletes.name: Hosea Wheeler
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Baylor roster valuation $720,000; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Wheeler is Baylor's projected starting nose tackle, a sixth-year defensive lineman who arrives from Indiana after stops at Western Kentucky and Sacramento City College.

athletes.name: Zavion Hardy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zavion Hardy is a senior defensive end from Macon, Georgia, who played at Howard High School and was ranked as the No. 1 junior college prospect nationally out of East Mississippi Community College before signing with South Carolina. He transferred to Baylor for 2026 and is listed at 281 pounds. Post-spring projections place him behind Jordan Mack in the defensive end rotation.

athletes.name: Dylan Schaub
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Schaub, a redshirt junior from New Waverly, Texas, played defensive line and tight end in high school and did not focus on long snapping until his junior year. Pressed into duty as a true freshman, he handled the primary long snapping role for Baylor's final eight games that season. He has since competed with Iowa State transfer Drake Knobloch for the starting job. Listed at 6-5 and 236 pounds, he wears No. 93 and remains in the mix for snapping duties in 2026.

athletes.name: Palmer Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Baylor roster valuation $110,000; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Williams is Baylor's returning punter and the 2025 Big 12 Special Teams Player of the Year, averaging 46.9 yards per punt as a Ray Guy Award finalist. He was named second-team All-America by The Athletic.

athletes.name: Kamren Washington
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Baylor roster valuation $827,999; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Washington is Baylor's projected starting defensive tackle, arriving from Texas State after earlier stops at Sam Houston and Memphis. The Arlington, Texas, native is in his final season.

athletes.name: Jordan Mack
athletes.source: Estimate (The NIL Standard 2026 Baylor roster valuation $700,000; no deal figure publicly disclosed)
athletes.blurb: Mack is Baylor's projected starting defensive end after transferring from Coastal Carolina, where he recorded nine tackles and a sack in 2025. He began his career at Division II Seton Hill.

athletes.name: Rhett Armstrong
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Armstrong, a sophomore from Monument, Colorado, kicked a 62-yard field goal at Palmer Ridge High School, the longest in Colorado 4A history, and finished as the state's all-time scoring leader among kickers with 279 career points. He went 2 for 2 on field goals in the 2024 U.S. Army All-America Game and chose Baylor over Tennessee, Colorado and Air Force. As a freshman he handled all 70 Baylor kickoffs, averaging 63.1 yards with 35 touchbacks, and projects into a larger kicking role in 2026.

athletes.name: Jackson Blackwell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Blackwell is a sophomore defensive lineman from Lorena, Texas, listed by Baylor at 6-3 and 314 pounds. He was named defensive line MVP at an Under Armour camp in March 2024, and his Power Four offers followed shortly after. He committed to Baylor over Texas Tech, Arizona, Houston and Kansas State, and also competed in track and weightlifting at Lorena High School.

athletes.name: Jamaal Whyce Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Whyce joined Baylor in January 2026 from Marshall with one season of eligibility remaining. athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The San Jose, California, native punted at Bellarmine College Preparatory and enters his senior year as a backup specialist behind the Cougars' starting punter in 2026.

athletes.name: Jack Carson-Wentz
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: McKenzie Agnello
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The Copperas Cove, Texas native played 773 snaps last season, allowed no sacks across 368 pass blocking snaps, graded as the team's top pass blocker and earned Big 12 All-Academic honors. He started all 12 games at New Mexico in 2024, mostly at center, and was a second team All-Mountain West selection. He began his college career at East Texas A&M.

athletes.name: Hingano Hautau
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The San Jose, California, native reached Houston by way of Willow Glen High School and Foothill College and enters his fifth year as interior line depth.

athletes.name: Sean Terrell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Weston Edwards
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He entered the transfer portal after spring practice in 2025 and committed to Houston, joining a Cougars long snapping group that also included Anthony Saragusa.

athletes.name: Larry Crawford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Noah Abebe

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

As a freshman in 2024 he was named Big 12 Special Teams Player of the Week and had a career long 65 yard punt against Kansas State.

athletes.name: Kaleb Walker

athletes.name: Carmello Brooks

At St. Stanislaus he made 25 of 40 field goals and 109 of 119 extra points for 184 career points, and his 61 yard field goal set a Mississippi high school record.

athletes.name: Eythan Thompson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He also earned Academic All-District honors. The Upper Arlington, Ohio, native came to Houston from Notre Dame and returns for a fifth year in the same specialist role.

athletes.name: Myles Parker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Parker played 12 games in 2025 and started one at defensive end, logging 113 snaps that came mostly on defense. He came to Houston from Tennessee Tech. The Snellville, Georgia, native played at Brookwood High School and enters his senior season as a rotational edge defender for the Cougars in 2026.

athletes.name: Quindario Lee
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lee played in all 12 games in 2024, his first season at Houston after transferring from Central Michigan, but did not see action in 2025. The McKenzie, Alabama, native played at McKenzie High School and returns for a fifth year looking to reclaim a rotational spot on the Cougars' defensive line.

athletes.name: Jordan Allen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Allen is a projected starting defensive back for the Houston Cougars out of Lafayette, La., after transferring from LSU for his fifth season.

athletes.name: AJ Ia
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ia arrived in Tempe as a four-star tight end from Orange Lutheran, the highest rated tight end Arizona State had signed in decades. The Santa Ana native posted 566 receiving yards and seven touchdowns as a high school senior, earned Trinity League offensive MVP honors and accepted a Polynesian Bowl invitation. He drew staff praise in his first preseason camp and enters 2026 as a sophomore working for snaps in a veteran tight end room.

athletes.name: Rodney Bimage Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bimage is Arizona State's projected No. 1 cornerback for 2026 after developing behind NFL draft pick Keith Abney II. The Houston native is expected to anchor a secondary rebuilt largely through the transfer portal.

athletes.name: Kyson Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is Arizona State's projected starting running back and the front-runner for RB1 after an early-season injury cut short his 2025 campaign. The senior has appeared in 30 career games for the Sun Devils.

athletes.name: Ashton Stamps
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stamps is a projected starting cornerback for Arizona State after transferring from LSU, where he was a two-year starter with 74 tackles and 16 pass breakups. He committed to the Sun Devils in January 2026.

athletes.name: Jake Fette
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fette is a true freshman quarterback from El Paso who signed with Arizona State in December 2025 after holding his pledge for roughly a year and a half despite interest from Ole Miss, Mississippi State and LSU. As a Del Valle senior he threw for 2,737 yards and 28 touchdowns and ran for 1,105 yards and 18 scores. He forwent the end of his high school season to enroll early and develop behind the veterans on the depth chart.

athletes.name: Lyrik Rawls
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rawls is Arizona State's projected starting free safety, a sixth-year transfer who made 12 starts at Kansas after beginning his career at Oklahoma State. Head coach Kenny Dillingham singled him out as a spring standout.

athletes.name: Albert Smith III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith joined Arizona State in the 2024 recruiting class as a three-star edge prospect out of Louisiana, choosing the Sun Devils over offers from Nebraska, Baylor, Missouri and Tulane. Listed at 6-1 and 232 pounds, the Terrytown native has been on the roster for two seasons and enters 2026 as a junior competing for edge rotation snaps in a defensive front that added several transfers.

athletes.name: Reed Harris
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Harris is a projected starting outside receiver for Arizona State after transferring from Boston College. The 6-foot-5 target started all 12 games in 2025 and posted 39 catches for 673 yards and a team-leading five touchdowns.

athletes.name: Omarion Miller
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation ~$508K; no deal terms publicly disclosed. Signed a vehicle deal with Jones Ford Verde Valley)
athletes.blurb: Miller is Arizona State's headline transfer receiver after arriving from Colorado, where he caught 45 passes for 808 yards and eight touchdowns in 2025. He was an All-Big 12 second-team pick and led the conference at 17.9 yards per catch.

athletes.name: Emar'rion Winston
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Winston is a fifth-year edge rusher from Portland, Oregon who signed with Arizona State after starting at defensive end for Baylor in 2025. He recorded 26 tackles, 5.5 tackles for loss, three sacks and five quarterback hurries that season. He began his career at Oregon, where he spent three years and totaled 19 tackles as a redshirt freshman. Listed at 6-foot-4 and 247 pounds, he arrives at a position of need and projects as an immediate starter on the Sun Devils defensive front.

athletes.name: Roman Pitre
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pitre began his career at Purdue without seeing game action, then signed with Arizona State in January 2024. The Baton Rouge native appeared in nine games in 2024, working mostly on special teams. He was a consensus three-star recruit rated among the top 35 prospects in Louisiana and a top-50 edge prospect nationally. Now a fifth-year defensive lineman listed at 6-5 and 265 pounds, he is competing for rotation snaps up front.

athletes.name: Derek Eusebio
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Eusebio is a senior wide receiver from Plano, Texas who walked on at Arizona State and was placed on scholarship ahead of the 2025 season. Listed at 5-foot-10 and 185 pounds, he caught 22 passes for 341 yards and two touchdowns last fall while averaging 15.5 yards per reception. He stepped in when Jordyn Tyson was unavailable, posting six catches for 74 yards against West Virginia and four for 87 at Colorado, including a 68-yard reception that tied for the team's longest play.

athletes.name: Adrian "Boogie" Wilson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilson is a veteran Arizona State defensive back transitioning to nickel for 2026 after transferring in from Washington State. He recorded 57 tackles and an interception in 2024 and was limited in spring by a shoulder injury.

athletes.name: Marquis Gillis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gillis spent four seasons at Delaware State, where he was the 2022 MEAC Rookie of the Year and rushed for 2,474 career yards and 19 touchdowns. He led the Hornets with 1,184 yards and nine scores on 183 carries in 2025, then committed to Arizona State in January 2026 as a graduate transfer for his final season. The Milford, Delaware, native joins a crowded backfield competing for carries as a sixth-year back.

athletes.name: Montana Warren
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Warren is a returning Arizona State defensive back moving back to safety after time at nickel, and he posted 40 tackles across 11 games in 2025. He earned Pat Tillman Leadership Council recognition.

athletes.name: Raiden Vines-Bright
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Martell Hughes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation ~$1.1M, No. 55 nationally; deal terms not disclosed. Signed a vehicle deal with Jones Ford Verde Valley, value undisclosed)

athletes.name: Cory Butler Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The sophomore is working for slot and return snaps in a transfer-heavy receiver room.

athletes.name: Jalen Thompson

athletes.name: Clayton Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Mikey Keene
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Cameron Dyer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Xavier Skowron
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Joseph Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He took second-team reps during his first spring in Tempe and enters 2026 as a sophomore pushing for a place in a rebuilt cornerback rotation.

athletes.name: Khamari Anderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Jaren Hamilton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The senior receiver is one of several veterans competing for rotation snaps in a room that added multiple transfers ahead of 2026.

athletes.name: Nigel Pringle
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He redshirted his first year with the Razorbacks, then committed to Arizona State in January 2026. Listed at 6-1, the sophomore cornerback brings the length the Sun Devils have prioritized on the perimeter and is competing for a two-deep spot this fall.

athletes.name: Michael "Butter" Tollefson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Joshua Shanklin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Jalen Moss
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Ramere Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Landen Miree
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Daquwan Dunn
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The freshman enrolled in early 2026 and is working at the back of the cornerback depth chart.

athletes.name: Maurice Williams

The junior from Alief is listed at 6-1 and 210 pounds and is competing for a rotational safety role in 2026.

athletes.name: Kyan McDonald

athletes.name: Grayson Rigdon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Jason Brown Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Owen Long
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Long is Arizona State's starting inside linebacker after transferring from Colorado State, where he led all of FBS with 151 total tackles in 2025. He was a first-team All-Mountain West selection and an Associated Press third-team All-American.

athletes.name: Demarius "Man Man" Robinson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Robinson totaled 4,271 rushing yards and 47 touchdowns across three varsity seasons at Edmond Santa Fe in Oklahoma and arrived as a unanimous three-star prospect ranked among the top 25 players in his state. He was one of the few true freshmen to get carries early in 2025, including five rushes against Texas State. The Oklahoma City sophomore is competing for backup carries behind Arizona State's transfer additions.

athletes.name: Jessiah McGrew
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McGrew spent his first college season at FIU, where he recorded 68 tackles, four interceptions and five pass breakups and was named a FWAA Freshman All-American, an All-Conference USA second-team selection and a member of the league's all-freshman team. He signed with Arizona State in December 2025. The Tallahassee native, who prepped at Florida State University School, arrives as a sophomore expected to compete immediately for a starting safety job.

athletes.name: Jalen Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: David Avit
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He finished with 1,610 rushing yards and 17 touchdowns across two FCS seasons before committing to Arizona State in January 2026. The junior from Frederick, Maryland, is in the mix for carries in a reworked backfield.

athletes.name: Cardae Mack
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He was rated among the top 20 running backs in his recruiting class despite playing mostly quarterback in high school, where he threw for 1,864 yards and 18 touchdowns. The freshman is learning the position behind veteran transfer additions.

He signed with Texas and played in one game for the Longhorns in 2025 before transferring to Arizona State with four years of eligibility. He reunites with position coach Bryan Carrington and enters 2026 as a sophomore competing for two-deep snaps after the Sun Devils lost both starting corners.

athletes.name: Carston Kieffer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He converted all 43 of his extra point attempts as a high school senior and finished a perfect 127 for 127 for his prep career, with a long field goal of 45 yards and first team 6A All-Central Region honors. He wears No. 26.

athletes.name: Davis Kinney
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Nasir Stephens
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The Long Beach, California, native signed with Arizona State ahead of the 2026 season. Listed at 5-11 and 185 pounds, the junior defensive back joins a cornerback group that lost both starters and is competing for a rotational role.

athletes.name: Zyrus Fiaseu
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Kanyon Floyd
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He handled Arizona State's punting in 2025, recording 36 punts for a 41.4-yard average with a long of 58 yards and six kicks placed inside the 20-yard line. He returns as the incumbent starter on special teams for the 2026 season.

athletes.name: Zeth Thues

He spent three earlier seasons at East Carolina and reunites at ASU with special teams coordinator Jack Nudo, whom he worked with at both previous stops. He projects as the starting place kicker.

athletes.name: Oscar Aguilar Jr.

The senior was added to a punting unit the staff openly targeted for improvement.

His older brother Netane Muti was a sixth-round NFL draft pick out of Fresno State. Now a sophomore listed at 6-7 and 305 pounds, he is developing as a tackle option.

athletes.name: Rob Lapuaho
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He comes from a large football family, with his father Robert having played at BYU in the 1980s and a brother who also played there. He projects into the Sun Devils' offensive line rotation in 2026.

athletes.name: Desean Bryant Jr.

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Filiva’a “Suka” Lokotui
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Tana Alo-Tupuola
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alo-Tupuola is a junior offensive lineman from Brownsburg, Indiana who transferred to Arizona State from Georgia Tech. He played 23 snaps at center over three games as a true freshman in 2024 and appeared in 10 games with the Yellow Jackets, whose offense finished 11th nationally in total yards per game in 2025. He began his prep career at Brownsburg High School before finishing at IMG Academy, where ESPN rated him a three-star recruit and the No. 7 center in the country.

athletes.name: Maki Stewart
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

Listed at 6-foot-5 and 330 pounds, he started his prep career at Los Alamitos before transferring to Millikan High School, where he led the program to an undefeated league record as a senior and a spot in the 2024 CIF Southern Section Division 3 playoffs. He chose the Sun Devils over offers that included Utah, Florida State and Texas A&M.

athletes.name: Wade Helton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

A three-star signee out of Centennial High in Corona, California, he redshirted his lone year with the Cyclones without appearing in a game. The junior is listed at 6-4 and 310 pounds and is competing for interior line snaps.

athletes.name: Brent Helton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The junior carries 315 pounds on a 6-4 frame and is competing for a rotational offensive line role.

athletes.name: Jalen Klemm
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He transferred to Arizona State from Washington, where he played seven games. The fifth-year lineman from Mars, Pennsylvania, logged 176 snaps as a backup in 2025, including work in the Sun Bowl against Duke.

athletes.name: Makua Pule

He prepped at Gilbert Highland, where he also competed in track and field, and arrived at Arizona State as a preferred walk-on before earning a scholarship. He has worked primarily at center and studies civil engineering.

athletes.name: Doughless Teloma

athletes.name: Siosaia “Leni” Lapuaho
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He started at tackle for two seasons at Garden City Community College in Kansas after prepping at Alta High in Sandy, Utah, where he was a three-star recruit. The junior is competing for tackle snaps in his first year in Tempe.

athletes.name: Jarmaine Mitchell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

Listed at 6-foot-8 and 310 pounds, he was the top-ranked junior college prospect in the country and flipped his commitment from Georgia to the Sun Devils, the first No. 1 overall JUCO recruit in any class to sign with the program. He started at left tackle as a senior at St. James High School, which reached a Louisiana state championship game.

athletes.name: Champ Westbrooks
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He worked his way up the depth chart at right tackle and earned the first collegiate start of his career in the Sun Bowl to close the 2025 season. He entered 2026 competing with Oklahoma transfer Luke Baklenko for the job and projects into the Sun Devils' starting offensive line.

athletes.name: Matai Jefferson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He moved to Arizona State with one season of eligibility remaining. The 6-7 senior brings Power Four starting experience to a line sorting out its tackle rotation this fall.

athletes.name: Xander Ruggeroli
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He signed with Nebraska and played in one game as a true freshman in 2024 before transferring to Arizona State in January 2025 with four years of eligibility. The 6-6 junior remains in the mix for a rotational spot on the offensive line.

athletes.name: Plas Johnson

Listed at 6-4 and 215 pounds, the sophomore redshirted while converting to wide receiver and is working for a rotational role in a deep, transfer-heavy position group.

The 6-5, 265-pound senior joins an experienced tight end room and is competing for the complementary role behind Khamari Anderson.

The fifth-year lineman is listed at 6-5 and 315 pounds and is pushing for interior rotation snaps.

athletes.name: Zac Swanson

athletes.name: MyKeil Gardner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He has yet to build on that start, missing the 2025 season and then being ruled out for 2026 with a ruptured Achilles tendon. The senior from El Mirage is listed at 6-2 and 300 pounds.

athletes.name: Jeffrey Manns
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Sinei Tengei
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Blazen Lono-Wong
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lono-Wong came to Arizona State as a three-star defensive end rated the No. 7 prospect in Hawaii, then added weight and moved inside to tackle. He played 14 games as a reserve in 2024, recording six tackles including a sack against Texas State, and caught a 32-yard pass on a fake punt against Texas in the Peach Bowl playoff quarterfinal. The fifth-year lineman from Waimanalo is a depth piece up front.

athletes.name: Julian Hugo
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hugo signed with Arizona State out of Steele High in Cibolo, Texas, choosing the Sun Devils over more than 25 offers that included USC, Utah, TCU, Baylor and Colorado. As a junior he posted 83 tackles, 21 for loss, 9.5 sacks and 30 quarterback hurries and was named District 29-6A defensive player of the year. The freshman edge, listed at 6-4 and 275 pounds, is developing behind the veteran rotation.

athletes.name: C.J. Fite
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fite is Arizona State's returning starting defensive tackle and passed on the NFL to return for his senior season. He has appeared in 38 career games with 76 tackles for the Sun Devils.

athletes.name: Dash Fifita
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fifita is a freshman linebacker from Huntington Beach, California, who prepped at Santa Margarita Catholic. As a senior in 2025 he recorded 101 tackles, 15 tackles for loss and seven sacks while helping Santa Margarita win a CIF Open Division state championship, and he was named CIF Defensive Player of the Year and Trinity League Defensive MVP. He is the brother of Arizona quarterback Noah Fifita.

athletes.name: Wesley Yarbrough
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

A three-star prospect, he chose the Wildcats over offers that included Houston, Oklahoma State, Utah and TCU. He is competing for carries in a backfield reshaped by transfer additions in 2026.

athletes.name: Noah Fifita
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL valuation reported around $2M in 2026, up from $712K in 2024; no contract figure disclosed)
