He is the program's all-time passing touchdown leader and enters 2026 within roughly 800 yards of Nick Foles' school passing yardage record.

athletes.name: Daylen Austin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Austin is Arizona's projected starting free safety after transferring from Oregon, where he recorded 10 tackles, three pass breakups and an interception in 13 games in 2025. The former four-star recruit was rated the No. 20 cornerback in the 2026 transfer portal by 247Sports.

athletes.name: R.J. Mosley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mosley is a freshman wide receiver from Brentwood, California, and a product of Pittsburg High School. He caught 82 passes for 1,302 yards and 14 touchdowns as a senior in 2025, earning all-conference, all-region and all-district honors. Rated a four-star recruit, he was the highest rated signee in Arizona's 2026 class and chose the Wildcats over Stanford, Georgia, UCLA and Utah.

athletes.name: Kedrick Reescano
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reescano is Arizona's projected lead running back after rushing for 396 yards and a team-high nine touchdowns in 2025. The Ole Miss transfer is used heavily in short-yardage and goal-line situations.

athletes.name: Tre Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is Arizona's starting defensive end and a sixth-year senior returning from a shoulder injury that limited him to five games in 2025. The Mesa, Arizona, native has 60 career tackles, 8.5 tackles for loss and 4.5 sacks for the Wildcats.

athletes.name: DJ Jordan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jordan is a sophomore wide receiver from Watts, California, who came to Arizona after beginning his college career at USC. He played his high school football at Sierra Canyon, one of Southern California's most heavily recruited programs. Jordan arrives in Tucson with eligibility remaining and enters 2026 competing for rotation snaps in a receiver room that turned over significantly through the transfer portal.

athletes.name: Matai Tagoa'i
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tagoa'i is a sophomore safety from Las Vegas who came to Arizona after a freshman season at USC, where he played in five games and recorded four tackles and a forced fumble. He prepped at San Clemente and Faith Lutheran, posting 58 tackles and 12.5 tackles for loss as a senior, and was rated a four-star prospect by 247Sports.

athletes.name: Giovanni Richardson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Richardson is a starting slot receiver for Arizona who caught 21 passes for 299 yards and two touchdowns as a freshman in 2025. The Basha High School product is one of three returning Wildcats receivers who combined for 1,052 yards last season.

athletes.name: Taye Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is Arizona's leading returning tackler and a third-team All-Big 12 linebacker who posted 93 tackles in 2025. He has started 24 games for the Wildcats, including the last 18, and was Arizona's Big 12 Media Days representative on defense.

athletes.name: Cornelius Warren III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Warren is a redshirt freshman running back from Fort Worth, Texas, out of North Crowley High School. He made his college debut on Nov. 1 at Colorado and carried seven times for 32 yards before redshirting. In high school he rushed for 2,073 yards and 35 touchdowns and helped North Crowley finish 16-0 and win the 2024 Texas 6A Division I state championship.

athletes.name: Sawyer Anderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anderson is a redshirt freshman quarterback from Dallas who signed with Purdue in December 2024, then requested his release amid coaching changes there and committed to Arizona. A four-year starter at Parish Episcopal, he threw for more than 14,600 yards and 158 touchdowns, including 5,134 yards and 49 scores as a senior, and is recognized as the all-time leading passer in the Dallas-Fort Worth area. He remains a developmental option in Arizona's quarterback room.

athletes.name: Chase Kennedy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kennedy is Arizona's projected starting weak-side linebacker and a senior named to the Shriners Children's East-West Bowl watch list. He pairs with Taye Brown in a linebacker group Arizona's staff calls deeper than in 2025.

athletes.name: Jay'Vion Cole
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cole is Arizona's returning starting cornerback and tied for the team lead with four interceptions in 2025, adding 23 tackles and three tackles for loss. The former San Jose State and Texas transfer helped Arizona finish first nationally in team pass efficiency defense.

athletes.name: Tyrese Boss
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Boss arrived at Arizona from Wyoming, where he signed as a two-star recruit out of Chino Hills High School in 2024 and started all 12 games as a redshirt freshman, finishing with 39 tackles and five pass breakups. The Rialto, Calif., native chose the Wildcats over interest from Kentucky, TCU, NC State, Louisville and UCLA, and arrived with three years of eligibility remaining. Now a redshirt sophomore wearing No. 9, he is expected to compete for a starting cornerback job in Arizona's rebuilt secondary in 2026.

athletes.name: Oscar Rios
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rios is a freshman quarterback from Norwalk, California, who prepped at Downey High School. Across four varsity seasons he threw for 8,070 yards and 77 touchdowns and added 2,227 rushing yards, and he was named 2024 Gateway League MVP. A four-star prospect in the 247Sports Composite, he took part in the 2025 Elite 11 finals and the 2026 Polynesian Bowl.

athletes.name: Myron Robinson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Robinson is a sophomore linebacker from San Antonio who signed with Arizona in the 2025 class out of East Central High School, where he logged 78 tackles and two sacks as a two-way player and also rushed for 686 yards. Rated a four-star by 247Sports and the highest-ranked prospect in the Wildcats' class, he played in the Navy All-American Bowl and is pushing for rotation snaps in 2026.

athletes.name: Chris Hunter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hunter is a senior starting wide receiver for Arizona who caught 27 passes for 372 yards and two touchdowns in 2025. The New Orleans native is one of the last remaining members of Arizona's 2022 recruiting class and represented the program at Big 12 Media Days.

athletes.name: Jabari Mann
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mann is a redshirt sophomore linebacker from San Mateo, California, who originally signed with San Jose State before following coach Brent Brennan to Arizona in the 2024 class. At Junipero Serra he recorded 177 career tackles over 28 defensive games and was named 2023 West Catholic Athletic League Player of the Year. He enters 2026 as a rotation linebacker and special teams contributor.

athletes.name: Dwight Bootle
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bootle is a redshirt junior cornerback who came to Arizona after stops at Nebraska and Charlotte. A three-star recruit out of Miami Palmetto High School in the 2023 class, he appeared in six games over two seasons at Nebraska before transferring to Charlotte in 2025, where he played 12 games with six starts and recorded 38 tackles, half a tackle for loss and a pass breakup. The Miami, Fla., native arrived with two years of eligibility and projects into the cornerback rotation for 2026. His older brother DiCaprio Bootle played in the NFL.

athletes.name: Tré Spivey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Spivey is Arizona's projected No. 1 receiver after catching 23 passes for 381 yards and seven touchdowns in his first season following a transfer from Kansas State. The 6-foot-4 Chandler, Arizona, native is projected by Arizona's coaching staff as a future NFL draft pick.

athletes.name: Cam Chapa
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chapa is a junior safety from Aurora, Colorado, who joined Arizona from Northern Colorado as one of seven defensive backs the Wildcats added through the transfer portal ahead of 2026. He prepped at Eaglecrest High School in Aurora. Chapa is competing for a rotation role in a secondary that was rebuilt almost entirely this offseason.

athletes.name: Hannibal Navies II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Navies is a freshman safety from Buford, Georgia, out of Grayson High School, where he helped the program win a Georgia 6A state championship as a junior in 2024. He was rated a three-star prospect by 247Sports and chose Arizona over offers from Michigan State, Kansas State and Arizona State. His father, Hannibal Navies, played nine seasons in the NFL.

athletes.name: Cole Rusk
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rusk is Arizona's projected starting tight end after transferring from Illinois, where he caught 19 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown in 2025. The 6-foot-5 senior was rated among the top 10 tight ends in the 2026 transfer portal.

athletes.name: Mason Bray
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bray is a redshirt sophomore quarterback from Phoenix who played at Saguaro High School. He completed 230 of 323 passes for 2,897 yards and 26 touchdowns in high school, throwing 25 of those scores as a senior in 2023, and led Saguaro to the 2023 Arizona state championship with a 40-20 win over Red Mountain. He also played basketball.

athletes.name: Malcolm Hartzog
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hartzog is Arizona's projected starting strong safety after transferring from Nebraska. He is expected to be a central piece of a secondary replacing longtime starters Treydan Stukes, Dalton Johnson and Genesis Smith.

athletes.name: Luke Haugo
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Haugo is a redshirt freshman quarterback from Scottsdale, Arizona, who prepped at Higley High School. He threw for 3,639 yards and 38 touchdowns across 22 varsity games and was rated a three-star prospect and the No. 12 quarterback in the state. He committed to Arizona in June 2024 over offers from Oregon, Utah and Arizona State, and also played basketball.

athletes.name: Everett Roussaw Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Roussaw is Arizona's projected starting strong-side linebacker and a senior on the Shriners Children's East-West Bowl watch list. The Atlanta native is part of a veteran linebacker corps returning for 2026.

athletes.name: Isaiah Mizell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mizell is a sophomore wide receiver from Orlando who signed with Arizona in the 2025 class out of Boone High School, where he caught 104 passes for 2,371 yards and 40 touchdowns over three varsity seasons. He chose the Wildcats over Kansas State, Syracuse, Georgia Tech and hometown UCF. A track sprinter as well, his speed points toward a vertical role as he competes for rotation snaps.

athletes.name: Lee Molette III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Molette is a senior safety from Nashville who transferred to Arizona from UConn, one of seven newcomers the Wildcats brought into their defensive secondary through the portal ahead of 2026. He played his high school football at Ravenwood High School in Tennessee. Molette adds veteran depth to a safety group that turned over heavily and is competing for a rotation role.

athletes.name: Carter Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a redshirt freshman linebacker from Coto De Caza, California, out of Crean Lutheran High School. He made 375 tackles with 16.5 tackles for loss over three varsity seasons and also played tight end, catching 35 passes for 283 yards and 10 touchdowns. A three-star recruit and team captain, he committed to Arizona in October 2024.

athletes.name: Brandon Phelps
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Phelps is a redshirt sophomore wide receiver from Gilbert, Arizona, who came to the Wildcats out of American Leadership Academy-Gilbert North. He saw his first extended action in 2025, catching six passes for 82 yards and a touchdown. Listed at 6-foot-3, he gives Arizona size on the perimeter and enters 2026 competing for rotation snaps in a receiver room reshaped by portal additions.

athletes.name: Michael Salgado-Medina
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Salgado-Medina is Arizona's returning placekicker after converting 16 of 31 field goal attempts in 2025. The junior hit several long and game-winning kicks and retained the staff's backing through an inconsistent season.

athletes.name: Dajon Hinton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hinton is a redshirt freshman safety from San Diego who prepped at Hamilton High School in Chandler, Arizona. He played both ways as a sophomore, catching 24 passes for 457 yards and three touchdowns while adding 25 tackles and an interception. Rated a three-star recruit, he committed to Arizona in June 2024. His father, David Hinton, also played for the Wildcats.

athletes.name: Johno Price
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Price is a redshirt junior safety from East Palo Alto, California, who reached Arizona by way of College of San Mateo after prepping at Menlo-Atherton High School. He is one of several junior college products on the Wildcats' defense. Listed at 6-foot-2 and 180 pounds, Price enters 2026 competing for a rotation role in the secondary along with special teams work.

athletes.name: Gavin Hunter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hunter signed with Arizona in the 2023 class as a three-star safety out of Mililani High School and has grown into a rotation piece for the Wildcats. The Ewa Beach, Hawai'i, native spent his early years largely on special teams before starting the first two games of 2025 against Hawaii and Weber State, recording his first career interception against his hometown Rainbow Warriors. Now a redshirt junior wearing No. 23, he is positioned as an experienced option in Arizona's safety group for 2026.

athletes.name: Quincy Craig
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Craig is Arizona's No. 2 running back and primary kick returner after rushing for 364 yards and two touchdowns and adding 14 catches for 114 yards and a score in 2025. The Mater Dei product forms a two-back rotation with Kedrick Reescano.

athletes.name: Kingston Spivey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Spivey is a freshman cornerback for the Arizona Wildcats from Chandler, Arizona, where he played at Hamilton High School. He is listed at 5-8 and 176 pounds and wears No. 24. Arizona's official roster does not carry a biography for him.

athletes.name: Zuri Watson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Watson is a sophomore cornerback from Saint Petersburg, Florida, who transferred to Arizona from Howard, joining six other defensive backs the Wildcats added through the portal ahead of 2026. He prepped at Northside Christian School in Saint Petersburg. Watson enters fall camp competing for rotation snaps in a cornerback group that was almost completely rebuilt this offseason.

athletes.name: Coleman Patmon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Patmon is a sophomore from Del Valle, Texas, who signed with Arizona in the 2025 class as a three-star defensive back out of Del Valle High School. He recorded 63 tackles, three interceptions and three pass breakups over 20 varsity games and chose the Wildcats over TCU, Oklahoma State, Arkansas and Kansas State. Arizona now lists him at linebacker, where he is competing for rotation snaps.

athletes.name: Keytrin Harris
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Harris is a freshman defensive lineman from Las Vegas who finished his prep career at Arizona Compass Prep and helped the program win a 2025 Arizona Division 3 state championship. As a senior he recorded 42 tackles, 19 tackles for loss and 13 sacks. Rated a three-star prospect, he chose Arizona over offers from Missouri, UCLA, Georgia and Texas A&M.

athletes.name: Swayde Griffin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Griffin is a redshirt freshman cornerback from Lago Vista, Texas, who played defensive back, receiver and safety at Lago Vista High School. He rushed for 482 yards and 10 touchdowns and added 19 catches for 342 yards in high school, and helped Lago Vista reach the 2024 Texas state championship game. He committed to Arizona in June 2024.

athletes.name: Anthony Wilhite
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilhite is a redshirt senior running back from Tucson who played at Salpointe Catholic High School, where he rushed for 2,058 yards and 24 touchdowns over three varsity seasons and averaged 112.5 yards per game as a senior in 2021. He spent a redshirt season at Ottawa University in 2023 before joining the Wildcats.

athletes.name: Jaden Parker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Parker is a freshman linebacker for the Arizona Wildcats from Anna, Texas, where he played at Anna High School. He is listed at 6-1 and 245 pounds and wears No. 29. The official roster does not include a biography for him.

athletes.name: Xaier Hiler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hiler is a freshman cornerback from Denton, Texas, who prepped at Ryan High School. Rated a four-star prospect and a top 200 national recruit by 247Sports, he was a key defensive contributor on a team that went 12-1 and reached the 2025 Texas 5A Division I quarterfinals, a year after a run to the state semifinals. He chose Arizona over Oregon State.

athletes.name: Aiden Miller
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Miller is a redshirt sophomore cornerback for the Arizona Wildcats from Phoenix, where he attended Brophy College Preparatory. He is listed at 5-11 and 190 pounds and wears No. 31. The official roster does not carry a biography for him.

athletes.name: Nela Taliauli
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taliauli is a redshirt sophomore linebacker from Puna, Hawai'i, who played football and basketball at Iolani High School and was named a defensive player of the year in 2023. He appeared in four games in 2024, working mostly on special teams against BYU, Colorado, West Virginia and UCF. His full first name is Taniela.

athletes.name: Kason Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is a redshirt freshman safety from Big Lake, Texas, out of Reagan County High School, where he played quarterback and defensive back and also competed in basketball. He threw for 5,110 yards and 54 touchdowns over four varsity seasons and added 31 tackles on defense as a senior. A three-star recruit, he committed to Arizona in December 2024.

athletes.name: James Pike
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pike is a freshman safety for the Arizona Wildcats from Phoenix, where he played at Brophy College Preparatory. He is listed at 5-11 and 190 pounds and wears No. 34. Arizona's official roster does not include a biography for him.

athletes.name: Carter Schwartz
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Schwartz is a junior punter who transferred to Arizona from Louisville, his hometown school, after prepping at Trinity High School in Louisville. He is one of two punters the Wildcats brought in ahead of 2026, along with Australian freshman Chase Ridley, and the two are competing for the starting job in fall camp. Schwartz is listed at 6-foot-3 and 232 pounds.

athletes.name: Quinn Olson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Olson is a redshirt sophomore safety from Sioux City, Iowa, who played quarterback and safety at Bishop Heelan Catholic High School and also played varsity basketball. He threw for 2,264 yards and 35 touchdowns in 2023 while helping Bishop Heelan to an 11-2 record and a second place finish in Class 3A, and was named large school player of the year.

athletes.name: Dominic Hanger
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hanger is a redshirt junior linebacker who walked on at Arizona out of Chandler High School in his hometown of Chandler. He worked his way into game action in 2025, seeing defensive snaps in the Wildcats' November win over Baylor. Listed at 6-foot-1 and 223 pounds, he enters 2026 as a depth linebacker and special teams contributor.

athletes.name: Chase Ridley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ridley is a freshman punter from Perth, Australia, who came to college football through ProKick Australia after growing up around Australian rules football. His father Paul played professionally in Melbourne and Perth. Ridley originally signed with West Virginia before being granted a release and joining Arizona, where he stepped into punting duties as a true freshman. Coaches have pointed to kicks of 50 and 60 yards with hang times in the 4.2 to 4.6 second range. He wears No. 37 for the Wildcats.

athletes.name: Kevin Moorer Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moorer is a junior defensive lineman from Mobile, Alabama, who arrived at Arizona through the junior college ranks at Hutchinson Community College in Kansas after prepping at Leflore High School. Listed at 6-foot-3 and 285 pounds, he adds interior size to a defensive front coached by Joe Salave'a and is competing for rotation snaps ahead of the 2026 season.

athletes.name: Jacob Buggie
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Buggie is a redshirt sophomore linebacker for the Arizona Wildcats from Phoenix, where he attended Brophy College Preparatory. He is listed at 6-2 and 214 pounds and wears No. 39. The official roster does not carry a biography for him.

athletes.name: Lachlan Teissier
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Teissier is a freshman tight end from Perth, Western Australia, and a 2025 graduate of Scotch College Perth. Listed at 6-8 and 250 pounds, he arrived at Arizona through the university's rugby program and was later added to the football roster after the staff saw him practicing nearby. He is studying business.

athletes.name: Brandon Craddock
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Craddock is a redshirt senior linebacker from Phoenix who played at Sandra Day O'Connor High School, where he was a three-year varsity starter with 350 career tackles, including 119 with 16 tackles for loss as a senior, and was named 2021 Southwest Region player of the year. He has earned Pac-12 and Big 12 fall academic honor roll recognition.

athletes.name: Julian Savaiinaea
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Savaiinaea is a redshirt junior defensive lineman from Tafuna, American Samoa, who signed with Arizona in the 2023 class out of St. Louis High School in Honolulu. He was rated the No. 16 edge rusher nationally by 247Sports and the No. 10 prospect from Hawaii. His older brother Jonah played offensive line for the Wildcats and was a second-round pick of the Miami Dolphins in 2025.

athletes.name: Dominic Lolesio
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lolesio signed with Arizona in December 2022 as a three-star recruit out of Long Beach Poly High School, where he totaled 89 tackles and 26 stops for loss with 8.5 sacks across his junior and senior seasons. The Long Beach, Calif., native is listed at 6-4 and 253 pounds and enters 2026 as a redshirt junior edge rusher wearing No. 42. Arizona defensive coordinator Danny Gonzales called him the most improved player on the team following spring practice, pointing him toward a larger role in the pass rush.

athletes.name: Drew Nicolson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nicolson is a redshirt junior long snapper from Tempe who came to Arizona after previous stops at Akron and Arkansas State. He prepped at Corona del Sol High School in Tempe. Nicolson is among the specialists the Wildcats added ahead of the 2026 season and is competing for the long snapping job in fall camp.

athletes.name: Antwan Roberts
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Roberts is a redshirt senior running back from Nashville who transferred to Arizona from Marshall, reuniting with Wildcats offensive coordinator Seth Doege. He rushed for 512 yards and four touchdowns on 90 carries in 12 games in 2025. A former Wisconsin signee who spent a season at Independence Community College, he prepped at Pope John Paul II High School and adds experienced depth to the backfield.

athletes.name: Prince Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a freshman defensive lineman from Las Vegas who prepped at Bishop Gorman and won three Nevada state championships. As a senior in 2025 he recorded 91 tackles, 44 tackles for loss and 13 sacks and was named Nevada MaxPreps player of the year. Rated a four-star recruit by ESPN, he played in the Under Armour All-America Game.

athletes.name: Victory Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a redshirt junior edge rusher from San Diego who joined Arizona after previous stops at Colorado and Cal Poly. He prepped at Cathedral Catholic High School in San Diego. Listed at 6-foot-3 and 246 pounds on Arizona's defensive line, Johnson is competing for rotation snaps off the edge in 2026.

athletes.name: Cooper Blomstrom
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Blomstrom is an edge rusher who transferred to Arizona from Georgetown with 16 sacks and 27 tackles for loss over three seasons. He is projected to lead the Wildcats in sacks in 2026.

athletes.name: Kaisi Lafitaga
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lafitaga is a freshman defensive lineman from Pago Pago, American Samoa, who signed with Arizona in the 2026 class out of Tafuna High School. A three-star prospect who also held offers from Hawaii and Alcorn State, he played mostly offensive line in high school and was recruited to the defensive front by Wildcats line coach Joe Salave'a. He is listed at 6-foot-2 and 301 pounds.

athletes.name: Christian Madoski
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Madoski is a redshirt junior defensive lineman from Glendale, Arizona, who played at Mountain Ridge High School. He appeared in 28 varsity games over three seasons and recorded 121 tackles, 13 tackles for loss, 10 sacks and 16 hurries. He redshirted in 2023 and did not appear in a game in 2024.

athletes.name: Keona Peat
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Peat is a redshirt junior offensive lineman from Chandler who transferred to Arizona from Arizona State in May 2025 after appearing in two games for the Sun Devils. He prepped at Corona del Sol High School and is a brother of NFL lineman Andrus Peat and Arizona basketball forward Koa Peat. Listed as a center by the Sun Devils, he gives the Wildcats an interior option in 2026.

athletes.name: Nathan Hale
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hale is a redshirt junior offensive lineman from Orange, California, who transferred to Arizona from San Jose State. He prepped at Orange Lutheran High School and is listed at 6-foot-4 and 307 pounds. Hale is one of several additions to an Arizona offensive line that turned over substantially ahead of 2026, and he is competing for a rotation role up front.

athletes.name: Leviticus Su'a
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Su'a is a redshirt junior linebacker from Moreno Valley, California, who signed with Arizona in the 2023 class as a four-star prospect out of Mater Dei High School. He announced his commitment during the Polynesian Bowl, choosing the Wildcats over Stanford and UCLA. Su'a was named Trinity League Most Valuable Player as a senior and finished at Mater Dei with 134 tackles, 4.5 sacks and three interceptions.

athletes.name: Sione Tohi
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tohi is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from San Francisco who played at Mater Dei High School, helping the program finish 12-0 and win the CIF Southern Section championship with a 31-24 win over St. John Bosco. A three-star recruit, he committed to Arizona in June 2024 over offers from Alabama, LSU and Oklahoma.

athletes.name: Zach Henning
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Henning transferred to Arizona from Washington, where he signed as a three-star prospect in 2023 and spent three seasons. The Centennial, Colo., native played all 13 games for the Huskies last year, starting four at center, and logged 333 offensive snaps without allowing a sack. A Grandview High School product and two-time first-team All-Centennial League selection, he is listed at 6-5 and 310 pounds. With Ka'ena Decambra graduating, Henning is in line to start at center for the Wildcats in 2026 as a redshirt junior with two years of eligibility.

athletes.name: Rhino Tapa'atoutai
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tapa'atoutai came to Arizona as a three-star recruit out of Bishop Alemany High School in Mission Hills, Calif., and has played several spots along the offensive line. He started at right tackle in 2024 before a season-ending knee injury after six games, then played swing tackle across the full 2025 season. The Wildcats have since moved the redshirt junior inside to guard, where coaches consider him a better fit. He is listed at 6-5 and 316 pounds and picked up the nickname Rhino playing youth football in West Valley City, Utah.

athletes.name: Javian Goo
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Goo is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Kapolei, Hawai'i, who played tackle and guard at Kapolei High School and helped the program to a top seven finish in the state in each of his three varsity seasons. A three-star recruit, he committed to Arizona in June 2024 over offers from Oregon State, Hawai'i and Air Force.

athletes.name: Alexander Doost
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Doost is Arizona's returning starting right guard and has started 22 consecutive games for the Wildcats. The Phoenix native played all but 20 offensive snaps in 2025 and allowed just one sack.

athletes.name: Jaxon Griffin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Griffin is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Mesa, Arizona, out of Red Mountain High School, where he also played tight end and defensive end and competed in basketball. He made 15 tackles with three sacks on defense and helped Red Mountain to a 7-4 record. Rated a three-star recruit and the No. 22 lineman in the state, he committed in December 2024.

athletes.name: Malachi Joyner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Joyner is a freshman offensive lineman for the Arizona Wildcats from Gilbert, Arizona, where he played at Williams Field High School. He is listed at 6-3 and 290 pounds and wears No. 68. The official roster does not carry a biography for him.

athletes.name: Tristan Bounds
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bounds is Arizona's starting right tackle and returns for a sixth season after a medical redshirt for a broken ankle suffered in November 2025. The 6-foot-8 Michigan transfer started eight games in 2025 and posted a 72.3 PFF offensive grade.

athletes.name: Louis Akpa
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Akpa is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from South San Francisco who signed with Arizona in the 2025 class out of Junipero Serra High School. A three-star tackle ranked No. 77 nationally at his position, he committed to the Wildcats over Boise State, California, Minnesota and Oregon State. Listed at 6-foot-6 and 299 pounds, he is developing as a depth option on the offensive line.

athletes.name: Matthew Lado
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lado signed with Arizona in the 2024 class as a three-star offensive lineman out of Apollo High School in Glendale, Ariz., committing in June 2023 alongside prep teammates Adam Mohammed and Michael Watkins. Listed at 6-6 and 308 pounds, he stepped into the lineup as a young player when injuries opened snaps at tackle and has since worked into the right side of the Wildcats' front. Now a redshirt sophomore wearing No. 73, he projects as a starting option at right tackle for Arizona in 2026.

athletes.name: Justin Morales
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Morales is a freshman offensive lineman from El Paso, Texas, who was a three-year starter at Franklin High School and helped the program to a combined 20-12 record over three seasons, including 8-3 as a senior. He is rated a four-star recruit and the No. 311 player nationally for 2026 by 247Sports, and he also competed in the shot put.

athletes.name: Khalil Sanogo
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sanogo is a freshman offensive lineman from Dallas who played both tackle and guard at Mansfield Legacy High School. He was a 2025 Whataburger Dave Campbell's Super Team nominee and is rated a three-star prospect by 247Sports. He chose Arizona over offers from Michigan State, California, Houston, Kansas State and UNLV.

athletes.name: Jake Griffin

He started all 14 games at center for the Hilltoppers in 2024 and was named to Phil Steele's postseason fourth team All Conference USA, and he appeared in four games for the Wildcats in 2025. He played at Dixie Heights High School.

athletes.name: Gradey Anthony

athletes.name: Ellis McAdoo

athletes.blurb: McAdoo is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman at Louisville, listed at 6-6 and 295 pounds. He is from Elmhurst, Illinois, and the Cardinals list St. Thomas More as his previous school.

athletes.name: Johnnie Brown III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is a redshirt senior offensive lineman from Atlanta listed at 6-foot-3 and 310 pounds. He played high school football at Parkview, began his career as a walk-on at Miami, then transferred to Georgia Southern, where he started all 13 games in 2025 with 12 of those at left tackle and earned third-team All-Sun Belt honors. Brown committed to Louisville as one of the Cardinals' portal additions this cycle and can play guard or tackle in Jeff Brohm's line.

athletes.name: James Glover-Tyson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Glover-Tyson is a redshirt junior offensive lineman on the Louisville roster, listed at 6-6 and 325 pounds. He is a Louisville native and played his high school football at DeSales.

athletes.name: Anwar O'neal
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He was an honorable mention All-CAA pick in 2024 with 11 starts and started 12 more games in 2025. O'neal has two years of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Cason Henry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Henry is a redshirt senior offensive lineman from Atlanta who joined Louisville after four seasons at South Carolina. The 6-foot-6, 300-pound Walton High School product was a three-star recruit in the 2022 class and started all 13 games at right tackle for the Gamecocks in 2024 before a shoulder issue ended his 2025 season early. He chose the Cardinals over Ole Miss in the portal and has one season of eligibility left as a projected starting tackle.

athletes.name: Sam Secrest
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sam Secrest is a redshirt senior offensive lineman from Greenwood, Indiana, who joined Louisville after three seasons at Houston. He played 27 snaps at center in the 2025 season opener against Eastern Kentucky and previously logged 15 snaps at center against Murray State for the Cougars in 2023. He played at Roncalli High School in Indianapolis and was rated the No. 104 interior offensive lineman nationally.

athletes.name: Ben Corhei
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Corhei is a freshman offensive lineman at Louisville, listed at 6-5 and 300 pounds. He is from Naples, Florida, and the Cardinals list Lowndes as the last school he attended.

athletes.name: Jarvis Strickland
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jarvis Strickland is a freshman offensive lineman from Chattanooga, Tennessee, who was the highest rated recruit in Louisville's signing class. Rated a four star prospect by Rivals and the top ranked player in Kentucky, he anchored a Paducah Tilghman line that went 15 and 0 and won the Class 4A state championship, and he earned first team all state honors from the Courier Journal in 2024. He picked Louisville over Michigan and Tennessee.

athletes.name: Cameron Gorin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cameron Gorin is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Fishers, Indiana, who made his collegiate debut against Eastern Kentucky in 2025 and logged 27 snaps at left tackle. A three star recruit out of Hamilton Southeastern High School, he chose Louisville over Boston College and Purdue. He enters 2026 as a developmental tackle competing for a spot in the Cardinals rotation up front.

athletes.name: Tyler Folmar
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Folmar is an offensive lineman from the Pensacola area who signed with Louisville in the 2025 class and wore No. 76. He made his college debut against Eastern Kentucky in 2025. A three-star recruit out of Tate High School, he recorded 16 pancake blocks in eight games as a senior, helped Tate to a 7-4 record and was named a Pensacola News Journal Super Senior. He does not appear on Louisville's current published roster.

athletes.name: Ryan Manis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A redshirt sophomore long snapper out of Wilmington, N.C., Manis is on the Louisville Cardinals' 2026 football roster and is competing for a spot in the Cardinals' two-deep this fall.

athletes.name: Charlie Edgeworth
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Brody Foley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Foley is Louisville's projected starting tight end after transferring from Tulsa, where he earned first-team All-AAC honors with 37 catches for 528 yards and seven touchdowns in 2025. Athlon named him a third-team preseason All-ACC tight end.

athletes.name: Jakob Dixon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He made five starts among seven games played in 2024 and caught 14 passes for 133 yards, scoring his first collegiate touchdown against West Georgia, then added a reception in 2025. He was an all state selection as a senior at Pleasure Ridge Park High School.

athletes.name: Montavin Quisenberry

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Justyn Reid is a senior tight end from Newnan, Georgia, who transferred to Louisville from Tulane. He caught 17 passes for 200 yards and three touchdowns in 2025 and logged 225 run blocking snaps for an offense that averaged 170.2 rushing yards per game. He spent his first two college seasons at Southern Miss, where he recorded seven receptions for 145 yards. He played at Newnan High School.

athletes.name: Jackson Voth
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson Voth is a junior receiver from Cheney, Kansas, who arrives at Louisville from Drake after redshirting at Kansas State. He earned All Pioneer Football League honors in 2025 while leading the Bulldogs with 51 receptions for 600 yards and five touchdowns, including 10 catches in an FCS playoff loss at South Dakota. He was the 2023 Kansas 3A Offensive Player of the Year at Cheney High School.

athletes.name: Dylan Mesman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He was a four star prospect on Rivals, which ranked him the No. 24 tight end nationally, and he caught 50 passes for 631 yards and seven touchdowns as a senior at Saline High School before choosing Louisville over Kentucky and Auburn.

athletes.name: Jaleel Skinner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Skinner is Louisville's No. 2 tight end and a former four-star Miami transfer who caught 21 passes for 204 yards and two touchdowns with six starts in 2025.

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gavin Waddell is a freshman receiver from Raleigh, North Carolina, who signed with Louisville out of Rolesville High School as a consensus three star prospect. He finished his prep career with 200 receptions for a school record 3,100 yards and 21 touchdowns, averaging 15.3 yards per catch, and he caught 67 passes for 1,025 yards as a senior. He chose the Cardinals over Miami, East Carolina and James Madison.

athletes.name: Hamilton Atkins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

Listed at 6-foot-3 and 300 pounds, he was a three-star prospect at Christopher Columbus High School, where he recorded 84 tackles and 10 sacks in 2022 and was named Miami-Dade Defensive Player of the Year. Russell appeared in five games for the Hurricanes and arrives in Louisville with three years of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Keon Webb
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He played 11 games for the Broncbusters, recording 37 tackles, six tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks, and he picked the Cardinals over Auburn, LSU and Florida among others. He attended Sumner High School and began his college career at North Carolina A&T.

athletes.name: Garth White
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The 6-foot-3, 205-pound Oaks Christian product began at Ventura College, spent time at USC without appearing in a game, then handled placekicking for the Rams in 2025, converting 14 of 18 field goals and 54 of 56 extra points. He made both of his attempts from beyond 50 yards, hitting a 52-yarder against Elon and a 54-yarder against Bryant, and projects as Louisville's starter.

athletes.name: Bailey Abercrombie
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bailey Abercrombie is a redshirt freshman defensive lineman from Birmingham, Alabama, who signed with Louisville out of Moody High School after transferring there from Gardendale. He recorded 79 tackles, 27 tackles for loss and 11 sacks in 12 games while helping Moody go 11 and 2 and reach the Class 5A state final, including nine tackles in the state semifinals. He committed two days after receiving his Louisville offer.

athletes.name: Dillon Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He recorded 56 tackles, eight sacks and three interceptions as a junior and helped lead Ryle to the Kentucky state title game. He is working for rotational snaps along the Cardinals defensive front in 2026.

athletes.name: Joshua Donald
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

Jordan High School product, he opened his career at Southern before moving to Appalachian State, where he posted 32 tackles, 5.5 tackles for loss and three sacks in 2024, then spent a season at Houston. Donald committed to the Cardinals in January 2026 through the transfer portal and projects as an interior run stopper for Jeff Brohm's defense.

athletes.name: Bode Shoaps

athletes.name: Tommy Ziesmer

athletes.blurb: Tommy Ziesmer is a redshirt junior defensive lineman from Danville, Kentucky, who has appeared in six college games, recording two tackles in 2024 and a sack against Akron in 2023. A three star recruit ranked the No. 7 player in Kentucky, he posted 83 tackles, nine sacks and 20 tackles for loss as a Boyle County senior and scored the winning touchdown in the 2022 Class 4A state championship game.

athletes.name: Maurice Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He debuted as a freshman against Austin Peay in 2024 and also played in the Sun Bowl. A consensus three star prospect at Dougherty High School, he was rated the No. 62 edge rusher nationally by the 247Sports Composite and chose Louisville over Ole Miss.

athletes.name: Sam Dawson

Listed at 6-foot-4 and 270 pounds, he played his senior season at Corbin High School and was a highly rated recruit who flipped his commitment from Michigan to the Wildcats. Smith played all 12 games in 2025 and recorded 27 tackles, 5.0 tackles for loss, a sack and a forced fumble as a rotational lineman.

athletes.name: Antonio Harris
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Isaiah Neal
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

Listed at 6-foot-4 and 240 pounds, he has played sparingly in his first two Pitt seasons and enters 2026 pushing for a regular spot in the Panthers' edge rotation.

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 NIL Valuation reported at ~$3M as of July 2026, up from ~$2.1M earlier in 2026; no deal figure officially disclosed)

He added 19 catches for 254 yards and three touchdowns for the Panthers in 2024. Listed at 5-11 and 170 pounds out of Clearwater High School, he wears No. 10.

athletes.name: Alex Sanford Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A senior linebacker from Oxford, Mississippi, Sanford arrived at Pitt in January 2026 after stops at Arkansas and Purdue. He appeared in all 12 games with nine starts for the Boilermakers in 2025, recording 46 tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss, a pass breakup and a fumble recovery. Pitt is his third program, and he brings Power Four starting experience to a linebacker room competing to replace departed production in the middle of Pat Narduzzi's defense.

athletes.name: Holden Geriner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Geriner is a redshirt senior quarterback from Savannah, Georgia who joined Pitt from Texas State, where he appeared in three games in 2025. He began his career at Auburn after signing out of Benedictine Military School as a four-star prospect in the 2022 class. Listed at 6-3 and 215 pounds and wearing No. 11, he arrived largely as a veteran presence behind Pitt's younger quarterbacks.

The Daytona Beach, Florida native posted back-to-back 1,000-yard receiving seasons at Spruce Creek, including 66 catches for 1,005 yards and 16 touchdowns as a senior.

athletes.name: Cole Woodson

He wears No. 17.

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

His 2025 breakout brought 774 receiving yards, seven scores and Second Team All-Southern Conference honors, production that made him a natural fit in offensive coordinator Kade Bell's system, which Bell first ran at Western Carolina.

athletes.name: Rashan Murray
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

There he was a Division II All-American selection and first-team All-PSAC, finishing with 78 tackles, four interceptions and 25 pass breakups in 32 games. A product of Obama Academy in the City League, he is listed at 6-2 and 185 pounds and wears No. 18.

Listed at 6-1 and 180 pounds in No. 22, he is competing for a larger role in the Panthers' cornerback rotation in 2026.

athletes.name: Cameron Lindsey
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

In 2025 he appeared in every game with five starts, catching three passes for 38 yards with a career-long 18-yard reception against Duke, and the staff has worked to expand his receiving role entering 2026.

athletes.name: Braheem Long Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Long is Syracuse's returning starting free safety after recording 53 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, 2.0 sacks, an interception and two pass breakups in 2025.

athletes.name: Demetres Samuel Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Samuel is Syracuse's returning starting cornerback and one of the youngest players in college football, having won the job as a 17-year-old true freshman in 2025. He posted 45 tackles, 2.0 tackles for loss, a team-best nine pass breakups and an interception while also taking snaps at receiver.

athletes.name: Umari Hatcher
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hatcher is a sixth-year Syracuse wide receiver with career totals of 52 catches for 797 yards and seven touchdowns. He missed the 2025 season with an injury and briefly entered the transfer portal in December 2025 before returning to the Orange's outside receiver rotation.

athletes.name: Zyian Moultrie-Goddard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He played in every game in 2025 and owns 15 career tackles with one tackle for loss. A three-star prospect by the 247Sports Composite out of Iona Prep, he was the New York City league's AAA defensive player of the year in 2021 and a three-time team captain.

athletes.name: Davien Kerr
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kerr, a junior from Bloomfield, Conn., has started in Syracuse's secondary since late in his freshman season, when he started the final four games of 2024 and finished with 14 tackles and an interception. He won the starting nickelback job in August 2025 and recorded interceptions against Pittsburgh, SMU and Clemson. His twin brother Davion is also on the Orange roster, and Kerr projects as a returning starter in the defensive backfield in 2026.

athletes.name: Davion Kerr
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kerr is a sophomore running back from Bloomfield, Connecticut who played in seven games as a freshman in 2025, handling five carries, two receptions for 13 yards and six kickoff returns for 119 yards. He appeared in all 11 games in 2025 with two starts, his first coming against Louisville, and finished with 12 tackles and a quarterback hurry. He played all 13 games in 2024 and blocked a field goal against Oregon State, and added 2.0 tackles for loss and a sack in 2023. Out of Santa Margarita Catholic he was ranked the No. 32 player in California by 247Sports after a junior season with 15.0 tackles for loss and 7.0 sacks.

athletes.name: Michael-Anthony Okwura
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Michael-Anthony Okwura is a redshirt sophomore defensive lineman for California. He is from Houston and played his high school football at St. Thomas High School. The Cal roster lists him at 6-3 and 310 pounds for the 2026 season.

athletes.name: Nate Burrell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Burrell is a projected starting defensive lineman for Cal with 21 career starts, having missed the 2025 season with an injury. He withdrew from the transfer portal in January 2026 to return to Berkeley for a final year.

athletes.name: Ashun Shepphard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Shepphard is a redshirt senior defensive lineman from Brandon, Mississippi, who transferred to Cal from Mississippi State. He played at Brandon High School before beginning his college career in the SEC. Listed at 6-foot-3 and 295 pounds, he is one of several defensive front transfers in Cal's 2026 class and competes for rotational snaps inside during his final season.

athletes.name: Andrew Powdrell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Powdrell is a senior safety from The Woodlands, Texas who arrived at West Virginia from UNLV, where he recorded 63 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss and five pass breakups in 2025. He began his career at Montana State, playing all 16 games with 14 starts during the Bobcats' 2024 run to the FCS championship game and earning Second Team All-Big Sky honors. He is expected to start in WVU's overhauled secondary, with the versatility to handle both safety and the nickel spot.

athletes.name: Josh Sapp
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sapp is West Virginia's projected starting tight end after transferring from Clemson, where he played 267 snaps and caught 11 passes for 150 yards in 2025. He has one year of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Amari Latimer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Latimer arrives at West Virginia as a freshman running back from Sandy Creek High in Fairburn, Georgia, where he finished as the school's all-time leading rusher with 5,595 yards and 78 touchdowns. He ran for 2,409 yards and 44 scores as a senior while Sandy Creek went 15-0 for the Class 3A state title, earning USA Today All-USA Southeast second-team offense honors. His brother Geimere joined WVU as a cornerback transfer. He competes for backfield rotation snaps in 2026.

athletes.name: Geimere Latimer II
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Latimer is West Virginia's projected starting nickel after transferring from Wisconsin, where he started all 12 games at cornerback in 2025 and made 28 tackles with a forced fumble. He previously played for Rich Rodriguez at Jacksonville State, where he had three interceptions in 2024.

athletes.name: DJ Epps
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Epps is West Virginia's projected starting slot receiver after a breakout 2025 at Troy, where he caught 47 passes for 512 yards and five touchdowns. He posted a season-high 148 yards and two scores against Texas State.

athletes.name: Michael Hawkins Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (College Front Office NIL valuation model ~$1.67M, reported as the highest figure on WVU's roster; not a disclosed contract)
athletes.blurb: Hawkins is West Virginia's projected starting quarterback after transferring from Oklahoma, where he completed 91 of 147 passes for 950 yards with six touchdowns and two interceptions across two seasons. He started as a true freshman for the Sooners in 2024.

athletes.name: Matt Sieg
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sieg is a freshman safety from Fort Cherry High in McDonald, Pennsylvania, where he played quarterback and free safety. He was named the Maxwell Football Club's National High School Player of the Year and set WPIAL career records for total offense with 12,592 yards and 139 touchdowns, finishing second in WPIAL history with 7,941 rushing yards. His teams went 49-7 and won two WPIAL championships. He moves to safety full time in 2026.

athletes.name: Da'Mun Allen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Allen is a junior cornerback from Sanford, Florida, who transferred to West Virginia from Hutchinson Community College after a season at Northeastern Oklahoma A&M. He was a 2025 NJCAA Division I All-American honorable mention and an All-Kansas junior college first-team cornerback, collecting 28 tackles, four interceptions and two pass breakups in 11 games as Hutchinson went 11-1 and reached the national championship game. He adds experience to the cornerback rotation.

athletes.name: Cam Cook
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cook is West Virginia's starting running back and a Walter Camp preseason second-team All-American after leading FBS with 1,659 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns at Jacksonville State in 2025. He was the Conference USA Player of the Year and is WVU's lone skill-position pick on the 2026 preseason All-Big 12 team.

athletes.name: Jaden Bray
athletes.source: Estimate (College Front Office NIL valuation model ~$638K, fourth on WVU's roster; not a disclosed contract)
athletes.blurb: Bray is West Virginia's veteran outside receiver and the leader of the wideout room, though season-ending injuries limited him to seven catches for 95 yards in two games in 2025. He transferred from Oklahoma State, where he totaled 48 receptions for 686 yards and four touchdowns.

athletes.name: Max Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is a redshirt senior quarterback from Lincoln Christian in Tulsa, Oklahoma, who came to West Virginia after stops at Charlotte and Florida. He appeared against Utah and Texas Tech in 2025, rushing four times for 23 yards. At Charlotte in 2024 he completed 43 of 93 passes for 561 yards and three touchdowns, and he threw for 192 yards at Florida in 2023. He is a veteran depth option behind the starter.

athletes.name: Da'Mare Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a redshirt sophomore safety from Sylvia, North Carolina, listed at 6-1 and 201 pounds. He played high school football at Smokey Mountain and reached West Virginia by way of junior college, spending time at Coffeyville Community College before joining the Mountaineers. He wears No. 6 and adds depth in the secondary.

athletes.name: Wyatt Walker Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Walker Brown is a freshman quarterback from Los Angeles who came to West Virginia out of Notre Dame High School. He wears No. 7 and is listed at 6-3 and 200 pounds on the Mountaineers roster.

athletes.name: Chams Diagne
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Diagne is a 6-foot-4 redshirt senior cornerback from Atlanta who transferred to West Virginia from Georgia State in January 2026 with one season of eligibility left. He began as a walk-on with the Panthers in 2022, spent a year at Independence Community College, then returned to Georgia State, where he played 11 games in 2025 with 25 tackles, three pass breakups and an interception against Ole Miss. His unusual length makes him a candidate to win an outside corner job in Morgantown.

athletes.name: Jyron Hughley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hughley is a freshman quarterback from Belle Glade, Florida, who played at Cardinal Newman High School. Listed at 6-2 and 199 pounds, he wears No. 8 and is part of West Virginia's quarterback group.

athletes.name: Kamari Wilson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilson is West Virginia's projected starting free safety after a career year at Memphis in 2025 with 84 tackles, 6.5 tackles for loss, two interceptions and two forced fumbles. The former top-20 national recruit also played at Florida and Arizona State.

athletes.name: Cam Ball
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ball is a redshirt senior tight end from Gonzaga College High who grew up in Glenn Dale, Maryland. He has played 35 career games with 10 starts across stops at Buffalo and Mississippi State. He appeared in 12 games with four starts for the Bulldogs in 2025 and caught eight passes for 82 yards at Buffalo in 2023. At six foot seven he gives West Virginia a large blocking presence in the tight end rotation.

athletes.name: Taron Francis
athletes.source: Estimate (College Front Office NIL valuation model $550K, seventh on WVU's roster; not a disclosed contract)
athletes.blurb: Francis is a West Virginia outside receiver who transferred from LSU, where he redshirted in 2025 after appearing in five games without a catch. The former four-star recruit out of New Orleans' Edna Karr drew consistent praise in spring practice.

athletes.name: Vincent Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Smith is a freshman cornerback listed at 6-1 and 215 pounds. His hometown is Orlando, Florida, and the West Virginia roster lists his last school as Sandburg in Illinois. He wears No. 11 for the Mountaineers.

athletes.name: Jacob Bradford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bradford is a redshirt freshman safety from Catholic High in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, who transferred to West Virginia from LSU. He redshirted in 2025 while appearing in five games for the Tigers, including the Texas Bowl. A consensus four-star recruit, he was a two-time Class 5A all-state first-team pick and ranked among the top safeties in Louisiana. He competes for a rotation role in the secondary in 2026.

athletes.name: Cam Torbor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Torbor is a redshirt freshman linebacker from Hoover, Alabama, who played at Hoover High School. He is listed at 6-3 and 239 pounds and wears No. 13 in West Virginia's linebacker room.

athletes.name: Kedrick Triplett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Triplett is a redshirt sophomore wide receiver from Florence, Alabama, who joined West Virginia from Pearl River Community College. He caught 25 passes for 399 yards and five touchdowns in nine games in 2025 and was named the Mississippi juco conference offensive player of the week after a 158-yard, two-touchdown game against Itawamba. On3 rated him the No. 21 junior college prospect. He works in the slot receiver rotation.

athletes.name: Keon Hutchins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hutchins is a junior wide receiver from Union, Mississippi, who arrived from Northwest Mississippi Community College after a freshman year at Hutchinson. He caught 35 passes for 667 yards and six touchdowns in 2025, ranking sixth nationally in junior college receiving yards and earning NJCAA Division I All-American honorable mention as Northwest went 10-1 and won the conference title. His best game brought 216 yards and three scores.

athletes.name: Tyler Stolsky
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stolsky is a redshirt senior linebacker from Portage Central in Portage, Michigan, who comes to West Virginia from Florida Atlantic after three seasons at Minnesota. He started all 12 games for the Owls in 2025 and posted five games of 12 or more tackles, including 13 at Navy. He started twice for Minnesota in 2023 and recorded 26 tackles with a sack. He brings starting experience to the linebacker rotation.

athletes.name: Ben Cutter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cutter is West Virginia's senior Mike linebacker and a four-year Mountaineer who has recorded more than 95 career tackles, including a 56-tackle, six-tackle-for-loss season with two sacks. He is one of the defense's returning leaders in 2026.

athletes.name: Scotty Fox Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (College Front Office NIL valuation model ~$333K; not a disclosed contract)
athletes.blurb: Fox is West Virginia's returning quarterback and set the program's true-freshman single-season passing record in 2025, throwing for 1,276 yards and seven touchdowns in nine games with five starts. He added 201 rushing yards and three scores and is competing with Michael Hawkins Jr. for the job.

athletes.name: Isaiah Patterson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Patterson is a redshirt sophomore linebacker from Yelm High in Tacoma, Washington, who enrolled at West Virginia in the spring of 2026 after transferring from UNLV. He appeared in all 13 games for the Rebels in 2025, finishing with 40 tackles, a tackle for loss and an assisted sack, with a season-high seven against Boise State in the Mountain West title game. He spent 2024 at UCLA on special teams.

athletes.name: Miles Khatri
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Khatri is a freshman defensive back from Montgomery, Alabama, listed by West Virginia at nickel and safety. He played at Pike Road High School, stands 6-0 and 208 pounds, and wears No. 17 for the Mountaineers.

athletes.name: Prince Strachan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Strachan is West Virginia's projected starting X receiver, a 6-foot-5 target who transferred from USC after two seasons at Boise State that produced 37 catches for 578 yards and three touchdowns. The Bahamas native caught one pass for 25 yards in a single 2025 appearance for the Trojans.

athletes.name: Zeke Durham-Campbell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Durham-Campbell, a redshirt senior from Atlanta, joined West Virginia in January 2026 for his final college season after stops at Lenoir-Rhyne, Louisiana Tech and Coastal Carolina. He broke out for the Chanticleers in 2025 with 42 tackles, eight tackles for loss, 5.5 sacks and two forced fumbles, making him the most productive pass rusher WVU added in the transfer cycle. He projects as a starting defensive end for the Mountaineers.

athletes.name: John Johnson III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a freshman quarterback from New Orleans who played at Edna Karr High School. Listed at 5-10 and 178 pounds, he wears No. 18 and is one of several young quarterbacks on the West Virginia roster.

athletes.name: Nick Taylor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taylor is a junior cornerback from Atlanta who transferred to West Virginia from Appalachian State, where he played seven games as a true freshman and finished the 2024 season with 10 tackles and a pass breakup across 147 snaps. His cornerbacks coach with the Mountaineers, Rod West, held the same role at Appalachian State when Taylor played there. Listed at 6-foot-1 and 215 pounds, he brings uncommon size to the position and has three years of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Martavious Boswell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Boswell is a junior running back from Fort Worth, Texas, who transferred to West Virginia from Copiah-Lincoln Community College after a freshman year at Blinn. He rushed for 1,109 yards and 13 touchdowns on 130 carries in 10 games in 2025, topping 100 yards seven times, and was named NJCAA Region 23 player of the year and a second-team junior college All-American. He adds depth to a crowded backfield.

athletes.name: Keyshawn Robinson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Robinson is a junior cornerback from Jefferson High in Ranson, West Virginia, one of the few in-state players on the roster. He played 12 games in 2025 and finished with 13 tackles, including nine solo stops, after appearing in 11 games as a freshman mostly on special teams. He was a two-time Class AAA all-state selection and a state track champion. He remains a rotation corner and special teams contributor.

athletes.name: Jaire Rawlison
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rawlison is a redshirt sophomore cornerback from Bishop McDevitt who lists York, Pennsylvania, as his hometown. He transferred to West Virginia from Kent State, where he played all 12 games and started 11 in 2025, recording 54 tackles with 34 solo stops, two tackles for loss and six pass breakups. He added 21 tackles in four appearances the year before. That starting experience puts him in the cornerback rotation.

athletes.name: Chris Talley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Talley is a freshman running back from Memphis, Tennessee, who came to West Virginia out of Whitehaven High School. He is listed at 5-11 and 194 pounds and wears No. 22 for the Mountaineers.

athletes.name: Emory Snyder
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Snyder is a freshman defensive back from Bixby, Oklahoma, listed at nickel and safety. He played at Bixby High School, stands 6-3 and 211 pounds, and wears No. 23 on the West Virginia roster.

athletes.name: Malachi Thompson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thompson is a freshman wide receiver from Charleston, West Virginia, who played at Nitro High School. One of the in-state additions to the roster, he is listed at 6-4 and 198 pounds and wears No. 23.

athletes.name: Landon Drumm
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Drumm is a freshman wide receiver listed at 6-3 and 187 pounds. His hometown is Anchorage, Alaska, and his last school was Arapahoe in Centennial, Colorado. He wears No. 24 for West Virginia.

athletes.name: Rayshawn Reynolds Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reynolds is a redshirt junior cornerback from Montgomery, Alabama, who came to West Virginia from Hutchinson Community College along with teammates Da'Mun Allen and Darius Wiley. Over 18 junior college games he totaled 29 tackles, two interceptions and 13 pass breakups. In 2025 he had 20 tackles and 11 pass breakups for a Hutchinson defense that allowed 10.7 points per game and reached the national championship game. He is six foot three.

athletes.name: Jayden Ballard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ballard is a freshman defensive back from Chesterfield, Virginia, who played at Manchester High School. West Virginia lists him at nickel and safety at 6-0 and 187 pounds, and he wears No. 25.

athletes.name: Armoni Weaver-Bomar
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Weaver-Bomar is a redshirt freshman wide receiver from Westside High in Spartanburg, South Carolina. He redshirted in 2025 while seeing action against Utah and Texas Tech, playing a season-high 12 offensive snaps against the Red Raiders. As a senior he caught 26 passes for 541 yards and seven touchdowns in nine games and made the South Carolina AAAA all-state team. He was a consensus three-star recruit and competes for receiver snaps.

athletes.name: Makhi Boone
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Boone is a freshman cornerback from Elyria, Ohio, who played at St. Edward High School. He is listed at 6-0 and 168 pounds and wears No. 26 in the Mountaineers secondary.

athletes.name: Andre Devine
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Devine is a redshirt sophomore running back from North Fort Myers, Florida, where he played at North Fort Myers High School. He came to West Virginia after time at Jacksonville State. Listed at 5-7 and 160 pounds, he wears No. 26 and adds depth in the Mountaineers backfield.

athletes.name: ChaMarryus Bomar
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bomar is a redshirt freshman cornerback from Duncan, South Carolina, who played at Westside High School. He is listed at 5-10 and 194 pounds and wears No. 27 for West Virginia.

athletes.name: Lawrence Autry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Autry is a freshman running back from Olive Branch, Mississippi, who played at Collierville High School in Tennessee. Listed at 5-10 and 221 pounds, he wears No. 28 and gives West Virginia a heavier back.

athletes.name: Rickey Giles
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Giles is a freshman safety from Oak Cliff, Texas, who played at South Oak Cliff High School. He is listed at 5-10 and 194 pounds and wears No. 28 for West Virginia.

athletes.name: Kameron Reddic
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Reddic is a junior safety from Hightower High in Houston who enrolled at West Virginia in January 2026 after transferring from Stephen F. Austin. He played all 14 games in 2025 and started the final 13, finishing with 42 tackles, two tackles for loss, an interception and four pass breakups as the Lumberjacks went 11-3 and reached the FCS quarterfinals. He gives the safety group experienced depth.

athletes.name: Antoine Sharp Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Sharp is a freshman linebacker from West Palm Beach, Florida, who played at Palm Beach Central High School. Listed at 6-0 and 225 pounds, he wears No. 30 on the West Virginia roster.

athletes.name: Shane Cornali
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cornali is a redshirt freshman safety from Hickory, Pennsylvania, who played at Fort Cherry High School. He joined West Virginia after beginning his college career at Wheeling. Listed at 6-2 and 195 pounds, he wears No. 31 and is part of the Mountaineers safety group.

athletes.name: Simaj Hill
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hill is a freshman cornerback from Philadelphia who played at St. Joseph's Prep. He is listed at 6-0 and 184 pounds and wears No. 32 among West Virginia's young defensive backs.

athletes.name: Brad Mossor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mossor is a freshman wide receiver from Princeton, West Virginia, who played at Princeton High School. An in-state addition listed at 5-11 and 187 pounds, he wears No. 32 for the Mountaineers.

athletes.name: Kayden Luke
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Luke is West Virginia's fullback and the media's preseason All-Big 12 pick at the position after transferring from Arizona, where he was the lead blocker for a 1,981-yard rushing attack in 2025. He is one of only two Mountaineers on the preseason all-conference team.

athletes.name: Ashton Woods
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Woods is a West Virginia linebacker entering his second season with the program after transferring from North Carolina, and he is projected into the starting lineup in 2026. He was a four-star recruit out of Walton High School in Georgia.

athletes.name: Darius Morant
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Morant is a redshirt sophomore running back from St. Anthony's High in Hempstead, New York, who enrolled at West Virginia in January 2026 after two years at Temple, where he joined as a walk-on and earned offensive practice player of the week honors. He rushed for 924 yards and 10 touchdowns as a high school senior and added 579 yards at Milford Academy. He is a depth back in 2026.

athletes.name: Tim Roberson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Roberson is a redshirt junior safety from Valdosta, Georgia, where he played at Valdosta High School. He reached West Virginia through the junior college route after playing at Iowa Western Community College. Listed at 5-11 and 182 pounds, he wears No. 34 in the Mountaineers secondary.

athletes.name: Cameron Dwyer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dwyer is a freshman linebacker from Delray Beach, Florida. The West Virginia roster lists his previous schools as Palm Beach Central and Rise Preparatory Academy. He is listed at 6-1 and 216 pounds and wears No. 35.

athletes.name: Maliek Hawkins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hawkins is a redshirt freshman defensive back from Emerson High in Dallas who transferred to West Virginia from Oklahoma, where he redshirted in 2025 and appeared against Kent State. He was rated a four-star recruit by Rivals and had 28 tackles, an interception and four pass breakups as a high school senior. His brother Michael Jr. is a West Virginia quarterback. He competes for rotation snaps in the secondary.

athletes.name: Macguire Moss
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moss is a redshirt senior long snapper from Batavia, Illinois entering the 2026 season as the veteran of West Virginia's specialist group, snapping on punts, field goals and extra points. He handled snapping duties at Batavia High School while also playing guard. Off the field he completed his bachelor's degree in business in December 2025 and is now pursuing his MBA at West Virginia.

athletes.name: Jayden Bell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bell is a redshirt junior cornerback from St. Thomas Aquinas in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. He redshirted in 2023 and has not seen game action in three seasons at West Virginia, leaving him as a developmental piece in the cornerback room.
