In high school he was part of three Class 7A championship teams that went a combined 36-2. His father is a former WVU receiver and a current NFL back judge.

athletes.name: Peter Notaro
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Notaro is a redshirt freshman kicker from Wexford, Pennsylvania, who kicked at North Allegheny High School. He came to West Virginia after beginning his college career at Alabama. Listed at 5-11 and 192 pounds, he wears No. 39 and is part of the Mountaineers specialist group.

athletes.name: Jason Hall Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hall is a redshirt junior linebacker from Fall River, Massachusetts, who prepped at Suffield Academy in Connecticut and enrolled at West Virginia in January 2026 after three seasons at Villanova. He played 14 games in 2025 and finished with 40 tackles, 28 of them solo, plus 3.5 sacks, 4.5 tackles for loss and a forced fumble. He appeared in all 14 games in 2024 and adds linebacker depth.

athletes.name: Noah Tishendorf
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tishendorf is a freshman defensive lineman from Sherwood, Oregon, who played at Lakeridge High School. Listed at 6-3 and 254 pounds, he wears No. 41 and is one of the few West Virginia players from the Pacific Northwest.

athletes.name: Alex Adebayo
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Adebayo is a redshirt sophomore safety from Howard High in Elkridge, Maryland, who enrolled at West Virginia in January 2026 after transferring from Delaware. He redshirted in 2024 and made one appearance against UTEP in 2025. A three-year letterwinner and senior captain in high school, he recorded 52 tackles, two interceptions and 12 pass breakups in 2023. He is a developmental safety competing for special teams work.

athletes.name: Jack Cassidy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cassidy, a 6-foot-6 redshirt senior kicker from Derry, Ireland, signed with West Virginia in January 2026 after a season at Western Kentucky, where he produced touchbacks on 51 of 72 kickoffs and made all three of his field goal attempts, connecting from 55, 53 and 41 yards. He began his career at the University of Ulster before moving to American college football, and Kohl's Kicking rated him a five-star transfer. He has one season of eligibility as he competes for the Mountaineers' kicking job.

athletes.name: KJ Henson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Henson is a redshirt junior defensive lineman from Annapolis, Maryland who signed with West Virginia out of Hutchinson Community College in Kansas, flipping from a Minnesota commitment on signing day. He earned First Team All-Jayhawk Conference honors in 2025 with 38 tackles, eight tackles for loss and five sacks, and On3 ranked him the No. 15 overall junior college prospect and the No. 4 JUCO defensive lineman. He has two years of eligibility to bolster the Mountaineers' interior front.

athletes.name: Malachi Hood
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hood is a redshirt senior linebacker from Plainfield, Illinois who transferred to West Virginia from Illinois in January 2026 with two years of eligibility remaining. A three-star recruit in the 2022 class, he became a starter for the Illini in 2025 and registered 44 tackles, a sack and a forced fumble. An Academic All-Big Ten selection who has already earned his undergraduate degree, he is expected to hold a significant role in WVU's rebuilt linebacker corps.

athletes.name: Xavier Anderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anderson is a freshman tight end from Martinsburg, West Virginia, who played at Spring Mills High School. An in-state prospect listed at 6-6 and 215 pounds, he wears No. 46 for the Mountaineers.

athletes.name: Wilnerson Telemaque
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Telemaque is a redshirt freshman defensive lineman from Miami Gardens, Florida, who played at Miami Northwestern. He is listed at 6-6 and 265 pounds, giving West Virginia length on the defensive front, and wears No. 47.

athletes.name: Troy Fischer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fischer is a redshirt senior linebacker from Mineral, Virginia, who played at Louisa High School. He arrived at West Virginia after playing at Christopher Newport, a Division III program in Virginia. Listed at 5-11 and 222 pounds, he wears No. 48 for the Mountaineers.

athletes.name: Nate Flower
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Flower is a redshirt junior kicker from Fairmont, West Virginia, who kicked at Fairmont Senior High School. An in-state addition listed at 6-2 and 188 pounds, he wears No. 48 and is part of the Mountaineers kicking group.

athletes.name: Carter Kessler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kessler is a freshman defensive lineman from Shelby, Ohio, who played at Shelby High School. He is listed at 6-2 and 250 pounds and wears No. 49 on the West Virginia roster.

athletes.name: Carter Zuliani
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zuliani is a redshirt freshman tight end from Bridgeport, West Virginia, who played at Bridgeport High School. Listed at 6-6 and 261 pounds, he wears No. 49 for the Mountaineers.

athletes.name: Harper Holloman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Holloman is a junior edge rusher from Atlanta who joined West Virginia from Western Kentucky, where he led all Conference USA edge defenders with 41 pressures in 2025 while totaling 39 tackles, 5.5 tackles for loss, two sacks and an interception in 13 games. A cousin of former NFL All-Pro defensive tackle Albert Haynesworth, he arrived in Morgantown with two years of eligibility and factors immediately into the Mountaineers' pass rush rotation.

athletes.name: Taylor Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is a redshirt freshman defensive lineman from Upper Marlboro, Maryland, who played at Wise High School. Listed at 6-3 and 290 pounds, he wears No. 51 and adds interior depth for West Virginia.

athletes.name: Raymond Kovalesky
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kovalesky is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Wheeling, West Virginia, who played at The Linsly School. An in-state addition listed at 6-3 and 278 pounds, he wears No. 51 for the Mountaineers.

athletes.name: Nick Krahe
athletes.source: Estimate (College Front Office NIL valuation model $800K, second on WVU's roster; not a disclosed contract)
athletes.blurb: Krahe is a returning West Virginia offensive lineman who started all 12 games at tackle in 2025 and is projected to move inside to left guard in 2026. He was an Academic All-Big 12 first-team selection.

athletes.name: Corey McIntyre Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McIntyre is a redshirt junior defensive lineman from Treasure Coast High in Port St. Lucie, Florida, and one of the few Mountaineers who has never transferred. He played nine games in 2025 and finished with 13 tackles, a half sack and 1.5 tackles for loss across 184 snaps. He made the Academic All-Big 12 rookie team in 2023. His father played for West Virginia from 1998 to 2001 and spent 11 years in the NFL.

athletes.name: Kaden Seller
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Seller is a redshirt sophomore long snapper from Hilliard, Ohio, who played at Darby High School. He is listed at 6-2 and 257 pounds and wears No. 53 as part of West Virginia's specialist group.

athletes.name: Amare Grayson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Grayson, a junior guard from Stockbridge, Georgia, transferred to West Virginia from Jacksonville State after earning First Team All-Conference USA honors in 2025. In Morgantown he reunited with offensive line coach Rick Trickett, his position coach with the Gamecocks, and through the offseason he has held down a starting guard spot in WVU's projected lineup. He has two years of eligibility remaining.

athletes.name: Yendor Mack
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mack is a freshman defensive lineman from Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, who played at Susquehanna Township High School. Listed at 6-3 and 288 pounds, he wears No. 55 and adds size to the West Virginia defensive front.

athletes.name: Aidan Woods
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Woods is a freshman offensive lineman from Abingdon, Virginia, who played at Abingdon High School. Listed at 6-5 and 310 pounds, he wears No. 55 for West Virginia.

athletes.name: Lamarcus Dillard
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dillard is a freshman offensive lineman from Glenarden, Maryland, who played at St. Frances Academy. He is listed at 6-1 and 297 pounds and wears No. 56 for West Virginia.

athletes.name: Josh Aisosa
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Aisosa is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman listed from McKinney, Texas, who transferred to West Virginia from Oklahoma and redshirted there in 2024. He played 12 games in 2025, seeing 82 snaps including 42 on offense, with a season-high 25 against Robert Morris. In high school he was named his conference and district offensive lineman of the year in 2023. At 320 pounds he provides interior line depth.

athletes.name: Jonas Muya
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Muya is a freshman offensive lineman from Fort Wayne, Indiana, who played at Bishop Luers. Listed at 6-7 and 293 pounds, he wears No. 60 on the West Virginia roster.

athletes.name: Gabe Ryan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ryan is a senior defensive lineman from Keyser, West Virginia, who played at Keyser High School. An in-state addition listed at 6-2 and 276 pounds, he wears No. 60 for the Mountaineers.

athletes.name: Trevor Bigelow
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bigelow is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman from Fairmont, West Virginia, who played at Fairmont Senior High School. Listed at 6-3 and 273 pounds, he wears No. 61 and is one of several in-state players on the roster.

athletes.name: Rhett Morris
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Morris is a freshman offensive lineman from Ridgewood, New Jersey, who played at Don Bosco Prep. He is listed at 6-2 and 308 pounds and wears No. 64 on the West Virginia roster.

athletes.name: Malik Agbo
athletes.source: Estimate (College Front Office NIL valuation model ~$716K, third on WVU's roster; not a disclosed contract)
athletes.blurb: Agbo is a West Virginia offensive tackle in his second season in Morgantown after transferring from Texas, appearing in all 12 games in 2025 with a start against TCU. He is competing at right tackle in 2026.

athletes.name: Landen Livingston
athletes.source: Estimate (College Front Office NIL valuation model ~$633K, fifth on WVU's roster; not a disclosed contract)
athletes.blurb: Livingston is a fifth-year West Virginia interior offensive lineman who played in 11 games with starting time in 2025 and competes at center in 2026.

athletes.name: Camden Goforth
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Goforth is a freshman offensive lineman from Athens, Tennessee, who played at McMinn County High School. Listed at 6-4 and 306 pounds, he wears No. 68 and is part of West Virginia's young offensive line group.

athletes.name: Devin Vass
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Vass is a redshirt junior offensive lineman from Lakeland High in Bartow, Florida, who came to West Virginia from Kansas State. He appeared in 11 games in 2025 and started the final seven, and he did not allow a sack or take a penalty across more than 200 snaps for an offense that averaged 171.3 rushing yards per game. At six foot six he is a candidate for the tackle rotation.

athletes.name: Cam Griffin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Griffin is a senior offensive lineman from Selma, Alabama, who prepped at Pinson Valley and followed Rich Rodriguez to West Virginia from Jacksonville State. He started all 13 games in 2025 at five different line positions and earned All-Conference USA first-team honors while the Gamecocks averaged 246.7 rushing yards per game, fifth nationally. He has made 36 career appearances and logged 1,231 snaps, giving West Virginia versatile interior depth.

athletes.name: Jaylen Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a junior defensive lineman from White Station High in Memphis who transferred to West Virginia after two seasons at Northwest Mississippi Community College. He was named the Mississippi juco conference North Division defensive player of the year in 2025 and earned NJCAA Division I All-American honorable mention, finishing with 18 tackles and 2.5 tackles for loss as Northwest went 10-1. At 316 pounds he competes for interior snaps.

athletes.name: Andreas Hunter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hunter is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman from Glen Dale, West Virginia, who played at John Marshall High School. An in-state player listed at 6-4 and 300 pounds, he wears No. 73 for the Mountaineers.

athletes.name: Kevin Brown
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brown is the headliner of West Virginia's 2026 signing class, a four-star offensive tackle ranked No. 49 nationally and the No. 5 tackle in the class who flipped from Penn State. He is projected to compete for the starting right tackle job as a true freshman.

athletes.name: Deshawn Woods
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Woods is a redshirt senior offensive lineman from Omaha Central in Omaha, Nebraska, who arrived at West Virginia from Butler Community College after two years at Wyoming. He earned All-Kansas junior college honorable mention in 2025 while helping Butler go 7-3 and rank ninth nationally, blocking for the country's leading junior college rusher. He played in the Under Armour All-America game in high school and adds tackle depth.

athletes.name: Wes King
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: King is West Virginia's projected starting center after transferring from Wyoming, where he was an experienced interior starter.

athletes.name: Carsten Casady
athletes.source: Estimate (College Front Office NIL valuation model $560K, sixth on WVU's roster; not a disclosed contract)
athletes.blurb: Casady is West Virginia's projected starting left tackle after transferring from Connecticut, where he was a multi-year starter.

athletes.name: John Neider
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Neider is a West Virginia receiver who transferred from Connecticut after his most productive season in 2025, catching 27 passes for 422 yards and two touchdowns with five starts.

athletes.name: Kade Bush
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bush is a freshman tight end from Chanhassen, Minnesota, who played at Chanhassen High School. Listed at 6-4 and 226 pounds, he wears No. 81 for West Virginia.

athletes.name: Bryan Hansen
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hansen is a redshirt senior punter from Colleyville, Texas who transferred to West Virginia after a standout 2025 season at Colorado State, where he averaged 47.9 yards on 57 punts with 13 downed inside the 20 and 23 traveling 50 yards or more. The 6-foot-3 specialist has also handled kickoffs in his career, totaling 55 touchbacks on 106 attempts, and he arrived in Morgantown in January 2026 as a leading candidate for the Mountaineers' punting job.

athletes.name: Ryan Ward
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ward is a junior tight end from Rutherford, New Jersey, who played his high school ball at Rutherford High and transferred to West Virginia from North Carolina. He appeared in 10 games in 2025, playing 321 snaps and catching six passes for 41 yards and a touchdown against Colorado, while earning Academic All-Big 12 first-team honors. He is expected to remain a rotation tight end and heavy special teams contributor.

athletes.name: Robert Oliver
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Oliver is a freshman wide receiver listed at 6-2 and 185 pounds. His hometown is Tucson, Arizona, and the West Virginia roster lists his last school as Niceville in Florida. He wears No. 85 for the Mountaineers.

athletes.name: Cyrus Traugh
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Traugh is a redshirt junior wide receiver from Parkersburg, West Virginia, who played at Parkersburg South High School. He returned to his home state after beginning his college career at Youngstown State. Listed at 5-11 and 193 pounds, he wears No. 86 for the Mountaineers.

athletes.name: Greg Wilfred
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilfred is a freshman wide receiver from New Orleans who played at Edna Karr High School, the same program as teammate John Johnson III. Listed at 5-9 and 175 pounds, he wears No. 87 for West Virginia.

athletes.name: Sam Hamilton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hamilton is a freshman tight end from Cincinnati who played at Archbishop Moeller High School. He is listed at 6-4 and 246 pounds and wears No. 88 on the West Virginia roster.

athletes.name: Charlie Hanafin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hanafin is a freshman wide receiver from Burlington, Massachusetts, who played at Dexter Southfield School. Listed at 6-0 and 186 pounds, he wears No. 89 for West Virginia.

athletes.name: Darius Wiley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wiley is a redshirt sophomore defensive lineman from North Hardin High in Elizabethtown, Kentucky, who transferred to West Virginia from Hutchinson Community College. He was a 2025 NJCAA Division I first-team All-American and the Kansas junior college conference defensive player of the year, leading the nation with 20 tackles for loss and ranking third with nine sacks while adding 57 tackles. He is a disruptive addition to the line rotation.

athletes.name: Emerson Joy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Joy is a junior defensive lineman from Calgary, Alberta, who played at St. Mary's. The West Virginia roster lists Alberta College as his previous school, making him one of the roster's international arrivals. He is listed at 6-6 and 253 pounds, giving the Mountaineers unusual length on the defensive front, and wears No. 92.

athletes.name: Nate Gabriel
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gabriel is a junior defensive lineman from Auburndale, Florida entering his third season in Morgantown despite being only 19 years old, having enrolled at West Virginia at age 17. He has appeared in 23 career games, saw the field as a true freshman and recorded 13 tackles in 2025, and he is expected to push into a starting role on the interior of the Mountaineers' defensive line in 2026.

athletes.name: Cam Mallory
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Mallory is a freshman defensive lineman from Moody, Alabama, who played at Moody High School. Listed at 6-0 and 298 pounds, he wears No. 94 and adds interior weight to the West Virginia defensive line.

athletes.name: Tobi Haastrup
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Haastrup is a redshirt freshman edge rusher from London, England, who transferred to West Virginia from Oregon after playing three games and recording a tackle against Oklahoma State in 2025. He did not play football until his senior year at Mayde Creek in Texas, then posted 48 tackles, 20 tackles for loss and nine sacks in that lone season. ESPN and Rivals rated him a four-star recruit. He competes for edge snaps.

athletes.name: Will LeBlanc
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: LeBlanc is a redshirt sophomore defensive lineman from Klein Oak High in Houston who enrolled at West Virginia in the spring of 2026 after transferring from UT Permian Basin. He appeared in all 14 games there in 2025 and started 13, recording his first career sack against Sul Ross State and recovering a fumble at Western New Mexico. At six foot five and 288 pounds he adds developmental depth up front.

athletes.name: Brandon Caesar
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Caesar is a redshirt freshman defensive lineman from Cleveland, Ohio, who played at Cleveland Heights High School. He is listed at 6-4 and 257 pounds and wears No. 98 for West Virginia.

athletes.name: David Afogho
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Afogho is a redshirt junior edge rusher from Boston who transferred to West Virginia from Bowling Green in January 2026 with two years of eligibility. The 6-foot-3, 245-pounder recorded 37 tackles, four tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks in 12 games in 2025 while generating 27 pressures, a total that would have led West Virginia's defense last season. As one of only four edge rushers on the WVU roster, he is positioned for significant snaps as a starter or rotation piece.

athletes.name: Jeremiah Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: A redshirt junior edge rusher out of Spanish Springs, Nev., Johnson is competing for a spot in the Mountaineers' two-deep this fall after transferring from Butte Community College.

athletes.name: Max Anderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anderson is a redshirt freshman quarterback for the West Virginia Mountaineers out of Martinsburg, W.Va.

athletes.name: Samaj Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones arrived at Cincinnati as the highest rated signee in the Bearcats' 2024 recruiting class, a four star quarterback who chose the program over Oklahoma, Penn State and West Virginia. At St. Joseph's Prep in Philadelphia, Pa., he led the Hawks to back to back PIAA 6A championships. He redshirted in 2024 and appeared in two games in 2025. The junior wears No. 5 and enters 2026 in a quarterback room reshaped by transfer additions.

athletes.name: Zion Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a sophomore running back from Newton High School in Covington, Georgia, where he rushed for 5,130 career yards and 44 touchdowns, including 2,185 yards and 16 scores as a senior at 11.3 yards per carry. A consensus three-star recruit rated among the top 40 running backs nationally by ESPN and On3, he signed with Cincinnati in February 2024. He redshirted in 2025 while appearing in four games and carrying 22 times for 106 yards and a touchdown.

athletes.name: Patrick Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Williams is a sophomore cornerback from Greenville, South Carolina, who came to Cincinnati from Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School and wears No. 13 at 5-10 and 175 pounds. A consensus three-star recruit, he made 143 tackles with 10 interceptions in his prep career and earned NCISAA Division I first-team all-state honors as a senior. Williams redshirted in 2025, appearing against Northwestern State and starting the Liberty Bowl, where he played 35 snaps.

athletes.name: Zay "Gravy" Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a junior cornerback from Clinton, South Carolina, who signed with Cincinnati as a consensus three star prospect and a 2023 Shrine Bowl of the Carolinas selection, choosing the Bearcats over Virginia and Liberty. He played in four games as a freshman in 2024 while retaining a year of eligibility, making his debut against Houston with one tackle and also appearing against Iowa State, Kansas State and TCU. He did not see game action in 2025.

athletes.name: Will Kocher
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Will Kocher is a senior quarterback on the Cincinnati roster, wearing No. 15 at 6-foot-2 and 205 pounds. He is from Kings Mills, Ohio, and played his high school football nearby at Kings High School.

athletes.name: Jaylon White-McClain
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: White-McClain joined Cincinnati from Old Dominion, where he spent his earlier college seasons after leaving Kempsville High School in Virginia Beach, Va. The fifth year edge rusher is one of the bigger players in the Bearcats' pass rush group at 6-4 and 265 pounds and wears No. 16. He arrived as part of the 22 player transfer class that enrolled at Cincinnati in January 2026 and adds experience to a defensive front that turned over heavily.

athletes.name: Giyahni Kontosis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Giyahni Kontosis is a sophomore wide receiver for Cincinnati, listed at 6-foot-1 and 205 pounds in No. 18. He comes from Beltsville, Maryland, and played his high school football at Riverdale Baptist.

athletes.name: Marqavious Saboor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Saboor is a junior outside linebacker at Cincinnati from Decatur, Georgia, where he played at Kell High School. He appeared in 12 games in 2025 and made his first career start in the AutoZone Liberty Bowl, finishing with seven tackles and a pass breakup. As a freshman he played all 12 games on defense and special teams, recording eight tackles and a fumble recovery. A three star recruit, he chose Cincinnati over Arkansas and Boston College.

athletes.name: Brian Simms III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Simms is a senior edge rusher from Baltimore who came to Cincinnati from St. Frances Academy and wears No. 17. Listed at 6-3 and 240 pounds, he appeared in 12 games in 2025 and posted 34 tackles, three tackles for loss and two sacks, with a career-high six stops against Baylor. He played all 12 games the prior season with 17 tackles and was a consensus three-star recruit.

athletes.name: CJ Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones is a sophomore safety at Cincinnati, listed at 5-9 and 195 pounds in No. 19. He appeared in six games as a freshman in 2025 and made four tackles, three of them solo stops in the AutoZone Liberty Bowl. A consensus three-star recruit out of Bolingbrook High School near Chicago, he was rated the nation's No. 72 cornerback and among the top 15 prospects in Illinois by On3 before choosing the Bearcats over Boston College.

athletes.name: CJ Crite
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Crite is a sophomore safety from Lincoln County, Georgia, who signed with Cincinnati out of Lincoln County High School, where he finished his career with 447 tackles. A three-star recruit, he chose the Bearcats over Appalachian State, South Florida and Western Kentucky. Crite played three games in 2025 while preserving a redshirt and made five tackles, four of them solo, including two stops at TCU and one in the Liberty Bowl.

athletes.name: Terrell Holcomb
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Holcomb signed with Cincinnati in the 2025 recruiting class as a three star prospect out of Gahanna Lincoln High School in Gahanna, Ohio, where he was recruited as a linebacker. He now appears on the Bearcats' 2026 roster as an edge rusher, listed at 6-1 and 230 pounds in No. 24. The sophomore is part of a young homegrown group rotating behind Cincinnati's veteran portal additions up front.

athletes.name: Jonathan Thompson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thompson is Cincinnati's returning starting linebacker and the defense's leader following Jake Golday's departure, recording 74 tackles and a team-high 8.5 tackles for loss in 2025. The Columbus native played all 13 games with nine starts.

athletes.name: Daniel James
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: James is Cincinnati's projected starting boundary cornerback and a former four-star recruit ranked as the nation's No. 18 corner by 247Sports. He appeared in 12 games in 2025 with two starts and 15 tackles.

athletes.name: Simeon Coleman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Coleman is a returning linebacker in Cincinnati's rotation who appeared in all 13 games with five starts in 2025, recording 39 tackles. He was named a Freshman All-American by PFF and 247Sports in 2024.

athletes.name: Max Fletcher
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fletcher is a fifth-year punter from Melbourne, Australia, who came to Cincinnati from Arkansas. A Prokick Australia product who converted from Australian rules football, he earned All-SEC second-team honors with the Razorbacks after leading the conference with 2,770 punting yards and averaging 46.9 yards per punt. His older brother Mason punted for Cincinnati, a connection he cited in choosing the Bearcats. Listed at 6-6, he is the incumbent starting punter heading into 2026.

athletes.name: Cam Roetherford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Roetherford is a fifth-year defensive lineman from Detroit who prepped at Martin Luther King High School and transferred to Cincinnati from Arkansas-Pine Bluff. In his final FCS season he posted 15 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, a forced fumble and a blocked kick. He debuted for the Bearcats in 2024, appearing in 10 games with 11 tackles, including two in the opener against Towson and a season-high three against Houston. Listed at 6-3 and 280 pounds, he factors into the interior line rotation.

athletes.name: Myles Harrison
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Harrison came to Cincinnati out of Pickerington Central in Pickerington, Ohio, flipping his commitment to the Bearcats after an earlier pledge to Buffalo in the 2025 class. Recruited as a linebacker, he is listed on the 2026 roster as an edge rusher at 6-2 and 235 pounds wearing No. 34. The sophomore is one of several Ohio natives working in Cincinnati's front seven rotation this fall.

athletes.name: Drew Robinson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Drew Robinson is a junior linebacker for the Bearcats, listed on the roster as an outside linebacker at 6-foot-2 and 195 pounds. He is from Clarksville, Ohio, and played at Moeller High School in Cincinnati.

athletes.name: Montay Weedon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Weedon is a junior inside linebacker at Cincinnati, listed at 6-0 and 217 pounds in No. 44. He appeared in all 13 games in 2025 and started against Northwestern State and in the AutoZone Liberty Bowl, finishing with 26 tackles, three for loss and his first two career sacks against TCU. The Silver Spring, Maryland native was a four-year starter and two-time captain at St. John's College High School.

athletes.name: Antwan Peek Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Peek is Cincinnati's veteran safety/linebacker hybrid and a 2025 Jim Thorpe Award semifinalist who graded as the Big 12's top safety per PFF at 85.0. The Cincinnati native and former preferred walk-on posted 59 tackles in 13 games and is the son of UC Hall of Famer Antwan Peek Sr.

athletes.name: Eli Stein
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stein is a fifth-year long snapper from Cambridge, Wisconsin, who joined Cincinnati after three seasons at Arkansas, where he was twice named to the Patrick Mannelly Award watch list. He snapped for current Bearcats punter Max Fletcher in 2023, when Fletcher earned All-SEC second-team honors. Stein handled Cincinnati's long snapping for the entire 2025 season, recorded four tackles on punt coverage and earned All-Big 12 recognition from Pro Football Focus. He returns as the established starter in 2026.

athletes.name: George Leibold
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: George Leibold is a junior inside linebacker at Cincinnati, listed at 6-foot-1 and 220 pounds in No. 33. He is from Sarasota, Florida, where he played his high school football at Cardinal Mooney.

athletes.name: Evan Tengesdahl
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tengesdahl is Cincinnati's returning starting left guard and a 2025 AP third-team All-American who graded 82.8 on PFF. He started all 13 games on a line that was a Joe Moore Award semifinalist and allowed only eight sacks, second nationally.

athletes.name: Kellen Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kellen Davis is a junior tight end for Cincinnati, listed at 6-foot-3 and 248 pounds and wearing No. 86. He is from Middletown, Ohio, and played his high school football at Middletown High School.

athletes.name: Zac Clarke
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zac Clarke is a junior offensive lineman for the Bearcats, one of the taller players on the line at 6-foot-6 and 312 pounds. He is from Plainfield, Illinois, and played at Oswego East High School.

athletes.name: Jake Wheelock
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wheelock is a junior offensive lineman from Dayton, Ohio, who signed with Cincinnati out of Stebbins High School as an early enrollee. He sat out 2024 to retain freshman eligibility and appeared against Northwestern State in 2025. A consensus three-star prospect and two-time Division II first team all-state pick, he was Scott Satterfield's first commitment in the Bearcats' 2024 class and chose them over Duke and Virginia Tech.

athletes.name: Xavier Lozowicki
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lozowicki is a senior offensive lineman from Ridley Park, Pennsylvania, who prepped at IMG Academy and signed with Maine in the 2023 class. He appeared in five games as a freshman for the Black Bears and was graded by Pro Football Focus at 87.9, third among FCS offensive linemen that season. He committed to Cincinnati in April 2024 after drawing transfer interest from USC, Miami, Kansas State and BYU. Listed at 6-5 and 320 pounds, he is a candidate for a starting tackle spot in 2026.

athletes.name: JP Schrieber
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: JP Schrieber is a junior offensive lineman at Cincinnati, listed at 6-foot-2 and 305 pounds in No. 69. He is from Berwyn, Pennsylvania, and played his high school football at St. Joseph's Prep in Philadelphia.

athletes.name: Cray Paich
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cray Paich is a sophomore offensive lineman for the Bearcats, listed at 6-foot-5 and 315 pounds and wearing No. 70. He is from Northbrook, Illinois, and played at Glenbrook North High School.

athletes.name: Nolan Latulippe
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Latulippe, a senior from Aylmer, Quebec, transferred to Cincinnati from Albany in the December 2024 portal window. He earned FCS All-American recognition as a true freshman in 2023, started 27 consecutive games at right tackle across roughly 1,848 snaps, and helped Albany win a Colonial Athletic Association title and reach the FCS semifinals. He prepped at Champlain College Lennoxville. Listed at 6-8 and 310 pounds, he entered the program positioned to compete for an immediate starting tackle job.

athletes.name: Judea Milon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Milon reached Cincinnati by way of Tyler Junior College in Texas after playing his high school football at Shoemaker High School in his hometown of Killeen, Texas. The fifth year offensive lineman is listed at 6-4 and 300 pounds and wears No. 71. He is one of several transfer additions along a Bearcats front that also brought in linemen from South Dakota, Maine and Ball State for 2026.

athletes.name: Joe Cotton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cotton is Cincinnati's returning starting left tackle and a preseason All-Big 12 pick who started all 13 games in 2025 after transferring from South Dakota. He earned Big 12 Offensive Line of the Week honors three times.

athletes.name: Aiden Pastoriza
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pastoriza is a junior offensive lineman from Jackson, Michigan, who came to Cincinnati from Lumen Christi Catholic, where he helped the team to a 13-1 record and the 2023 state championship and earned Michigan AP Division 7-8 All-State honors. A consensus three-star recruit ranked No. 9 in the state by On3, he redshirted in 2024 and played in the Oklahoma State and Baylor games in 2025.

athletes.name: Marcus McGregor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Marcus McGregor is a sophomore offensive lineman at Cincinnati, listed at 6-foot-3 and 312 pounds in No. 75. He is from West Des Moines, Iowa, and played his high school football at Valley.

athletes.name: Taran Tyo
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tyo is Cincinnati's returning starting right guard and started all 13 games in 2025, ranking seventh among Big 12 guards by PFF grade. The Ball State transfer was a 2024 third-team All-MAC selection.

athletes.name: Grant Edgington
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Edgington is a senior offensive lineman who has appeared in three games across three seasons at Cincinnati. He redshirted in 2023, played in the 2024 opener against Towson and saw action in the Northwestern State and Oklahoma State games in 2025. The Madeira, Ohio native grew up a short drive from campus and is listed at 6-4 and 307 pounds in No. 78 on the 2026 roster.

athletes.name: Elijah Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jones came to Cincinnati from St. Joseph's Prep in Philadelphia, part of the same pipeline that delivered quarterback Samaj Jones to the Bearcats, and the two worked together as a passing combination in high school. The junior receiver, a Norristown, Pa. native listed at 5-11 and 195 pounds, wears No. 14 and competes in a wideout room that added five transfers ahead of the 2026 season.

athletes.name: James Early
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: James Early is a sophomore edge rusher for Cincinnati, listed at 6-foot-3 and 257 pounds and wearing No. 82. He is from Fort Wayne, Indiana, and played his high school football at North Side.

athletes.name: Ka'Maurri Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ka'Maurri Smith is a sophomore tight end from Dayton, Ohio, who played at Wayne High School. Listed at 6-foot-5 and 252 pounds, he was the first commitment Scott Satterfield's staff secured in Cincinnati's 2025 recruiting class, choosing the Bearcats over offers from Kentucky, Purdue, Rutgers and Pittsburgh. He caught 17 passes for 200 yards and two touchdowns as a high school senior.

athletes.name: Devyn Zahursky
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zahursky is a junior tight end from Berea, Ohio, who came to Cincinnati from Midpark High School and wears No. 83 at 6-4 and 247 pounds. A consensus three-star recruit and Ohio Division I second-team all-state pick, he chose the Bearcats over Pittsburgh, Indiana and Rutgers among others. Zahursky caught one pass for seven yards against Houston in 2024, then played all 13 games in 2025 in an expanded offensive and special teams role.

athletes.name: Lyviel Waters
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lyviel Waters is a junior tight end for the Bearcats, listed at 6-foot-2 and 245 pounds in No. 85. He is a Cincinnati native who played his high school football locally at Winton Woods.

athletes.name: CD McFee
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: CD McFee is a sophomore defensive lineman at Cincinnati, listed at 6-foot-4 and 312 pounds and wearing No. 88. He is from Elkhart, Indiana, and played his high school football at Elkhart High School.

athletes.name: Gavin Grover
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Grover is a junior tight end from Lewis Center, Ohio, who signed with Cincinnati as a three-star recruit in the 2024 class and enrolled early. At Olentangy High School he caught 63 passes for 853 yards and 10 touchdowns as a senior, earned All-Ohio Division I second-team honors and was a two-time all-district first-team selection, choosing the Bearcats over Kentucky, West Virginia and Michigan State among others. He played in all 12 games as a freshman in 2024, starting against Pitt and contributing on special teams.

athletes.name: DaMari Witherspoon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: DaMari Witherspoon is a sophomore tight end for the Bearcats, listed at 6-foot-5 and 245 pounds in No. 88. He is from Dallas, Georgia, and played his high school football at East Paulding.

athletes.name: Elijah Gunn
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gunn is a senior defensive lineman from LaGrange, Georgia, who transferred to Cincinnati from Southern Illinois in April 2025. He redshirted in 2023 and recorded 19 tackles for the Salukis in 2024. At Callaway High School he was a two-time honorable mention all-state selection, helped his team to a 43-10 record over four years and a 2020 state championship, and also lettered in basketball and track. Listed at 6-0 and 307 pounds, he adds interior size to the Bearcats' defensive front in 2026.

athletes.name: Drew Logan
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Logan joined Cincinnati as a preferred walk on out of Hoover High School in North Canton, Ohio, where he recorded 13 sacks as a senior and helped Hoover to a Federal League title. He redshirted in 2022, appeared in six games in 2024 and was placed on scholarship in August 2025. Now a fifth year lineman listed at 6-4 and 270 pounds in No. 91, he provides depth in the Bearcats' edge rotation.

athletes.name: Kamron Neal
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Neal is a sophomore defensive lineman from Fort Myers, Florida, who signed with Cincinnati out of Campbell High School in Georgia, where he was a three season defensive line contributor and also played tight end. Rated among the nation's top 60 edge prospects by On3, he appeared in two games as a freshman in 2025 while preserving a redshirt and led the Bearcats with five tackles against Norfolk State. His brother James plays offensive line at Iowa State.

athletes.name: Max Lemasters
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Max Lemasters is a senior kicker for Cincinnati, listed at 5-foot-6 and 175 pounds and wearing No. 93. He is a Cincinnati native and a graduate of Elder High School on the city's west side.

athletes.name: Marquaze Parker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Parker is Cincinnati's projected starting defensive end in Nate Woody's new 3-4 front after playing all 13 games in 2025 with 19 tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks. He made his first career start in the Liberty Bowl.

athletes.name: Nathan Nunn
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nathan Nunn is a junior defensive lineman at Cincinnati, listed at 6-foot-2 and 282 pounds in No. 96. He is from Medina, Ohio, and played his high school football at Medina High School.

athletes.name: Stephen Rusnak
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rusnak is a sixth-year kicker from Clarkston, Michigan, who transferred to Cincinnati from Charlotte ahead of the 2025 season. In his final year with the 49ers he made all 11 field goal attempts, including three from beyond 50 yards, and all 25 extra points, one of only two qualified kickers nationally not to miss a field goal. In his first season as a Bearcat he converted 13 of 17 field goals and all 47 extra points. He returns as the starting placekicker in 2026.

athletes.name: Taizaun Burns
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taizaun Burns is a sophomore wide receiver for the Bearcats, listed at 5-foot-10 and 175 pounds and wearing No. 27. He is from Columbus, Ohio, and played his high school football at Gahanna-Lincoln.

athletes.name: Dino Beslagic
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Beslagic transferred to Cincinnati from San Jose State after playing his high school football at Santa Clara High School in his hometown of Santa Clara, Calif. The fifth year punter is listed at 6-4 and 203 pounds in No. 35. He shares the Bearcats' punting duties on the 2026 roster with Max Fletcher, an Australian and former Arkansas punter, in what shapes up as an open competition.

athletes.name: Ronan Casanova
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ronan Casanova is a senior inside linebacker at Cincinnati, listed at 5-foot-10 and 225 pounds in No. 52. He is from Middletown, Ohio, and played his high school football at Middletown High School.

athletes.name: Landen Schaefer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Landen Schaefer is a sophomore safety for the Bearcats, listed at 6-foot and 185 pounds and wearing No. 32. He is a Cincinnati native who played his high school football at Reading High School.

athletes.name: Luke Collins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Luke Collins is a freshman offensive lineman at Cincinnati, listed at 6-foot-5 and 305 pounds in No. 79. He is from Gahanna, Ohio, and played his high school football at Gahanna-Lincoln.

athletes.name: Lance Dawson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lance Dawson is a freshman edge rusher from Avon, Ohio, listed at 6-foot-4 and 258 pounds. He blocked two kicks and recorded three sacks in a senior season playoff win over Highland, and he was part of Avon's 2024 state championship run. A three-star prospect, he chose Cincinnati over Illinois, West Virginia and Virginia.

athletes.name: Brooks Goodman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brooks Goodman is a freshman quarterback from Atlanta who played at Blessed Trinity Catholic, the same high school as Bearcats quarterback JC French IV. He committed to Cincinnati in May 2025 as the first quarterback in the 2026 class, choosing the Bearcats from a group of offers that included Indiana and Charlotte.

athletes.name: Luke Grover
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Luke Grover is a freshman offensive lineman for Cincinnati, listed at 6-foot-5 and 308 pounds in No. 67. He is from Lewis Center, Ohio, and played his high school football at Olentangy.

athletes.name: Austin Hoane
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Austin Hoane is a freshman offensive lineman from Cookeville, Tennessee, listed at 6-foot-5 and 295 pounds. He grew up in Augusta, Georgia, and moved to Cookeville as a sophomore. A two-time first team all-state selection in Class 6A, he signed with Cincinnati over West Virginia, Memphis and James Madison.

athletes.name: Keegan Horn
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Keegan Horn is a freshman edge rusher from Hueytown, Alabama, listed at 6-foot-3 and 235 pounds. He served as a team captain at Hueytown High School in both his junior and senior seasons and committed to Cincinnati in August 2025, a three-star prospect who chose the Bearcats over West Virginia, Tulane and Wake Forest.

athletes.name: Kameron Hurst
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kameron Hurst is a freshman cornerback from St. Louis who played at Lift for Life Academy and recorded 74 total tackles as a senior. He was committed to Washington State before flipping to Cincinnati late in the cycle, signing as a three-star prospect ranked among the top 25 players in Missouri.

athletes.name: H'eij Jackson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: H'eij Jackson is a freshman wide receiver from New Orleans who came to Cincinnati out of McDonogh 35 after beginning his high school career at Sarah T. Reed. He caught 42 passes for 547 yards and 10 touchdowns as a junior and earned first team all-district honors. A three-star signee, he also competed in basketball and track.

athletes.name: Solomon Mathis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Solomon Mathis is a freshman offensive lineman from Hephzibah, Georgia, who played tackle at Hephzibah High School. He recorded 17 pancake blocks as a senior across 10 games and was selected for the Georgia versus Carolina Border Bowl. A three-star prospect, he was Cincinnati's first offensive line commitment in the 2026 recruiting class.

athletes.name: Jamarion McKinney
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jamarion McKinney is a freshman cornerback from Greenville, South Carolina, listed at 6-foot-2. He finished his high school career at Greenville High after transferring from Wade Hampton, and he was selected for the Shrine Bowl of the Carolinas. A three-star signee who also played high school basketball, he committed to Cincinnati in September 2025.

athletes.name: Jaxon Newton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jaxon Newton is a freshman linebacker from Anniston, Alabama, who played at Wellborn High School. As a senior he recorded 22 tackles with six for loss and four sacks while also seeing time at defensive end, safety, running back, tight end and receiver. He played basketball and baseball as well, and chose Cincinnati over Toledo and Southern Miss.

athletes.name: Jonathan Rulo
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jonathan Rulo is a freshman defensive lineman from Belleville, Illinois, who played at Belleville East. He finished his high school career with 204 tackles, 55 of them for loss, and 17 sacks, earning 2024 IHSFCA Class 8A all-state honors. Rulo is also a state champion wrestler and chose Cincinnati over Iowa and Kansas State.

athletes.name: Darrius Simmons
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Darrius Simmons is a freshman defensive lineman listed at 6-foot-3 and 300 pounds in No. 90. He is from Cairo, Georgia, and played at Gadsden County High School. A three-star signee in Cincinnati's 2026 class, he chose the Bearcats over South Carolina, Kansas State and Houston and signed in December 2025.

athletes.name: Joshua Smith
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Joshua Smith is a freshman wide receiver from Columbus, Ohio, listed at 6-foot-5. He played quarterback at Columbus Africentric, where he worked as a dual threat passer and runner before projecting outside as a receiver for the Bearcats. He was committed to Bowling Green before flipping to Cincinnati in the 2026 class.

athletes.name: Xavier Starks
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Xavier Starks is a freshman safety from Birmingham, Alabama, who played at Clay-Chalkville High School. He committed to Cincinnati in February 2025 and signed as a three-star prospect ranked among the top 75 players in Alabama and as the No. 93 safety nationally by 247Sports.

athletes.name: Markell Taylor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Markell Taylor is a freshman safety from Dallas, Georgia, who played at North Paulding High School. He committed to Cincinnati in June 2025 as a three-star prospect ranked among the top 50 safeties nationally by 247Sports and ESPN, choosing the Bearcats over Kansas State, Memphis and Toledo.

athletes.name: Dadrien Waller
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dadrien Waller is a freshman wide receiver from Guntersville, Alabama, listed at 6-foot-3 and 205 pounds. He caught 34 passes for 712 yards and six touchdowns in 2024 as Guntersville went 9-2 and shared the Class 5A, Region 8 title. A three-star signee, he was Cincinnati's first offensive commitment in the 2026 class.

athletes.name: Evan Weinberg
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Evan Weinberg is a freshman inside linebacker at Cincinnati, listed at 6-foot-3 and 230 pounds in No. 36. He is from Springboro, Ohio, and played his high school football at Springboro High School.

athletes.name: Jaidon Windom
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jaidon Windom is a freshman outside linebacker from Detroit who played at Martin Luther King High School, where he lined up at safety. He committed to Cincinnati in February 2025 and signed as a three-star prospect rated among the top 15 players in Michigan by 247Sports.

athletes.name: Nathan Zappitelli
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nathan Zappitelli is a freshman offensive lineman from Mentor, Ohio, who played tackle at Lake Catholic. He signed with Cincinnati as a three-star prospect, choosing the Bearcats over finalists that included Wake Forest, West Virginia and Pittsburgh, and he has been working at interior line drills with guard and center as his projected spots.

athletes.name: JC French IV
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: French is Cincinnati's projected starting quarterback after transferring from Georgia Southern, where he started all 13 games in 2025 for 2,929 passing yards and 20 touchdowns plus 315 rushing yards and six scores. He replaces Brendan Sorsby and arrives with one year of eligibility.

athletes.name: KK Meier
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Meier transferred to Cincinnati from UTSA, where he spent his earlier college seasons after playing at Frenship High School in Wolfforth, Texas. The fifth year cornerback from Lubbock is listed at 6-0 and 205 pounds and wears No. 14. He is one of six defensive backs in a Bearcats transfer class of 22 players that enrolled in January 2026.

athletes.name: Jasper Beeler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Beeler is a fifth-year safety from Farmington, Michigan, who prepped at North Farmington and joined Cincinnati from Northern Illinois for his final season of eligibility. He spent two years at Saginaw Valley State, posting 53 tackles in 2024, then recorded 77 tackles, three interceptions, two pass breakups, half a sack and a forced fumble at Northern Illinois in 2025. Pro Football Focus graded him at 77.3 overall that season. Listed at 6-1 and 194 pounds, he arrives as a likely starter in the Bearcats secondary.

athletes.name: Chidera Otutu
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Otutu joined Cincinnati from UTSA after coming out of Weiss High School in Pflugerville, Texas. The junior defensive lineman is listed at 6-1 and 300 pounds and wears No. 11, giving the Bearcats interior bulk alongside fellow portal additions on a defensive front that saw significant turnover during the 2026 transfer cycle.

athletes.name: MJ Cannon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cannon is a projected starting safety for Cincinnati after transferring from Bowling Green, where he started all 12 games in 2025 for 57 tackles, seven tackles for loss and two interceptions en route to third-team All-MAC honors. He was a second-team All-MVC pick at Illinois State in 2024.

athletes.name: Jacob Finley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Finley is a projected starting cornerback for Cincinnati after transferring from Northern Illinois, where he started all 11 games he played in 2025 and led the Huskies with eight pass breakups. He also tied for the NIU team lead in breakups in 2024.

athletes.name: Gi'Bran Payne
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Payne returns to his hometown for a final season after four years at Notre Dame, where he rushed for 226 yards and two touchdowns. A four star recruit out of La Salle High School in Cincinnati, he signed with the Fighting Irish in 2022 before entering the portal and committing to the Bearcats. The fifth year back wears No. 6 and joins a group that also added transfers from Stanford and Louisiana.

athletes.name: Kenny Worthy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Worthy joined Cincinnati from Washington State, where he played cornerback before entering the portal. He came out of Centennial High School in Buckeye, Ariz. and is listed at 6-0 and 188 pounds on the Bearcats' 2026 roster wearing No. 8. The junior is one of six defensive backs Cincinnati added in a transfer class of 22 players that enrolled in January.

athletes.name: Josh Hough
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hough arrives at Cincinnati from California University of Pennsylvania, a Division II program, after playing his high school football at Beaver Falls High School in his hometown of Beaver Falls, Pa. At 6-2 and 335 pounds he is the heaviest player listed on the Bearcats' 2026 roster, giving the interior defensive line a true nose tackle body. The sixth year lineman wears No. 95.

athletes.name: Malachi Henry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Henry is a projected starting outside receiver for Cincinnati after transferring from Central Arkansas, where he caught 69 passes for 889 yards and 10 touchdowns in 2025 and made first-team All-UAC. He posted four 100-yard games including a career-high 142 against Abilene Christian.

athletes.name: Cade Wolford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wolford is a starting slot receiver and Cincinnati's projected punt and kick returner after transferring from Kent State, where he was an All-MAC third-team pick in 2025 with 19 catches for 509 yards and seven touchdowns. He averaged 26.8 yards per reception.

athletes.name: Ty Goodwill
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Goodwill transferred to Cincinnati from South Alabama, where he began his career after playing at Faith Academy near his hometown of Prichard, Ala. The junior safety is listed at 6-3 and 195 pounds in No. 7, making him one of the taller safeties on the roster. He joins a secondary that brought in six defensive backs through the portal for 2026.

athletes.name: JV Gibson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gibson is Cincinnati's projected No. 1 receiver after transferring from Oklahoma, where he caught 18 passes for 199 yards and a touchdown in 2025. He was a second-team FCS All-American at Arkansas-Pine Bluff in 2024 with 70 catches for 1,215 yards.

athletes.name: Thomas Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is Cincinnati's projected starting edge rusher after transferring from North Carolina Central, where his 12 sacks ranked seventh in the FCS in 2025 alongside 49 tackles and 18 tackles for loss. He was a first-team All-MEAC selection.

athletes.name: Patrick Bauer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bauer came to Cincinnati from Illinois State, where he played after leaving St. Viator High School in his hometown of Mount Prospect, Ill. The senior edge rusher is listed at 6-3 and 235 pounds and wears No. 10 for the Bearcats. He is one of three linebackers Cincinnati added in a January transfer class of 22 players.

athletes.name: Larenzo Fenner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Fenner is a projected starting receiver for Cincinnati after transferring from South Dakota, where his 15 touchdown catches set a program record and his 1,001 receiving yards ranked third in school history. His 22.75 yards per catch ranked second in the FCS in 2025.

athletes.name: Filip Maciorowski
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Maciorowski is Cincinnati's projected starting middle linebacker after transferring from Northern Illinois, where he was second on the team with 87 tackles and led the Huskies with 2.5 sacks in 2025. He posted a career-high 13 tackles against San Diego State.

athletes.name: Flynn Schiele
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Schiele arrives from Division II Colorado School of Mines, where he caught 138 passes for 2,345 yards and 23 touchdowns across four years, including 1,000 yard receiving seasons in 2023 and 2024. The sixth year receiver played at West Linn High School in his hometown of West Linn, Ore. He is listed at 6-4 and 210 pounds in No. 16 and projects into Cincinnati's outside receiver rotation.

athletes.name: Damaine Wilson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wilson transferred to Cincinnati from Georgia State after playing at Coconut Creek High School near his hometown of Pompano Beach, Fla. The junior inside linebacker is listed at 6-3 and 235 pounds and wears No. 9. He is one of three linebackers the Bearcats added in a transfer class of 22 players that enrolled in January 2026.

athletes.name: Zylan Perry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Perry is Cincinnati's projected lead running back after transferring from Louisiana, where he ran for 689 yards and eight touchdowns in 2025 and earned honorable mention All-Sun Belt. He led the FBS in kickoff return yards in 2023 with 862.

athletes.name: Cole Tabb
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tabb is a key addition in Cincinnati's running back room after transferring from Stanford, where he won the program's Outstanding Freshman Award in 2025 with 114 carries for 445 yards and three touchdowns. The former four-star recruit earned ACC Running Back of the Week honors against Florida State.

athletes.name: Gavin Gregory
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gavin Gregory is a freshman tight end from Alliance, Ohio, who played at West Branch and stands 6-foot-7. He caught 38 passes for 714 yards and eight touchdowns as a senior and finished with 77 career receptions for 1,369 yards and 15 scores. He was committed to Toledo before signing with Cincinnati.

athletes.name: Jayzon Thompson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jayzon Thompson is a freshman running back from Knoxville, Tennessee, who finished his high school career at Anderson County after beginning it at Bearden. As a senior he ran for 1,970 yards and 28 touchdowns on 216 carries and added a team high 48 catches for 627 yards and seven scores, earning first team All-PrepXtra recognition.

athletes.name: Liam O'Brien
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: O'Brien spent four seasons at Penn, earning first team All Ivy honors as a senior after throwing for 2,376 yards and completing 67.2 percent of his passes. He committed to Cincinnati in January 2026 for his final year of eligibility. A Boulder, Colo. native out of Fairview High School, the fifth year quarterback wears No. 10 and is competing with Georgia Southern transfer JC French for the starting job.

athletes.name: Pierce Ayers
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pierce Ayers is a sophomore wide receiver for Cincinnati, listed at 5-foot-10 and 185 pounds and wearing No. 89. He is from Alexandria, Virginia, and played his high school football at Williamsburg.

athletes.name: Juan Bates
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Juan Bates is a freshman defensive lineman at Cincinnati, listed at 6-foot-3 and 290 pounds in No. 94. He is from Mason, Ohio, and played his high school football locally at Mason High School.

athletes.name: Kenny Baker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kenny Baker is a freshman long snapper for the Bearcats, listed at 6-foot and 218 pounds and wearing No. 41. He is a Cincinnati native who played his high school football at Elder High School.

athletes.name: JJ Miller
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: JJ Miller is a junior quarterback at Cincinnati, listed at 6-foot and 185 pounds and wearing No. 22. He is from Amelia, Ohio, and played his high school football at Williamsburg High School.

athletes.name: James Lewis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: James Lewis is a junior running back for the Bearcats, listed at 6-foot and 200 pounds in No. 25. He is from Bloomfield, Indiana, and played his high school football at Eastern Greene.

athletes.name: Isaiah Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Johnson is a projected starting wide receiver for the Cincinnati Bearcats out of Fort Walton Beach, Fla., after transferring from Western Carolina.

athletes.name: Jamari Johnson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jamari Johnson is a sophomore listed as an outside linebacker on Cincinnati's roster at 5-foot-10 and 175 pounds in No. 15. He is from Birmingham, Alabama, and played his high school football at Pell City.

athletes.name: Zach Taylor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zach Taylor is a sophomore offensive lineman at Cincinnati, listed at 6-foot-3 and 315 pounds and wearing No. 76. He is from Kingsland, Georgia, and played his high school football at Camden County.

athletes.name: Jalen Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jalen Williams is a freshman receiver from Bloomington, Indiana, listed at 6-foot-5 and 220 pounds. He played at Bloomington South and was committed to South Florida before flipping to Cincinnati, joining the 2026 class as a three-star prospect whom recruiting services also evaluated at tight end.

athletes.name: Nicholas Antoine
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nicholas Antoine is a redshirt senior defensive back at UCF, listed at 6-foot-4 and 205 pounds in No. 27. He comes from Daytona Beach, Florida, and played his high school football at Mainland.

athletes.name: Thomas Wadsworth
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas Wadsworth is a redshirt senior tight end for UCF who wears No. 84 and is listed at 6-foot-3 and 245 pounds. He is a Melbourne, Florida, native and attended Melbourne High School.

athletes.name: Braeden Marshall
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Marshall is UCF's projected nickel back and a former four-star recruit from nearby Lake Mary who has appeared in 37 games with 19 starts. He set a career high with two interceptions in 2025.

athletes.name: Demari Henderson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Henderson is UCF's returning starting safety and was the team's third-leading tackler in 2025 with 61 stops, a sack and an interception. He was named Walter Camp National Defensive Player of the Week as a sophomore in 2023.

athletes.name: Isaiah Nixon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Nixon is a returning edge rusher projected to start for UCF after both 2025 starters left for the NFL. The former four-star recruit set career highs with 24 tackles and 3.5 tackles for loss in 11 games last season.

athletes.name: Matthew Prigmore
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Matthew Prigmore is a redshirt junior offensive lineman at UCF, listed at 6-foot-3 and 315 pounds in jersey No. 74. He grew up in Weston, Florida, and played at Cypress Bay High School.

athletes.name: Quentin Hatch
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Quentin Hatch is a redshirt senior edge rusher at UCF who arrived by way of Lake Erie College, a Division II program in Ohio, after playing his high school football at West Orange in the Orlando area. The Knights list him at 6-foot-1 and 225 pounds in jersey No. 45, making him one of the shorter, more compact ends on the defensive front.

athletes.name: Ethan Higgins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ethan Higgins is a redshirt junior offensive lineman for UCF, listed at 6-foot-6 and 270 pounds in No. 68. He is from Brooksville, Florida, and played high school football at Hernando Christian.

athletes.name: Jordyn Bridgewater
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bridgewater is a redshirt sophomore wide receiver at UCF who was born in Louisiana and grew up in Winter Garden, Florida, where he played at West Orange High School. He enrolled early in January 2024 and redshirted that fall, then appeared in three games in 2025 against North Carolina A&T, West Virginia and Baylor. He caught 40 passes for 886 yards and nine touchdowns as a high school junior and chose UCF over Tulane and Pittsburgh.

athletes.name: Antione Jackson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson is a returning starting cornerback and UCF's punt returner, averaging a Big 12-best 11.8 yards per return in 2025 while making 39 tackles. The East Carolina transfer is a Phil Steele preseason All-Big 12 fourth-team selection.

athletes.name: Carson Hinshaw
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Carson Hinshaw is a redshirt sophomore wide receiver at UCF, listed at 5-foot-10 and 165 pounds in jersey No. 85. He is a Lake Mary, Florida, product who played at Lake Mary High School.

athletes.name: Caleb Rollerson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rollerson is a redshirt sophomore wide receiver from Ocala, Florida, who came to UCF after transferring to Hawthorne High School for his senior year. Listed at 6-2 and 210 pounds, he redshirted in 2024 without appearing in a game and caught three passes for 67 yards in 2025. He was named to the Gainesville Sun All-Area small school offensive team after an 800-yard receiving season.

athletes.name: Dylan Wade
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wade is UCF's returning starting tight end and set program FBS-era tight end records in 2025 with 43 catches for 523 yards and five touchdowns. The Maryland transfer was an All-Big 12 honorable mention selection.

athletes.name: Taevion Swint
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Swint is a redshirt freshman running back from Kissimmee who starred at Osceola High School, rushing for 1,778 yards and 25 touchdowns as a senior in 2024 and helping the Kowboys reach the state championship game. Rated a four-star prospect by most services, he missed all of 2025 after a knee injury in fall camp and returns in 2026 to compete for carries in the Knights backfield.

athletes.name: DJ Bell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bell is a redshirt senior cornerback from Pensacola, Florida who played at Pensacola High School and spent three seasons at Memphis before transferring to UCF. He appeared in 11 games for the Knights in 2025, recording 17 tackles and four pass breakups, with a season high of five tackles at BYU. He returns as an experienced piece of the secondary rotation.

athletes.name: Ric'Darious "DayDay" Farmer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Farmer is a redshirt sophomore receiver from Melbourne, Florida who played at Melbourne Central Catholic and was rated a four-star recruit. He signed with West Virginia and caught six passes for 54 yards as a true freshman before transferring to UCF in December 2024. A knee injury cost him the 2025 season, and he wears No. 6 as he works back into the receiver rotation.

athletes.name: Duane Thomas Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is UCF's returning leading receiver, catching 53 passes for 528 yards with nine starts in 2025 and earning All-Big 12 honorable mention. The Charlotte transfer also handles kickoff returns for the Knights.

athletes.name: Sincere Edwards
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Edwards is a junior edge rusher from Orlando who played at Wekiva High School and was a four-star recruit. He appeared in all 13 games as a freshman at Pittsburgh in 2024, recording 17 tackles and three sacks, then transferred home to UCF. He played six games in 2025 with 11 tackles, 4.5 tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks before a foot injury ended his season.

athletes.name: Horace Lockett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lockett is a returning starting defensive tackle for UCF at 6-6 and 355 pounds, recording 13 tackles, three tackles for loss and his first career sack in 2025. The Georgia Tech transfer withdrew from the transfer portal to return to Orlando.

athletes.name: Caden Piening
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Piening is a redshirt freshman tight end at UCF, listed at 6-5 and 245 pounds in No. 18. He appeared in four games in 2025, including a start against North Carolina, and earned a redshirt. A three-star recruit rated the nation's 13th best tight end, he caught 43 passes for 769 yards and seven touchdowns as a senior at Anderson High School in Cincinnati and was a first team all-conference pick.

athletes.name: Waden Charles
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Charles is a returning starting wide receiver for UCF who caught 26 passes for 290 yards as a true freshman in 2025, starting six games including the final five. He was a four-star prospect out of Somerset Academy Canyons.

athletes.name: Lewis Carter
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Carter is UCF's returning leading tackler, posting 92 tackles, four tackles for loss and two sacks in 2025 for All-Big 12 honorable mention honors. The Oklahoma transfer started 11 games in his first season with the Knights.

athletes.name: Rukeem Stroud
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stroud is a redshirt freshman cornerback from Plant City, Florida, who signed with UCF out of Tampa Bay Tech after committing to Wisconsin and flipping to the Knights weeks later in June 2024. A four-star prospect, he posted 16 tackles, 11 pass breakups and an interception as a senior and had six interceptions with 17 breakups as a junior. Stroud appeared in three games in 2025 while preserving a redshirt.

athletes.name: Jayden Bellamy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bellamy is UCF's returning starting cornerback and an Athlon Sports preseason All-Big 12 second-team pick after leading the Knights with eight pass breakups in 2025. The son of 14-year NFL veteran Jay Bellamy, he previously played at Notre Dame and Syracuse.

athletes.name: Phil Picciotti
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Picciotti is a redshirt junior linebacker from Perkasie, Pennsylvania who recorded 144 tackles as a junior at Pennridge before spending his senior year at IMG Academy, where he led the linebackers with 63 tackles. He signed with Oklahoma out of the 2023 class, transferred to UCF in December 2024 and made his college debut in 2025, playing mostly on special teams over the final six games.

athletes.name: Agyeman Addae
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Addae is a sophomore running back at UCF, listed at 5-10 and 190 pounds in No. 35. He joined the Knights as a walk-on and appeared in eight games as a freshman in 2025, rushing 12 times for 50 yards and catching seven passes for 70 yards and a touchdown, including five receptions for 62 yards at BYU. The Miami native won two state championships at Columbus High School and made the 2025 Big 12 All-Academic Team.

athletes.name: Andrea Parisi
