athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Andrea Parisi is a redshirt sophomore wide receiver for UCF who came to the program from Bergamo, Italy. He prepped at Saint Andrews and is listed by the Knights at 5-foot-11 and 195 pounds in No. 39.

athletes.name: LaParka Langston
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Langston is a redshirt junior offensive lineman from Atlanta who played at Mundy's Mill High School and arrived at UCF from Northwest Mississippi Community College. At 6-7 and 285 pounds he is among the taller linemen on the roster, and he wears No. 53 as he competes for a rotation spot up front in 2026.

athletes.name: Noah Senka
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Noah Senka is a redshirt sophomore offensive lineman at UCF, listed at 6-foot-2 and 295 pounds in jersey No. 67. He is from Seminole, Florida, and played his high school football at Indian Rocks Christian.

athletes.name: Justin Royes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Royes is a redshirt junior offensive lineman from Suffolk, Virginia who played at Lakeland High School and transferred to UCF from Division II Virginia Union. Listed at 6-5 and 300 pounds, he announced his return for the 2026 season and is one of the veterans competing for interior snaps for the Knights.

athletes.name: Preston Cushman
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Cushman is UCF's returning starting right tackle and the offensive line's leader, starting all 12 games and leading the team with 753 offensive snaps in 2025. The Ole Miss transfer is an Athlon Sports preseason All-Big 12 fourth-team selection.

athletes.name: RJ Jackson Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jackson is UCF's returning starting defensive tackle and an All-Big 12 honorable mention pick after 33 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks in 2025. He transferred to UCF from Tulsa.

athletes.name: Mason Denaburg
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Denaburg is a redshirt freshman kicker and punter from Merritt Island, Florida who was a first-round pick of the Washington Nationals in the 2018 MLB Draft. He retired from professional baseball in May 2025 and joined UCF, returning to a sport in which he earned first team all-state punting honors at Merritt Island High School in 2016.

athletes.name: Chase Hinshaw
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chase Hinshaw is a redshirt freshman wide receiver for UCF who wears No. 86 and is listed at 6-foot-2 and 175 pounds. He grew up in Lake Mary, Florida, and played at Lake Mary High School.

athletes.name: Rocklyn Kelley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kelley is a redshirt freshman long snapper from Denton, Texas, who came to UCF out of Guyer High School, where he also competed in the discus for the track team. He did not see game action in 2025. In July 2026 he represented UCF at the Big 12 Beyond Borders program in Washington, D.C. He wears No. 37.

athletes.name: Aymeric Koumba
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Koumba is a redshirt junior edge rusher from Bordeaux who became the first French-born player in UCF history when he signed with the Knights out of Michigan. A three-star prospect developed through the PPI Recruits program, he had earlier been the first player from France to sign with Michigan. Listed at 6-5 and 245 pounds, he enters his second season in Orlando wearing No. 12.

athletes.name: Jeffson Lafontant
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Lafontant is a redshirt junior defensive lineman from North Miami Beach, Florida who played at North Miami Beach Senior High School and transferred to UCF from Bethune-Cookman. Listed at 6-3 and 295 pounds, he wears No. 92 and competes for interior snaps in a defensive tackle room stocked with transfers in 2026.

athletes.name: Camp Lott
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Camp Lott is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman at UCF, listed at 6-foot-6 and 265 pounds in No. 57. He is from McComb, Mississippi, and played his high school football at Parklane Academy.

athletes.name: Jayden Jennings
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jennings is a fifth-year linebacker from Salem, Virginia who played at Salem High School and spent four seasons at Virginia Tech before transferring to UCF. He appeared in nine games with two starts in 2025, recording 15 tackles, his first career interception against North Carolina A&T and a fumble recovery against Houston. He received a waiver for a fifth season and wears No. 38.

athletes.name: Noah McGough
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: McGough is a redshirt freshman kicker and punter from Dallas who came to UCF out of Jesuit High School. He led Texas in field goals made in a season with 17 and was twice named District 7-6A Special Teams Player of the Year. He appeared in one game in 2025 while preserving his redshirt, converting an extra point and recording a touchback against North Carolina A&T.

athletes.name: RaiShaun McHaney
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: RaiShaun McHaney is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman for UCF and one of the tallest players on the roster at 6-foot-8 and 270 pounds. He wears No. 70 and came from Indianapolis Lutheran in Indianapolis, Indiana.

athletes.name: Connor Meadows
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Meadows is a redshirt senior offensive lineman from Trenton, Tennessee who played at Peabody High School and reached UCF by way of Tennessee State and Tennessee. He played eight games in 2025 with four starts, taking most of his snaps at guard while backing up at right tackle, and he confirmed his return for 2026 with the starting right guard job open.

athletes.name: Zack Palmer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Zack Palmer is a redshirt freshman wide receiver at UCF, listed at 6-foot and 190 pounds in jersey No. 81. He is a hometown product from Orlando who played his high school football at Boone.

athletes.name: Owen Spell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Spell is a senior offensive lineman from Jesup, Georgia who played at Wayne County High School and transferred to UCF from Division II Limestone University. Listed at 6-8 and 305 pounds, he wears No. 61 and enters 2026 competing for tackle snaps in an offensive line group heavily reworked through the transfer portal.

athletes.name: Trenton Turner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Trenton Turner is a redshirt freshman defensive tackle for UCF, listed at 6-foot-2 and 320 pounds in No. 54. He is from Lakeland, Florida, and played his high school football at Lakeland High School.

athletes.name: Jacob Maiava
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jacob Maiava is a redshirt freshman offensive lineman at UCF, listed at 6-foot-2 and 280 pounds in jersey No. 55. His hometown is Kahuku, Hawaii, and he played high school football at Santa Margarita Catholic in California.

athletes.name: Dominick Campbell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dominick Campbell is a redshirt senior offensive lineman whose path to UCF ran through Phillips Exeter Academy in New Hampshire, then Howard and Notre Dame before he joined the Knights. A native of Scarborough, Maine, he is listed at 6-foot-9 and 310 pounds, among the tallest linemen on the roster, and wears jersey No. 72.

athletes.name: Anthony Coaxum
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Anthony Coaxum is a fifth-year edge rusher with one of the longest college routes on the UCF roster, listing stops at West Virginia Wesleyan, Kentucky Christian and Carson-Newman before Orlando. He played his high school football at Western in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, and the Knights list him at 6-foot-4 and 270 pounds in jersey No. 96.

athletes.name: Donnell Johnson III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Donnell Johnson III is a redshirt junior defensive back for UCF who wears No. 49 and is listed at 180 pounds. He is from Orlando and played his high school football at Monroe.

athletes.name: Chance Nixon
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chance Nixon is a redshirt freshman running back at UCF, listed at 5-foot-9 and 179 pounds in jersey No. 42. He grew up in Oviedo, Florida, and played his high school football at Oviedo High School.

athletes.name: Alonza Barnett III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Barnett is UCF's projected starting quarterback after transferring from James Madison, where he was the 2025 Sun Belt Player of the Year and led the Dukes to a College Football Playoff berth. He threw for 2,806 yards and 23 touchdowns and rushed for 589 yards and 15 scores in 2025.

athletes.name: Keyone Jenkins
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jenkins is a senior quarterback who transferred to UCF after three seasons as FIU's starter, finishing third in Panthers history with 6,721 career passing yards and 42 touchdowns. He threw for 1,742 yards and nine scores in ten games in 2025.

athletes.name: Kaleb Annett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Annett is a redshirt sophomore quarterback from Newport Beach, California who threw for nearly 3,000 yards and 30 touchdowns as a senior at Corona del Mar and led the team to the CIF Southern Section Division 4 title game in 2023. A three-star recruit, he spent two seasons at Boise State without appearing in a game and signed with UCF in January 2026, where he is competing for the backup job.

athletes.name: Dante Carr
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Dante Carr is a freshman quarterback for UCF with prototypical size at 6-foot-4 and 220 pounds. He wears No. 16 and came to Orlando from Minersville, Pennsylvania, where he played at Minersville High School.

athletes.name: Rocco Marriott
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Rocco Marriott is a freshman quarterback at UCF, listed at 6-foot-4 and 220 pounds in jersey No. 8. He is from Kansas City, Missouri, and played his high school football at Platte County.

athletes.name: Landen Chambers
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Chambers is a Central Arkansas transfer projected to lead UCF's backfield after rushing for 1,273 yards and 10 touchdowns in 2025, ninth in the FCS. He was a first-team All-UAC pick and set a school record with eight straight 100-yard games.

athletes.name: Duke Watson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Watson is a Louisville transfer competing for UCF's lead running back job and an Athlon Sports preseason All-Big 12 fourth-team pick. He led the nation at 8.9 yards per carry as a 2024 freshman before an injury-limited 2025 season of 158 rushing yards.

athletes.name: Kaj Baker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kaj Baker is a freshman running back for UCF and one of the smallest listed players on the roster at 5-foot-8 and 160 pounds. He wears No. 20 and came from Somerset Academy in Miami, Florida.

athletes.name: Arthur Lewis IV
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Arthur Lewis IV is a freshman running back at UCF, listed at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds in jersey No. 24. His hometown is Palatka, Florida, and he played his high school football at Bartram Trail.

athletes.name: Josh Derry
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Derry is a senior wide receiver from Baltimore who played at Concordia Preparatory School and transferred to UCF from Monmouth in January 2026. He caught 76 passes for 1,123 yards and 13 touchdowns in his final season with the Hawks, earning first team All-CAA recognition and FCS All-American honors from the Associated Press and Phil Steele. He wears No. 5 for the Knights.

athletes.name: Jonathan Bibbs
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bibbs is a redshirt sophomore wide receiver from Birmingham, Alabama, who transferred to UCF from Louisiana-Monroe in the 2026 portal cycle. Listed at 6-foot-1, he led the Warhawks in both receptions and receiving yards in 2025, catching 26 passes for 383 yards and three touchdowns while averaging 14.7 yards per catch. He earned first team All-County and All-Metro honors at Spain Park High School. The Knights added him as a vertical threat and he projects into the receiver rotation for his first season in Orlando.

athletes.name: Tyren Hornes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tyren Hornes is a freshman wide receiver for UCF who wears the single-digit No. 2 and is listed at 6-foot and 175 pounds. He is from Bradenton, Florida, and played his high school football at Booker.

athletes.name: Jordan Nunuha
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Jordan Nunuha is a freshman wide receiver at UCF with good size at 6-foot-3 and 195 pounds. He wears jersey No. 23 and came to Orlando from Nanakuli, Hawaii, by way of Saint Louis School.

athletes.name: Grayson Brousseau
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brousseau is a redshirt sophomore tight end from Lehi, Utah who played at Lehi High School and arrived at UCF after stops at Oklahoma State and Utah State. Listed at 6-5 and 245 pounds, he wears No. 88 and is part of a tight end group that also includes transfers Dylan Wade and Dylan Burk heading into 2026.

athletes.name: Brooks Hall
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Brooks Hall is a freshman tight end for UCF, listed at 6-foot-5 and 225 pounds in jersey No. 87. He is from Platte City, Missouri, and played his high school football at Platte County.

athletes.name: Tyler Gibson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gibson is a redshirt senior offensive lineman from Atlanta who joins UCF for 2026 after two seasons apiece at Georgia Tech and Charlotte. A four-star prospect out of Johns Creek High School, he redshirted as a true freshman with the Yellow Jackets in 2022 and played two games in each of his seasons there. At Charlotte he appeared in every game in 2025 and started the final six contests at right tackle. He cited his relationship with new UCF offensive line coach AJ Blazek in choosing the Knights.

athletes.name: Henry Tabansi
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Tabansi is a redshirt junior offensive lineman from Staten Island, New York, who transferred to UCF from Buffalo in January 2026. A Moore Catholic High School product listed at 6-foot-5 and 306 pounds, he started every collegiate game he has played, running his total to 25 consecutive starts at left tackle across 26 career appearances for the Bulls. He entered the portal on Jan. 6 and committed to the Knights the same day. Among UCF's Group of Five line additions he carries the strongest case for a starting job in 2026.

athletes.name: Cooper Terpstra
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Terpstra is a redshirt junior offensive lineman from Holland, Michigan, and UCF's first offensive line addition of the 2026 transfer cycle. A West Ottawa High School product listed at 6-foot-4 and 305 pounds, he began his career at Michigan State as a walk-on and worked into the lineup there, making his first career start at center in the Spartans' final game of the 2025 season. He arrives in Orlando as an interior option under new line coach AJ Blazek and figures into the center and guard competition.

athletes.name: Brady Wayburn
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Wayburn is a redshirt senior offensive lineman from Gastonia, North Carolina, who transferred to UCF from UConn ahead of the 2026 season. He prepped at the Loomis Chaffee School and has logged 728 career snaps for the Huskies, including five starts at right guard in 2025 during back-to-back nine-win campaigns. Offensive line coach AJ Blazek has pointed to his strength and his wide zone experience at UConn. He entered the offseason as the favorite to take over at right guard for the Knights.

athletes.name: Kasiyah Charlton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Kasiyah Charlton is a freshman offensive lineman at UCF and one of the largest players on the roster at 6-foot-7 and 315 pounds. He wears No. 77 and played high school football at Brunswick in Brunswick, Georgia.

athletes.name: Amahn Williams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Amahn Williams is a freshman offensive lineman for UCF, listed at 6-foot-4 and 280 pounds in jersey No. 71. He is from Randolph, Massachusetts, and played his high school football at Tabor Academy.

athletes.name: Will Stone
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Stone is UCF's projected placekicker after four seasons at Texas, where he handled kickoffs and produced 139 touchbacks on 390 attempts. A five-star kicking recruit from Austin, he has yet to attempt a college field goal.

athletes.name: Atticus Bertrams
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Bertrams is a senior punter from Sydney, Australia, who transferred to UCF after three seasons at Wisconsin, which were also his first three years playing the sport. A three-year starter for the Badgers, he averaged 42.8 yards per punt for his career with 28 kicks of 50 or more yards and 65 downed inside the 20. In 2024 he averaged 45.3 yards per punt, ranking 12th nationally and second in the Big Ten, and he opened 2025 on the Ray Guy Award preseason watch list. He is the projected starting punter in 2026.

athletes.name: Kyle Hicks
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hicks is a redshirt sophomore long snapper from Nashville who transferred to UCF from Tennessee State for the 2026 season. He works in a cornerback room stocked with transfers including Jaylen Mbakwe and Zachary Tobe, pointing to nickel depth and special teams snaps in 2026.

athletes.name: Lawson Pritchett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Pritchett is a junior linebacker from Mt. Pleasant, South Carolina, who came to Georgia Tech from Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School. He played on special teams in three games as a true freshman in 2024 before redshirting. His father, Wes, was an All-America linebacker at Notre Dame and the leading tackler on the 1988 national championship team, and his brother Marshall is a tight end at Alabama.

athletes.name: Fenix Felton
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Felton signed with Georgia Tech in the 2025 class out of Eagle's Landing Christian Academy, where the McDonough, Ga., native was a team captain, all-state honoree and two-way player. He recorded 90 tackles and five interceptions on defense while adding 31 receptions for 489 yards on offense during his prep career. Felton saw his first extended college work late in his freshman season, playing more than 80 snaps over the final two games. Now a sophomore wearing No. 31, he moves up in a safety group that turned over significantly.

athletes.name: Jayden Barr
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Barr is a sophomore running back from Covington, Georgia, who redshirted as a true freshman in 2025. A two-way standout at Eastside High School, he rushed for 941 yards and 23 touchdowns while adding 57 tackles and two interceptions as a senior, and he finished his prep career with 1,877 rushing yards and 45 total touchdowns. He was named Region 8-4A Two Way Player of the Year as a junior.

athletes.name: Aidan Birr
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Birr is Georgia Tech's returning place-kicker and a 2025 Lou Groza Award finalist and third-team All-American. He made a school-record 25 of 29 field goals and all 45 extra points for 120 points in 2025.

athletes.name: C.J. Gamble
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Gamble is a freshman linebacker from Carrollton, Georgia, and a three-star signee out of Carrollton High School who was ranked the No. 47 linebacker in the nation. He was a defensive contributor on a team that reached the Georgia 6A state semifinals in 2025, making seven tackles in the region championship clincher and five more in a playoff win over Grayson.

athletes.name: Braylon Outlaw
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Braylon Outlaw is a freshman linebacker for Georgia Tech, listed at 6-1 and 220 pounds in No. 35. The Montgomery, Alabama native signed out of Pike Road High School. He joins a linebacker group that includes fifth-year players E.J. Lightsey, Melvin Jordan IV and Kyle Efford, so his 2026 role projects as developmental with special teams the likely first opportunity.

athletes.name: Kymani Morales
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Morales is a freshman safety from Miami who signed out of American Heritage School in Plantation as a three-star prospect ranked the No. 78 linebacker nationally by ESPN. He finished his prep career with 213 tackles, 36 tackles for loss and 19 sacks across three seasons, including 112 tackles as a junior, when he was named his team's defensive MVP. He was a two-year captain.

athletes.name: Rocco Xerogeanes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Xerogeanes is a freshman tight end from Atlanta who came to Georgia Tech from Woodward Academy. Listed at 6-4 and 245 pounds and wearing No. 36, he is majoring in industrial engineering and has not yet appeared in a game for the Yellow Jackets.

athletes.name: Alex Hunt
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Hunt is a freshman safety from Ruston, Louisiana, who joined Georgia Tech from Ruston High School. He is listed at 6-0 and 185 pounds, wears No. 37 and is majoring in business administration.

athletes.name: Joseph Moseley
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Moseley is a junior wide receiver from Marietta, Georgia, who came to Georgia Tech from Marietta High School. He redshirted as a true freshman in 2024 and has not seen game action through his first two seasons. He is majoring in civil engineering.

athletes.name: Isaac Obrokta
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He caught 35 passes for 528 yards and six touchdowns as a senior in 2025 and helped Rabun Gap win a district championship. He was rated a three-star prospect and is majoring in business administration.

athletes.name: Wills Campbell
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Campbell is a freshman wide receiver from Roswell, Georgia, who came to Georgia Tech from Roswell High School. He is listed at 6-3 and 205 pounds, wears No. 38 and is majoring in biomedical engineering.

athletes.name: Jack Richerson
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Richerson is a freshman tight end from Brookhaven, Georgia, who plans to play both football and baseball at Georgia Tech. At Marist he was a three-star prospect ranked the No. 31 tight end in the country and earned first-team all-region, all-county and Class 4A all-state honors as a junior, when he also posted 67 tackles and 15 sacks playing defensive end. He carried a 4.3 grade point average.

athletes.name: Will Kiker
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Will Kiker is a senior safety at Georgia Tech, listed at 6-1 and 200 pounds and wearing No. 39. The Ellijay, Georgia native signed out of Gilmer County High School in the north Georgia mountains. He has stayed with the program through his career and works behind Savion Riley and Tae Harris in the safety rotation, with special teams his primary 2026 avenue.

athletes.name: Joshua Taylor
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Taylor is a senior punter from Sharpsburg, Ga., who came to Georgia Tech out of Trinity Christian School. Listed at 6-3 and 220 pounds, he made his college debut as a true freshman in 2023 at then No. 17 Ole Miss, recording a 40-yard punt on his only attempt that season. He has since worked as a developmental option in the Yellow Jackets' specialist room and wears No. 40 heading into 2026.

athletes.name: Jordan Woods
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He was an all-region honoree, a four-year letterwinner and a senior captain at Pell City High School, and he was selected to play in the Alabama North-South all-star game. He helped the program reach the state playoffs in each of his final two seasons.

athletes.name: Landon Shaffer
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He made his collegiate debut with a 60-yard kickoff against Gardner-Webb in September 2025. As a high school senior he converted 14 of 18 field goal attempts with a long of 53 yards, made 38 of 39 extra points and put 56 of 60 kickoffs into the end zone.

athletes.name: Taje McCoy
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The Wichita, Kansas native transferred in from Oklahoma State and brings Big 12 experience to the defensive front. He adds depth to an end rotation led by A.J. Hoffler and Jordan Walker, so situational pass rush and special teams define his 2026 outlook.

athletes.name: Spencer Mermans
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

His size fits an in-line blocking role in a tight end room that also includes New Mexico State transfer Gavin Harris and Dartmouth transfer Chris Corbo.

athletes.name: Lex Willis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He recorded 31 tackles, including eight for loss, with a forced fumble and a fumble recovery in eight games as a junior. The only catch of his prep career was a 10-yard touchdown that decided his final high school game.

athletes.name: Kyle Efford
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Efford is Georgia Tech's starting linebacker and an honorable-mention All-ACC selection in 2025. He started all 13 games and led the Yellow Jackets in tackles for a third consecutive season with 77 stops.

athletes.name: Jonathan Genty
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Genty is a freshman punter from Roswell, Georgia, who came to Georgia Tech from Blessed Trinity High School. A consensus top-20 national punting prospect who Rivals ranked as high as fifth, he set a school record with a 73-yard punt as a junior and put more than half of his 40 kickoffs into the end zone as a senior. He also played soccer and basketball.

athletes.name: Alex Bacchetta
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Alex Bacchetta is a fifth-year punter for Georgia Tech, listed at 6-2 and 235 pounds in No. 47. The Atlanta native transferred in from Rice and returns to his home city for 2026. He competes for the punting job with senior Joshua Taylor and freshman Jonathan Genty, making the fall camp specialist competition the deciding factor in his role.

athletes.name: Cal Keeler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He is one of two long snappers on the 2026 roster along with fifth-year Ronnie Thomas III, so his role depends on the specialist competition for field goal and punt snapping duties.

athletes.name: Ronnie Thomas III
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Thomas is a fifth-year long snapper from Warner Robins, Ga., who attended Houston County High School. He began his college career at Kennesaw State, redshirting in 2022 after appearing in four games, then playing all nine of the Owls' games in 2023 and handling 91 total snaps before transferring to Georgia Tech. Listed at 5-10 and 180 pounds, he wears No. 50 for the Yellow Jackets and is the experienced snapper on a special teams unit heading into 2026.

athletes.name: Xavier Canales
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Canales is a sophomore offensive lineman from Marietta, Georgia, who redshirted as a true freshman in 2025. At Douglass High School he was a four-year letterwinner, a three-year captain and an all-state and all-region selection who allowed two sacks across four seasons. He also lettered twice in track and field and ranked in the top 15 of his class academically.

athletes.name: Kevin Peay, Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Peay signed with Georgia Tech out of Lancaster High School in Lancaster, S.C., where he played four years on varsity, served as captain for three seasons and helped the Bruins win two conference titles and an Upper State championship. A two-time all-state selection who was named offensive lineman MVP at an Under Armour Next camp in Charlotte, he was rated a three-star by 247Sports and a four-star by Rivals, which listed him as the top offensive lineman in South Carolina. The sophomore is listed at 6-4 and 310 pounds.

athletes.name: Christian Garrett
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The Monroe, Ga., native won back to back state championships in high school and ranked among the top 20 defensive linemen nationally in recruiting rankings. He appeared in four games as a true freshman in 2025 and enters his sophomore season at 6-4 and 265 pounds, wearing No. 55 and pushing for a larger interior role.

athletes.name: Tim Griffin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

Rivals rated him a four-star prospect and the nation's No. 21 defensive end out of nearby Alcovy High School, where he was a first-team all-region pick with 25 tackles as a senior.

athletes.name: Jacob Benjamin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

A Cherokee Bluff High School product listed at 6-4 and 300 pounds, he has not yet seen game action for the Yellow Jackets. He is majoring in economics.

athletes.name: Jimmy Bryson

He came to Georgia Tech from the Baylor School as a three-star prospect ranked the No. 26 recruit in Tennessee, where he was a two-time all-state and all-region selection, a three-year letterwinner and a senior captain. He also lettered three years in track as a shot putter.

athletes.name: Blake Belin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

At Cardinal Hayes he was a first-team all-state pick and the defensive MVP of a New York state Catholic school championship game. His father, Henry, played at Vanderbilt.

athletes.name: Courtlin Heard

The Newnan, Georgia native signed out of East Coweta High School alongside fellow Yellow Jackets freshman lineman Courtlin Heard. With transfers Markell Samuel, Will Reed and Favour Edwin in the room, his 2026 season projects as developmental.

He adds veteran depth to a line that also carries Oklahoma State transfer Markell Samuel and Auburn transfer Favour Edwin.

athletes.name: Eli Rickell

athletes.name: Joseph Ionata
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ionata is Georgia Tech's projected starting center after transferring from Alabama, where he spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons. He was a four-star recruit ranked among the nation's top interior offensive linemen out of Clearwater, Florida.

athletes.name: Jameson Riggs
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The Douglasville, Ga., native redshirted his first season, then appeared in all 13 games in 2025 as a reserve, playing 196 snaps split between left and right tackle without allowing a sack. Listed at 6-6 and 305 pounds, the junior serves on the team leadership council and is in position to start at right tackle in 2026.

athletes.name: Markell Samuel
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Markell Samuel is a fifth-year offensive lineman at Georgia Tech, listed at 6-4 and 305 pounds and wearing No. 71. The Fayetteville, North Carolina native transferred in from Oklahoma State with Power Four experience. He is one of several veteran transfer linemen on the 2026 roster along with Will Reed and Malachi Carney, and he competes for interior rotation snaps.

athletes.name: Malachi Carney
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Carney is a returning starting offensive lineman for Georgia Tech and an honorable-mention All-ACC pick in 2025, when he started all 13 games at right tackle. The South Alabama transfer allowed just three quarterback hits over 768 snaps.

athletes.name: Favour Edwin
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The McDonough, Georgia native returned to his home state after beginning his career at Auburn. His height stands out among the tackles on the 2026 roster, and he competes for rotation snaps with Joseph Ionata and Jameson Riggs.

athletes.name: Andrew Rosinski

He adds interior depth to a line that also includes transfers Will Reed, Markell Samuel and Joseph Ionata.

athletes.name: Krew Moledor

athletes.name: Josh Petty
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He was rated a five-star prospect and the No. 21 overall recruit in the nation by 247Sports, making him the second five-star signee in Georgia Tech history. He also won the Georgia 285-pound state wrestling title as a sophomore.

athletes.name: Ethan Mackenny
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Jordan Floyd
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The Lilburn, Georgia native signed out of Parkview High School, one of the state's larger classification programs. He is among the heaviest linemen on the 2026 roster and competes for interior rotation snaps behind the veteran transfers in the room.

athletes.name: Connor Roush
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He came from the Wesleyan School as a three-star prospect ranked the No. 44 tight end nationally, where he was a four-year letterwinner, a senior captain and the owner of the second-most tackles for loss in school history. He also lettered in track and field and baseball.

athletes.name: Cal Faulkner
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He played quarterback at Lumpkin County, where he was named Region 7-3A Player of the Year and first-team all-state as a junior after throwing for 1,706 yards and 19 touchdowns and rushing for 969 yards and 18 scores while leading the school to its first region title.

athletes.name: Kentrell Davis
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

Parker High School he caught 34 passes for 619 yards and 10 touchdowns as a senior and finished with 1,490 receiving yards over three varsity seasons. He led Parker with 165 receiving yards during its playoff run.

athletes.name: Blake Ragsdale
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)
athletes.blurb: Ragsdale is a junior tight end from Nashville, Tennessee, who came to Georgia Tech from Montgomery Bell Academy. He redshirted as a true freshman in 2024 and has not seen game action through two seasons. He is majoring in international affairs and modern languages.

athletes.name: Evan Haynes
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

His size gives the Yellow Jackets an outside option behind transfers Debron Gatling, Jaiven Plummer and Isaiah Fuhrmann, so 2026 projects as rotational work with special teams snaps available.

athletes.name: J.J. Winston
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He totaled 1,325 receiving yards over 13 games while helping Rome to an 11-2 record and the Georgia 5A state semifinals, after catching 34 passes for 703 yards and 10 touchdowns as a junior.

athletes.name: Kevin Roche, Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Coi Jean-Noel
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

A four-year letterwinner, he set career highs as a senior with 53 catches for 713 yards and six touchdowns and accounted for 890 total yards, including 166 passing.

athletes.name: Nate Agyemang
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

ESPN ranked him the No. 22 tight end in the nation. He totaled 760 career receiving yards and averaged 23.2 yards per catch as a senior while helping Kell win a region title and reach the Class 4A state semifinals.

athletes.name: A.J. Hoffler
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He is one of the more experienced defensive ends on the 2026 roster alongside Rutgers transfer Jordan Walker and Alabama transfer Noah Carter, and he factors into the pass rush rotation.

athletes.name: Chris Elko
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

The Roswell, Georgia native signed out of Roswell High School and has stayed with the program locally. He works behind a receiver group reshaped by transfers including Debron Gatling and Jaiven Plummer, with special teams his clearest route to 2026 snaps.

athletes.name: Andre Fuller, Jr.
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He started each of the first three games of his career. At Grayson High School he was a four-time all-county honoree and helped win a 7A state title in 2020.

athletes.name: Christian Speakman

athletes.name: Drew Cohen

He is listed at 6-3 and 245 pounds and is majoring in business administration.

athletes.name: Derry Norris, Jr.

athletes.name: Tawfiq Thomas
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Shymeik Jones
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

He is among the taller interior linemen on the 2026 roster and competes for rotation snaps with Tawfiq Thomas and Derry Norris, Jr.

athletes.name: Landen Marshall

He works in an interior rotation that also carries Colorado transfer Tawfiq Thomas and sophomore Christian Garrett, so nose and three-technique depth snaps are his likely role.

athletes.name: Amier Clarke
athletes.source: Estimate (On3 does not publicly disclose a figure)

athletes.name: Vincent Carroll-Jackson
